kept.title: TakesNoThinkingDepth refuses budgets for GLM/Kimi/MiniMax on every host, breaking OpenRouter calls that worked on base
kept.summary: TakesNoThinkingDepth (via thinksBySwitchOnly) looks only at the model name. It says kimi-k2*, glm below 5.2 and minimax-m* take no budget or effort on any host, so the openai door returns ErrThinkingBudgetUnsupported before sending on OpenRouter and vLLM, even though those hosts accept the unified reasoning field.
kept.failure_scenario: openai.New(WithBaseURL("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"), WithModernReasoningFormat(), WithModel("z-ai/glm-4.6" | "moonshotai/kimi-k2.5" | "minimax/minimax-m2")) + llms.WithReasoning(ReasoningNone, 4000). HEAD returns `model "z-ai/glm-4.6" takes no thinking budget or effort level; leave the budget unset` and sends no request. BASE sent {"reasoning":{"effort":"low"}} and the call succeeded. The same local error hits vLLM names such as zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air when the caller passes an explicit budget.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeORBudget (overlay in llms/openai, custom Doer capturing the body, base URL openrouter.ai, modern format). HEAD: err=takes no thinking budget... body= (empty) for all three models. BASE: err=<nil>, body carries "reasoning":{"effort":"low"}. Door path: openaillm.go budgetHasNoField → reasoning.TakesNoThinkingDepth. It is bypassed only when ModernReasoningFormat && UseReasoningMaxTokens. Commit 2f174a8 and 51b63ac: the refusal was measured on Z.ai/Moonshot/LiteLLM ('zai does not support parameters: [reasoning_effort]'), not on OpenRouter. OpenRouter documents reasoning.effort for GLM-4.5-Air/DeepSeek (search result; openrouter.ai is egress-blocked here).

repro.evidence: Probe TestProbeVF (probes/vf-effortwire, package openai_test, custom Doer capturing the body; overlay in llms/openai, run at HEAD 355dc71 and BASE da7016e). OpenRouter base URL + WithModernReasoningFormat + WithReasoning(ReasoningNone, 4000): HEAD returns `model "z-ai/glm-4.6" takes no thinking budget or effort level; leave the budget unset` with an empty body (no request sent) for z-ai/glm-4.6, moonshotai/kimi-k2.5, minimax/minimax-m2 and zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air. BASE: err=nil, body {"reasoning":{"effort":"low"}}. vLLM URL (http://localhost:8000/v1, legacy format) + zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air + budget 4000: HEAD same local error; BASE sent reasoning_effort:"low". Path: openaillm.go:440 budgetHasNoField -> reasoning.TakesNoThinkingDepth(model), which ignores o.host; only bypassed when ModernReasoningFormat && UseReasoningMaxTokens. Commits 2f174a8/51b63ac justify the rule with Z.ai, Moonshot and MiniMax native APIs and the LiteLLM gateway ('zai does not support parameters'), not OpenRouter; the tests that say 'openrouter' use LiteLLM-style `openrouter/...` model prefixes, not the openrouter.ai host. OpenRouter documents a unified `reasoning` object and normalises effort/max_tokens across providers (docs page found via search; openrouter.ai is egress-blocked here, so no live check).
repro.comment: `TakesNoThinkingDepth` only looks at the model name, so `budgetHasNoField` (openaillm.go:440) returns `ErrThinkingBudgetUnsupported` for kimi-k2*, glm before 5.2 and minimax-m* on every host, not only on the Z.ai/Moonshot/MiniMax APIs where the refusal was measured. I ran a probe with a body-capturing Doer, `WithBaseURL("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1")`, `WithModernReasoningFormat()` and `WithReasoning(llms.ReasoningNone, 4000)`. HEAD fails locally with `model "z-ai/glm-4.6" takes no thinking budget or effort level` and sends nothing, and it does the same for moonshotai/kimi-k2.5, minimax/minimax-m2 and zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air. The same happens on a vLLM URL with zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air. The previous release sent `{"reasoning":{"effort":"low"}}` (or `reasoning_effort:"low"` on vLLM), and these calls worked. OpenRouter documents that its `reasoning` object is normalised across providers, but I could not reach openrouter.ai from here, so how it treats these models is unverified. Suggested fix: make the check host-aware, as `ServedByDeepSeek`/`DashScopeRoute` are (for example, apply it only on api.z.ai, api.moonshot.ai and api.minimax.io, or on the native provider routes), or at least exempt `ModernReasoningFormat` clients.

refute.reason: My own probe (HEAD vs BASE, modern format, WithReasoning(ReasoningNone,4000)) reproduces it. On HEAD, z-ai/glm-4.6, moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 and minimax/minimax-m2 each return ErrThinkingBudgetUnsupported and no request is sent. BASE sent reasoning:{effort:"low"}. The strongest case for dismissing it: commit 2f174a8 (PAGI-345) is deliberate, and thinking_budget_field_test.go pins a 'modern format alone' row as refused. Callers also have a workaround, WithUsingReasoningMaxTokens, which is exempt. That does not hold up. The commit justifies the refusal by saying no field on the vendor's own door (Z.ai, Moonshot, MiniMax) can carry a budget. On OpenRouter the unified reasoning object carries it, and OpenRouter documents reasoning effort for Kimi K2.6 and GLM. The rule looks only at the model name, never the host, so an OpenRouter or vLLM call that succeeded on BASE now fails locally. The HEAD door itself turns a budget into an effort level for GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3, and BASE did exactly that for these names.

kept.title: RejectsSamplingWhileThinking keys on a classified OpenAI name, so deployments, aliases and unclassified GPT-5 variants now send temperature with reasoning_effort
kept.summary: Base dropped temperature and top_p whenever an effort went on the wire. HEAD drops them only when openAIProperName(model) && OpenAIReasoningCapsFor(model).Known, and only when IsReasoningModel(model) is true. Azure deployment names, LiteLLM aliases and unclassified OpenAI reasoning models (gpt-5.3-codex, gpt-5-codex) therefore carry the caller's temperature and top_p next to reasoning_effort, which OpenAI reasoning models reject.
kept.failure_scenario: Azure: openai.New(WithAPIType(APITypeAzure), WithBaseURL("https://myres.openai.azure.com"), WithModel("prod-reasoner")) + WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0) + WithTemperature(0.2). HEAD body is {"temperature":0.2,"reasoning_effort":"high"}; BASE sent only reasoning_effort. On a GPT-5/o-series deployment the vendor returns 400 "Unsupported value: 'temperature' ... Only the default (1) value is supported". The same happens on api.openai.com with gpt-5.3-codex and gpt-5-codex, and on a LiteLLM alias such as my-gpt5-deployment.
kept.evidence: Probes TestProbeAzure, TestProbeAlias and TestProbeOpenAICodex in llms/openai, comparing HEAD and BASE bodies. HEAD: my-gpt5-deployment → "temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.9,"reasoning_effort":"high"; gpt-5.3-codex and gpt-5-codex → "temperature":0.2,"reasoning_effort":"high". BASE: temperature and top_p absent in every case, because of the deferred drop in the base setReasoning. Intent (e7ef066, PAGI-288) was to stop applying OpenAI's rule to GLM and Kimi, not to start sending sampling to OpenAI reasoning deployments.

repro.evidence: Same probe, WithTemperature(0.2)+WithTopP(0.9)+WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0). HEAD bodies: Azure (WithAPIType(APITypeAzure), base https://myres.openai.azure.com, model prod-reasoner) -> {"temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.9,"reasoning_effort":"high"}; api.openai.com my-gpt5-deployment, gpt-5.3-codex, gpt-5-codex -> {"temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.9,"reasoning_effort":"high"}; gpt-5 and o3 -> only reasoning_effort. BASE bodies for all of them: only reasoning_effort (base setReasoning had a defer that nils Temperature/TopP whenever ReasoningEffort/Reasoning is set). HEAD enforceSamplingPolicy only strips sampling when refusesSamplingWhileThinking -> thinkingRuns requires IsReasoningModel(model) and RejectsSamplingWhileThinking requires openAIProperName && OpenAIReasoningCapsFor(model).Known, so an effort on the wire alone no longer strips anything. Intent of e7ef066 (PAGI-288) was to exempt GLM/Kimi, not OpenAI deployments. OpenAI reasoning models reject non-default temperature ('Unsupported value: temperature ... Only the default (1) value is supported' / 'Unsupported parameter: temperature'), per OpenAI community threads and error libraries found by search.
repro.comment: The previous release dropped `temperature`/`top_p` whenever a reasoning effort went on the wire. HEAD drops them only when `IsReasoningModel(model)` and `RejectsSamplingWhileThinking(model)` (a classified OpenAI name with known caps) are both true. Azure deployment names, proxy aliases and unclassified models such as gpt-5.3-codex and gpt-5-codex therefore send the caller's sampling next to `reasoning_effort`. A probe with a body-capturing Doer, `WithTemperature(0.2)`, `WithTopP(0.9)` and `WithReasoning(llms.ReasoningHigh, 0)` shows HEAD sending `{"temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.9,"reasoning_effort":"high"}` for Azure `prod-reasoner`, `my-gpt5-deployment`, `gpt-5.3-codex` and `gpt-5-codex`, while the previous release sent only `reasoning_effort`. OpenAI's reasoning models reject a non-default temperature with a 400 ("Only the default (1) value is supported"), so these calls now fail at the vendor if the deployment is a GPT-5/o-series model. Suggested fix: keep the vendor exemption from e7ef066 for known non-OpenAI families (GLM, Kimi and so on), but restore the old default of stripping temperature/top_p when an effort is sent for any name that is not positively classified as another vendor.

refute.reason: My probe confirms it. On HEAD, gpt-5-codex, gpt-5.3-codex and my-gpt5-deployment with WithReasoning(High)+WithTemperature(0.2)+WithTopP(0.9) send temperature:0.2 and top_p:0.9 next to reasoning_effort:high. BASE dropped both whenever an effort went on the wire, and gpt-5 and o3 still drop them on HEAD. Commit e7ef066 (PAGI-288) meant only to stop applying OpenAI's rule to GLM and Kimi. b43095c/d926315 say OpenAI reasoning models reject temperature and top_p while they think. Gating the drop on openAIProperName && OpenAIReasoningCapsFor.Known therefore also covers arbitrary Azure deployment names, gateway aliases and unclassified or future GPT-5 names. That regression was not intended. One weak spot: gpt-5-codex is a Responses-API model, so that example is less realistic on chat completions. The Azure deployment and alias cases are enough on their own.

Suggested fix: keep the vendor exemption from e7ef066 for known non-OpenAI families (GLM, Kimi and so on), but restore the old default of stripping temperature/top_p when an effort is sent for any name that is not positively classified as another vendor.

kept.title: AcceptsEffortWire drops reasoning effort on OpenRouter/Groq and turns WithReasoningDisabled into a local error
kept.summary: AcceptsEffortWire encodes that DashScope, Moonshot and Z.ai refuse reasoning_effort, but it keys on the model name alone. On OpenRouter (modern `reasoning` object) and Groq the effort is therefore dropped for every qwen/qwq, kimi-k2*, glm<5.2, minimax-m* and grok-code-fast/grok-4.20 name. openAIOffWire (off.go:195) then answers OffUnsupported for these names, so an explicit off fails locally on hosts that serve it.
kept.failure_scenario: (1) OpenRouter with modern format, model qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b, qwen/qwen3-max, z-ai/glm-4.6, moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking, minimax/minimax-m2 or x-ai/grok-code-fast-1, plus WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0). BASE sent {"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}}; HEAD sends nothing and only records a drop warning. (2) Groq (api.groq.com) qwen/qwen3-32b + WithReasoningDisabled(): HEAD returns ErrReasoningOffUnsupported, but Groq documents reasoning_effort "none" for this model and BASE made the call. OpenRouter qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b off also errors now.
kept.evidence: Probes TestProbeOpenRouterEffort and TestProbeGroqOff in llms/openai, comparing HEAD and BASE. HEAD bodies have no reasoning field; qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b off → `reasoning cannot be disabled`; Groq qwen/qwen3-32b off → `reasoning cannot be disabled`. BASE: reasoning.effort high/none present and no error. Commits 333a9c7 and 51b63ac measured the refusal on DashScope, Moonshot and LiteLLM routes only. Groq doc (search result): reasoning_effort for qwen3-32b accepts "none" and "default".

repro.evidence: Same probe. OpenRouter + WithModernReasoningFormat + WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0): HEAD body has no reasoning field for qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b, qwen/qwen3-max, z-ai/glm-4.6, moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking, minimax/minimax-m2, x-ai/grok-code-fast-1; BASE sent {"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}} for all. Groq (https://api.groq.com/openai/v1) qwen/qwen3-32b + ReasoningHigh: HEAD sends nothing, BASE sent reasoning_effort:"high". WithReasoningDisabled(): HEAD returns `reasoning cannot be disabled for model "qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b"` (OpenRouter) and `... "qwen/qwen3-32b"` (Groq) without sending; BASE made the call (note: BASE omitted the field rather than sending "none", so BASE did not actually disable thinking, but the call succeeded). Path: openaillm.go:424 AcceptsEffortWire(DashScopeRoute(model, host)) - DashScopeRoute only adds a prefix for DashScope hosts, and AcceptsEffortWire itself ignores host; off.go:195 openAIOffWire returns OffUnsupported when !AcceptsEffortWire. Commits 333a9c7/51b63ac cite DashScope, Moonshot and LiteLLM refusals only. Groq docs (search: console.groq.com/docs/reasoning, /docs/model/qwen/qwen3-32b) document reasoning_effort "none"/"default" for qwen/qwen3-32b, so Groq serves the disable HEAD refuses.
repro.comment: `AcceptsEffortWire` treats a model name as proof that the host refuses `reasoning_effort`, but the refusals it encodes were measured only on DashScope, Moonshot and the LiteLLM gateway. On other hosts the effort is now silently dropped, and an explicit off fails locally. A probe with a body-capturing Doer against `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` (modern format) and `WithReasoning(llms.ReasoningHigh, 0)` shows HEAD sending no `reasoning` field for qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b, qwen/qwen3-max, z-ai/glm-4.6, moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking, minimax/minimax-m2 and x-ai/grok-code-fast-1, where the previous release sent `{"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}}`. On Groq, `qwen/qwen3-32b` + `WithReasoningDisabled()` now returns `ErrReasoningOffUnsupported` before sending (the same happens on OpenRouter), although Groq documents `reasoning_effort: "none"` for that model; the previous release let the call through. How OpenRouter and Groq handle the field depends on the vendor, and I checked it only in their docs, not live. Suggested fix: apply the refusal only on the hosts or routes where it was observed (DashScope, the Moonshot and Z.ai APIs, LiteLLM provider prefixes), using the same host-aware pattern as `ServedByDeepSeek`.

refute.reason: My probe confirms that, with the modern format, HEAD sends no reasoning field for qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b, z-ai/glm-4.6, moonshotai/kimi-k2.5, minimax/minimax-m2 and x-ai/grok-code-fast-1 on WithReasoning(High); BASE sent reasoning:{effort:"high"}. AcceptsEffortWire looks only at the model name, but the refusal it encodes was measured on DashScope, Moonshot, Z.ai and LiteLLM (333a9c7, 51b63ac). On OpenRouter the reasoning object is normalised per model, so the effort is dropped on a host that serves it. Only a warning tells the caller. The off path in the finding is partly overstated. For qwen/qwen3-32b (the Groq case) and qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b, BASE sent no disable token, so the base call 'worked' only as a silent no-op. HEAD now fails with ErrReasoningOffUnsupported, even though Groq documents reasoning_effort "none" for qwen3-32b. For grok-code-fast, kimi-k2.5 and minimax-m2, BASE did send reasoning:{effort:"none"}, and HEAD now errors (grok, minimax) or sends a Z.ai/Moonshot-only thinking object (glm, kimi). The core defect stands: capabilities measured on the vendors' own hosts are applied to every host.

kept.comment: `AcceptsEffortWire` treats a model name as proof that the host refuses `reasoning_effort`, but the refusals it encodes were measured only on DashScope, Moonshot and the LiteLLM gateway. On other hosts the effort is now silently dropped, and an explicit off fails locally. A probe with a body-capturing Doer against `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` (modern format) and `WithReasoning(llms.ReasoningHigh, 0)` shows HEAD sending no `reasoning` field for qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b, qwen/qwen3-max, z-ai/glm-4.6, moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking, minimax/minimax-m2 and x-ai/grok-code-fast-1, where the previous release sent `{"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}}`. On Groq, `qwen/qwen3-32b` + `WithReasoningDisabled()` now returns `ErrReasoningOffUnsupported` before sending (the same happens on OpenRouter), although Groq documents `reasoning_effort: "none"` for that model; the previous release let the call through. How OpenRouter and Groq handle the field depends on the vendor, and I checked it only in their docs, not live. Suggested fix: apply the refusal only on the hosts or routes where it was observed (DashScope, the Moonshot and Z.ai APIs, LiteLLM provider prefixes), using the same host-aware pattern as `ServedByDeepSeek`.

kept.title: Claude Opus 5.5 is classified as disablable (Opus 5 rules), but the vendor documents its thinking as always on
kept.summary: The substring entry "claude-opus-5" in defaultOnClaude also matches claude-opus-5-5, and alwaysOnClaude has no entry for it. ResolveOff therefore returns OffDisableClaude (Anthropic and Bedrock) or OffDisableThinkingObject (OpenAI-shaped). Anthropic's docs say Opus 5.5 thinking is "Always on" and reject thinking.type=disabled with 400.
kept.failure_scenario: anthropic.New(WithModel("claude-opus-5-5")) + llms.WithReasoningDisabled() sends {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}. The API answers 400 `"thinking.type.disabled" is not supported for this model` instead of the local ErrReasoningOffUnsupported that claude-fable-5-1 gets. Bedrock (anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 / us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5) behaves the same way. llms.ReasoningSupportFor("claude-opus-5-5", ProviderAnthropic).CannotDisable is false, so a UI offers an off switch that always fails. The OpenRouter alias claude-opus-latest, which now points at the newest Opus, has the same gap.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeDump (llms/reasoning): claude-opus-5-5 alwaysOn=false, defOn=true, offA=1(OffDisableClaude), offB=1, offO=6(OffDisableThinkingObject). Probe TestProbeOpus55Off (llms/anthropic): body has "thinking":{"type":"disabled"}, err=nil, cannotDisable=false, while claude-fable-5-1 → ErrReasoningOffUnsupported. Vendor: platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-troubleshooting table: 'Claude Opus 5.5 | Adaptive only | Always on | "enabled", "disabled"' rejected with 400. models/opus-5-5/migration-guide: 'thinking: {"type": "disabled"} ... are rejected'. Opus 5.5 retirement is 'not sooner than September 22, 2027', so it was released before the PR head (2026-09-25), and reasoning_test.go already lists claude-opus-5-5.

repro.evidence: Probe TestProbeOpus55 (llms/reasoning, overlay) at HEAD 355dc71: claude-opus-5-5, anthropic.claude-opus-5-5, us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 and anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 all give ClaudeThinkingAlwaysOn=false, ClaudeThinkingDefaultsOn=true, ResolveOff Anthropic=OffDisableClaude(1), Bedrock=OffDisableClaude(1), OpenAI=OffDisableThinkingObject(6), and ReasoningSupportFor(...,ProviderAnthropic).CannotDisable=false. claude-fable-5-1 gets OffUnsupported(8) and CannotDisable=true. Cause: alwaysOnClaude (claude_capability.go:88-91) has no Opus 5.5 entry, and the substring "claude-opus-5" in defaultOnClaude also matches claude-opus-5-5. anthropicllm.go:228 turns OffDisableClaude into thinking:{type:"disabled"}, and the Bedrock converse path does the same (bedrockclient_converse.go:283). BASE da7016e also classified claude-opus-5-5 as defaultOn and not alwaysOn, so this is a gap the PR leaves open rather than a regression. The PR rewrote these tables, and reasoning_test.go:773-775 lists claude-opus-5-5, so the model was known. Vendor: Anthropic's bundled Claude API reference (claude-api skill, Thinking & Effort table) says for Claude Opus 5.5: '{type: "disabled"} and {type: "enabled", budget_tokens} return 400 at every effort level - omit the param and lower effort instead', and 'thinking can't be disabled'. For claude-opus-latest the probe shows HEAD now resolves OffDisableClaude, while BASE resolved OffOmit. Whether that alias already points to Opus 5.5 depends on the vendor and was not verified.
repro.comment: `alwaysOnClaude` has no entry for Claude Opus 5.5. The substring `claude-opus-5` in `defaultOnClaude` also matches `claude-opus-5-5`, so the model gets the Opus 5 "default-on but disablable" rules. As a result, `ResolveOff` returns `OffDisableClaude` for Anthropic and Bedrock and `OffDisableThinkingObject` for OpenAI-shaped doors, and `ReasoningSupportFor("claude-opus-5-5", ProviderAnthropic).CannotDisable` is false. A probe calling these functions for claude-opus-5-5, anthropic./us.anthropic. and anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 shows this, while claude-fable-5-1 correctly gets `OffUnsupported`. Anthropic documents that Opus 5.5 thinking cannot be disabled: `{"type":"disabled"}` returns 400 at every effort level. So `WithReasoningDisabled()` produces a vendor 400 instead of the local `ErrReasoningOffUnsupported`, and a UI built on the hint offers an off switch that always fails. Suggested fix: add `claude-opus-5-5` (and its dotted/Bedrock spellings via `canonicalClaude`) to `alwaysOnClaude`, plus a test next to the existing claude-fable-5-1 case. Also re-check `claude-opus-latest` once it points to Opus 5.5 (that part depends on the vendor).

refute.reason: Anthropic's troubleshooting table (fetched from platform.claude.com) lists Opus 5.5 as 'Adaptive only | Always on | rejects "enabled", "disabled"', and its 400 section names Opus 5.5. On HEAD, alwaysOnClaude has no claude-opus-5-5 entry, and the defaultOnClaude substring "claude-opus-5" matches it. ResolveOff therefore sends thinking:{type:disabled} instead of returning ErrReasoningOffUnsupported, and CannotDisable comes out false. Nothing in the code, tests or commits marks this as intended; reasoning_test.go only checks that the name counts as a reasoning model. The Anthropic and OpenAI-shaped paths already behaved this way in BASE (same tables, and BASE ResolveOff returned OffDisableClaude for default-on Claude). One part is new: on Bedrock, BASE returned OffUnsupported for every default-on Claude model, while HEAD sends the disable, so the Bedrock case is a regression.

The substring `claude-opus-5` in `defaultOnClaude` also matches `claude-opus-5-5`, so the model gets the Opus 5 "default-on but disablable" rules. As a result, `ResolveOff` returns `OffDisableClaude` for Anthropic and Bedrock and `OffDisableThinkingObject` for OpenAI-shaped doors, and `ReasoningSupportFor("claude-opus-5-5", ProviderAnthropic).CannotDisable` is false. Anthropic documents that Opus 5.5 thinking cannot be disabled: `{"type":"disabled"}` returns 400 at every effort level. So `WithReasoningDisabled()` produces a vendor 400 instead of the local `ErrReasoningOffUnsupported`, and a UI built on the hint offers an off switch that always fails. Suggested fix: add `claude-opus-5-5` (and its dotted/Bedrock spellings via `canonicalClaude`) to `alwaysOnClaude`, plus a test next to the existing claude-fable-5-1 case. kept.title: qwenFlagThinkers matches exact names only, so DashScope -latest and dated snapshots never get enable_thinking or thinking_budget
kept.summary: QwenThinkingEnabledByFlag and DashScopeTakesThinkingBudget look the name up in an exact-key map. qwen-plus-latest, qwen-plus-2025-07-28, qwen-flash-2025-07-28, qwen3-max-2026-01-23 and qwen-turbo-latest are the same hybrid-thinking models, but they get neither enable_thinking:true nor thinking_budget. AcceptsEffortWire also drops the effort for them, so a reasoning request sends nothing.
kept.failure_scenario: openai.New(WithBaseURL("https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1"), WithModel("qwen-plus-latest")) + WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0) or WithReasoning(ReasoningNone,2000). The body has no enable_thinking, no thinking_budget and no effort, so the model answers without thinking and only a drop warning is recorded. The same call with qwen-plus sends enable_thinking:true (and thinking_budget:2000).
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeDashScope (llms/openai, HEAD): qwen-plus → {"enable_thinking":true[,"thinking_budget":2000]}; qwen-plus-latest, qwen-plus-2025-07-28, qwen-flash-2025-07-28 and qwen3-max-2026-01-23 → body with only model+messages. Alibaba Model Studio deep-thinking doc (search result): 'qwen-plus, qwen-plus-latest, and qwen-plus-2025-04-28 and later snapshot versions, operating in hybrid thinking mode with thinking disabled by default'; 'qwen-flash, qwen-flash-2025-07-28 and later'.

repro.evidence: Probe TestProbeDS (llms/openai, captured request body via WithHTTPClient; base URL https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1). HEAD: qwen-plus + WithReasoning(High,0) sends {"enable_thinking":true}; with WithReasoning(None,2000) it sends {"enable_thinking":true,"thinking_budget":2000}. qwen-plus-latest, qwen-plus-2025-07-28, qwen-flash-2025-07-28, qwen3-max-2026-01-23 and qwen-turbo-latest send only model+messages in both cases, with no error. Cause: qwenFlagThinkers (qwen_capability.go:46) is an exact-key map used by QwenThinkingEnabledByFlag (openaillm.go:321) and DashScopeTakesThinkingBudget (openaillm.go:496), and AcceptsEffortWire returns false for every qwen* name (effort_wire.go:185), so nothing is sent. BASE sent reasoning_effort high/low for all of these names. Vendor: Alibaba Model Studio deep-thinking doc (help.aliyun.com/en/model-studio/deep-thinking, search result) says qwen-plus, qwen-plus-latest and qwen-plus-2025-04-28 and later snapshots run in hybrid thinking mode with thinking off by default, and enable_thinking turns it on.
repro.comment: `qwenFlagThinkers` is looked up by exact name, so DashScope's `-latest` aliases and dated snapshots of the same hybrid-thinking models are not recognised. This affects `qwen-plus-latest`, `qwen-plus-2025-07-28`, `qwen-flash-2025-07-28`, `qwen3-max-2026-01-23` and `qwen-turbo-latest`. They get neither `enable_thinking:true` nor `thinking_budget`, and `AcceptsEffortWire` drops the effort for every `qwen*` name, so a reasoning request sends nothing. A probe that captures the request body on the dashscope-intl host shows `qwen-plus` + `WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0)` sending `"enable_thinking":true` (and `"thinking_budget":2000` for a 2000-token budget), while the five names above send only model+messages and return no error. kept.title: Thinking-object off wire is chosen by model name, so OpenRouter gets Z.ai/DeepSeek-native `thinking` instead of its reasoning field
kept.summary: disablesByThinkingObject/thinkingObjectOffOnHost pick OffDisableThinkingObject for glm-4.5..5.x, kimi-k2.5/2.6, deepseek-v4 and minimax-m3 on any host except DashScope and Mistral. On OpenRouter, even with WithModernReasoningFormat, WithReasoningDisabled therefore sends {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}, a field OpenRouter's schema does not define, instead of the reasoning.effort "none" that base sent.
kept.failure_scenario: OpenRouter + WithModernReasoningFormat + WithModel("z-ai/glm-4.6") + WithReasoningDisabled(). HEAD body: {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}. BASE body: {"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}}. If OpenRouter drops the unknown field, thinking stays on and is billed although the caller turned it off.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeOpenRouterEffort off rows: HEAD z-ai/glm-4.6 → "thinking":{"type":"disabled"}; BASE → "reasoning":{"effort":"none"}. OpenRouter documents disabling via reasoning.effort "none" (search result; openrouter.ai docs egress-blocked). Whether OpenRouter forwards `thinking` to the provider could not be checked here.

repro.evidence: Probe TestProbeOR (llms/openai, captured body, base URL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, WithReasoningDisabled). HEAD, with or without WithModernReasoningFormat: z-ai/glm-4.6, moonshotai/kimi-k2.5, deepseek/deepseek-v4 and minimax/minimax-m3 all send {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}. BASE sent {"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}} with the modern format and reasoning_effort:"none" without it. Cause: openAIOffWire → disablesByThinkingObject → thinkingObjectOffOnHost (off.go:164-172) looks only at the model name. The only host-aware exception is the dashscope/ route; ModernReasoningFormat and the host are never consulted. setReasoningOff (openaillm.go:604-609) gates the Claude thinking object with sendsClaudeThinkingObject, which is false for ModernReasoningFormat and public hosts, but it applies no such gate for GLM/Kimi/DeepSeek/MiniMax. Intent commit 870c4dc ('disable thinking the way Zhipu and MiniMax actually accept') targeted the vendors' own APIs. OpenRouter documents disabling via reasoning.effort "none" (search result, openrouter.ai reasoning-tokens guide). The OpenRouter docs are egress-blocked here, so whether OpenRouter forwards or ignores a top-level `thinking` field could not be verified.
repro.comment: The thinking-object off wire is chosen from the model name alone. On OpenRouter, even with `WithModernReasoningFormat()`, `WithReasoningDisabled()` for `z-ai/glm-4.6`, `moonshotai/kimi-k2.5`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4` or `minimax/minimax-m3` now sends `{"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}` instead of the `{"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}}` the previous release sent. I confirmed both bodies with a probe that captures the request at HEAD and at base. OpenRouter documents disabling reasoning through its unified `reasoning` object (`effort: "none"`). `thinking` is the Z.ai/Moonshot/MiniMax native field, and the Claude branch of `setReasoningOff` already avoids it on public hosts and in modern format through `sendsClaudeThinkingObject`. If OpenRouter drops the unknown field (this depends on the vendor and I could not check it here), thinking stays on and is billed although the caller turned it off. Suggested fix: make `thinkingObjectOffOnHost` or `setReasoningOff` aware of the host and the format, and fall back to the effort-none wire on aggregators or when `ModernReasoningFormat` is set.

refute.reason: Reproduced with an overlay probe against a local httptest server. With WithModernReasoningFormat, z-ai/glm-4.6 and WithReasoningDisabled, HEAD sends {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}} and BASE sends {"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}}; without the modern format, BASE sends reasoning_effort "none". The rule is chosen by model name only. thinkingObjectOffOnHost treats only dashscope/ and Mistral-served names specially; nothing reads an OpenRouter host or the modern-format flag, and no test pins the thinking object for OpenRouter. The commits that justify the rule (870c4dc, 51b63ac) cite measurements on the native vendor or LiteLLM gateway, not OpenRouter, whose documented normalized control is reasoning.effort/enabled. I could not check whether OpenRouter forwards an unknown `thinking` field (openrouter.ai is egress-blocked here), so the billing impact is unconfirmed. The code clearly changes the wire away from OpenRouter's documented field, so the finding stands. Side note from the same probe: on HEAD, z-ai/glm-4.6 with ReasoningHigh now sends no reasoning field at all, while BASE sent reasoning.effort "high".

I confirmed both bodies with a probe that captures the request at HEAD and at base. If OpenRouter drops the unknown field (this depends on the vendor and I could not check it here), thinking stays on and is billed although the caller turned it off. Suggested fix: make `thinkingObjectOffOnHost` or `setReasoningOff` aware of the host and the format, and fall back to the effort-none wire on aggregators or when `ModernReasoningFormat` is set.

kept.title: Bedrock effort gate removes xhigh and max from Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 although their AWS model cards list them
kept.summary: bedrockTopEfforts allows xhigh only for claude-opus-5* and max only for opus-4-6, sonnet-4-6 and opus-5*. On Bedrock, Fable 5.x and Mythos 5.x requests at xhigh or max are clamped to high, and the hint hides those levels. The commit that added the gate itself notes that the Fable 5.1 card lists both levels.
kept.failure_scenario: Bedrock us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1 + WithAdaptiveReasoning(ReasoningXHigh) or ReasoningMax sends effort "high" with a clamp warning. ClaudeEffortsFor("us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1", ProviderBedrock) = [low medium high], so the caller can never get the documented top levels.
kept.evidence: claude_name_forms_test.go pins us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1 → [low medium high] and xhigh → high. Commit cf4df89: 'the Fable 5.1 card lists both levels. With the copies disagreeing the narrower set goes into code'. AWS model cards for Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1 and Opus 5.5 list low, medium, high, xhigh and max (search results; docs.aws.amazon.com is egress-blocked here).

repro.evidence: Probe TestProbeV3Effort (llms/reasoning) at HEAD: on ProviderBedrock, ClaudeEffortsFor returns [low medium high] for us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1 and us.anthropic.claude-mythos-5-1, and ClaudeClampEffort(xhigh|max) returns high. The same names on ProviderAnthropic return [low medium high xhigh max]. Opus 5.5 keeps both levels on Bedrock. BASE had no ClaudeClampEffort or Bedrock gate, so the requested effort passed through unchanged, which makes this a behaviour change for Bedrock callers of Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1. Commit cf4df89 knowingly picks the narrower set: 'the Fable 5.1 card lists both levels. With the copies disagreeing the narrower set goes into code'. Vendor docs: docs.aws.amazon.com is egress-blocked here. Search-result snippets of the AWS model cards for Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 list effort 'low, medium, high, xhigh, and max'. A snippet of the Bedrock adaptive-thinking page says xhigh is available on Fable 5, Mythos 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7 and Sonnet 5, which is also broader than the gate. Third-party catalog oh-my-pi PR #13433 gives Bedrock Claude 5.1+ the five-level ladder. The AWS documentation pages contradict each other, so I rate this plausible rather than confirmed.
repro.comment: `bedrockTopEfforts` allows `xhigh` only for `claude-opus-5*` and `max` only for Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 5*. On Bedrock, `us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1` and `us.anthropic.claude-mythos-5-1` are therefore limited to `[low medium high]`. A probe shows `ClaudeClampEffort(<model>, "xhigh"|"max", ProviderBedrock) == "high"` and `ClaudeEffortsFor(..., ProviderBedrock) == [low medium high]`, so callers asking for xhigh/max get high with a clamp warning and the hint hides both levels. The previous release passed the effort through unchanged. The AWS model cards for Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 (per search results; I could not fetch docs.aws.amazon.com here) list low, medium, high, xhigh and max, and commit cf4df89 notes the same for Fable 5.1. Whether this is a real regression depends on what Bedrock actually accepts. Consider adding the 5.1 families (or a version-based rule) to the gate, or letting unknown/newer Claude generations pass through instead of clamping.

refute.reason: The gate is deliberate (commit cf4df89, pinned in claude_name_forms_test.go), but the commit rests it on AWS's general adaptive-thinking guide, which predates the 5.1 models. The commit itself admits that the Bedrock model card for Fable 5.1 lists xhigh and max. A web search confirms the Bedrock Fable 5.1 card and third-party reports list all five levels for Fable 5.1 on Bedrock. Another project shipped a fix giving Bedrock Claude 5.1+ the full effort ladder. So the table is narrower than the vendor documents: every Bedrock Fable 5.x or Mythos 5.x request at xhigh or max is lowered to high, and the hint hides those levels. A warning is emitted, but the caller has no way to get a documented capability. BASE sent xhigh and max unchanged, so this is new in the PR. kept.title: EffortWithTools checks only the model name, so OpenRouter's openai/gpt-5.4, 5.5 and 5.6 lose effort-with-tools
kept.summary: EffortWithTools uses only the model name. Its forms strip the `openai/` prefix, so OpenAI's chat-completions rule (no reasoning_effort together with function tools on gpt-5.4, 5.5 and 5.6) also fires on OpenRouter, where `openai/` is the vendor slug and not LiteLLM's OpenAI route.
kept.failure_scenario: The client points at http(s)://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with WithModel("openai/gpt-5.4") (or openai/gpt-5.5, openai/gpt-5.6), and the call uses WithTools plus WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0). The door returns ErrEffortWithTools before any request is sent. BASE sent reasoning_effort:"high" with the tools. With openai/gpt-5.6, tools and no reasoning option, HEAD also adds reasoning_effort:"none" (or reasoning.effort none in the modern format), which silently switches reasoning off on OpenRouter.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/r2door (package openai_test, a transport that dials a local server, baseURL http://openrouter.ai/api/v1). HEAD: 'A1 OR gpt-5.4 tools+high err=model "openai/gpt-5.4" rejects reasoning effort "high" on a request carrying function tools ... wire=<no request>'; A2 gives the same for gpt-5.5; 'A3 OR gpt-5.6 tools no reasoning wire={"reasoning_effort":"none"}'; A4 gpt-5.6 tools+high is an error. BASE: A1, A2 and A4 send {"reasoning_effort":"high"} and A3 sends {}. Probe r2tables: EffortWithTools("openai/gpt-5.4")=1 (Omit) and ("openai/gpt-5.6")=2 (Disable). The OpenAI restriction itself is real (commit df2e5f7; issue 'Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for gpt-5.4 in /v1/chat/completions'). It belongs to OpenAI's /chat/completions, not to OpenRouter, which lists reasoning and tool calling for openai/gpt-5.4. The test effort_wire_test.go pins {"openai/gpt-5.6", EffortToolsDisable} without looking at the host. The door already knows its host (o.host, publicProviderHost).

repro.evidence: Code at HEAD: EffortWithTools(model) (llms/reasoning/effort_wire.go:301) iterates modelSpellings(model), which drops everything up to the last '/', so 'openai/gpt-5.4' becomes 'gpt-5.4'. setReasoning (llms/openai/openaillm.go:406-433) calls it with no host, although o.host is known ('openrouter.ai'). Probe probes/v3or (package openai_test, a capturing Doer, WithBaseURL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1). HEAD: 'A1 gpt-5.4 tools+high | err=model "openai/gpt-5.4" rejects reasoning effort "high" on a request carrying function tools ... | wire=<no request>'. A2 (gpt-5.5) is the same. 'A3 gpt-5.6 tools only | wire=reasoning_effort=none'. A4 (gpt-5.6 tools+high) is refused. A5 (gpt-5.4 high, no tools) sends reasoning_effort=high. BASE: A1, A2 and A4 send reasoning_effort=high, and A3 sends no reasoning field. The restriction is real on OpenAI's own /v1/chat/completions (commit df2e5f7; pipecat issue #4043, LibreChat #14355). OpenRouter's model page for openai/gpt-5.4 lists tools and reasoning as supported. I could not confirm whether OpenRouter forwards this combination to OpenAI chat completions (where it would 400 anyway) or serves it through the Responses API. Direct fetch of openrouter.ai is blocked by the egress proxy. So the local refusal and the silent 'none' are demonstrated, but the harm depends on how OpenRouter routes the request.
repro.comment: `EffortWithTools` only looks at the model name, and `modelSpellings` strips the `openai/` prefix. OpenAI's own chat-completions rule (gpt-5.4/5.5/5.6 take no reasoning_effort when function tools are present) therefore also fires on OpenRouter, where `openai/` is just the vendor slug. A probe with a capturing HTTP client and `WithBaseURL("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1")` shows the effect. `WithModel("openai/gpt-5.4")` (and 5.5) with `WithTools` and `WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh, 0)` returns `ErrEffortWithTools` before any request is sent, while the previous release sent `reasoning_effort:"high"`. `openai/gpt-5.6` with tools and no reasoning option now gets `reasoning_effort:"none"` added, which silently turns reasoning off. The harm depends on vendor behaviour: OpenRouter lists tools and reasoning for these slugs, but I could not confirm whether it relays the request to OpenAI's /chat/completions, where the 400 would still occur. Suggested fix: pass `o.host` into the rule, the same way `ServedByDeepSeek`/`DashScopeRoute` take the host, and apply it only for api.openai.com, Azure, and bare or LiteLLM-routed names.

refute.reason: EffortWithTools (effort_wire.go:301) gets only the model name. modelSpellings drops everything up to the last '/', so openai/gpt-5.4, 5.5 and 5.6 match on any host. setReasoning (openaillm.go:407-433) returns ErrEffortWithTools before any request when tools are present, and setDeferredReasoning writes reasoning_effort "none" for gpt-5.6. Commit df2e5f7 grounds the rule in OpenAI's /v1/chat/completions refusal and says it was reproduced against the vendor through a gateway where openai/ is a LiteLLM route. Nothing in the code or commit shows OpenRouter rejecting this combination. OpenRouter serves gpt-5.4 through OpenAI, Azure and Bedrock behind its own reasoning API, and web search did not show OpenRouter returning this error. The door knows o.host and uses host-aware checks elsewhere (ServedByDeepSeek, DashScopeRoute), and doc.go says the provider API, not a local table, is the final arbiter. BASE sent the effort with the tools. The strongest counter-argument is that OpenRouter might pass the request to OpenAI chat completions unchanged and get the same 400; I could not prove this either way. Even so, the change turns a request that used to work into a local error and silently switches reasoning off for gpt-5.6, so it stands.

The harm depends on vendor behaviour: OpenRouter lists tools and reasoning for these slugs, but I could not confirm whether it relays the request to OpenAI's /chat/completions, where the 400 would still occur. Suggested fix: pass `o.host` into the rule, the same way `ServedByDeepSeek`/`DashScopeRoute` take the host, and apply it only for api.openai.com, Azure, and bare or LiteLLM-routed names.

kept.title: onMiniMaxAPI reads OpenRouter's minimax/ slug as MiniMax's own API: structured output refused, top_k dropped
kept.summary: onMiniMaxAPI strips `minimax/` and matches on any host. TakesNoResponseFormat, TakesNoTopK and ReplaysReasoningInThinkTags therefore apply MiniMax's own API limits to OpenRouter's `minimax/minimax-m*` slugs, which several providers serve and whose OpenRouter listing includes json_schema response_format.
kept.failure_scenario: On openrouter.ai, WithModel("minimax/minimax-m2") with WithStructuredOutput(...) returns ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported ('the vendor's chat completions API takes no response_format for this model') before any request. BASE sent the json_schema response_format. With WithTopK(40), top_k is dropped with a warning. With PreserveReasoningContent, earlier reasoning is folded into <think> tags in content instead of the reasoning field.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/r2door on http://openrouter.ai/api/v1. HEAD: 'B1 OR minimax-m2 structured err=structured output: unsupported on openai for model minimax/minimax-m2 ... wire=<no request>' and 'B2 OR minimax-m2 topk wire={}'. BASE: B1 sends response_format json_schema, B2 sends {"top_k":40}. Probe r2tables: TakesNoResponseFormat("minimax/minimax-m2")=true, TakesNoTopK=true, ReplaysReasoningInThinkTags=true. Commit 7032ea0 intends 'MiniMax-Text-01 and MiniMax on another host still get the schema', but the predicate takes no host. The OpenRouter page for minimax/minimax-m2 lists response_format and structured_outputs as supported (web search of openrouter.ai/minimax/minimax-m2; direct fetch blocked by the egress proxy).

repro.evidence: Code at HEAD: onMiniMaxAPI(model, family) = HasPrefix(TrimPrefix(lower(model), "minimax/"), family) (llms/reasoning/effort_wire.go:48-50) takes no host. It drives TakesNoResponseFormat (structured_output.go:38/143/237), TakesNoTopK (openaillm.go:370) and ReplaysReasoningInThinkTags (openaillm.go:192). OpenRouter's slug for MiniMax is exactly 'minimax/minimax-m2'. Probe probes/v3or on https://openrouter.ai/api/v1. HEAD: 'B1 minimax-m2 structured | err=structured output: unsupported on openai for model minimax/minimax-m2: the vendor's chat completions API takes no response_format for this model | wire=<no request>'. 'B2 minimax-m2 topk | wire=' (top_k dropped). 'B3 minimax-m2 preserve | asst.content=<think>THOUGHT</think>hello'. B4 minimax-01 still gets json_schema. BASE: B1 sends response_format=json_schema, B2 sends top_k=40, and B3 sends content=hello. Commit 7032ea0 states the intent 'MiniMax-Text-01 and MiniMax on another host still get the schema', but the predicate cannot see the host. OpenRouter's minimax/minimax-m2 listing says it supports structured outputs via json_schema in response_format (web search result for openrouter.ai/minimax/minimax-m2; direct fetch is egress-blocked).
repro.comment: `onMiniMaxAPI` strips `minimax/` and matches on any host. `TakesNoResponseFormat`, `TakesNoTopK` and `ReplaysReasoningInThinkTags` therefore apply the limits of MiniMax's own API to OpenRouter's `minimax/minimax-m*` slugs. A probe against `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` (capturing HTTP client) shows three changes. `WithModel("minimax/minimax-m2")` + `WithStructuredOutput(...)` now returns `ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported` without sending a request, where the previous release sent `response_format: json_schema`. `WithTopK(40)` is dropped, where it was sent before. With `WithPreserveReasoningContent`, earlier reasoning is folded into `<think>` tags in the content. kept.title: Undated OpenRouter slugs anthropic/claude-opus-4 and claude-sonnet-4 are unclassified, so temperature now goes out with thinking
kept.summary: The budget-only table covers every other spelling of Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4: dated, -0 alias, Vertex @date, Bedrock and dotted 4.x. It misses the undated OpenRouter slugs `anthropic/claude-opus-4` and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`, which fall to ClaudeReasoningUnknown, even though ClaudeInterleavesOnBudget already recognises the bare form. The openai door then neither drops the caller's temperature nor pins it to 1 while thinking; BASE dropped it.
kept.failure_scenario: On openrouter.ai, WithModel("anthropic/claude-sonnet-4") (or anthropic/claude-opus-4) with WithTemperature(0.2) and WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0) sends {"reasoning_effort":"high","temperature":0.2}. Anthropic requires temperature 1 while thinking, so the request fails upstream if OpenRouter forwards it. anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 and anthropic/claude-opus-4.1 get temperature:1 on the same call, and BASE sent no temperature for any of the four names.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/r2door on http://openrouter.ai/api/v1. HEAD: 'D1 OR claude-sonnet-4 wire={"reasoning_effort":"high","temperature":0.2}', 'D3 OR claude-opus-4 ... "temperature":0.2', 'D2 OR claude-sonnet-4.5 ... "temperature":1', 'D4 OR claude-opus-4.1 ... "temperature":1'. BASE: all four send only {"reasoning_effort":"high"}. Probe r2tables: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 kind=0 thinks=false predates=false interleaves=true; claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-sonnet-4-0 and claude-opus-4@20250514 have kind=3 (budget-only). The Anthropic troubleshooting page lists Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 as extended-thinking-only. This is separate from the first reviewer's #2 (RejectsSamplingWhileThinking on OpenAI names): here the Claude kind table has a spelling gap, and refusesSamplingWhileThinking relies on ClaudeSupportsThinking.

repro.evidence: Code at HEAD: budgetOnlyClaude (llms/reasoning/claude_capability.go:47-52) lists 'claude-opus-4-0', 'claude-opus-4-2025', 'claude-sonnet-4-0' and 'claude-sonnet-4-2025', but not the undated form. canonicalClaude('anthropic/claude-sonnet-4') = 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4', which contains none of them, so the model is ClaudeReasoningUnknown and ClaudeSupportsThinking is false. ClaudeInterleavesOnBudget (line 245-259) does accept rest=="" for claude-opus-4/claude-sonnet-4, so the package already treats the bare form as a thinking model. refusesSamplingWhileThinking (openaillm.go:678-683) relies on ClaudeSupportsThinking, so enforceSamplingPolicy neither nils nor pins the temperature. Probe probes/v3or on https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with WithTemperature(0.2)+WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0). HEAD: 'D1 claude-sonnet-4 | wire=reasoning_effort=high temperature=0.2', 'D3 claude-opus-4 | reasoning_effort=high temperature=0.2', 'D2 claude-sonnet-4.5 | temperature=1', 'D4 claude-opus-4.1 | temperature=1', 'D5 claude-sonnet-4-20250514 | temperature=1'. BASE: all five send only reasoning_effort=high, with no temperature. Anthropic's extended-thinking docs list Sonnet 4/Opus 4 among the extended-thinking (budget-only) models, and Anthropic's thinking page states that thinking is not compatible with temperature modifications. Whether OpenRouter forwards the 0.2 or normalises it is vendor behaviour, but the classification gap and the wire change from BASE are demonstrated.
repro.comment: `budgetOnlyClaude` covers the dated, `-0`, `@date`, Bedrock and dotted 4.x spellings of Opus 4 / Sonnet 4, but not the undated OpenRouter slugs `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4` and `anthropic/claude-opus-4`. `ClaudeInterleavesOnBudget` already recognises the bare form, yet `ClaudeReasoningKindFor` returns Unknown for it. As a result, `refusesSamplingWhileThinking` in the openai door neither drops nor pins the caller's temperature. A probe against `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` with `WithTemperature(0.2)` + `WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh, 0)` sends `{"reasoning_effort":"high","temperature":0.2}` for both slugs. For `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`, `anthropic/claude-opus-4.1` and `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` it sends `temperature:1`, and the previous release sent no temperature for any of them. Anthropic requires the default temperature while extended thinking is on, so the request can fail upstream; this depends on whether OpenRouter forwards the value. Suggested fix: classify the bare `claude-opus-4` / `claude-sonnet-4` (end of name) as budget-only, reusing the `rest == ""` check from `ClaudeInterleavesOnBudget`, and add both slugs to the kind table tests.

It then matches no budgetOnlyClaude entry ('claude-sonnet-4-0', 'claude-sonnet-4-2025', ...), so ClaudeReasoningKindFor returns Unknown. The same happens for claude-opus-4. The dated and dotted siblings get temperature 1. BASE removed temperature and top_p for every reasoning model under reasoning, so this regression is new. No test pins the undated slug as Unknown, so the gap looks accidental rather than intended.

kept.title: glm-latest and glm-flash-latest skip the GLM 5.3 closed effort enum, although other tables treat them as 5.3
kept.summary: nonOpenAILowHighMax clamps the closed low/high/max enum only by hasGeneration("glm-5.3"). mandatoryThinking and the catalogue treat glm-latest and glm-flash-latest as the 5.3 line (commits c25e3d1, c2a4f22), yet those aliases get the caller's medium, xhigh or minimal sent verbatim.
kept.failure_scenario: Against api.z.ai, WithModel("glm-latest") with WithReasoning(ReasoningMedium,0) sends reasoning_effort:"medium", while glm-5.3 on the same call sends "low". glm-flash-latest with ReasoningXHigh sends "xhigh", while glm-5.3-flash sends "high". Commit 3bd7abd records that Z.AI documents that any value outside low/high/max 'produces an error'.
kept.evidence: Probe r2tables: 'GLM glm-latest mandatory=true caps=false/[] medium->"medium" xhigh->"xhigh"' against 'glm-5.3 mandatory=true caps=true/[low high max] medium->"low" xhigh->"high"', with the same result for glm-flash-latest and glm-5.3-flash. Door probe r2door on http://api.z.ai: C1 glm-latest wire={"reasoning_effort":"medium"}, C2 glm-5.3 wire={"reasoning_effort":"low"}, C3 glm-flash-latest wire={"reasoning_effort":"xhigh"}, C4 glm-5.3-flash wire={"reasoning_effort":"high"}. Commit 3bd7abd (closed-enum clamp) landed after c25e3d1, which says 'glm-flash-latest points at glm-5.3-flash', and did not add the aliases. Caveat: commit 33830c8 measured the alias to be lenient about 'none', so whether the vendor rejects the value is not certain.

repro.evidence: Code: nonOpenAILowHighMax (llms/reasoning/openai_capability.go:116) matches only hasGeneration(m,"kimi-k3") || hasGeneration(m,"glm-5.3"); modelSpellings has no alias mapping for glm-latest/glm-flash-latest, while mandatoryThinking (off.go:228-229) and IsReasoningModel (reasoning.go:367) treat both aliases as the 5.3 line (commits c25e3d1, 33830c8, c2a4f22). Probe v3door (openai door, httptest, base URL http://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4) at HEAD: glm-latest medium -> {"reasoning_effort":"medium"}; glm-5.3 medium -> "low"; glm-flash-latest xhigh -> "xhigh"; glm-5.3-flash xhigh -> "high"; glm-latest minimal -> "minimal"; glm-5.3 minimal -> "low". BASE sent the caller's value verbatim for every name (glm-5.3 medium -> "medium"), so this is an incomplete fix from 3bd7abd, not a regression against the previous release. Vendor impact differs from the finding's wording: public reports on GLM-5.3 (aihubmix guide, opencrabs issue #1349, OpenViking issue #4686; docs.z.ai itself is blocked by the egress proxy) say that values outside low/high/max, including medium and xhigh, return 200 and fall back to the default max. So the likely effect is maximum-depth, maximum-cost reasoning instead of an error. Commit 3bd7abd's claim that other values 'produce an error' could not be verified.
repro.comment: `nonOpenAILowHighMax` clamps only names of the `glm-5.3` generation. `glm-latest` and `glm-flash-latest` are treated as the 5.3 line elsewhere (`mandatoryThinking`, `IsReasoningModel`), but they skip the closed low/high/max enum. A probe through the OpenAI door on the Z.AI host sends `reasoning_effort:"medium"` for `glm-latest` but `"low"` for `glm-5.3`. It sends `"xhigh"` for `glm-flash-latest` but `"high"` for `glm-5.3-flash`, and `"minimal"` for `glm-latest`. According to public GLM-5.3 reports (not verified against docs.z.ai from here), the vendor accepts an out-of-enum value with 200 and silently falls back to the default `max`. A caller asking the alias for medium would then get the deepest, most expensive reasoning. Suggested fix: add `glm-latest` and `glm-flash-latest` to `nonOpenAILowHighMax`, for example with a shared GLM-5.3-alias helper that `mandatoryThinking` also uses, and add them to the clamp test.

refute.reason: nonOpenAILowHighMax (llms/reasoning/openai_capability.go:116) matches only hasGeneration(m,"kimi-k3")||hasGeneration(m,"glm-5.3"). The same PR treats glm-latest and glm-flash-latest as the 5.3 line everywhere else: mandatoryThinking in off.go:228-229, IsReasoningModel in reasoning.go:367, the AcceptsEffortWire tables (c2a4f22 says the catalogue 'already treats [them] as the 5.3 line'), and c25e3d1 ('glm-flash-latest points at glm-5.3-flash'). 3bd7abd adds the clamp because Z.AI says any value outside low/high/max 'produces an error'. Its test covers glm-5.3 and glm-5.3-flash only; no test sends medium to the aliases on purpose. The only argument against is 33830c8, which measured glm-latest as lenient about 'none'. That is one measurement of one value, so the code still leads to a value the vendor documents as invalid. BASE had no GLM tables and sent every effort verbatim, so the aliases already got medium/xhigh there. What is new is the gap: the aliases don't get the clamp that the 5.3 names now get.

It sends `"xhigh"` for `glm-flash-latest` but `"high"` for `glm-5.3-flash`, and `"minimal"` for `glm-latest`. According to public GLM-5.3 reports (not verified against docs.z.ai from here), the vendor accepts an out-of-enum value with 200 and silently falls back to the default `max`. A caller asking the alias for medium would then get the deepest, most expensive reasoning. Suggested fix: add `glm-latest` and `glm-flash-latest` to `nonOpenAILowHighMax`, for example with a shared GLM-5.3-alias helper that `mandatoryThinking` also uses, and add them to the clamp test.

kept.title: ServedByDeepSeek treats OpenRouter's deepseek/ slug as DeepSeek's own API on every host
kept.summary: ServedByDeepSeek skips the host check for any `deepseek/<name>`. OpenRouter serves deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash through many third-party providers, so DeepSeek-API-only drops (temperature while thinking, top_p when not, top_k) also hit OpenRouter calls.
kept.failure_scenario: On openrouter.ai, WithModel("deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash") with WithTemperature(0.3), WithTopP(0.9) and WithTopK(20) sends only {"top_p":0.9}; temperature and top_k are dropped with warnings. BASE sent all three. OpenRouter routes this slug to DeepInfra, GMICloud and others that honour these parameters.
kept.evidence: Probe r2door on http://openrouter.ai/api/v1: HEAD 'B3 OR deepseek-v4-flash temp+topp wire={"top_p":0.9}'; BASE wire={"temperature":0.3,"top_k":20,"top_p":0.9}. Probe r2tables: ServedByDeepSeek("deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash","openrouter.ai")=true. Commit 1d8ad3c keeps 'the deepseek/ route of LiteLLM ... on any host', but the same prefix is OpenRouter's vendor slug. openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash lists 16 serving providers (web search).

repro.evidence: Code: ServedByDeepSeek (llms/reasoning/effort_wire.go:27-32) returns true for any `deepseek/<name>` in deepSeekAPIModels, whatever the host. The openai door uses it in applySampling (openaillm.go:667: drops temperature while thinking, top_p otherwise) and in the top_k drop (openaillm.go:370). Commit 1d8ad3c meant the prefix to cover LiteLLM's deepseek/ route. The unit test even excludes `openrouter/deepseek/...`, but on openrouter.ai itself the vendor slug is the bare `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`. The door knows the OpenRouter base URL (apikey.go:33). Probe v3door against base URL http://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with WithTemperature(0.3), WithTopP(0.9), WithTopK(20): HEAD deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash -> {"top_p":0.9}, and the same for deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro; BASE -> {"temperature":0.3,"top_k":20,"top_p":0.9}. The control deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash keeps all three on HEAD. OpenRouter's listing (via web search; openrouter.ai is blocked by the egress proxy) shows deepseek-v4-flash served by 16 providers, including DeepInfra, GMICloud, Venice and DigitalOcean. Requests route to the best provider with failover, so the DeepSeek-API-only rules are applied to third-party backends.
repro.comment: `ServedByDeepSeek` counts any `deepseek/<name>` as DeepSeek's own API on every host. The `deepseek/` prefix is also OpenRouter's vendor slug, so calls to openrouter.ai get the DeepSeek-API-only drops. A door probe on `http://openrouter.ai/api/v1` with `WithModel("deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash")`, `WithTemperature(0.3)`, `WithTopP(0.9)` and `WithTopK(20)` sends only `{"top_p":0.9}` at HEAD; the previous release sent all three. OpenRouter serves this slug through many third-party providers (DeepInfra, GMICloud, Venice and others) that honour temperature and top_k, so the caller's sampling is silently replaced (only a warning is emitted). Suggested fix: keep the prefix rule for the LiteLLM route but not on OpenRouter. For example, return false when the host is openrouter.ai, or make the prefixed form host-aware like the bare form. Pin the OpenRouter case in `TestServedByDeepSeek`.

refute.reason: ServedByDeepSeek (effort_wire.go:27-33) returns true for any 'deepseek/<api-name>' on any host. Commit 1d8ad3c says the exception is meant for LiteLLM's deepseek/ route. The code never looks at the host, though, and the OpenAI door keeps its host (o.host). On openrouter.ai, 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash' is OpenRouter's normal vendor slug, and third-party providers can serve it. The result is applySampling (openaillm.go:667) removing temperature while thinking, or top_p otherwise, and openaillm.go:370 removing top_k. The reason given is 'the vendor's API has no top_k field', which does not hold for OpenRouter. Even on DeepSeek's own API, 1d8ad3c describes these parameters as ignored, not rejected, so dropping them buys nothing there, while on OpenRouter it changes sampling. TestServedByDeepSeek covers only a litellm.example host and 'openrouter/deepseek/...' (LiteLLM's OpenRouter spelling). No test pins the direct OpenRouter host. BASE had no ServedByDeepSeek and sent temperature, top_p and top_k unchanged.

kept.comment: `ServedByDeepSeek` counts any `deepseek/<name>` as DeepSeek's own API on every host. The `deepseek/` prefix is also OpenRouter's vendor slug, so calls to openrouter.ai get the DeepSeek-API-only drops. A door probe on `http://openrouter.ai/api/v1` with `WithModel("deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash")`, `WithTemperature(0.3)`, `WithTopP(0.9)` and `WithTopK(20)` sends only `{"top_p":0.9}` at HEAD; the previous release sent all three. OpenRouter serves this slug through many third-party providers (DeepInfra, GMICloud, Venice and others) that honour temperature and top_k, so the caller's sampling is silently replaced (only a warning is emitted). Suggested fix: keep the prefix rule for the LiteLLM route but not on OpenRouter. For example, return false when the host is openrouter.ai, or make the prefixed form host-aware like the bare form. Pin the OpenRouter case in `TestServedByDeepSeek`.

kept.title: ResolveOff on Google sends a thinking config to TTS and image surfaces that GeminiSupportsThinking excludes
kept.summary: The diff added the geminiNonChatSurface gate to GeminiSupportsThinking, so the reasoning-on path now sends nothing for TTS and image routes. The Google branch of ResolveOff has no such gate and still answers OffMinimalLevel or OffZeroBudget for them.
kept.failure_scenario: WithModel("gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview") with WithReasoningDisabled sends thinkingConfig {thinkingLevel: MINIMAL}. The repo's own drift table records the vendor answer '400 Thinking level is not supported'. The same model with WithReasoning(High) sends no thinking config. gemini-2.5-flash-image with an explicit off sends thinkingBudget 0, and the drift table records that this route rejects effort. An app that sets WithReasoningDisabled globally therefore fails on these routes.
kept.evidence: Probe r2gem (internal googleai test calling resolveThinkingConfig). HEAD: 'gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview on=null | off={"thinkingLevel":"MINIMAL"}', 'gemini-2.5-flash-image on=null | off={"thinkingBudget":0}'. BASE: on sends HIGH, and off returns ErrReasoningOffUnsupported for 3.1 TTS and image. Probe r2tables: GeminiSupportsThinking=false for all four surfaces, yet ResolveOff returns 3 (minimal) or 2 (zero budget). knownDrift in models_dev_drift_test.go: 'google/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview': 'speech route: 400 Thinking level is not supported'.

repro.evidence: Code: the PR added geminiNonChatSurface to GeminiSupportsThinking (gemini_capability.go:37), so resolveThinkingConfig's ReasoningOn branch (googleai.go:1143) sends nothing for tts/image/live-translate/transcribe names. The ProviderGoogleAI branch of ResolveOff (off.go:88-100) has no such gate, and the PR added OffMinimalLevel for Gemini 3 names at off.go:97. Probe v3gem (internal googleai test calling resolveThinkingConfig) at HEAD: gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview on=null | off={"thinkingLevel":"MINIMAL"}; gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview on=null | off=MINIMAL; gemini-2.5-flash-image, gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts and gemini-2.5-flash-live-translate on=null | off={"thinkingBudget":0}; gemini-3-pro-image-preview on=null | off=ErrReasoningOffUnsupported. BASE: 3.x TTS/image on sent HIGH and off returned ErrReasoningOffUnsupported locally; 2.5 surfaces sent budget 0 on off, the same as HEAD. So the explicit off still fails for 3.x surfaces (now as a vendor 400 instead of a local typed error), is unchanged for 2.5, and on/off now disagree. Vendor: the repo's own knownDrift in models_dev_drift_test.go records 'google/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview': 'speech route: 400 Thinking level is not supported' and 'gemini-2.5-flash-image': 'image route: effort is rejected by Gemini'. LiteLLM docs say it excludes Gemini image models from thinking config to avoid API errors. ai.google.dev is blocked by the egress proxy.
repro.comment: The PR makes `GeminiSupportsThinking` return false for TTS, image, live-translate and transcribe surfaces, so `WithReasoning` sends no thinking config there. The Google branch of `ResolveOff` has no such gate. A probe calling `resolveThinkingConfig` shows that `gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` and `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` with `WithReasoningDisabled` send `thinkingConfig{thinkingLevel: MINIMAL}`, and `gemini-2.5-flash-image` sends `thinkingBudget: 0`. The same models with reasoning on send nothing. The repo's own drift table records `400 Thinking level is not supported` for the 3.1 TTS route and says the image route rejects effort. An app that sets `WithReasoningDisabled` globally therefore gets vendor 400s on surfaces that cannot think at all; the previous release failed here too, but with a local `ErrReasoningOffUnsupported`. Suggested fix: return `OffOmit` early in the `ProviderGoogleAI` branch for `geminiNonChatSurface` names (or when `!GeminiSupportsThinking` for a known Gemini name), so on and off agree.

refute.reason: 96a8bd1 and the tests TestNonChatGoogleSurfacesAreNotThinkingModels and TestGoogleSurfacesThatRefuseThinkingStayOut added geminiNonChatSurface to GeminiSupportsThinking on purpose. Those tests quote the vendor: 'Thinking level is not supported for this model'. resolveThinkingConfig checks that gate on the ReasoningOn path only (googleai.go:1143). The ReasoningOff path calls ResolveOff(ProviderGoogleAI), and that branch (off.go:89-99) never checks it. GeminiCanDisable returns true for gemini-3.1-*-tts (GeminiAcceptsMinimalLevel matches the gemini-3.1 family), so the call sends thinkingLevel MINIMAL. For gemini-2.5-flash-image and the 2.5 TTS names it sends thinkingBudget 0. The drift table records the vendor rejecting exactly those routes. This breaks the stated ResolveOff contract that 'Off and On can never classify a model differently'. I found no test that pins the off wire for these surfaces. The failure itself is mostly not new. BASE also sent thinkingBudget 0 for 2.5-flash-image and 2.5 TTS, and for 3.1 TTS it failed locally with ErrReasoningOffUnsupported. What changes for 3.1 TTS is that the local typed error becomes a vendor 400. The mismatch between On and Off is new, because the PR added the gate to the On path only.

kept.comment: The PR makes `GeminiSupportsThinking` return false for TTS, image, live-translate and transcribe surfaces, so `WithReasoning` sends no thinking config there. The Google branch of `ResolveOff` has no such gate. A probe calling `resolveThinkingConfig` shows that `gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` and `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` with `WithReasoningDisabled` send `thinkingConfig{thinkingLevel: MINIMAL}`, and `gemini-2.5-flash-image` sends `thinkingBudget: 0`. The same models with reasoning on send nothing. The repo's own drift table records `400 Thinking level is not supported` for the 3.1 TTS route and says the image route rejects effort. kept.title: Tool-choice translation drops disable_parallel_tool_use from a map choice
kept.summary: anthropicToolChoice rebuilds every classified tool choice as a fresh {type,name} struct, so a raw map choice that carried disable_parallel_tool_use:true reaches the wire without it. BASE forwarded that map unchanged, and it was the only way to set the flag, because llms.ToolChoice has no field for it and no option exists.
kept.failure_scenario: WithToolChoice(map[string]any{"type":"auto","disable_parallel_tool_use":true}) plus tools. BASE sent the flag; HEAD sends {"type":"auto"} with no warning. The model can now return several tool_use blocks, and a caller written to handle one call per turn misses tool_results; the next turn gets a 400. The same happens for {type:any|tool, name, disable_parallel_tool_use:true}.
kept.evidence: Probe llms/anthropic/zz_probe_anth_a1_test.go, run through the overlay with a fake Doer, captured the wire body. HEAD printed `in={"disable_parallel_tool_use":true,"type":"auto"} wire tool_choice={"type":"auto"}` (the same for any and tool). BASE printed `wire tool_choice={"disable_parallel_tool_use":true,"type":"auto"}`. Commit bce683d says it should 'leave every other choice untouched'. 20acb40 then translated every spelling but never carries extra keys. The Anthropic tool_choice docs (platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages/create) list disable_parallel_tool_use on auto, any and tool. llms.ClassifyToolChoice (llms/turn.go:62) reads only type and name from a map.

repro.evidence: HEAD llms/anthropic/anthropicllm.go:1059-1072: anthropicToolChoice classifies via llms.ClassifyToolChoice (llms/turn.go, reads only type/name/function.name from a map) and returns a new anthropicclient.ToolChoice{Type,Name} (messages.go:116 has only Type and Name), so extra keys are dropped. BASE (anthropicllm.go:295) passed opts.ToolChoice through unchanged. Probe TestProbeV3ToolChoice (probes/v3anth, fake Doer capturing the body), HEAD: in={"disable_parallel_tool_use":true,"type":"auto"} -> wire tool_choice={"type":"auto"}; any -> {"type":"any"}; tool -> {"name":"get","type":"tool"}; err=nil, no warning. Anthropic Messages API docs list disable_parallel_tool_use (optional boolean) on ToolChoiceAuto/Any/Tool ('model will output at most/exactly one tool use'). repro.comment: Regression: `anthropicToolChoice` rebuilds every recognised choice as a fresh `{type,name}` struct, so a map choice such as `map[string]any{"type":"auto","disable_parallel_tool_use":true}` goes out as `{"type":"auto"}` with no warning. Suggested fix: when the input is a map, copy the keys other than `type`, `name` and `function` (at least `disable_parallel_tool_use`) into the translated choice, or return the map with only `type`/`name` normalised.

kept.title: model_context_window_exceeded is not reported as truncation
kept.summary: The new Truncated flag and WithFailOnTruncation use llms.IsTruncated, which knows length/max_tokens/model_length but not Anthropic's model_context_window_exceeded stop reason. An answer cut off at the context window therefore counts as complete.
kept.failure_scenario: Sonnet 4.6 with a prompt near the 1M window and WithMaxTokens(64000) plus WithFailOnTruncation(). The API stops with stop_reason model_context_window_exceeded mid-answer. GenerateContent returns err=nil and Truncated=false, so the caller consumes a half-written answer or half-written JSON. validateAnthropicStructuredOutput also skips validation for this stop reason, so a structured call gets no error at all.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeA1ContextWindowStop, HEAD, canned response. The model_context_window_exceeded case printed `ctxwindow: err=<nil> truncated=false stop="model_context_window_exceeded"`; the same response with max_tokens printed `max_tokens: err=truncated: choice 0 stopped at the output token limit ... truncated=true`. The Messages API docs (platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages/create.md, the stop_reason list) name model_context_window_exceeded: 'we exceeded the model's context window'. llms/stopreason.go:8 truncationStopReasons lacks it.

repro.evidence: llms/stopreason.go:8 (new in PR) truncationStopReasons = {length, max_tokens, model_length}; anthropicllm.go:435 sets Truncated: llms.IsTruncated(result.StopReason); CheckTruncation uses the same set; validateAnthropicStructuredOutput (~1033) only validates on end_turn/stop_sequence and returns nil for any other stop reason. Probe TestProbeV3Stop at HEAD with canned response containing half JSON: 'model_context_window_exceeded: err=<nil> truncated=false' vs 'max_tokens: err=truncated: choice 0 stopped at the output token limit (stop reason "max_tokens") truncated=true' (both with WithMaxTokens(64000)+WithFailOnTruncation()). Anthropic docs 'Handling stop reasons': model_context_window_exceeded = 'Claude stopped because it reached the model's context window limit'; quick-reference action: 'Treat the response as truncated'; returned without a beta header on Sonnet 4.5 and newer. New feature (Truncated/WithFailOnTruncation did not exist in BASE), so not a regression, but the new contract is wrong for this stop reason.
repro.comment: Anthropic's `model_context_window_exceeded` stop reason is not counted as truncation. `llms.IsTruncated` (llms/stopreason.go) only knows `length`/`max_tokens`/`model_length`, so an answer cut off at the context window gets `Truncated=false`, and `WithFailOnTruncation()` does not fire. I checked this with a canned response containing half-written JSON and `WithMaxTokens(64000)` + `WithFailOnTruncation()`. With `stop_reason: model_context_window_exceeded` the call returns `err=nil truncated=false`, while the same response with `max_tokens` returns the truncation error. `validateAnthropicStructuredOutput` also skips validation for this stop reason, so a structured-output call hands back the partial JSON without any error. Anthropic's stop-reason docs say to treat this stop reason as truncated, and Sonnet 4.5+ return it without a beta header. Suggested fix: add `model_context_window_exceeded` to `truncationStopReasons`, and include it in the truncation branch of the structured-output check.

refute.reason: llms/stopreason.go truncationStopReasons contains only length, max_tokens and model_length, and the anthropic door sets Truncated from llms.IsTruncated(result.StopReason). Anthropic documents model_context_window_exceeded as a stop reason that newer Claude models return when generation runs out of context window, which cuts the answer off in the same way. The docs for Truncated and WithFailOnTruncation say 'output token limit', but the effective output budget is capped by the context window, and the purpose of the feature is to flag cut-off answers. validateAnthropicStructuredOutput also returns nil for this stop reason. Truncated, IsTruncated and WithFailOnTruncation do not exist in BASE, so this is a gap in a feature new to the PR, not a regression.

kept.title: Fast-mode beta header silently replaces client-level beta headers
kept.summary: extractBetaHeaders now adds fast-mode-2026-02-01 to the per-request list whenever InferenceSpeed is set. Client.setHeaders uses client-level WithAnthropicBetaHeader values only when the per-request list is empty, so asking for fast mode drops every beta the client was configured with.
kept.failure_scenario: anthropic.New(WithAnthropicBetaHeader("server-side-fallback-2026-07-01")) (or any other client-level beta), then a call with llms.WithInferenceSpeed("fast"). anthropic-beta carries only fast-mode-2026-02-01, the client beta is gone, and nothing is reported. The same pattern already existed for the auto-added interleaved-thinking header; this PR adds a second trigger.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeA1Speed/TestProbeA1ClientBeta, HEAD: `plain: anthropic-beta="context-1m-2025-08-07"`, `speed: anthropic-beta="fast-mode-2026-02-01"` (client beta server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 missing), `budget+tools: anthropic-beta="interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14"`. The fallback rule is in llms/anthropic/internal/anthropicclient/anthropicclient.go setHeaders: `if len(betaHeaders) > 0 {...} else if len(c.anthropicBetaHeaders) > 0`.

repro.evidence: HEAD anthropicllm.go:966-968 appends anthropicFastModeBeta to the per-request list whenever opts.InferenceSpeed != nil. anthropicclient.go setHeaders (226-237): 'if len(betaHeaders) > 0 {use per-request} else if len(c.anthropicBetaHeaders) > 0 {use client-level}', so client-level betas are dropped as soon as the per-request list is not empty. Probe TestProbeV3Beta at HEAD, client built with WithAnthropicBetaHeader("context-1m-2025-08-07"): plain call -> anthropic-beta="context-1m-2025-08-07"; with llms.WithInferenceSpeed("fast") -> anthropic-beta="fast-mode-2026-02-01" (client beta gone, err=nil, no warning). InferenceSpeed/fast mode is new in this PR (absent in BASE llms/options.go), so this is a defect in the new option. The same override already happened in BASE for the auto interleaved-thinking header. Anthropic docs: fast mode requires speed:"fast" plus the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header, and fast mode is priced across the full context window including >200k, so combining it with a 1M-context client beta is a realistic use.
repro.comment: `WithInferenceSpeed` now adds `fast-mode-2026-02-01` to the per-request beta list. `anthropicclient.Client.setHeaders` falls back to the client-level `WithAnthropicBetaHeader` values only when the per-request list is empty, so turning on fast mode silently drops every beta the client was configured with. I checked this with a fake `Doer`. A client built with `WithAnthropicBetaHeader("context-1m-2025-08-07")` sends `anthropic-beta: context-1m-2025-08-07` on a plain call, but only `anthropic-beta: fast-mode-2026-02-01` once `llms.WithInferenceSpeed("fast")` is added, with no error or warning. A 1M-context client using fast mode would then get prompt-too-long errors above the standard window, and other client betas simply stop applying. The auto-added interleaved-thinking header already had this problem, and this PR adds a second trigger. Suggested fix: have `setHeaders` merge the client-level and per-request lists (deduplicated) instead of choosing one.

refute.reason: extractBetaHeaders (anthropicllm.go:966) now appends fast-mode-2026-02-01 to the per-request list whenever InferenceSpeed is set. anthropicclient.setHeaders applies the client-level WithAnthropicBetaHeader values only in an else branch, which runs when the per-request list is empty, so the client's betas are silently dropped. kept.title: InferenceSpeed (and ServiceTier) are empty on every streamed response
kept.summary: The new GenerationInfo["InferenceSpeed"] is read from usage.speed. Only the non-streaming JSON decode fills that field: handleMessageStartEvent/handleMessageDeltaEvent never parse usage.speed, which the API sends in the message_start usage, so streamed fast-mode calls always report an empty speed.
kept.failure_scenario: llms.WithInferenceSpeed("fast") plus WithStreamingFunc on claude-opus-4-8. message_start carries usage.speed="fast", yet resp.Choices[0].GenerationInfo["InferenceSpeed"] is "". A caller that bills or logs by the speed actually used sees nothing. The non-streamed call reports "fast".
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeA1StreamSpeed, HEAD, fake Doer: `nonstream: err=<nil> speed="fast" tier="standard"`, `stream: err=<nil> content="hi" speed="" tier=""`. The beta Messages docs (platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/messages/create.md) put `speed: "standard" or "fast" or null` on the Message usage object, which the stream delivers in message_start. ServiceTier being empty on streams predates this PR.

repro.evidence: HEAD messages.go: MessageResponsePayload.Usage gains `ServiceTier`/`Speed` (line 266-267), and these are filled only by the non-streaming JSON decode. handleMessageStartEvent (messages.go:543-573) copies only input_tokens and the cache counters from message.usage, and handleMessageDeltaEvent (~807-830) copies only the token counts. Vendor docs: platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/messages/create.md lists `speed: "standard" or "fast" or null` ("The inference speed mode used for this request") on the response usage. The streaming guide says `message_start` "contains a Message object", and that object carries usage. BASE has no WithInferenceSpeed or InferenceSpeed key, so this is a new feature that does not work on streams rather than a regression. The empty ServiceTier on streams predates the PR.
