kept.title: Federated token with a 60s lifetime is never cached: every request re-exchanges
kept.summary: accessToken reuses the cached token only while now+60s is before expiresAt. A minted token of 60s or less (the documented floor of token_lifetime_seconds, and the floor the server applies when the IdP JWT is near expiry) is therefore never reused, and each API request makes a new token exchange with the same assertion.
kept.failure_scenario: A federation rule with token_lifetime_seconds=60, or an identity token with less than 30s left. Every GenerateContent call first posts to /v1/oauth/token. If the JWT in the file carries a jti (check_jti is on by default) and has not rotated yet, the second exchange is rejected 401 (jti_reused) and the request fails. Unlike the documented SDK schedule (advisory refresh at expiry-120s that keeps serving the cached token, mandatory at expiry-30s), a failed exchange here returns an error while the cached token is still valid.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeFedLifetime (internal package, fake Doer), HEAD: `expires_in=60: 3 messages -> 3 exchanges`, `expires_in=90: 3 messages -> 1 exchanges`, `expires_in=600: 3 messages -> 1 exchanges`. Docs: WIF reference (token_lifetime_seconds range 60 to 86400, jti single use) and the 'Token lifetime and refresh' section at platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation.

repro.evidence: federation.go (new in this PR; BASE has no federation) at line 101 reuses the cached token only when `f.now().Add(tokenRefreshSkew).Before(f.expiresAt)` with tokenRefreshSkew=60s. For expires_in<=60 that is never true, so every authorize() does a fresh exchange. Probe TestProbeV3FedLifetime (internal package, using the existing federationStub) at HEAD: `expires_in=60: 3 token requests -> 3 exchanges`, `expires_in=61: ... -> 1`, `expires_in=90: ... -> 1`, `expires_in=600: ... -> 1`. With the stub switched to 401 after the first exchange (simulating jti_reused): `first err=<nil> second err=token exchange failed: ... 401` even though the cached token was still valid for ~60s. Vendor docs (platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation): token_lifetime_seconds is 60 to 86400. The minted lifetime is the lesser of the rule's lifetime and twice the JWT's remaining lifetime, and "is never less than 60 seconds". SDKs refresh advisorily at expiry-120s and keep serving the cached token if that fails, and mandatorily at expiry-30s. Tokens with a jti are single-use by default, so re-presenting an unrotated JWT from ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE fails with jti_reused. The 401 part depends on the server's jti enforcement; the lack of caching is shown directly.
repro.comment: `accessToken` reuses the cached token only while `now+60s` is before `expiresAt`, so a token minted with a lifetime of 60 s or less is never cached. 60 s is the documented floor of `token_lifetime_seconds`, and the server also mints 60 s tokens when the IdP JWT has under 30 s left. In that case every API request first does a fresh `/v1/oauth/token` exchange. A probe with the package's `federationStub` shows `expires_in=60: 3 requests -> 3 exchanges` versus 1 exchange for 61/90/600 s. Tokens that carry a `jti` are single-use by default (per the WIF docs), so an unrotated JWT in the token file makes the second exchange fail with 401 `jti_reused`, and the call errors while the cached token is still valid. The probe reproduces this by returning 401 on the second exchange; the actual rejection depends on Anthropic's jti enforcement. Suggested fix: scale the skew to the lifetime (e.g. `min(60s, lifetime/2)`), and follow the SDKs' two-tier schedule: advisory refresh at expiry-120 s that keeps serving the cached token when the exchange fails, mandatory refresh at expiry-30 s.

refute.reason: federation.go is new in this PR, so BASE has no equivalent. With tokenRefreshSkew = 60s, the check now+60s < expiresAt can never pass for a 60s token, so every request exchanges the assertion again. The WIF docs confirm the input can occur. token_lifetime_seconds ranges from 60 to 86400. The minted lifetime is min(rule lifetime, 2 x remaining JWT lifetime) and is 'never less than 60 seconds'. Identity tokens with a jti are single-use by default (jti_reused). The documented SDK schedule refreshes at expiry-120s but keeps serving the cached token until expiry-30s. Here the code re-exchanges on every call and fails hard even while the cached token is still valid. The strongest mitigation is that the default lifetime (3600s, or 600s from the wizard) and normal Kubernetes rotation make this an edge case, but a 60s rule is a documented, valid configuration. Severity is low to moderate, but it is a real defect.

Suggested fix: scale the skew to the lifetime (e.g. `min(60s, lifetime/2)`), and follow the SDKs' two-tier schedule: advisory refresh at expiry-120 s that keeps serving the cached token when the exchange fails, mandatory refresh at expiry-30 s.

kept.title: ExtraBody drop warning names a vendor SDK the Anthropic door does not use
kept.summary: The warning reason says the door 'builds its request through a vendor SDK and has nowhere to merge them', but the Anthropic door marshals its own messagePayload struct. The reason in the diagnostic is false.
kept.failure_scenario: WithExtraBody(map[string]any{"metadata":...}) on the anthropic door yields a WithExtraBody drop warning that blames a vendor SDK. Callers reading the warning are misled about why the field was dropped and whether support is possible.
kept.evidence: llms/anthropic/internal/anthropicclient/messages.go builds messagePayload and posts it with json.Marshal; the package imports no vendor SDK. The same constant is copied into several doors (grep 'vendor SDK' llms/*/warnings.go).

repro.evidence: At HEAD, llms/anthropic/sampling_warnings.go:152 defines `const extraBodyUnread = "the door builds its request through a vendor SDK and has nowhere to merge them"`. It is used in reportAnthropicUnread (line 15, the messages path) and reportAnthropicCompletions (line 172, the legacy completions path), both through llms.Warnings.AddUnreadExtraBody, which emits a WarningDrop for Option "WithExtraBody" with that Reason. The whole constant and its call sites are new in the PR diff. The Anthropic door imports no third-party SDK: the only non-module imports in the non-test files of llms/anthropic are the standard library and testify (tests only). llms/anthropic/internal/anthropicclient builds its own payload structs and posts them with encoding/json and net/http. Ollama, by contrast, really does import github.com/ollama/ollama/api. So the reason text is false for the Anthropic door. The same string was copy-pasted into the ollama, googleai, mistral, huggingface and bedrock warnings.go files, where it is accurate. Because the door owns the JSON body, merging ExtraBody is technically possible here, so the diagnostic wrongly suggests the drop cannot be avoided. The claim is unambiguous from the code, so no probe was needed.
repro.comment: The anthropic door's reason for dropping `WithExtraBody` says "the door builds its request through a vendor SDK and has nowhere to merge them". That is not true for this door: `internal/anthropicclient` marshals its own `messagePayload` with `encoding/json`, and `llms/anthropic` imports no vendor SDK (unlike ollama, which uses `ollama/api`). The string looks copied from the SDK-based doors. So `WithExtraBody(map[string]any{"metadata": ...})` on anthropic returns a drop warning that blames an SDK that isn't used, and suggests the field can't be supported when the door could actually merge it into the body it builds. Suggest either giving anthropic its own accurate reason (for example "the door does not merge extra body fields yet") or actually merging `ExtraBody` into the marshalled payload, for both the messages path (line 15) and the completions path (line 172).

refute.reason: Confirmed. llms/anthropic/sampling_warnings.go:152 defines extraBodyUnread = "the door builds its request through a vendor SDK and has nowhere to merge them", and lines 15 and 172 use it for both the messages path and the legacy completions path. Its internal/anthropicclient imports only langchaingo packages (httputil, streaming, reasoning) and marshals its own payload structs, so the stated reason is false. The door could merge ExtraBody the way the openai door does. The best case for dismissing it: the warning itself is right, because the fields really are dropped, and only the Reason text is wrong. kept.title: Partial stream response contains a made-up "{}" tool call when the stream breaks mid tool_use
kept.summary: When a stream fails partway through a tool call, the partial response now returned with the error contains that call as a finished ToolCall with Arguments "{}". The input_json_delta chunks already received are only decoded at content_block_stop, which never arrived, so the empty map from content_block_start is what gets marshalled.
kept.failure_scenario: Streaming call. The vendor sends content_block_start{tool_use id=toolu_1 name=delete_files input:{}} and input_json_delta '{"path": "/tmp/bui'. Then an overloaded_error event arrives, or a malformed line, or the consumer's StreamingFunc returns an error. GenerateContent returns the error together with resp.Choices[0].ToolCalls=[{ID:toolu_1, Name:delete_files, Arguments:"{}"}]. The model never produced those arguments. A caller that uses the partial response (the purpose of this change) may run the tool with empty arguments, or store a tool_use that has no tool_result. BASE returned resp=nil. The same partial can also carry a thinking block with no signature (signature_delta not received yet), which the vendor rejects if the turn is replayed.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/anth2-partialtool (streams message_start, tool_use start, one partial input_json_delta, then an error event or a malformed line). HEAD printed: "[error event] partial tool call id=toolu_1 name=delete_files args=\"{}\"" and "[malformed] partial tool call ... args=\"{}\"", with stop="". BASE printed "resp=nil" for both. Code path: messages.go handleContentBlockStartEvent sets Input=getMap(cb,"input")={}. handleInputJSONDelta only appends rawStreamInput, and DecodeStream runs only in handleContentBlockStopEvent. anthropicllm.go:335 builds the partial through processAnthropicResponse, which json.Marshal's cv.Input. The intent commits 496c267 and 5bfc410 only talk about keeping delivered text.

repro.evidence: Own probe probes/v3-anthpartial streams message_start, content_block_start{tool_use toolu_1 delete_files input:{}}, one input_json_delta '{"path": "/tmp/bui', then (a) an overloaded_error event, (b) a malformed data line, (c) a StreamingFunc error on the tool-call chunk. HEAD prints for all three: err=true stop="" toolcall id=toolu_1 name=delete_files args="{}". BASE prints resp=nil with the error for all three. Cause: messages.go handleContentBlockStartEvent stores Input=getMap(cb,"input") ({}); handleInputJSONDelta only appends rawStreamInput; DecodeStream runs only in handleContentBlockStopEvent, which never arrives; the error exits in parseStreamingMessageResponse/processStreamEvent send `partial := response`, and anthropicllm.go:335 runs processAnthropicResponse, which json.Marshal's cv.Input to "{}". Intent commits 5bfc410/496c267 speak only of keeping delivered text. The error is still returned, so callers that check err first are unaffected; the harm is to callers that use the partial as the contract invites.
repro.comment: When a stream breaks in the middle of a `tool_use` block (vendor `error` event such as overloaded_error, an unparseable line, or the StreamingFunc returning an error), the partial response now returned with the error contains that call as a finished ToolCall with `Arguments: "{}"`. The input_json_delta chunks are only decoded at content_block_stop, which never arrived, so the empty `input` from content_block_start is what gets marshalled. The model never produced those arguments. A probe that streams tool_use `delete_files` plus one delta `{"path": "/tmp/bui` and then fails printed `toolcall id=toolu_1 name=delete_files args="{}"` at HEAD in all three failure modes; BASE returned `resp=nil`. A caller that uses the partial (the point of 5bfc410/496c267) may run the tool with empty arguments or store a tool_use that has no tool_result. Suggest dropping unfinished tool_use blocks (and unsigned thinking blocks) from the partial, or at least marking them as incomplete, instead of emitting `{}`.

refute.reason: The code does this. handleContentBlockStartEvent (messages.go ~600) sets ToolUseContent.Input = getMap(cb,"input"), which is {}. handleInputJSONDelta only appends to rawStreamInput. DecodeStream runs only in handleContentBlockStopEvent. The intent commits 5bfc410 and 496c267 are about returning text that was already delivered. No test covers a partial response with a half-streamed tool_use, so nothing shows the fabricated "{}" is intended. The arguments shown are neither the partial JSON received nor empty, and StopReason "" is the only signal that the call is incomplete. BASE returned resp=nil on these paths.

kept.title: Legacy completions stream leaks one goroutine each time a consumer aborts
kept.summary: The scanner error is now sent on the unbuffered responseChan instead of being logged. When the reader has already returned because the StreamingFunc failed, nothing will ever receive from responseChan, so the goroutine blocks on that send forever.
kept.failure_scenario: The legacy text-completions door (WithLegacyTextCompletionsAPI) streams, and the StreamingFunc returns an error on the first chunk. parseStreamingCompletionResponse returns, and createCompletion closes the body. The goroutine's scanner then fails with 'use of closed network connection' and blocks forever on `responseChan <- CompletionEvent{...}`. Every aborted call leaks one goroutine plus its buffers.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/anth2-leak runs 5 legacy streaming calls whose StreamingFunc returns an error, while the server holds the stream open. After 3s it counts goroutines in parseStreamingCompletionResponse.func1. HEAD: "before=0 after=5". BASE: "before=0 after=0"; BASE logged 'issue scanning response: ... use of closed network connection' and exited.

repro.evidence: Own probe probes/v3-anthleak: 5 legacy (WithLegacyTextCompletionsAPI) streaming calls whose StreamingFunc fails on the first chunk while the server holds the connection, then counts parseStreamingCompletionResponse.func1 goroutines after 3s. With one event sent: HEAD leaked=5, BASE leaked=0 (BASE logged 'issue scanning response: ... use of closed network connection' and exited). With 4 events sent at once (more lines already buffered): HEAD leaked=5, BASE leaked=5 too, because BASE's goroutine already blocked on the unbuffered `responseChan <- CompletionEvent{Response: streamPayload}` send. So the leak pattern predates the PR. The PR's change at completions.go:121 extends it to the case where nothing more was buffered, making the leak happen on every abort. Legacy door only.
repro.comment: The scanner error is now sent on the unbuffered `responseChan`, but when the reader has already returned because the StreamingFunc failed, nothing will ever receive it, and the goroutine blocks forever. A probe with 5 legacy-completions streaming calls (WithLegacyTextCompletionsAPI) whose StreamingFunc errors on the first chunk left 5 `parseStreamingCompletionResponse.func1` goroutines alive at HEAD vs 0 at BASE, where the error was only logged. BASE already leaked the same way whenever more events were buffered (4 events sent → 5 leaked at BASE as well), so this makes an existing leak happen on every aborted call rather than creating a new one. Suggest making every send in the goroutine `select` on a done channel that the reader closes on return (or on ctx.Done()), as the messages path should too.

refute.reason: completions.go:120-122 now sends the scanner error on the unbuffered responseChan instead of logging it. When the StreamingFunc fails, the reader returns at completions.go ~135 without draining the channel and nothing selects on ctx, so the goroutine blocks forever once the closed body makes Scan fail. BASE logged the error and exited in this scenario (server still holding the stream open). BASE could already leak by the same mechanism when further data lines were buffered, because it blocked on the data-event send. So the defect class is partly older, but this change adds a new leak on the common abort path. The door is legacy, but it is still public through WithLegacyTextCompletionsAPI.

kept.title: Stream that ends at EOF without message_stop still drops delivered text and reports "no response"
kept.summary: The PR keeps text already delivered on every stream interruption that raises an error. A stream that ends cleanly (EOF with no scanner error) before message_stop sends nothing on eventChan, so the caller gets ErrEmptyResponse ("no response") with resp=nil even though text was already streamed.
kept.failure_scenario: A proxy or network path closes the SSE body cleanly after message_start, content_block_start and a text_delta "sixty rooms are free". The StreamingFunc has received that text, but GenerateContent returns (nil, "no response"): the error says the response was empty, not that it was cut short, and the delivered text is lost. The error-event, malformed-line and scanner-error paths now return it.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/anth2-partialtool TestProbeCleanEOF on HEAD: "streamed=\"sixty rooms are free\" err=no response resp=<nil>". BASE is identical, so this is not a regression; it is a gap in the new partial-response handling (commit 496c267 'keep the text a stream already delivered when it then fails').

repro.evidence: HEAD llms/anthropic/internal/anthropicclient/messages.go:414-466: the reader goroutine sends on eventChan only for message_stop (processStreamEvent line ~528), for an error event, for parse/process errors, or when scanner.Err() != nil (line 450). If the body reaches EOF cleanly before message_stop, the loop ends, scanner.Err() is nil and nothing is sent. parseStreamingMessageResponse then returns (nil, nil), and processAnthropicResponse (anthropicllm.go:391) turns a nil result into ErrEmptyResponse "no response". Probe probes/vfy-anth-ultra TestProbeVfyCleanEOF serves message_start, content_block_start and a text_delta "sixty rooms are free", then closes. HEAD prints `streamed="sixty rooms are free" err=no response resp=<nil>`. Control case, same stream plus a malformed `data: {not json` line: HEAD prints `err=...failed to parse stream event... resp="sixty rooms are free"`, which is the new partial-response behaviour from 496c267. BASE gives `err=no response resp=<nil>` for the clean-EOF case and resp=<nil> for the malformed one, so the clean-EOF gap is not a regression. It is an inconsistency left by the new partial-text handling: the error wrongly says the response was empty, and the caller cannot tell a truncated stream from an empty one.
repro.comment: Commit 496c267 hands back the partial response when a stream fails with an error event, a malformed line or a scanner error, but not when the body just ends before `message_stop`. On a clean EOF the goroutine sends nothing on `eventChan`, `parseStreamingMessageResponse` returns `(nil, nil)` and `GenerateContent` reports `ErrEmptyResponse` ("no response"). A probe with an httptest SSE server that sends `message_start`, `content_block_start` and a `text_delta` "sixty rooms are free" and then closes gives `streamed="sixty rooms are free" err=no response resp=<nil>`. Adding a malformed line to the same stream returns the partial text with a parse error. This matches the base, so it is not a regression, but a proxy or network cut that closes the body cleanly loses the delivered text and gets misreported as an empty response. Suggested fix: after the scan loop, if `scanner.Err()` is nil but no `message_stop` was seen and `response` has content, send `MessageEvent{Response: &partial, Err: <typed 'stream ended before message_stop' error>}`.

refute.reason: Confirmed in the code. In parseStreamingMessageResponse (messages.go ~412-462), when the scan loop ends with scanner.Err()==nil before any message_stop, nothing is sent on eventChan. The consumer loop then returns (nil, nil), and processAnthropicResponse(nil) returns ErrEmptyResponse ('no response'), so text already given to the StreamingFunc is thrown away. The error also claims the reply was empty when it was actually cut short. The input is realistic. The PR's own test harness (partial_stream_error_test.go streamThenFail) produces exactly this clean EOF whenever the tail has no error event. Gateways, proxies and close-delimited HTTP/1.x responses also end streams cleanly. Commit 496c267 set out to keep delivered text on every exit of this loop but skipped the end-of-loop exit. Its message lists the exits it left alone, and this one is not among them, so the gap was not intended. BASE behaves the same, so it is not a regression, only a gap in the new partial-response handling.

kept.comment: Commit 496c267 hands back the partial response when a stream fails with an error event, a malformed line or a scanner error, but not when the body just ends before `message_stop`. On a clean EOF the goroutine sends nothing on `eventChan`, `parseStreamingMessageResponse` returns `(nil, nil)` and `GenerateContent` reports `ErrEmptyResponse` ("no response"). Adding a malformed line to the same stream returns the partial text with a parse error. This matches the base, so it is not a regression, but a proxy or network cut that closes the body cleanly loses the delivered text and gets misreported as an empty response. Suggested fix: after the scan loop, if `scanner.Err()` is nil but no `message_stop` was seen and `response` has content, send `MessageEvent{Response: &partial, Err: <typed 'stream ended before message_stop' error>}`.

kept.title: Empty-stream test only covers a tiny max_tokens; with the default limit every empty stream is reported as token_limit
kept.summary: TestStreamWithoutCandidatesIsNotASilentSuccess checks the empty-stream error only with WithMaxTokens(24). In production, checkEmptyStream's `opts.MaxTokens == nil` escape can never fire, because GenerateContent always fills MaxTokens from DefaultMaxTokens (now 16384). So any stream that closes without a candidate is reported as ErrCodeTokenLimit with the message "max_tokens is too small to start an answer", even when the caller set no limit or a very large one.
kept.failure_scenario: googleai.New(WithDefaultModel("gemini-2.5-flash")) plus a streaming call with no WithMaxTokens. The server returns 200 text/event-stream with an empty body (a proxy that closes cleanly, or a vendor hiccup). The caller gets llms.Error{Code: token_limit, Message: "the model returned no candidates: max_tokens is too small to start an answer"}. The same happens with WithMaxTokens(65536). llms.IsTokenLimitError(err) is true; this code is also what the error mapper uses for "context length" failures. A caller that reacts by trimming history or raising max_tokens does the wrong thing. The base release returned an empty success, and the non-streaming path returns ErrNoContentInResponse for the same situation.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeEmptyStreamDefaultMaxTokens (overlay in package googleai on HEAD, reusing the emptyStream transport) printed: `no WithMaxTokens (default 16384): code=token_limit msg="the model returned no candidates: max_tokens is too small to start an answer"` and `WithMaxTokens(65536): code=token_limit ...`. The same probe on BASE printed `base: err=<nil> content=""`. Code: googleai.go:108 sets `MaxTokens: getIntPointer(g.opts.DefaultMaxTokens)` unconditionally, and googleai.go:1230 `if opts == nil || opts.MaxTokens == nil || *opts.MaxTokens <= 0 { return nil }` is therefore dead for callers that set no limit. Commit c61cb2d says the heuristic targets a caller-set limit too small to start an answer (measured with 24 on gemini-2.5-flash). The default became always-present in 476f3a6.

repro.evidence: At HEAD, GenerateContent always sets opts.MaxTokens = getIntPointer(g.opts.DefaultMaxTokens) (googleai.go:108; getIntPointer never returns nil, DefaultMaxTokens = llms.DefaultMaxTokens). The guard in checkEmptyStream (googleai.go:1230, `opts.MaxTokens == nil || *opts.MaxTokens <= 0`) therefore never fires for a caller who set no limit. I ran probe TestProbeVEmpty (package googleai, overlay; transport returns 200 text/event-stream with an empty body). HEAD printed: `no max: code=token_limit msg="the model returned no candidates: max_tokens is too small to start an answer" tokenLimit=true`, `max 65536: code=token_limit ... tokenLimit=true`, and `nonstream: err=no content in generation response`. BASE printed `no max: err=<nil> content=""` and `max 65536: err=<nil> content=""`. The heuristic came in with c61cb2d, which measured it with a caller-set limit of 24. TestStreamWithoutCandidatesIsNotASilentSuccess only exercises WithMaxTokens(24), so it cannot catch this.
repro.comment: A stream that ends with no candidate and no block reason is reported as `ErrCodeTokenLimit` ("max_tokens is too small to start an answer") for every caller, whatever limit they set. `GenerateContent` always fills `opts.MaxTokens` from `DefaultMaxTokens` (googleai.go:108), so the `opts.MaxTokens == nil` escape here is never taken. I ran a probe with a 200 `text/event-stream` empty body on `gemini-2.5-flash`. With no `WithMaxTokens` and with `WithMaxTokens(65536)`, HEAD returns `code=token_limit` and `llms.IsTokenLimitError(err) == true`. The previous release returned an empty success, and the non-streaming path returns `ErrNoContentInResponse` for the same situation. A caller that reacts to token_limit by trimming history or raising max_tokens does the wrong thing, and `TestStreamWithoutCandidatesIsNotASilentSuccess` only covers `WithMaxTokens(24)`. Suggested fix: use the budget explanation only when the caller set the limit explicitly (or it is below a small threshold). Otherwise return a generic empty-response error such as `ErrNoContentInResponse`, and add a test case with no `WithMaxTokens`.

refute.reason: Confirmed by reading the code. GenerateContent (googleai.go:108) always sets opts.MaxTokens = &g.opts.DefaultMaxTokens. The default is 16384 on HEAD, and even BASE's 2048 was always set, so the problem is not caused by 476f3a6. As a result, checkEmptyStream's `opts.MaxTokens == nil || <= 0` guard (googleai.go:1230) only returns nil if the caller explicitly passes WithDefaultMaxTokens(0). Every other stream that ends with no candidate, no content and no blockReason becomes ErrCodeTokenLimit with the message 'max_tokens is too small to start an answer', whatever the actual limit. Commit c61cb2d's message says the heuristic is meant for a caller-set limit that is too small (24 measured on gemini-2.5-flash). The limit's size is never compared, and the only test pins the 24 case. Nothing in the code, the commits or the tests says the default-limit case is meant to be labelled token_limit. It is a misclassification, and it drives callers who branch on IsTokenLimitError to the wrong remedy. BASE returned an empty success here (checkEmptyStream did not exist), so the typed error is new in this PR. Surfacing an error is still better than a silent success; the wrong code is the defect.

kept.title: "Counters add up" test uses a fixture without thoughts; on a thinking response the totals do not add up
kept.summary: TestAStreamedAnswerReportsCountersThatAddUp asserts TotalTokens == PromptTokens + CompletionTokens "as every other door reports it". Its fixture has no thoughtsTokenCount, so the check passes trivially. For any Gemini thinking response the door reports CompletionTokens = candidatesTokenCount (thoughts excluded) and TotalTokens = totalTokenCount (thoughts included), which breaks the invariant the test claims.
kept.failure_scenario: A streamed gemini-2.5-flash answer, which thinks by default, with usage {promptTokenCount:9, candidatesTokenCount:7, thoughtsTokenCount:189, totalTokenCount:205} yields PromptTokens=9, CompletionTokens=7, TotalTokens=205, and Prompt+Completion=16. A caller relying on the documented cross-door invariant, or pricing output from CompletionTokens as with OpenAI (completion_tokens includes reasoning) and Anthropic (TotalTokens = input+cache+output, output includes thinking), misses the 189 thought tokens Gemini bills as output. The test cannot catch this because its fixture has no thoughts.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeStreamedTotalsWithThoughts (HEAD, package googleai, SSE body copied from the usage block of cassette testdata/TestGoogleAITruncationIsReportedWhenStreaming.httprr) printed `Prompt=9 Completion=7 Reasoning=189 Total=205; Prompt+Completion=16`. Code: googleai.go streaming path sets CompletionTokens=CandidatesTokenCount and TotalTokens=TotalTokenCount. anthropicllm.go:440 computes TotalTokens as input+cache+output. The mapping itself predates this PR (base googleai.go:467-468); the defect here is the new test asserting an invariant the door does not keep.

repro.evidence: The streaming path sets CompletionTokens = CandidatesTokenCount and TotalTokens = TotalTokenCount (googleai.go:495-496). Gemini's candidatesTokenCount excludes thoughtsTokenCount, while totalTokenCount includes it. The PR's own cassette llms/googleai/testdata/TestGoogleAITruncationIsReportedWhenStreaming.httprr records `promptTokenCount 9, candidatesTokenCount 7, totalTokenCount 205, thoughtsTokenCount 189`. I ran probe TestProbeVUsage (HEAD, package googleai) with that usage block and it printed `Prompt=9 Completion=7 Reasoning=189 Total=205; Prompt+Completion=16`. The fixture in TestAStreamedAnswerReportsCountersThatAddUp (usage_stream_test.go:21-23) has no thoughtsTokenCount, so its assertion at line 50, "prompt plus completion must equal the total, as every other door reports it", passes trivially. Commit 3099dd6 states the invariant explicitly, and bedrockllm_test.go:3281 asserts it for Bedrock. The mapping itself predates the PR (lines 618-619 in the non-streaming path do the same), so this is a gap in the new test and the invariant it claims, not a behaviour regression.
repro.comment: This test asserts `TotalTokens == PromptTokens + CompletionTokens` "as every other door reports it", but its fixture has no `thoughtsTokenCount`, so the check passes trivially. For a thinking response the door does not keep this invariant. `CompletionTokens` comes from `candidatesTokenCount`, which excludes thoughts, while `TotalTokens` comes from `totalTokenCount`, which includes them. With the usage block from this PR's own cassette `TestGoogleAITruncationIsReportedWhenStreaming.httprr` (prompt 9, candidates 7, thoughts 189, total 205), a probe prints `Prompt=9 Completion=7 Total=205; Prompt+Completion=16`. A caller that prices output from `CompletionTokens`, as OpenAI's `completion_tokens` allows because it includes reasoning, misses the 189 thought tokens Gemini bills as output. Please add a thinking fixture to this test. Then either report `CompletionTokens = candidates + thoughts` in both the streaming and non-streaming paths, or narrow the invariant and document that Gemini's `CompletionTokens` excludes `ReasoningTokens`.

refute.reason: The mapping is unchanged from BASE: CompletionTokens=CandidatesTokenCount and TotalTokens=TotalTokenCount, both streaming (base googleai.go:467-468) and non-streaming (base 591-592). The strongest reason to dismiss is that the test's commit (3099dd6) is about the cache fix, where the remainder overwrote PromptTokens, and for that fixture the test is correct. But that same commit and the test's assertion message state the general invariant 'prompt plus completion must equal the total, as every other door reports it'. The door breaks that invariant on every Gemini thinking response, because totalTokenCount includes thoughtsTokenCount while CompletionTokens excludes it. The fixture has no thoughts, so the test cannot catch this. The PR's claimed fix is therefore partial and the test overstates what it covers. Nothing in the code or docs says thought tokens are meant to be left out of the prompt+completion=total contract. It is low severity and the behaviour predates this PR: nothing new breaks for callers, but the new test asserts a guarantee the door does not keep.

kept.comment: This test asserts `TotalTokens == PromptTokens + CompletionTokens` "as every other door reports it", but its fixture has no `thoughtsTokenCount`, so the check passes trivially. With the usage block from this PR's own cassette `TestGoogleAITruncationIsReportedWhenStreaming.httprr` (prompt 9, candidates 7, thoughts 189, total 205), a probe prints `Prompt=9 Completion=7 Total=205; Prompt+Completion=16`. A caller that prices output from `CompletionTokens`, as OpenAI's `completion_tokens` allows because it includes reasoning, misses the 189 thought tokens Gemini bills as output. Then either report `CompletionTokens = candidates + thoughts` in both the streaming and non-streaming paths, or narrow the invariant and document that Gemini's `CompletionTokens` excludes `ReasoningTokens`.

kept.title: The seven new pgvector integration tests always skip in CI
kept.summary: narrowingURL skips when PGVECTOR_CONNECTION_STRING is unset. It never starts the testcontainers Postgres that preCheckEnvSetting in the same package starts, and ci.yaml does not set that variable, so every new test that runs the rewritten SimilaritySearch, metadata-index DDL or init rollback against a real database is skipped in CI.
kept.failure_scenario: CI job 'test' runs `go test ./...` with only OPENAI/GOOGLE/ANTHROPIC keys in env. These tests are skipped without an error: TestSimilaritySearchToleratesAMixedWidthTableUnderFiltersAndThreshold, TestSimilaritySearchKeepsTheFilterScope, TestSimilaritySearchRefusesAFilterKeyItCannotInline, TestStoreCreatesTheDeclaredMetadataIndexes, TestSimilaritySearchReadsOnlyTheFilteredRows (narrowing_test.go), TestInitCancelledBeforeCommitKeepsTheCallersConnection and TestFailedInitReturnsItsConnectionToThePool (init_test.go). Suppose the dimension guard ends up after the `<=>` operator (every search on a mixed-width table fails), a filter stops scoping results, Postgres rejects the generated CREATE INDEX, or a cancelled init commits. The PR still merges green. The scripted-tx and string-rendering unit tests do not execute any SQL.
kept.evidence: On HEAD I ran `go test -run '^(<the 22 test funcs in filter_test/init_test/metadata_index_test/narrowing_test>)$' -v ./vectorstores/pgvector/`. It printed `--- SKIP` for exactly the 7 tests above, and they all go through narrowingURL (narrowing_test.go:59-69). pgvector_test.go:85 preCheckEnvSetting falls back to tcpostgres.Run when PGVECTOR_CONNECTION_STRING is empty, and narrowingURL has no such fallback. .github/workflows/ci.yaml test step env holds only OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The helper came in with commit 504595c (feat: implement metadata indexing and filtering in pgvector).

repro.evidence: narrowing_test.go:59-69 narrowingURL skips when PGVECTOR_CONNECTION_STRING is empty. Unlike preCheckEnvSetting (pgvector_test.go:85-110), it has no tcpostgres.Run fallback. It is called from narrowing_test.go:100,134,157,176,213 and init_test.go:161,191. I ran it on HEAD with that variable unset: `go test -p 2 -run 'TestSimilaritySearch|TestStoreCreates|TestInitCancelled|TestFailedInit' -v ./vectorstores/pgvector/`. It printed `--- SKIP ... PGVECTOR_CONNECTION_STRING is not set` for exactly the 7 named tests. The only failure was the Docker-backed TestSimilaritySearchWithInvalidScoreThreshold, because this sandbox has no Docker. The CI runner (ubuntu-latest) does have Docker, so the preCheckEnvSetting tests run there, but these 7 do not. .github/workflows/ci.yaml test step env sets only OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. All files are new in the PR diff.
repro.comment: `narrowingURL` skips when `PGVECTOR_CONNECTION_STRING` is unset, and it never falls back to the testcontainers Postgres that `preCheckEnvSetting` (pgvector_test.go:85) starts. CI does not set that variable, so the 7 new DB-backed tests are always skipped there: the five in narrowing_test.go and `TestInitCancelledBeforeCommitKeepsTheCallersConnection` / `TestFailedInitReturnsItsConnectionToThePool` in init_test.go. I ran them on HEAD with the variable unset and each prints `--- SKIP: ... PGVECTOR_CONNECTION_STRING is not set`. None of the rewritten SimilaritySearch SQL, the metadata-index DDL or the init rollback ever runs against a real Postgres in CI. A regression there, such as the dimension guard placed after `<=>`, a filter that no longer scopes, or an invalid CREATE INDEX, would still merge green. Suggest having `narrowingURL` reuse `preCheckEnvSetting` (or share its container) so these tests run wherever the existing pgvector suite runs.

refute.reason: narrowingURL (narrowing_test.go:59-69) only reads PGVECTOR_CONNECTION_STRING and skips otherwise. preCheckEnvSetting (pgvector_test.go:85) falls back to tcpostgres.Run, and ubuntu-latest runners have Docker. ci.yaml sets only the OPENAI, GOOGLE and ANTHROPIC keys, so the 7 in-package tests that run real SQL (5 in narrowing_test.go, 2 in init_test.go) always skip in CI while the external suite still runs. The comment says the tests 'cannot borrow the external suite's helpers'. That explains why they live in the package, but it does not justify dropping the container fallback. These tests are all new; BASE had only the external suite.

kept.title: Truncation table misses Anthropic/Bedrock model_context_window_exceeded
kept.summary: TestIsTruncatedCoversEveryVendorSpelling claims to cover every vendor spelling of a cut-off answer, but IsTruncated does not know `model_context_window_exceeded`. The Anthropic API returns it by default on Sonnet 4.5+ and the vendored Bedrock Converse SDK enumerates it, so such an answer is reported as complete even with WithFailOnTruncation. Mistral's equivalent, model_length, was added.
kept.failure_scenario: Take a Claude Sonnet 4.5+ call through the anthropic door, or any Bedrock Converse call, with a large max_tokens so the reply fills the context window. The vendor returns stop_reason/stopReason `model_context_window_exceeded`. anthropicllm.go:165/435 and bedrockclient_converse.go:967 set Truncated = llms.IsTruncated(...) = false, and CheckTruncation(resp, {FailOnTruncation:true}) returns nil. The caller who opted in to an error gets a cut-off answer as a success.
kept.evidence: Probe llms/zz_probe_trc_llms_test.go (overlay): `IsTruncated(model_context_window_exceeded)=false CheckTruncation(fail)=<nil>`. The vendored SDK bedrockruntime@v1.50.4 types/enums.go:835 has `StopReasonModelContextWindowExceeded StopReason = "model_context_window_exceeded"`. Anthropic docs (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/handling-stop-reasons) say: 'model_context_window_exceeded – Claude stopped because it reached the model's context window limit… On Sonnet 4.5 and newer models the API returns this value without a beta header.' Commit 71a53d5 added Mistral's context-limit spelling model_length for the same reason, but not this one. grep finds no `context_window_exceeded` anywhere on HEAD.

repro.evidence: llms/stopreason.go:8-12 (new file) maps only length, max_tokens and model_length, and grep finds no `context_window_exceeded` anywhere on HEAD. I ran an overlay probe in ./llms: `model_context_window_exceeded: IsTruncated=false CheckTruncation(fail)=<nil>`, while max_tokens and model_length return the truncated error. The anthropic door (anthropicllm.go:165, 435) and Bedrock Converse (bedrockclient_converse.go:967, 1092) pass the raw stop reason to IsTruncated. The vendored bedrockruntime v1.50.4 types/enums.go:835 defines StopReasonModelContextWindowExceeded = "model_context_window_exceeded". The Anthropic docs (platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/handling-stop-reasons) say: 'Claude stopped because it reached the model's context window limit… On Sonnet 4.5 and newer models the API returns this value without a beta header… Treat the response as truncated.'
repro.comment: `truncationStopReasons` does not include `model_context_window_exceeded`. Anthropic returns it by default on Sonnet 4.5 and newer when the reply fills the context window before `max_tokens`, and the vendored Bedrock Converse SDK enumerates it (`StopReasonModelContextWindowExceeded`). Anthropic's docs say to "treat the response as truncated". A probe shows `IsTruncated("model_context_window_exceeded") == false`, and `CheckTruncation(resp, CallOptions{FailOnTruncation: true})` returns nil. So a caller who opted into `WithFailOnTruncation` gets a cut-off answer as a success, with `Truncated=false`, from the anthropic door or Bedrock Converse. Suggest adding the spelling to the map, next to Mistral's `model_length`, and a row for it in `TestIsTruncatedCoversEveryVendorSpelling`. Seeing it live depends on Anthropic/Bedrock returning this value, which both document.

refute.reason: llms/stopreason.go knows only length, max_tokens and model_length. The vendored bedrockruntime types/enums.go:835 enumerates StopReasonModelContextWindowExceeded = "model_context_window_exceeded", and Anthropic documents this value for Sonnet 4.5+. Commit 71a53d5 added Mistral's context-limit spelling model_length for exactly this kind of cut-off, so leaving out Anthropic/Bedrock's spelling breaks the table's stated intent ('every vendor spelling'). anthropicllm.go:165/435 and bedrockclient_converse.go:967/1092 derive Truncated and CheckTruncation from IsTruncated, so WithFailOnTruncation stays silent. IsTruncated/FailOnTruncation do not exist in BASE.

kept.title: Sampling-hint tests compare the hint with the same function it is computed from
kept.summary: Both tests assert support.RejectsSampling == reasoning.RejectsSamplingWhileThinking(model), but ReasoningSupportFor fills RejectsSampling with that same call, so the assertion cannot fail. TestAForeignVendorOnTheOpenAIDoorKeepsItsSampling never checks that sampling is kept. Neither test looks at the wire rule reasoning.FixesSampling, so the hint says kimi-k3/k2.6/k2.7-code accept temperature while the openai door always strips it.
kept.failure_scenario: (a) Change RejectsSamplingWhileThinking to return true for every model, so the door would strip temperature from deepseek-v3.1/qwen3-max while thinking: both tests still pass. (b) ReasoningSupportFor("kimi-k3", ProviderOpenAI).RejectsSampling is false, so a UI built from the hint offers a temperature control. enforceSamplingPolicy (openaillm.go:643) removes temperature/top_p/penalties for FixesSampling models on every request, and the test that claims 'the hint and the wire disagree about sampling' does not see it.
kept.evidence: Mutation via overlay: replaced effort_wire.go:76 with `return true` and ran `go test -run '^(TestAForeignVendorOnTheOpenAIDoorKeepsItsSampling|TestTheHintReportsTheSamplingTheWireRefuses)$' ./llms/`. Result: `--- PASS` for both, while 16 llms/openai tests failed under the same mutation. Probe: `kimi-k3: RejectsSampling(hint)=false RejectsSamplingWhileThinking=false FixesSampling=true`, and the same for kimi-k2.6 and kimi-k2.7-code. `deepseek-v3.1`/`qwen3-max` take the IsReasoningModel branch (reasoning_support.go:134), which uses the same predicate.

repro.evidence: reasoning_support.go:120 and :134 fill RejectsSampling from reasoning.RejectsSamplingWhileThinking(model), and the tests compare it against that same call. I ran an overlay mutation that replaced effort_wire.go:76 with `return true`, then `go test -run '^(TestAForeignVendorOnTheOpenAIDoorKeepsItsSampling|TestTheHintReportsTheSamplingTheWireRefuses)$' ./llms/`. Both still printed `--- PASS`. The first test's extra assert.True only catches a mutation toward false, and the second test has no independent assertion. A probe on ProviderOpenAI shows kimi-k3 / moonshotai/kimi-k3 / kimi-k2.6 / kimi-k2.7-code with hint RejectsSampling=false and FixesSampling=true. enforceSamplingPolicy (openaillm.go:642-646) drops temperature, top_p and penalties for FixesSampling models on every request.
repro.comment: Both tests assert `support.RejectsSampling == reasoning.RejectsSamplingWhileThinking(model)`, but `ReasoningSupportFor` fills `RejectsSampling` with that same call (reasoning_support.go:120/134), so the comparison cannot fail. I tested this with an overlay mutation that makes `RejectsSamplingWhileThinking` return `true` for every model: both tests still pass. `TestAForeignVendorOnTheOpenAIDoorKeepsItsSampling` therefore never checks that deepseek-v3.1/qwen3-max keep their sampling. The tests also ignore `reasoning.FixesSampling`. A probe shows `ReasoningSupportFor("kimi-k3", ProviderOpenAI).RejectsSampling == false`, while `enforceSamplingPolicy` (openaillm.go:642) strips temperature/top_p/penalties for kimi-k3/k2.6/k2.7-code on every request, so a UI built from the hint offers a control the wire drops. Suggest asserting literal expected values, e.g. `assert.False` for the foreign vendors, and either folding `FixesSampling` into the hint or adding a test that the hint and `enforceSamplingPolicy` agree.

refute.reason: For deepseek-v3.1 and qwen3-max, ReasoningSupportFor fills RejectsSampling with reasoning.RejectsSamplingWhileThinking(model) (reasoning_support.go:134, and :120 for the caps branch). TestAForeignVendorOnTheOpenAIDoorKeepsItsSampling compares the field with that same call, so it never checks that sampling is kept, and a mutation to 'return true' passes. Only the first test has an independent assertion (assert.True). The hint also ignores FixesSampling: enforceSamplingPolicy (openaillm.go:643ff) always strips temperature, top_p and penalties for kimi-k3/k2.6/k2.7-code, while the hint documents RejectsSampling as rejecting temperature/top_p. The test file is new (commit d926315); BASE has no such test.

kept.comment: Both tests assert `support.RejectsSampling == reasoning.RejectsSamplingWhileThinking(model)`, but `ReasoningSupportFor` fills `RejectsSampling` with that same call (reasoning_support.go:120/134), so the comparison cannot fail. I tested this with an overlay mutation that makes `RejectsSamplingWhileThinking` return `true` for every model: both tests still pass. `TestAForeignVendorOnTheOpenAIDoorKeepsItsSampling` therefore never checks that deepseek-v3.1/qwen3-max keep their sampling. The tests also ignore `reasoning.FixesSampling`. A probe shows `ReasoningSupportFor("kimi-k3", ProviderOpenAI).RejectsSampling == false`, while `enforceSamplingPolicy` (openaillm.go:642) strips temperature/top_p/penalties for kimi-k3/k2.6/k2.7-code on every request, so a UI built from the hint offers a control the wire drops. Suggest asserting literal expected values, e.g. `assert.False` for the foreign vendors, and either folding `FixesSampling` into the hint or adding a test that the hint and `enforceSamplingPolicy` agree.

kept.title: Catalogue completeness test mirrors a hand list; new WithInferenceSpeed is dropped silently
kept.summary: TestADoorThatCarriesNothingReportsTheWholeCatalogue checks unreadCatalogue against catalogueOptionNames, a hand-copied list of the same options, so it cannot notice a missing option. WithInferenceSpeed was added in this PR and is in neither list, so every door except anthropic drops it without the WarningDrop the new warnings mechanism promises.
kept.failure_scenario: On the openai door (also googleai, bedrock, mistral, ollama, huggingface), GenerateContent with WithInferenceSpeed("fast") sends no speed field, and resp.Warnings stays empty. In the same call, WithMinLength(5) is reported as dropped.
kept.evidence: Probe llms/openai/zz_probe_trc_speed_test.go (overlay, httptest server): body=`{"model":"gpt-4.1","messages":[...],"seed":3}` warnings=`[drop: WithMinLength asked 5 ...]`, with no entry for WithInferenceSpeed. `grep InferenceSpeed` over non-test code: only llms/options.go and llms/anthropic/anthropicllm.go read it. warning.go unreadCatalogue has no InferenceSpeed entry. The option came in with commit 66d7efe.

repro.evidence: At HEAD `grep -rn InferenceSpeed` over non-test code finds only llms/options.go (field plus WithInferenceSpeed at 702) and llms/anthropic/anthropicllm.go (321, 966). BASE has no InferenceSpeed at all; commit 66d7efe 'feat(anthropic): let the caller pick the inference speed' adds it. llms/warning.go:93 unreadCatalogue has no InferenceSpeed entry. catalogueOptionNames in llms/unread_catalogue_test.go:23 is a hand copy of the same 15 names, so ElementsMatch cannot notice an option missing from both lists. Probe /tmp/.../scratchpad/probes/v3speed/probe_test.go was overlaid into llms/openai and called against an httptest server: openai.New(WithModel("gpt-4.1")).GenerateContent(..., WithInferenceSpeed("fast"), WithMinLength(5)). Output: body={"model":"gpt-4.1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}, warnings=[drop: WithMinLength asked 5 ... (the door builds no field for it)]. Speed is not on the wire and there is no warning for it. The googleai, bedrock, mistral, ollama and huggingface doors use the same AddUnreadOptions catalogue, so they drop it the same way. This is a new option, not a regression.
repro.comment: `WithInferenceSpeed` is new in this PR (66d7efe), but it is missing from `unreadCatalogue` in llms/warning.go. Only the anthropic door reads it, so every other door drops it without a `WarningDrop`. I overlaid a probe on the openai door with an httptest server and called `GenerateContent(..., WithInferenceSpeed("fast"), WithMinLength(5))`. The body sent was `{"model":"gpt-4.1","messages":[...]}` and `resp.Warnings` listed only `WithMinLength`. This test can't catch the gap because `catalogueOptionNames` is a hand copy of the catalogue. Suggested fix: add an `InferenceSpeed` entry to `unreadCatalogue`, list it as carried in the anthropic door, and derive the expected names in the test from `CallOptions` fields (e.g. via reflection with an explicit allow-list of options that aren't in the catalogue). Then a new option can't be forgotten silently again.

refute.reason: Confirmed in code. WithInferenceSpeed (llms/options.go:703, commit 66d7efe, 2026-08-31) is read only by the anthropic door (anthropicllm.go:321 and :966). The unread-option catalogue in llms/warning.go:93-127 has no InferenceSpeed entry, although it was built later (fc7e513 and 7fb2a4c, 2026-09-10/12). Commit 7fb2a4c says its purpose is to give 'every door one list of the options it never reads' so that 'a missing option is a difference in one place instead of a silence'. Every other door (openai, googleai, bedrock, mistral, ollama, huggingface) reports through AddUnreadOptions, so each of them drops the speed without a warning. The catalogue already lists another non-sampling option (WithVerbosity), so leaving InferenceSpeed out does not look like a deliberate choice. Commit 66d7efe only notes that Bedrock and Vertex never read the field, which predates the warnings mechanism. The test's catalogueOptionNames is a hand-copied mirror of the same list and cannot notice a missing option. Not preexisting: both the option and the warnings mechanism are new in this PR.

kept.comment: `WithInferenceSpeed` is new in this PR (66d7efe), but it is missing from `unreadCatalogue` in llms/warning.go. Only the anthropic door reads it, so every other door drops it without a `WarningDrop`. I overlaid a probe on the openai door with an httptest server and called `GenerateContent(..., WithInferenceSpeed("fast"), WithMinLength(5))`. The body sent was `{"model":"gpt-4.1","messages":[...]}` and `resp.Warnings` listed only `WithMinLength`. This test can't catch the gap because `catalogueOptionNames` is a hand copy of the catalogue. Suggested fix: add an `InferenceSpeed` entry to `unreadCatalogue`, list it as carried in the anthropic door, and derive the expected names in the test from `CallOptions` fields (e.g. via reflection with an explicit allow-list of options that aren't in the catalogue). Then a new option can't be forgotten silently again.

kept.title: TestCountTokens still downloads a tiktoken encoding and fails offline
kept.summary: The PR documents that each tiktoken encoding 'is downloaded on first use, which would make the count depend on the network' and adds a hermetic approximation test. TestCountTokens (gpt-3.5-turbo → cl100k_base) still fetches from openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net, and without network it gets 6 instead of 4.
kept.failure_scenario: In any environment without outbound access to openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net (sandbox, restricted CI runner), `go test ./llms/` fails with `expected: 4, actual: 6` after logging `[WARN] Failed to load the token encoding for model gpt-3.5-turbo ... Forbidden`.
kept.evidence: `env -u AWS_CA_BUNDLE go test -p 2 -count=1 ./llms/` on HEAD: `--- FAIL: TestCountTokens` at count_tokens_test.go:18 (expected 4, actual 6); the log shows the 403 on cl100k_base.tiktoken. Pre-existing: the same test fails the same way on BASE (count_tokens_test.go:13). This is the only failure in the slice's non-Docker packages.

repro.evidence: `env -u AWS_CA_BUNDLE go test -p 2 -count=1 -run TestCountTokens -v ./llms/` at HEAD logs `[WARN] Failed to load the token encoding for model gpt-3.5-turbo, falling back to approximate count: Get "https://openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net/encodings/cl100k_base.tiktoken": Forbidden`, then fails at count_tokens_test.go:18 with expected 4, actual 6. TestCountTokensApproximation passes. BASE fails the same way, so the failure predates the PR. The PR still touches the adjacent lines: it adds failingBpeLoader, TestCountTokensApproximation, and the CountTokens doc comment (count_tokens.go:79-84) saying each encoding 'is downloaded on first use, which would make the count depend on the network'. Yet it leaves TestCountTokens depending on that download. Line 18 is a context line inside the hunk @@ -13,6 +18,43 @@.
repro.comment: `TestCountTokens` still downloads `cl100k_base` from openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net. Without outbound access (sandbox, restricted CI) it logs a 403, falls back to the rune approximation and fails with `expected: 4, actual: 6`. I reproduced this with `go test -run TestCountTokens ./llms/`. Alternatively, skip the test when the encoding cannot be loaded, so `go test ./llms/` passes offline.

kept.title: WithReasoningDisabled now fails locally for Qwen/QwQ names outside DashScope (vLLM, OpenRouter, Together)
kept.summary: setReasoningOff resolves the off wire from the model name alone. Any qwen*/qwq* name that is not a DashScope spelling reaches `!AcceptsEffortWire → OffUnsupported`, so the door returns ErrReasoningOffUnsupported before sending anything. The base made these calls.
kept.failure_scenario: vLLM serving Qwen3 under its default served name: openai.New(WithBaseURL("http://vllm:8000/v1"), WithModel("Qwen/Qwen3-8B")) and then GenerateContent(..., llms.WithReasoningDisabled()) returns `reasoning cannot be disabled for model "Qwen/Qwen3-8B"` on every call. The same happens with OpenRouter qwen/qwen3-32b (also with WithModernReasoningFormat), Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507, Qwen/QwQ-32B and qwq-32b. An agent configured with reasoning off stops working entirely, although Qwen3 hybrids can be turned off on these hosts (vLLM chat_template_kwargs, OpenRouter reasoning.enabled=false). ReasoningHigh on the same names also stops sending any effort field (base sent reasoning_effort/reasoning.effort).
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai-hosts/probe3_test.go (httptest capture) ran in both trees. HEAD: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B off: err=reasoning cannot be disabled ... body=null`, the same for qwen/qwen3-32b, Qwen/QwQ-32B, qwq-32b and Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507. BASE: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B off: err=<nil> body={"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-8B"}`, qwq-32b sends reasoning_effort none, no errors. probe4 with base URL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 and WithModernReasoningFormat gives HEAD `qwen off: err=reasoning cannot be disabled for model "qwen/qwen3-32b"` and BASE err=<nil>. Code path: llms/reasoning/off.go openAIOffWire: `if !AcceptsEffortWire(model) { return OffUnsupported }`; AcceptsEffortWire returns false for any `qwen`/`qwq` prefix. The rule comes from DashScope's door (commit df2e5f7 / 86ae410) but is applied on every host.

repro.evidence: Own probe probes/vx3-f123/probe_test.go (captures the request body with an openai.WithHTTPClient Doer, so host detection sees the real base URL), run in both trees through overlay. HEAD, base URLs http://vllm:8000/v1, https://api.together.xyz/v1 and https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 (+WithModernReasoningFormat): WithReasoningDisabled on Qwen/Qwen3-8B, qwen/qwen3-32b, Qwen/QwQ-32B, qwq-32b and Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 returns `reasoning cannot be disabled for model ...`, body=null (no request sent). ReasoningHigh on the same names sends no effort field at all. BASE: every off call returns err=<nil> (QwQ/Thinking-2507 send reasoning_effort/reasoning.effort "none", Qwen3-8B/qwen3-32b send nothing), and high sends reasoning_effort:"high" / reasoning:{effort:"high"}. On DashScope (qwen3-32b) HEAD correctly sends enable_thinking:false. Code path: openaillm.go:596 setReasoningOff -> ResolveOff(DashScopeRoute(model, host), ProviderOpenAI) -> off.go openAIOffWire; for non-DashScope Qwen names it reaches off.go:195 `if !AcceptsEffortWire(model) { return OffUnsupported }`, and effort_wire.go:185 AcceptsEffortWire returns false for any `qwen`/`qwq` prefix regardless of host. Vendor side: OpenRouter documents reasoning.enabled for toggling reasoning and vLLM/Qwen3 accept chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking:false, so the models can be switched off on these hosts; even without that, the base sent the request instead of failing. Not a duplicate of earlier #5 (that one is the stream-only/enable_thinking rule on bare qwen3-<N>b); this is the OffUnsupported path for every qwen*/qwq* name off DashScope.
repro.comment: `openAIOffWire` returns `OffUnsupported` for every `qwen*`/`qwq*` name that is not a DashScope spelling, because `AcceptsEffortWire` (effort_wire.go:185) rejects the prefix on any host. As a result `WithReasoningDisabled()` now fails locally, before any request, for Qwen served by vLLM, Together or OpenRouter: e.g. `openai.New(WithBaseURL("http://vllm:8000/v1"), WithModel("Qwen/Qwen3-8B"))` returns `reasoning cannot be disabled for model "Qwen/Qwen3-8B"` on every call; the same for `qwen/qwen3-32b` on openrouter.ai (with WithModernReasoningFormat), `Qwen/QwQ-32B`, `qwq-32b` and `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507`. I checked this with a probe that captures the request body in both trees: at da7016e every one of these calls goes out with err=nil, and ReasoningHigh sends `reasoning_effort`/`reasoning.effort`; at HEAD the off calls send nothing and return the error, and high sends no effort field. An agent configured with reasoning off stops working entirely on these hosts. OpenRouter (`reasoning.enabled=false`) and vLLM (`chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`) can in fact turn Qwen3 hybrids off. The Qwen rule came from DashScope's door, so it should only apply on the DashScope route; elsewhere, fall back to the host's own wire, or to OffOmit/effort none as before, and keep sending an effort level for On.

refute.reason: llms/reasoning/off.go openAIOffWire returns OffUnsupported whenever AcceptsEffortWire(model) is false, and AcceptsEffortWire returns false for any qwen*/qwq* spelling except qwen3.8, whatever the host. setReasoningOff only rewrites the name for DashScope hosts (DashScopeRoute), so on vLLM, OpenRouter or Together names like Qwen/Qwen3-8B, qwen/qwen3-32b and qwq-32b go straight to ErrReasoningOffUnsupported. Commit 333a9c7, which added the rule, says it exists because DashScope (and Kimi k2) answer 400 to reasoning_effort. That reason does not apply to other hosts, which can turn Qwen3 thinking off. The test pin openrouter/qwen/qwen3.7-plus -> OffUnsupported only locks in the over-broad rule; it gives no vendor reason. In BASE the same calls succeeded (either nothing was sent or reasoning_effort none), so this is a new hard failure for callers. The root cause (a name rule that ignores the host) is the same as #5/#6, but the code path and the symptom are different, so it is not a duplicate.

kept.title: A named tool_choice whose function value is not map[string]any is rewritten to "required"
kept.summary: openaiToolChoice rewrites every tool choice that ClassifyToolChoice recognises. ClassifyToolChoice reads the name only when `function` is a map[string]any. A map[string]any choice whose function is map[string]string, llms.FunctionReference or *llms.FunctionReference is classified as "any tool" and sent as "required", which silently drops the forced tool name.
kept.failure_scenario: llms.WithTools(tools a and b) plus llms.WithToolChoice(map[string]any{"type":"function","function":map[string]string{"name":"b"}}) (or `"function": llms.FunctionReference{Name:"b"}` / `&llms.FunctionReference{...}`) sends tool_choice:"required". The model may then call tool a instead of the forced tool b, with no error or warning. The base sent {"type":"function","function":{"name":"b"}} verbatim.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai-toolchoice/probe_test.go, run in both trees. HEAD: `map-string-string-function: tool_choice="required"`, `funcref-value: tool_choice="required"`, `funcref-ptr: tool_choice="required"`; map-any and the llms.ToolChoice struct keep the name. BASE: all five shapes send `{"function":{"name":"b"},"type":"function"}`. The cause is llms/turn.go ClassifyToolChoice, case map[string]any: `if fn, ok := c["function"].(map[string]any)`; otherwise name stays "" and kindOf("function","") returns ToolChoiceAny. tool_choice_wire_test.go covers only map[string]any and the ToolChoice struct.

repro.evidence: Own probe TestProbeVX2ToolChoice (gpt-4.1 on api.openai.com, tools a and b, WithToolChoice forcing b) in both trees. HEAD: map[string]any{"function": map[string]any{...}} and llms.ToolChoice struct -> tool_choice {"function":{"name":"b"},"type":"function"}; map[string]any with function = map[string]string{"name":"b"}, llms.FunctionReference{Name:"b"} or &llms.FunctionReference{Name:"b"} -> tool_choice:"required", err=nil. BASE: all five shapes send {"function":{"name":"b"},"type":"function"}. Cause: llms/turn.go:65 ClassifyToolChoice reads the name only when c["function"] is map[string]any; otherwise name stays "" and kindOf("function","") returns ToolChoiceAny, which openaiToolChoice (openaillm.go:1018) turns into "required". Other doors (anthropic, bedrock, googleai, mistral) use the same classifier, so the lost name may affect them too, though only the OpenAI door was probed.
repro.comment: `ClassifyToolChoice` reads the forced tool's name only when `function` is a `map[string]any`. For a `map[string]any` choice whose `function` is a `map[string]string`, an `llms.FunctionReference` or a `*llms.FunctionReference`, the name is lost, the choice is classified as `ToolChoiceAny`, and `openaiToolChoice` (openaillm.go:1018) sends `tool_choice:"required"`. With tools a and b and `WithToolChoice(map[string]any{"type":"function","function":llms.FunctionReference{Name:"b"}})`, the model may call a instead of the forced b, and the caller gets no error or warning. I checked this with a probe that captures the request body: at HEAD these three shapes send `"required"`, while at da7016e all five shapes, including these three, sent `{"type":"function","function":{"name":"b"}}` unchanged. Fix: also read the name from `map[string]string`, `FunctionReference` and `*FunctionReference`, or pass the choice through unchanged when the type is `function` and the name can't be read. Add these shapes to tool_choice_wire_test.go.

refute.reason: In llms/turn.go ClassifyToolChoice, the map[string]any case reads the forced name only when c["function"] is a map[string]any. Any other value (map[string]string, llms.FunctionReference, *llms.FunctionReference) leaves the name empty, so kindOf("function","") returns ToolChoiceAny. openaiToolChoice then rewrites that to "required", and the forced tool name is dropped without an error or warning. BASE passed opts.ToolChoice through unchanged (openaillm.go:243 in base). The shapes are uncommon, but WithToolChoice takes `any` and they are natural things to write. The loss is silent, and the rewrite could fall back to passing the value through unchanged. None of the tests pin these shapes as intended behaviour.

kept.title: MiniMax and DeepSeek "vendor API" rules match OpenRouter's own model slugs (minimax/..., deepseek/...)
kept.summary: onMiniMaxAPI treats the minimax/ prefix, and ServedByDeepSeek treats deepseek/ plus a V4 name, as the vendor's own API on any host. OpenRouter's native slugs use exactly these prefixes. On openrouter.ai the door therefore drops JSON mode, top_k and temperature, and refuses structured output. The commits (4ba2e12, 9f2d8d7, 1d8ad3c) say the same model served by another host should keep them.
kept.failure_scenario: WithBaseURL("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1") with model minimax/minimax-m2: WithJSONMode sends no response_format (drop warning only); WithStructuredOutput returns ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported; WithTopK(40) is dropped; with WithPreserveReasoningContent the reasoning is inlined as <think> tags. Model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (a real OpenRouter slug served by 21 providers) with WithTemperature(0.3), WithTopK(40) loses both ("the model ignores temperature while thinking"). The base sent response_format json_object, json_schema, top_k and temperature to OpenRouter.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai-hosts/probe4_test.go uses base URL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with a transport that redirects to httptest. HEAD: `minimax json: body={"model":"minimax/minimax-m2"} warn=[drop: WithJSONMode ...]`, `minimax schema: err=structured output: unsupported ...`, `deepseek v4 temp: body={"model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro","top_p":0.9} warn=[drop WithTopK..., drop WithTemperature ...]`. BASE: `response_format:{type:json_object}`, a full json_schema, `temperature:0.3, top_k:40`. Code: llms/reasoning/effort_wire.go onMiniMaxAPI trims "minimax/"; ServedByDeepSeek accepts the `deepseek/` prefix on any host. The tests only cover the LiteLLM spelling openrouter/minimax/... on a gateway. OpenRouter model pages (openrouter.ai/minimax/minimax-m2, openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro) list response_format/structured outputs as supported.

repro.evidence: Own probe TestProbeVX3OpenRouterSlugs with base URL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 (request captured by a WithHTTPClient Doer, so the door sees the openrouter host). HEAD, minimax/minimax-m2: WithJSONMode -> body {"model":"minimax/minimax-m2"} (response_format dropped); WithStructuredOutput -> error `structured output: unsupported on openai for model minimax/minimax-m2: the vendor's chat completions API takes no response_format`; WithTemperature(0.3)+WithTopK(40) -> top_k dropped; with WithPreserveReasoningContent, WithTopK(40) is dropped too. deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash: WithTemperature(0.3)+WithTopK(40) -> body {"model":...} with both dropped (deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1 keeps both, so this is the ServedByDeepSeek list). BASE: json_object, a full json_schema, and temperature 0.3/top_k 40 are all sent for every one of these. Code: effort_wire.go:48-49 onMiniMaxAPI trims "minimax/" with no host check (TakesNoTopK/TakesNoResponseFormat), and effort_wire.go:29-30 ServedByDeepSeek treats the `deepseek/` prefix as DeepSeek's API on any host. Commit 1d8ad3c keeps that on purpose for LiteLLM's deepseek/ route, and 9f2d8d7 says 'MiniMax served by another host keeps it', but OpenRouter's native slugs use the same prefixes. Vendor: OpenRouter's MiniMax M2 model page lists structured outputs (response_format json_schema) as supported (WebSearch; openrouter.ai is blocked from this sandbox, so supported_parameters could not be fetched directly). The deepseek structured-output refusal on OpenRouter is the same defect as earlier #2 (TakesNoJSONSchema) and is not counted here; the new parts are MiniMax JSON mode/schema/top_k and the DeepSeek V4 temperature/top_k drop.
repro.comment: `onMiniMaxAPI` (and `ServedByDeepSeek` at line 29 for the `deepseek/` prefix) treats `minimax/…` and `deepseek/<v4 name>` as the vendor's own API on any host. OpenRouter's native slugs use exactly these prefixes, so on `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` the door strips parameters OpenRouter supports. For `minimax/minimax-m2`, `WithJSONMode` sends no `response_format` (only a drop warning), `WithStructuredOutput` fails with ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported, and `WithTopK(40)` is dropped. For `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`/`-flash`, both `WithTemperature(0.3)` and `WithTopK(40)` are dropped. I checked this with a probe that captures the request body sent to the openrouter host: at da7016e all of these reached the wire (json_object, the full json_schema, temperature 0.3 and top_k 40). OpenRouter's MiniMax M2 page lists structured outputs as supported, and the commits (9f2d8d7, 1d8ad3c) say the same model on another host should keep these fields; what each upstream provider behind OpenRouter then does is vendor behaviour. Suggest counting the `minimax/`/`deepseek/` prefix as the vendor route only off OpenRouter (or only on the vendor/LiteLLM hosts), the same way the bare names are already host-gated. (The DeepSeek json_schema refusal on OpenRouter is the separate TakesNoJSONSchema issue already reported.)

refute.reason: onMiniMaxAPI strips a "minimax/" prefix and matches on the family, whatever the host. ServedByDeepSeek counts "deepseek/"+name as DeepSeek's own API on any host (commit 1d8ad3c says this is on purpose for LiteLLM's route prefix). OpenRouter's own slugs use exactly these prefixes (for example minimax/minimax-m2), and the door already knows its host (o.host) but does not check it here. Commit 9f2d8d7 says "MiniMax served by another host keeps it", and 4ba2e12 checks that other hosts keep json_object only through the LiteLLM spelling openrouter/minimax/minimax-m3. The code therefore contradicts the stated intent for OpenRouter-native slugs: JSON mode and top_k are dropped, WithStructuredOutput is refused (TakesNoResponseFormat), and DeepSeek-V4 slugs lose temperature and top_k. BASE sent all of these fields. It is not a duplicate of #2: #2 covers TakesNoJSONSchema for deepseek-*/glm-*, while this finding is about the MiniMax predicates and ServedByDeepSeek.

kept.title: Off and effort ignore WithModernReasoningFormat for GLM/Kimi/MiniMax/DeepSeek-V4/Qwen: OpenRouter gets a thinking object or nothing
kept.summary: With WithModernReasoningFormat (OpenRouter's reasoning object), setReasoningOff still sends the vendor-native thinking:{type:disabled} for thinking-object models. The ReasoningOn path applies the native door's "refuses reasoning_effort" rule to the reasoning object, so no effort goes out for qwen*, glm<5.2, kimi-k2* and minimax-m*. The base sent reasoning:{effort:"none"} and reasoning:{effort:"high"}.
kept.failure_scenario: OpenRouter + WithModernReasoningFormat + z-ai/glm-4.6 + WithReasoningDisabled sends {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}} with no warning. This is not an OpenRouter parameter, so thinking likely stays on (base: {"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}}). The same models with WithReasoning(High) send no reasoning field at all (base: reasoning.effort high). The Claude branch already treats the modern format as a door without a thinking object (sendsClaudeThinkingObject requires !ModernReasoningFormat, and claude_thinking_off_route_test expects ErrReasoningOffUnsupported there), so the two branches disagree.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai-hosts/probe4_test.go (OpenRouter base URL): HEAD `glm off: body={"model":"z-ai/glm-4.6","thinking":{"type":"disabled"}} warn=[]`, BASE `{"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}}`. Probe probe_test.go (modern format, ReasoningHigh): HEAD `qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b`, `z-ai/glm-4.6`, `moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking`, `minimax/minimax-m2` → body without reasoning, drop warning; BASE `"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}` for each. The code writes the thinking object in OffDisableThinkingObject without checking o.client.ModernReasoningFormat; writeEffort only fills req.Reasoning when `sends` (from AcceptsEffortWire). Whether OpenRouter ignores the thinking object could not be run here.

repro.evidence: Probe probes/vx-f123/probe_test.go (TestProbeVXF1). The client points at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with WithModernReasoningFormat, and requests go to an httptest server through a redirecting RoundTripper. HEAD: `off z-ai/glm-4.6: body={"model":"z-ai/glm-4.6","thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}` and `off deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro: body={..."thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}`. With WithReasoning(High,0), qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b, z-ai/glm-4.6, moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking and minimax/minimax-m2 send a body with no reasoning field. BASE, same probe: `{"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}}` for off and `{"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}}` for high on every one of these models. Cause: setReasoningOff (openaillm.go:604-609) writes req.Thinking in the OffDisableThinkingObject case without checking o.client.ModernReasoningFormat, while writeDisableEffort does check it. In setReasoning, acceptsEffort comes from AcceptsEffortWire, which returns false for qwen*, kimi-k2*, minimax-m*, glm<5.2 (thinksBySwitchOnly), so writeEffort never fills req.Reasoning. The Claude branch does exclude the modern format: sendsClaudeThinkingObject requires !ModernReasoningFormat. OpenRouter's docs describe only the `reasoning` object (effort / max_tokens / exclude / enabled) to control reasoning (https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/reasoning-tokens), and no `thinking` parameter. openrouter.ai is blocked by the sandbox egress, so I could not check what OpenRouter does with an unknown `thinking` field. The wire regression is demonstrated. That thinking then stays on depends on OpenRouter. Note: thinking_budget_field_test.go has a 'modern format alone' case for GLM budgets, so the native-door rule under the modern format looks partly intended for budgets. It does not cover the off path.
repro.comment: With `WithModernReasoningFormat()` (OpenRouter's `reasoning` object), `setReasoningOff` still writes the vendor-native `thinking:{type:"disabled"}` for thinking-object models: `OffDisableThinkingObject` never checks `o.client.ModernReasoningFormat`, although `writeDisableEffort` and `sendsClaudeThinkingObject` both do. A probe against an OpenRouter base URL shows `z-ai/glm-4.6` and `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` + `WithReasoningDisabled()` sending `{"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}` with no warning, where the previous release sent `{"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}}`. With `WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh, 0)` the effort is dropped for `qwen/*`, `z-ai/glm-4.6`, `moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking` and `minimax/minimax-m2`, because `AcceptsEffortWire` (a rule for the native `reasoning_effort` field) also gates the `reasoning` object; the base sent `reasoning.effort:"high"`. OpenRouter documents only the `reasoning` object for controlling thinking, so the off request most likely leaves thinking on. That last part depends on OpenRouter and I could not check it from here. Suggested fix: when the modern format is on, route off to `writeDisableEffort` and let `writeEffort` fill `req.Reasoning` regardless of the native door's effort rule, as the Claude branch already does.

refute.reason: I reproduced it with my own probe (probes/skeptic-oai3) against an openrouter.ai base URL with WithModernReasoningFormat.
