Suggested fix: when the modern format is on, route off to `writeDisableEffort` and let `writeEffort` fill `req.Reasoning` regardless of the native door's effort rule, as the Claude branch already does.

kept.title: WithLogProbs/WithTopLogProbs are sent but the logprobs are never returned; top_logprobs goes out without logprobs
kept.summary: The new options put logprobs/top_logprobs on the wire (commit a0fdfa7: "connect logprobs and top_logprobs to the caller"). processResponse ignores choices[].logprobs, so the caller never receives them. WithTopLogProbs alone sends top_logprobs without logprobs:true, which OpenAI documents as requiring logprobs=true.
kept.failure_scenario: GenerateContent(..., llms.WithLogProbs(true), llms.WithTopLogProbs(1)) against a server that returns choices[0].logprobs gives a ContentChoice with no logprob data in any field or GenerationInfo key. GenerateContent(..., llms.WithTopLogProbs(3)) sends {"top_logprobs":3} with no logprobs field, which OpenAI rejects with a 400.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai-logprobs/probe_test.go (HEAD): the request is `"logprobs":true,"top_logprobs":1`, and the marshalled choice has GenerationInfo keys only for token counts and no logprobs. The top_logprobs-only request is `{"model":"gpt-4o",...,"top_logprobs":3}`. grep over llms/openai/*.go (non-test) shows LogProbs used only when building the request and in the sampling snapshot, never in processResponse. OpenAI chat completions reference: "logprobs must be set to true if this parameter [top_logprobs] is used".

repro.evidence: Probe probes/vx-f123/probe2_test.go (TestProbeVXF2, HEAD). The server returns choices[0].logprobs.content with a token and top_logprobs. With WithLogProbs(true)+WithTopLogProbs(1) the request is `{"logprobs":true,"model":"gpt-4o","top_logprobs":1}`, but the marshalled ContentChoice is `{"Content":"ok",...,"GenerationInfo":{token counters only},...}`: no logprob data anywhere. With WithTopLogProbs(3) alone the request is `{"model":"gpt-4o","top_logprobs":3}` with no logprobs field. grep over llms/openai/*.go (non-test): LogProbs/TopLogProbs appear only at openaillm.go:298-299 (request build), :665-666 (drop) and in sampling_warnings.go. processResponse (openaillm.go ~784-800) never reads c.LogProbs, although openaiclient parses it (chat.go:571). The repo's own openaiclient/chat.go:94 comment and the OpenAI chat-completions reference both say 'logprobs must be set to true if this parameter is used'. These options are new in this PR (commit a0fdfa7, 'connect logprobs and top_logprobs to the caller'), so this is an incomplete feature, not a regression. The 400 for top_logprobs without logprobs is documented vendor behaviour; I did not reproduce it live.
repro.comment: `WithLogProbs`/`WithTopLogProbs` now reach the wire, but the logprobs never come back to the caller: `processResponse` ignores `choices[].logprobs`, although `openaiclient` already parses it (`ChatCompletionChoice.LogProbs`). A probe with a stub server that returns `choices[0].logprobs.content` gives a `ContentChoice` with only token counters in `GenerationInfo` and no logprob data in any field. The caller pays for the feature and gets nothing back. Separately, `llms.WithTopLogProbs(3)` alone sends `{"top_logprobs":3}` without `logprobs:true`. OpenAI documents that logprobs must be true when top_logprobs is used, so that request is rejected (vendor behaviour, per the API reference and the comment in `openaiclient/chat.go`). Suggested fix: expose the choice logprobs, for example under a `GenerationInfo["LogProbs"]` key (streaming too), and either imply `logprobs:true` when `TopLogProbs > 0` or refuse the option locally.

refute.reason: WithLogProbs and WithTopLogProbs are new public options; BASE had neither. The WithLogProbs doc says it will 'return the log probability of each token'. My probe used a server that returns choices[0].logprobs, and the ContentChoice held no logprob data in any field or GenerationInfo key. In the non-test openai code, LogProbs is used only to build the request, in the sampling gate and in warnings, never in processResponse. openaiclient.ChatCompletionChoice decodes LogProbs, but that value is thrown away. WithTopLogProbs(3) alone sends {"top_logprobs":3} without logprobs:true, and the repo's own openaiclient comment says 'logprobs must be set to true if this parameter is used'. The strongest counter-argument is that top_logprobs alone is caller misuse the vendor will report. But the main defect remains: the new option charges for logprobs and never returns them.

kept.title: The effort-with-tools rule reads only opts.Tools, not opts.Functions that also become tools
kept.summary: setReasoning derives toolsRule from len(opts.Tools). The deprecated WithFunctions path puts the same function tools on the wire (addToolsToRequest), but the GPT-5.4/5.5/5.6 tools rule never applies to it.
kept.failure_scenario: gpt-5.6 with WithFunctions(...) and no reasoning option omits reasoning_effort, although commit df2e5f7 records that 5.6 rejects an omitted field when function tools ride along (400). With WithReasoning(High) the door sends reasoning_effort:"high" with tools instead of returning ErrEffortWithTools as it does for WithTools.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai-hosts/probe5_test.go (HEAD): `gpt-5.6 functions default: body={... no reasoning_effort, "tools":[...]}` vs `gpt-5.6 tools default: body={"reasoning_effort":"none","tools":[...]}`. `gpt-5.4 functions high: body={"reasoning_effort":"high","tools":[...]}` vs `gpt-5.4 tools high: err=model "gpt-5.4" rejects reasoning effort "high" on a request carrying function tools`.

repro.evidence: Probe probes/vx-f123/probe_test.go (TestProbeVXF3) with base URL https://api.openai.com/v1. HEAD: `gpt-5.6 functions default: body={"model":"gpt-5.6","tools":[...]}` (no reasoning_effort) vs `gpt-5.6 tools default: body={"model":"gpt-5.6","reasoning_effort":"none","tools":[...]}`. `gpt-5.6 functions high` sends reasoning_effort:"high" with tools, while `gpt-5.6 tools high` returns ErrEffortWithTools. gpt-5.4 behaves the same way: functions+high sends "high", tools+high gets the error. setReasoning (openaillm.go:407-409) sets toolsRule only when len(opts.Tools) > 0, while addToolsToRequest (openaillm.go:721-736) turns opts.Functions into the same `tools` array and already checks `len(opts.Tools) > 0 || len(opts.Functions) > 0` for ChatToolsUnsupported. Commit df2e5f7 says 5.4/5.5/5.6 answer 400 on a level with function tools, and 5.6 also on an omitted field. BASE sends the same bodies for the WithFunctions calls, so this is an incomplete fix and not a regression. The 400 itself is vendor behaviour recorded by the commit; I did not reproduce it live.
repro.comment: The effort-with-tools rule is keyed on `len(opts.Tools)` only, but the deprecated `WithFunctions` path puts the same function tools on the wire through `addToolsToRequest`, which itself checks `len(opts.Tools) > 0 || len(opts.Functions) > 0`. A probe shows `gpt-5.6` + `WithFunctions` sending no `reasoning_effort`, where the `WithTools` call sends `"none"`. It also shows `gpt-5.4`/`gpt-5.6` + `WithFunctions` + `WithReasoning(High)` sending `reasoning_effort:"high"` alongside `tools`, where the `WithTools` call returns `ErrEffortWithTools`. According to df2e5f7, the vendor answers both of these with 400. That relies on OpenAI behaviour recorded in the commit; I did not reproduce it live here. Suggested fix: derive `toolsRule` from `len(opts.Tools) > 0 || len(opts.Functions) > 0`, or better from `len(req.Tools) > 0` after `addToolsToRequest`.

refute.reason: Confirmed by probe. The deprecated WithFunctions path still puts the functions on the wire as tools (openaillm.go:721/728), but setReasoning sets toolsRule only from len(opts.Tools). Results: gpt-5.6 plus WithFunctions sends no reasoning_effort (WithTools sends "none"). gpt-5.4 and 5.6 plus WithFunctions plus High send reasoning_effort:"high" with tools (WithTools returns ErrEffortWithTools). Commit df2e5f7 records that these exact combinations get a 400 from the vendor, so the new guard is incomplete. WithFunctions is deprecated but still supported and converted to tools, so the vendor sees the same request. BASE sent byte-identical bodies for the WithFunctions cases, because it had no tools rule at all. So this is a gap the PR's fix did not close, not a regression from the previous release.

kept.title: budgetHasNoField reads the raw model while the other rules read the DashScope route
kept.summary: setReasoning and setReasoningOff pass DashScopeRoute(model, host) to the capability rules, as commit a0fffdf intends. budgetHasNoField passes the raw model to TakesNoThinkingDepth, so a bare name on DashScope's own host is refused while the equivalent dashscope/ route is not.
kept.failure_scenario: WithBaseURL("https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1"), model MiniMax-M2.5, WithReasoning("", 4000) returns ErrThinkingBudgetUnsupported. dashscope/MiniMax-M2.5 on a gateway makes the call and only reports the budget as dropped.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai-hosts/probe6_test.go (HEAD, redirected transport): `MiniMax-M2.5 on dashscope host budget: err=model "MiniMax-M2.5" takes no thinking budget or effort level` vs `dashscope/MiniMax-M2.5 on gateway budget: err=<nil> ... warn=[drop: WithReasoning asked 4000 tokens ...]`. TakesNoThinkingDepth returns false early only when dashScopeGuestSpelling(model) != "", which requires the dashscope/ prefix.

repro.evidence: At HEAD, setReasoning (llms/openai/openaillm.go:424) and writeVendorBudget (:494) read reasoning.DashScopeRoute(model, o.host), but budgetHasNoField (:515-519) calls reasoning.TakesNoThinkingDepth(model) with the raw name. TakesNoThinkingDepth (llms/reasoning/effort_wire.go:211) returns false early only when dashScopeGuestSpelling(model) != "", which needs the literal dashscope/ prefix; otherwise thinksBySwitchOnly matches the minimax-m prefix and returns true. Commit a0fffdf says a name sent to DashScope's own host should read as its dashscope/ route for 'the off wire, the budget, the enable_thinking flag and effort acceptance', and deepseek_sampling_test.go already treats 'dashscope/MiniMax-M2.5 on a gateway' as the gateway spelling of the same model. I ran probe probes/vf1-budgetroute/probe_test.go (httptest server, redirected transport, WithReasoning("", 4000)). HEAD: dashscope-intl host + MiniMax-M2.5 -> err='model "MiniMax-M2.5" takes no thinking budget or effort level; leave the budget unset', nothing sent. Gateway + dashscope/MiniMax-M2.5 -> err=nil, request sent. BASE (da7016e), same probe: both calls succeed and send reasoning_effort=low, so the bare-name case on DashScope's host is a regression. Moonshot-Kimi-K2-Instruct and glm-4.5-air behave the same on both spellings, so of the models I probed only MiniMax diverges. Alibaba Model Studio's MiniMax page (search result for help.aliyun.com/en/model-studio/minimax-api) lists the model id as plain 'MiniMax-M2.5' at https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1. The page body was not fetchable here (egress blocked).
repro.comment: `budgetHasNoField` passes the raw model to `reasoning.TakesNoThinkingDepth`, but `setReasoning` and `writeVendorBudget` read `reasoning.DashScopeRoute(model, o.host)`. Commit a0fffdf says a name sent to DashScope's own host should use its `dashscope/` route for the budget too. Because of this, `WithBaseURL("https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1")` + `WithModel("MiniMax-M2.5")` + `WithReasoning("", 4000)` now fails before any request with `ErrThinkingBudgetUnsupported`. The same model as `dashscope/MiniMax-M2.5` on a gateway sends the request. A probe with an httptest server shows this at HEAD. On the base (da7016e) both spellings made the call with `reasoning_effort: low`, so on DashScope's own host this is a regression (Model Studio documents `MiniMax-M2.5` as the plain model id there). Fix: call `reasoning.TakesNoThinkingDepth(reasoning.DashScopeRoute(model, o.host))` and add a bare `MiniMax-M2.5`-on-DashScope budget row to `TestDashScopeHostGetsTheGuestWireForNamesWithoutTheRoutePrefix`.

refute.reason:
The finding treats the wrong side of the inconsistency as the bug. Commit 2f174a8 states the intent: when no field can carry a thinking budget, return ErrThinkingBudgetUnsupported before the request leaves, because a dropped-option warning alone is not enough. The DashScope exemption exists only because DashScope caps its GLM and Kimi guests with thinking_budget. Commit a0fffdf quotes Alibaba's reference: thinking_budget applies to "GLM and Kimi models", and MiniMax only gets the thinking object. So MiniMax on DashScope has no budget field.

Budget-taking guests never reach budgetHasNoField: bare glm-5.1 or kimi-k2.6 on a DashScope host is caught first by writeVendorBudget, which already reads DashScopeRoute. That is what a0fffdf fixed for a bare glm-5.1 on the DashScope host. The only bare names that reach budgetHasNoField on a DashScope host are guests DashScope gives no budget field (MiniMax, plain Kimi K2). AcceptsEffortWire is also false for them via thinksBySwitchOnly, so no effort level would be sent either. For these, refusing is exactly what 2f174a8 intends.

Reading the route in budgetHasNoField, as the finding suggests, would turn that correct refusal into a silent drop and regress 2f174a8. The real inconsistency is in TakesNoThinkingDepth: it returns false for any dashscope/ guest, which is broader than the GLM and Kimi guests it is meant for. As a result, dashscope/MiniMax-M2.5 on a gateway only gets a warning. That exemption is untested for MiniMax: TestTakesNoThinkingDepth lists only dashscope/glm-* and dashscope/kimi-* rows. It is a different defect in llms/reasoning/effort_wire.go:212, not the one claimed here. BASE has no TakesNoThinkingDepth, DashScopeRoute or budgetHasNoField, so the behaviour is new.

kept.judge_reason: The divergence is real, but the finding blames the wrong side, and the fix it proposes (have budgetHasNoField read DashScopeRoute) would turn a correct refusal into a silent drop. Commit 2f174a8 says a budget that no field can carry must return ErrThinkingBudgetUnsupported before the request is sent, and that a dropped-option warning alone is not enough. Alibaba's docs (quoted in a0fffdf; search results for help.aliyun.com model-studio deep-thinking and minimax-api) say the same: thinking_budget applies to Qwen, GLM and Kimi, MiniMax takes only the thinking switch, and MiniMax-M2.5 on Model Studio is thinking-only. So refusing bare MiniMax-M2.5 on DashScope's host is intended behaviour. Budget-taking guests (GLM, Kimi) never reach budgetHasNoField, because writeVendorBudget already reads the route. The actual gap is in TakesNoThinkingDepth (effort_wire.go:212): it returns false for every dashscope/<guest>, MiniMax included. My probe at HEAD (httptest server, redirected transport, WithReasoning("", 4000)) refused MiniMax-M2.5 on dashscope-intl, MiniMax/MiniMax-M3 on dashscope-intl, dashscope/MiniMax/MiniMax-M3 on a gateway and minimax/MiniMax-M2.5 on a gateway. Only dashscope/MiniMax-M2.5 on a gateway went through: the body had no reasoning field at all, and the caller got only a drop warning. That is the exact case 2f174a8 set out to close. TestTakesNoThinkingDepth has only dashscope/glm-* and dashscope/kimi-* rows, so this exemption is not tested for MiniMax. The code is new in the PR (effort_wire.go is a new file). I re-anchored the finding to the exemption.
kept.comment: The `dashscope/` exemption here is broader than the guests DashScope actually caps with `thinking_budget`. Alibaba's reference limits that field to Qwen, GLM and Kimi; MiniMax gets only the thinking switch. As a result, `WithModel("dashscope/MiniMax-M2.5")` on a gateway with `WithReasoning("", 4000)` sends a body with no reasoning field at all and only reports the budget as dropped. Every other spelling of the same model is refused with `ErrThinkingBudgetUnsupported` before the network, as 2f174a8 intends: `MiniMax-M2.5` sent to dashscope-intl, `dashscope/MiniMax/MiniMax-M3` and `minimax/MiniMax-M2.5` (probe at 355dc71). Suggest limiting the early return to guests that really take a budget, e.g. `if DashScopeTakesThinkingBudget(model) { return false }`. Also add a `dashscope/MiniMax-M2.5` row to TestTakesNoThinkingDepth. Budget-taking guests never reach `budgetHasNoField` anyway, since `writeVendorBudget` handles them first. Once the exemption is narrowed, `budgetHasNoField` can safely read `DashScopeRoute(model, o.host)` like the other rules.

kept.title: Delegated adaptive reasoning on Claude is dropped with no warning when no adaptive object is sent
kept.summary: setDeferredReasoning warns about a lost delegation only when the model is in reasoning.ThinkingOptIn. Claude models are not in that set, so a WithAdaptiveReasoning("") call on a Claude model that is off by default and gets no adaptive thinking object goes out with no reasoning field and no warning. This covers Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5 and 3.7 Sonnet on every host, and Opus/Sonnet 4.6-4.8 under WithModernReasoningFormat. The base sent an effort of "high".
kept.failure_scenario: openai.New(WithBaseURL("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"), WithModernReasoningFormat(), WithModel("anthropic/claude-opus-4.6")) + llms.WithAdaptiveReasoning("") sends {"model":...,"messages":[...]} with no reasoning object and resp.Warnings is empty, so the model answers without thinking and nothing tells the caller. The same happens for claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-5 and claude-3-7-sonnet-latest behind LiteLLM or OpenRouter without the modern format. The base sent reasoning:{effort:"high"} or reasoning_effort:"high". Commit dc9cfa3 names exactly this silent failure ('went out ... with neither thinking nor reasoning_effort and without a warning'), and 8c74336 says the door reports a delegation it cannot carry; the fix covered only adaptive-kind Claude on the flat reasoning_effort format. Also, OpenRouter's reasoning object has reasoning:{enabled:true} for 'let the provider decide'.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai2-harness/s2.go and s4.go (capturing Doer, HEAD vs BASE). HEAD: [or-modern-opus46-adaptive] REQ: {"model":"anthropic/claude-opus-4.6","messages":[...]} with no WARN line. [litellm-haiku45], [litellm-sonnet45], [litellm-sonnet37], [or-legacy-sonnet45], [or-modern-sonnet45] and [or-modern-opus48] all show a body without reasoning and no WARN. By contrast, [or-legacy-opus46-adaptive] prints 'drop: WithAdaptiveReasoning ... sent nothing' and gpt-5.1 also warns. BASE sent "reasoning":{"effort":"high"} or "reasoning_effort":"high" in every case. Test TestDelegatedAdaptiveKeepsItsObjectOffOtherWires ('the reasoning object format', 'a generation that predates adaptive') asserts only the absence of "adaptive", never a warning. Code: openaillm.go:459-474; reasoning.ThinkingOptIn (reasoning.go:465) has no Claude entry.

repro.evidence: My own probe (probes/ver-oai-f12, a capturing HTTP Doer, run against HEAD and BASE through overlays) called GenerateContent with llms.WithAdaptiveReasoning(""). At HEAD these requests went out with no reasoning field and resp.Warnings was empty (warnings=0): OpenRouter anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 with WithModernReasoningFormat; LiteLLM claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-5 and claude-3-7-sonnet-latest on the legacy format. In the same run, legacy-format OpenRouter anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 and openai/gpt-5.1 both got 'drop: WithAdaptiveReasoning ... sent nothing', and LiteLLM claude-opus-4-6 got thinking:{type:adaptive}. BASE sent reasoning_effort:"high" (legacy) or reasoning:{effort:"high"} (modern) in every case. Cause: in setDeferredReasoning (openaillm.go:459-474), the sendsClaudeAdaptive branch needs !ModernReasoningFormat and an adaptive-kind Claude. The only other branch that warns is reasoning.ThinkingOptIn(model), and ThinkingOptIn (reasoning.go:465) has no Claude entry, so budget-kind Claude and any Claude on the modern format fall through to 'return ""' without a warning. Commit a459111 meant for the dropped request to behave as unset while 'the caller is told' when the model will not reason. dc9cfa3 describes this exact silent failure for Claude but fixed only the adaptive-kind, legacy-format case.
repro.comment: `setDeferredReasoning` warns about a dropped delegation only for adaptive-kind Claude on the flat `reasoning_effort` format, or for models in `reasoning.ThinkingOptIn`, and no Claude model is in that set. So `WithAdaptiveReasoning("")` on a Claude model that is off by default goes out with no reasoning field and no warning. This covers Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5 and 3.7 Sonnet on any host, and Opus/Sonnet 4.6-4.8 under `WithModernReasoningFormat`. The model then answers without thinking and nothing tells the caller. A capturing-Doer probe showed it: OpenRouter `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` with the modern format, and LiteLLM `claude-haiku-4-5`/`claude-sonnet-4-5`/`claude-3-7-sonnet-latest`, all sent `{"model":...,"messages":[...]}` with `resp.Warnings` empty, while the previous release sent `reasoning_effort:"high"` or `reasoning:{effort:"high"}`. Legacy-format OpenRouter opus-4.6 in the same run does get the `drop: WithAdaptiveReasoning ... sent nothing` warning. Suggested fix: call `reportDelegatedDepth` for any Claude that supports thinking and is not on by default whenever no thinking object is written, or on the modern format send OpenRouter's `reasoning:{enabled:true}`, which lets the provider pick the depth.

refute.reason: I reproduced it with my own probe (probes/skv12-oai, run on HEAD and BASE). With the modern format on anthropic/claude-opus-4.6, and without it on claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-sonnet-4-5, WithAdaptiveReasoning("") sends a body with no reasoning field, and resp.Warnings is empty. BASE sent reasoning:{effort:"high"} or reasoning_effort:"high". Commits a459111 and bd34934 did mean delegation to send no depth field. But a459111 also says that where this means the model will not reason at all, the caller is told. setDeferredReasoning (openaillm.go:470-472) warns only for reasoning.ThinkingOptIn, which has no Claude entry, so Claude models that are off by default lose thinking without a warning. dc9cfa3 calls exactly this a bug. No test requires the warning to be absent: TestDelegatedAdaptiveKeepsItsObjectOffOtherWires only checks that "adaptive" is not sent. The design's own promise is broken, and BASE made these models think.

kept.title: WithReasoning("none") now fails before the request instead of sending OpenAI's disable value
kept.summary: The new ValidateReasoning gate accepts only "", minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh and max. So llms.WithReasoning("none", 0) returns invalid_request "unknown reasoning effort" before anything is sent. The base put reasoning_effort:"none" (or reasoning.effort:"none" with the modern format) on the wire, and OpenAI and OpenRouter document it as turning reasoning off on gpt-5.1 and later.
kept.failure_scenario: WithModel("gpt-5.1") + llms.WithReasoning("none", 0): HEAD returns 'invalid_request: unknown reasoning effort "none"' and sends no request. The base sent {"reasoning_effort":"none"} and got a non-reasoning answer. The same happens on OpenRouter with WithModernReasoningFormat, where the base sent reasoning:{effort:"none"}. The commit that added the gate targets garbage values (its test uses "banana"). "none" is the vendor's own spelling of off and could map to ReasoningOff instead of failing.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai2-harness/s5.go. HEAD: [gpt51-effort-none] ERR: invalid_request: unknown reasoning effort "none" (empty REQ); likewise gpt-5.2 and openai/gpt-5.1 modern. BASE: REQ {"model":"gpt-5.1",...,"reasoning_effort":"none"} and REQ {..."reasoning":{"effort":"none"}} with success. Code: llms/options.go:179 ValidateReasoning switch. BASE ClampEffort returned an unranked "none" unchanged. reasoning_validation_test.go only covers "banana".

kept.title: Cancelled or timed-out stream returns a truncated answer with a nil error about half the time
kept.summary: The stream producer selects on producerCtx.Done(), which derives from the caller's ctx. When the caller's context is cancelled or its deadline passes mid-stream, the producer often returns without sending an error and closes the channel. combineStreamingChatResponse then returns the partial text as a normal success, with an empty StopReason and no truncation error.
kept.failure_scenario: The caller uses context.WithTimeout or cancels during a long streamed generation. GenerateContent returns (resp, nil) with resp.Choices[0].Content holding only the text streamed so far ('w0 w1 w2 ') and StopReason "". A caller that checks only err takes the cut-off answer as complete. Which result comes back depends on select ordering between the producer's Done case and its error send, and on the Done check at the top of each scanned line. The PR rewrote this path (1eecb8f producerCtx, 377b41d partial-with-error) but left the cancellation branches silent. The same race existed in the base.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai2-cancel/probe_test.go: an httptest SSE server streams 50 chunks 20ms apart, and the streaming func cancels ctx after the 3rd text chunk; 20 trials. HEAD: 'cancelled mid-stream: nil error 12/20, error 8/20', trial 0 'err=nil content="w0 w1 w2 " stop=""'. BASE: 'nil error 6/20, error 14/20'. Code: chat.go:871-876 (Done check before each line returns silently) and 913-924 (scanner error vs Done race).

repro.evidence: My probe (probes/ver-oai-f3): an httptest SSE server streams 40 chunks 15ms apart, with 30 trials per mode. When the streaming func cancels ctx after the 3rd text chunk, HEAD returned a nil error in 11/30 trials, e.g. content="w0 w1 w2 " stop="". With context.WithTimeout(80ms), HEAD returned a nil error in 14/30 trials, e.g. content="w0 w1 w2 w3 w4 w5 " stop="". BASE showed the same race: 20/30 and 14/30 nil errors. Code: in the producer goroutine (chat.go:870-876, 913-918), both the Done check before each scanned line and the select between producerCtx.Done() and sending the scanner error return without emitting an error. The channel then closes, and combineStreamingChatResponse returns the partial response with streamErr == nil. Nothing downstream checks ctx.Err(). This is not a regression, but the PR rewrote this path (producerCtx, partial-with-error) and left the cancellation branches silent.
repro.comment: When the caller's context is cancelled or its deadline passes mid-stream, the producer goroutine often leaves through a `producerCtx.Done()` branch without sending an error, and `combineStreamingChatResponse` returns the partial text with a nil error and an empty `StopReason`. I tested this against an httptest SSE server (40 chunks, 15ms apart): cancelling after the 3rd chunk gave `err == nil` with content `"w0 w1 w2 "` in 11 of 30 trials, and a `context.WithTimeout` deadline gave a nil error in 14 of 30. The outcome depends on the select race between the Done case and the scanner-error send. A caller that checks only `err` will treat a truncated answer as complete. The previous release had the same race, so this is not a regression, but this PR rewrote the path. Suggested fix: after the stream ends, return the partial response together with `ctx.Err()` when `ctx.Err() != nil` (or send `ctx.Err()` from the Done branches), the same way other stream errors are already returned with a partial response.

refute.reason: This is a real defect. The stream producer returns silently on producerCtx.Done(), both in the check before each line and in the select against the scanner-error send. combineStreamingChatResponse then returns the partial response with a nil streamErr, and nothing downstream checks ctx.Err(). The cancellation logic in parseStreamingChatResponse is the same as in BASE: the PR only renamed ctx to producerCtx, which derives from ctx and is cancelled by the defer. The 12/20 vs 6/20 split in the reviewer's probe comes from scheduling nondeterminism, not a change in behaviour. So the PR did not cause this; the previous release already had it.

kept.title: WithExtraBody deep-merges two json_schema response formats into one invalid schema
kept.summary: mergeJSON merges objects key by key whenever both carry the same "type". An extra-body response_format of type json_schema is therefore merged into the library's json_schema object down into schema.properties. The result is the union of both property sets with only the extra body's required array, which OpenAI strict mode rejects. The base replaced response_format whole.
kept.failure_scenario: The client is created with WithResponseFormat(json_schema 'a' with property city), and one call passes openai.WithExtraBody({response_format: json_schema 'b' with property score, required [score], strict true}) to swap the schema for that call. HEAD sends name 'b' with properties {city, score} and required ["score"]. OpenAI strict json_schema requires every property in required, so the call gets a 400. If it were accepted, the model would answer a schema the caller never wrote. The base sent schema 'b' unchanged. The merge commit (61477f9) aimed at thinking.clear_thinking, thinking.keep and stream_options siblings; merging JSON Schemas key by key is a different, unintended effect.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/oai2-harness/s3.go. HEAD REQ: "response_format":{"json_schema":{"name":"b","schema":{"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"city":{...},"score":{"type":"number"}},"required":["score"],...},"strict":true},"type":"json_schema"}. BASE REQ: the same response_format with properties {score} only. Code: chat.go:801-816 (mergeJSON, selectsAnotherVariant); commits 61477f9 and 689197b.

repro.evidence:
Reproduced end to end through the public door with an httptest server (probe probes/v-f1-extrabody-rf, same file run through an overlay in both checkouts). Setup: openai.New(WithModel("gpt-4o"), WithResponseFormat(json_schema "a", properties {city}, required [city])), then GenerateContent(..., openai.WithExtraBody({response_format: {type: json_schema, json_schema: {name: b, strict: true, schema: {properties {score}, required [score], additionalProperties false}}}})).

HEAD sent: "response_format":{"json_schema":{"name":"b","schema":{"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"city":{"type":"string","additionalProperties":false},"score":{"type":"number"}},"required":["score"],"type":"object"},"strict":true},"type":"json_schema"}.
BASE sent: the same object with properties {score} only.

Cause: mergeJSON (chat.go:801-815) recurses into every object on both sides. selectsAnotherVariant only stops the recursion when the "type" values differ, and here both are json_schema. The recursion therefore reaches schema.properties, where the two property maps are unioned, while the required array is replaced as a leaf. A caller cannot opt out: a null for properties.city would put null into the schema. The merge is intentional and documented in the WithExtraBody doc (options.go:50-53), and commit 61477f9 mentions a depth-two response_format leaf. Merging whole JSON Schemas, however, is an unintended side effect of that contract.

The harm depends on the vendor. In OpenAI Structured Outputs strict mode, every property must be listed in required, so the merged schema is expected to be rejected with a 400. This rule is from OpenAI's documentation and was not checked with a live call. If a provider accepts the schema, the model answers a schema the caller never wrote.
repro.comment: `mergeJSON` recurses into every object pair whose `type` values are equal. When the client was built with `WithResponseFormat` (json_schema `a` with property `city`) and a call passes `openai.WithExtraBody` with its own json_schema `response_format` (`b` with property `score`, required `[score]`, strict), the request goes out as schema `b` with properties `{city, score}` and required `["score"]`. That is a union of the two schemas that nobody wrote. I reproduced it with an httptest probe through `GenerateContent`, and the previous release sent schema `b` unchanged. OpenAI strict mode documents that every property must be in `required`, so this request should get a 400; I did not check that with a live call. With a lenient provider the model would follow the wrong schema. Merging siblings such as `thinking.clear_thinking` or `stream_options` is fine, but JSON Schema subtrees (`response_format.json_schema.schema`, and probably tool `parameters`) should be replaced whole rather than merged, for example by stopping the recursion at `schema`, or by replacing `response_format` as a whole whenever extra body supplies a `json_schema`.

refute.reason: Not preexisting. BASE chat.go:630-643 used maps.Copy at the top level, so an extra-body response_format replaced the door's whole. HEAD mergeJSON (chat.go:801-822) merges key by key and replaces only when both objects carry a different "type". On the path in the finding, the top-level types are both "json_schema", json_schema has no type, and schema has "type":"object" on both sides, so everything keeps merging. properties becomes the union of both sets, and required is an array, so the extra body's version replaces the door's. That matches the reviewer's wire output. The strongest reason to dismiss it: the key-by-key merge is documented on CallOptions.ExtraBody in llms/options.go:330-334, and the test 'a nested leaf is replaced and its siblings stay' in extra_body_merge_test.go pins merging into response_format.json_schema on purpose. That argument fails on three counts. (1) Commits 61477f9 and 689197b give their reason as sibling flags beside a door toggle (thinking.clear_thinking, keep, display, reasoning.exclude, stream_options). In a JSON Schema, "type" is a schema keyword, not a variant tag, and merging two schemas produces something neither side wrote. (2) The caller has no other way to swap the schema: with a client-level WithResponseFormat, a per-call WithStructuredOutput is refused with ErrStructuredOutputConflict (structured_output.go:97-102). ExtraBody was the only per-call override, it worked in BASE, and there is no longer any way to replace a same-typed object whole. (3) With strict mode, OpenAI requires every property to be listed in required, so the merged request is invalid, or it silently constrains the model to a schema the caller never wrote. This is a silent behaviour change on a realistic input, not something ruled out by docs or vendor behaviour.

kept.comment: `mergeJSON` recurses into every object pair whose `type` values are equal. When the client was built with `WithResponseFormat` (json_schema `a` with property `city`) and a call passes `openai.WithExtraBody` with its own json_schema `response_format` (`b` with property `score`, required `[score]`, strict), the request goes out as schema `b` with properties `{city, score}` and required `["score"]`. That is a union of the two schemas that nobody wrote. I reproduced it with an httptest probe through `GenerateContent`, and the previous release sent schema `b` unchanged. OpenAI strict mode documents that every property must be in `required`, so this request should get a 400; I did not check that with a live call. With a lenient provider the model would follow the wrong schema. Merging siblings such as `thinking.clear_thinking` or `stream_options` is fine, but JSON Schema subtrees (`response_format.json_schema.schema`, and probably tool `parameters`) should be replaced whole rather than merged, for example by stopping the recursion at `schema`, or by replacing `response_format` as a whole whenever extra body supplies a `json_schema`.

kept.title: Grok is pinned to the deprecated max_tokens field, and the xAI cassettes that showed otherwise were rewritten by hand
kept.summary: TestTheOutputLimitPicksTheFieldTheRouteUnderstands requires every grok model to get max_tokens and never max_completion_tokens. xAI's OpenAPI marks max_tokens as deprecated in favour of max_completion_tokens, and the repository's own August 2026 xAI recordings show 200 OK for max_completion_tokens. Those ten cassettes had their request bodies rewritten instead of re-recorded, so no recording backs the new request shape.
kept.failure_scenario: WithModel("grok-4.5") + WithMaxTokens(100) sends {"max_tokens":100}. The rewritten xAI cassettes (TestMultiContentTextWithReasoning-*-xai-grok-*, TestXAI_ImplicitCaching_*) replay a 200 that xAI returned for a max_completion_tokens request. If xAI drops or reinterprets the deprecated field, every grok call either loses its output limit or fails, and the offline suite stays green because this test and the rewritten cassettes are the only guards.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeMisc (overlay, HEAD) printed: grok max: {"model":"grok-4.5",...,"max_tokens":100}. In BASE, grepping the xAI cassettes that carry max_completion_tokens gives HTTP/2.0 200 OK for 9 files: grok-4.3-medium and grok-4.5-low/high, streaming and sync, plus 3 ImplicitCaching files. The 10th is 400, and only for presencePenalty. All date from 2026-08-03. Commit b9f989b says "xAI refuses it outright" and "only the request bodies and the block lengths were rewritten". In HEAD, no api.x.ai cassette contains max_completion_tokens. xAI's OpenAPI, quoted on pkg.go.dev/github.com/Tangerg/scope/models/xai: max_tokens "[DEPRECATED] ... Deprecated in favor of max_completion_tokens". docs.x.ai itself is blocked by the sandbox egress proxy.

repro.evidence: Code: llms/reasoning/effort_wire.go:164-175 UsesLegacyMaxTokens returns true for any grok* spelling, and openaillm.go:328 then sends req.MaxTokens instead of MaxCompletionTokens. Probe TestProbeVF3 (overlay, HEAD): grok-4.5 + WithMaxTokens(100) -> {"model":"grok-4.5",...,"max_tokens":100}; the same probe in BASE -> {...,"max_completion_tokens":100}. BASE cassettes (llms/openai/testdata, recorded 2026-08-03 against api.x.ai): all 9 that carry max_completion_tokens (TestMultiContentTextWithReasoning-{streaming,synchronous}-xai-grok-4.3-medium/4.5-low/4.5-high, TestXAI_ImplicitCaching_{Streaming,IdenticalRequests,Conversation_WithTools}) show HTTP/2.0 200 OK; the 10th (TestXAI_ReasoningModel_RejectsPenalties) is 400 with body {"code":"invalid-argument","error":"Model grok-4.5 does not support parameter presencePenalty."}, i.e. not about the limit field. Commit b9f989b claims "xAI refuses it outright" and says "only the request bodies and the block lengths were rewritten"; git diff da7016e 355dc71 of e.g. ...synchronous-xai-grok-4.5-high.httprr shows exactly that: Content-Length 185->174 and max_completion_tokens:8192 -> max_tokens:8192 with the same recorded 200 response. In HEAD no grok cassette carries max_completion_tokens, and the only grok cassettes carrying max_tokens are these 9 hand-edited ones, so no genuine recording backs the new wire shape. xAI's OpenAPI (quoted on pkg.go.dev/github.com/Tangerg/scope/models/xai): max_tokens "[DEPRECATED] ... Deprecated in favor of max_completion_tokens". docs.x.ai is blocked by the sandbox egress proxy, so whether xAI still honours max_tokens today could not be confirmed directly; the harm is future/vendor-dependent.
repro.comment: This test pins every grok* model to `max_tokens` (via `reasoning.UsesLegacyMaxTokens`, llms/reasoning/effort_wire.go:166), but the repository's own xAI recordings from 2026-08-03 show api.x.ai answering 200 OK to `max_completion_tokens` for grok-4.3 and grok-4.5 (9 cassettes; the only 400 was about `presencePenalty`), and xAI's OpenAPI marks `max_tokens` as deprecated in favour of `max_completion_tokens`. kept.title: The positive check in TestABudgetLargerThanTheAnswerLimitRaisesTheLimit matches the budget, not the answer limit
kept.summary: The test expects the answer limit to become 1024 and accepts any "max_tokens":1024. The reasoning object always carries {"max_tokens":1024}, so the check passes whatever happens to the answer limit, which is really 2048. The test cannot detect the raised limit being lost.
kept.failure_scenario: A regression that drops max_completion_tokens from the request (answer limit gone) still passes. The body {"reasoning":{"max_tokens":1024}} satisfies the first assertion, and the second assertion only rules out 512.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeBudgetLimitBody printed body {..."max_completion_tokens":2048,"reasoning":{"max_tokens":1024}}. I mutated raiseAnswerLimitForBudget through an overlay (`*limit = nil`), so the body became {..."reasoning":{"max_tokens":1024}} with no answer limit. With that mutation TestABudgetLargerThanTheAnswerLimitRaisesTheLimit still PASSED, while TestAnswerLimitClearsTheBudgetTheThinkingWillSpend FAILED.

repro.evidence: Probe TestProbeVF3 (HEAD) for the test's exact inputs (anthropic/claude-opus-4-5, WithModernReasoningFormat+WithUsingReasoningMaxTokens, WithReasoning(None,100), WithMaxTokens(512)) prints {..."max_completion_tokens":2048,"reasoning":{"max_tokens":1024}}: the answer limit is 2048, not 1024 as the test message claims, and the substring "max_tokens":1024 is matched by the reasoning object. Mutation via overlay of llms/openai/openaillm.go line 588 (`*limit = &raised` -> `*limit = nil` in raiseAnswerLimitForBudget) makes the body {..."reasoning":{"max_tokens":1024}} with no answer limit at all; with that mutation TestABudgetLargerThanTheAnswerLimitRaisesTheLimit still PASSES while TestAnswerLimitClearsTheBudgetTheThinkingWillSpend FAILS on all 5 subcases.
repro.comment: The positive assertion here accepts any `"max_tokens":1024`, but the `reasoning` object always carries `{"max_tokens":1024}` (the floored budget), so it passes regardless of what happens to the answer limit; the real answer limit on the wire is `max_completion_tokens:2048`, not the 1024 the message describes. I mutated `raiseAnswerLimitForBudget` through a Go overlay to drop the limit entirely (`*limit = nil`): the body became `{..."reasoning":{"max_tokens":1024}}` with no answer limit, and this test still passed while `TestAnswerLimitClearsTheBudgetTheThinkingWillSpend` failed. Suggest asserting on the answer-limit field explicitly (e.g. `"max_completion_tokens":2048`, or unmarshal the body and check `max_completion_tokens` > budget) and fixing the message.

refute.reason: I ran a probe on HEAD: sendModernReasoningBody('anthropic/claude-opus-4-5', None, 100, 512) produces {"max_completion_tokens":2048,"reasoning":{"max_tokens":1024}}. The test's positive assertion ("max_tokens":1024 or "max_completion_tokens":1024) passes only through the substring inside the reasoning object. The real answer limit is 2048, not the 1024 the failure message claims. So the test pins a wrong value and passes by accident, and dropping the answer limit would not fail it. The strongest mitigation is that the sibling test TestAnswerLimitClearsTheBudgetTheThinkingWillSpend does catch that regression, per the reviewer's mutation. That leaves no coverage gap, but this test remains incorrect and misleading. It was added in this PR (31dbf42).

Suggest asserting on the answer-limit field explicitly (e.g. `"max_completion_tokens":2048`, or unmarshal the body and check `max_completion_tokens` > budget) and fixing the message.

kept.title: The 'reasons anyway' silence test uses gpt-4o, a model that never reasons, and pins a silent loss
kept.summary: TestDelegatedDepthOnAModelThatReasonsAnywayIsSilent uses gpt-4o, which is not a reasoning model. It pins that WithAdaptiveReasoning on gpt-4o gives no warning. The same file pins a Drop warning for WithReasoning(High) on gpt-4o, and commit a459111 says the caller is told whenever the model will not reason at all.
kept.failure_scenario: gpt-4o or gpt-4.1 with WithAdaptiveReasoning(ReasoningNone): nothing reasoning-related goes on the wire and resp.Warnings is empty, so the caller is never told that thinking was lost. With WithReasoning(High) on the same model the caller does get a Drop warning. The case the name describes (a model that reasons by default) is already covered by TestAModelThatAlreadyReasonsIsNotReportedAsDropped with o3-mini, so this test only adds the silent-loss pin.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeDelegated (HEAD): gpt-4o adaptive-none gave warnings=[] and body without reasoning fields. gpt-4o effort-high gave [drop: WithReasoning asked high ... sent nothing on gpt-4o]. gpt-4.1 behaves the same. gpt-5.1 adaptive-none gives drop: WithAdaptiveReasoning. The same probe in BASE sent reasoning_effort:"high" for gpt-4o. Commit a459111: "Where that means the model will not reason at all ... the caller is told."

repro.evidence: Probe TestProbeVF3 (HEAD): gpt-4o WithAdaptiveReasoning(ReasoningNone) -> body {"model":"gpt-4o",...} with no reasoning field, warnings=[]; gpt-4o WithReasoning(High,0) -> same body, warnings=[drop: WithReasoning asked high ... sent nothing on gpt-4o (the door sends no effort field on this model)]; gpt-4.1 identical; gpt-5.1 adaptive-none -> drop: WithAdaptiveReasoning ("this model does not reason unless an effort asks it to"); o3-mini adaptive-none -> no warning (genuinely reasons by default). BASE: gpt-4o adaptive-none sent reasoning_effort:"high". Code: openaillm.go:453-472 setDeferredReasoning only calls reportDelegatedDepth for EffortToolsDisable, Claude adaptive, or reasoning.ThinkingOptIn(model); a non-reasoning model like gpt-4o hits none of these, so the delegated request is dropped silently. Commit a459111 (which added this test) states: "Where that means the model will not reason at all ... the caller is told." The case the test name describes (a model that reasons by default) is already covered with o3-mini by TestAModelThatAlreadyReasonsIsNotReportedAsDropped.
repro.comment: This test is named for a model that "reasons anyway", but it uses gpt-4o, which never reasons, so what it actually pins is a silent loss: `WithAdaptiveReasoning(ReasoningNone)` on gpt-4o (or gpt-4.1) sends no reasoning field and returns no warning, while `WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh, 0)` on the same model returns a `drop` warning, and gpt-5.1 with the same adaptive request also gets a `drop`. I confirmed this with a probe against an httptest server; commit a459111 says the caller is told whenever the model will not reason at all, which this contradicts. Suggest using a model that reasons by default (e.g. o3-mini, already covered elsewhere) for the silence case, and making `setDeferredReasoning` report a `WithAdaptiveReasoning` drop for models the door knows do not reason (the same condition that yields the `WithReasoning` drop).

refute.reason: I confirmed it with a probe on HEAD. gpt-4o/gpt-4.1 + WithAdaptiveReasoning(ReasoningNone) sends a body with no reasoning field and returns Warnings=[]. Commit a459111 states the principle 'Where that means the model will not reason at all ... the caller is told'. gpt-4o will not reason at all, yet the test named 'ReasonsAnyway' pins silence with the message 'nothing was lost'. Its premise, a model that reasons by default, is false for gpt-4o. The code's warning covers only reasoning.OpenAIThinkingOptIn models and the forced-disable-with-tools case, so non-reasoning models fall through silently. The best argument against it is that the commit lists only 'an opt-in generation, or one that demands an explicit disable' as examples, and delegated depth means 'the vendor default'. That does not explain why the test's own rationale is wrong, or why an explicit effort on the same model warns while an adaptive one does not. BASE sent reasoning_effort:"high" to gpt-4o, so the silent drop is new.

kept.title: Stale comment states the opposite of the renamed test's assertion
kept.summary: The comment above TestAdaptiveReasoningWithNoEffortSendsNoEffort still says adaptive with no effort "defaults to high" and "must not silently disable reasoning", but the test now asserts that no reasoning_effort is sent.
kept.failure_scenario: A maintainer who trusts the comment may 'fix' the test or the door back to sending high, which brings back the behaviour commit a459111 removed (the most expensive effort for a delegated request).
kept.evidence: HEAD lines 72-74: comment "...must not silently disable reasoning here: it defaults to high, matching the Anthropic/Bedrock paths." above a test that fails if body contains "reasoning_effort". Probe: reasoning-model + WithAdaptiveReasoning(None) sends no reasoning_effort, while WithReasoning(High) sends "high".

repro.evidence: At HEAD, lines 72-73 of llms/openai/reasoning_effort_passthrough_test.go still read "WithAdaptiveReasoning with no explicit effort must not silently disable reasoning here: it defaults to high, matching the Anthropic/Bedrock paths." The PR diff shows these two lines as unchanged context. The function below was renamed from TestAdaptiveReasoningNoEffortDefaultsToHighOnWire to TestAdaptiveReasoningWithNoEffortSendsNoEffort (line 74). Its assertion was flipped from requiring `"reasoning_effort":"high"` to failing if `"reasoning_effort"` appears at all. Commit a459111 ("let an adaptive request without an effort take the vendor default") explains the new intent: an adaptive request with no effort is treated as an unset mode, so no effort field is sent. I ran `go test -run TestAdaptiveReasoningWithNoEffortSendsNoEffort ./llms/openai/` at HEAD and it passes. So the comment directly contradicts both the code and the test. This affects only documentation. Runtime behaviour does not change.
repro.comment: The comment above this test is stale: it still says adaptive reasoning with no effort "defaults to high, matching the Anthropic/Bedrock paths". The renamed test now asserts the opposite, failing if any `reasoning_effort` is sent, which is the behaviour a459111 introduced (the vendor picks its default). The test passes at 355dc71, so the comment, not the assertion, is wrong. A maintainer who trusts the comment could restore `reasoning_effort: high` for delegated requests, bringing back the most expensive effort that a459111 removed. Suggest rewording it to something like: "WithAdaptiveReasoning with no explicit effort hands the depth decision to the model: no reasoning_effort is sent, so the vendor default applies."

kept.title: String think levels are refused by Ollama servers up to v0.17 for every model except gpt-oss
kept.summary: resolveThink sends a string level ("low"/"medium"/"high"/"max") to every model outside gpt-oss. Ollama servers v0.12 through v0.17 accept a string think value only for harmony (gpt-oss) models and answer HTTP 400 for thinking models such as qwen3 or deepseek-r1. Servers before v0.22 also reject "max" when they decode the request. The base door sent no think field, so these calls worked with thinking on by default. This is not the same as #1: #1 covers models that cannot think at all, while this one breaks models that can.
kept.failure_scenario: An Ollama v0.17 (or earlier 0.12+) server with WithModel("qwen3:8b") or "deepseek-r1:8b" and WithReasoning(llms.ReasoningHigh, 0), or WithAdaptiveReasoning(ReasoningLow). The request carries "think":"high" and the server answers 400 `think value "high" is not supported for this model`. On the base the same call succeeded with thinking on. With ReasoningMax on v0.18–v0.21 the request fails with 400 "invalid think value". Sending `true` for non-gpt-oss models, which every server version accepts for a thinking model, would keep the intent.
kept.evidence: Probe llms/ollama/zz_probe_mho_think_test.go uses a fake server that behaves like Ollama <=0.17 and returns 400 for a string think value on a non-gpt-oss model. HEAD printed: `model=qwen3:8b think="think":"high"} err=400 Bad Request: think value "high" is not supported for this model`, the same for deepseek-r1:8b, and `model=gpt-oss:20b ... err=<nil>`. BASE printed `think=<absent> err=<nil>` for all three. Vendor source from raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/<tag>/server/routes.go: v0.12.0, v0.12.6, v0.13.0, v0.14.0, v0.15.0 and v0.17.0 contain `if req.Think != nil && req.Think.IsString() && m.Config.Parser != "harmony" { 400 "think value %q is not supported for this model" }` (v0.12.0 uses `!useHarmony`). The check is gone in v0.18.0. In api/types.go, ThinkValue validation accepts "max" only from v0.22.0 (v0.20.0: `must be "high", "medium", "low", true, or false`). Commit 74419cd says "a level Ollama accepts (low, medium, high, max) travels as itself". The README states no minimum server version.

repro.evidence: HEAD llms/ollama/ollamallm.go:338-356 resolveThink: for any model not starting with gpt-oss it sends string(effort) whenever api.ThinkValue.IsValid() accepts it (vendored client v0.32.5 accepts high/medium/low/max). Probe probes/vrf_f1_think (internal test calling resolveThink) at HEAD printed think="low"/"high"/"max" for qwen3:8b and deepseek-r1:8b, and low/high/high for gpt-oss:20b. BASE llms/ollama has no reference to Think at all (grep), so the field was never sent. Vendor source fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama: v0.12.0 server/routes.go:304 and :1923 `if req.Think != nil && req.Think.IsString() && !useHarmony { 400 "think value %q is not supported for this model" }`; v0.17.0 routes.go:374 and :2237 same check with `m.Config.Parser != "harmony"`; v0.18.0 has no such check. api/types.go ThinkValue.UnmarshalJSON in v0.21.0 (line 1172) rejects any string except high/medium/low with `invalid think value`; "max" is accepted only from v0.22.0. Intent commit 74419cd: "a level Ollama accepts (low, medium, high, max) travels as itself"; README/doc state no minimum server version. Distinct from #1 (#1 = models that cannot think at all; this = thinking models on older servers).
repro.comment: `resolveThink` sends the effort as a string (`"think":"high"`) to every model except gpt-oss. Ollama servers v0.12 to v0.17 accept a string think only for harmony (gpt-oss) models. For any other model they return 400 `think value "high" is not supported for this model` (server/routes.go in v0.12.0 and v0.17.0; the check was removed in v0.18.0). Servers before v0.22 also reject `"max"` when decoding the request (api/types.go ThinkValue.UnmarshalJSON). So `WithModel("qwen3:8b")` or `"deepseek-r1:8b"` with `WithReasoning(llms.ReasoningHigh, 0)` now fails on those servers. On the base the same call worked with thinking on, because the field was never sent. A probe calling `resolveThink` shows `"high"`/`"max"` for qwen3:8b and deepseek-r1:8b. Suggested fix: send `true` for non-gpt-oss models, which every server version accepts for a thinking model. Alternatively, document a minimum Ollama version and map `max` to `high`/`true` for older servers. This depends on the Ollama server version the caller runs.

refute.reason: Checked against Ollama's source in the Go module cache. In v0.17.0, server/routes.go:374 and :2237 return 400 "think value %q is not supported for this model" when a string think value is sent to a model whose parser is not harmony. That check is gone in v0.18.0. In v0.21.0, ThinkValue.UnmarshalJSON accepts only high/medium/low, so "max" is refused; v0.32.5 accepts "max". But neither the README nor the code states a minimum server version, and older servers are common in deployments with pinned Docker images. That makes this a silent regression for existing callers. It is not a duplicate of #1: #1 is about models that cannot think, and gating think on model capability would not fix this one.

kept.title: Embeddings through a named inference provider go to an hf-inference-only path
kept.summary: createEmbedding builds {url}/{provider}/models/{model}/pipeline/{task} with body {inputs} for every provider and decodes a bare [][]float32. That route, body and response shape exist only on hf-inference. Other providers that serve feature extraction through the router (for example scaleway) expose {router}/{provider}/v1/embeddings, take {input, model} and return {data:[{embedding}]}. Commit 1aeb83b intends provider routing, and embeddings_wire_test.go pins the wrong scaleway path.
kept.failure_scenario: huggingface.New(WithInferenceProvider("scaleway")) followed by CreateEmbedding(ctx, texts, "Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B", "feature-extraction") POSTs to https://router.huggingface.co/scaleway/models/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B/pipeline/feature-extraction instead of /scaleway/v1/embeddings, so the call fails. The same happens with any chat provider set on the client, such as "groq", because the chat provider is reused for embeddings. This is not a regression: the base sent router/models/{model}, which also failed.
kept.evidence: Probe llms/huggingface/zz_probe_mho_hf_test.go printed on HEAD: `provider=scaleway urls=[... https://router.huggingface.co/scaleway/models/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B/pipeline/feature-extraction] bodies=[... {"inputs":["hi"]}]`. On BASE it printed `https://router.huggingface.co/models/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B`. In huggingface.js main, packages/inference/src/providers/scaleway.ts has ScalewayFeatureExtractionTask with makeRoute() "v1/embeddings", payload {input, model} and response.data.map(item=>item.embedding), and providerHelper.ts makeBaseUrl returns `${HF_ROUTER_URL}/${provider}`. Only hf-inference.ts builds `models/${model}/pipeline/${task}`. The test TestTheNamedInferenceProviderReplacesTheDefaultSegment asserts "/scaleway/models/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B/pipeline/feature-extraction". huggingface.co docs could not be fetched because of an egress block.

Probe probes/vrf_f23_hf at HEAD: New(WithInferenceProvider("scaleway")) + CreateEmbedding(..., "Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B", "feature-extraction") hit path /scaleway/models/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B/pipeline/feature-extraction with body {"inputs":["hi"]}. The PR test TestTheNamedInferenceProviderReplacesTheDefaultSegment (llms/huggingface/embeddings_wire_test.go) pins the scaleway path. huggingface.js main packages/inference/src: providerHelper.ts:110 makeBaseUrl = `${HF_ROUTER_URL}/${provider}`; scaleway.ts ScalewayFeatureExtractionTask makeRoute "v1/embeddings", payload {input, model}, response data[].embedding; together.ts "v1/embeddings"; deepinfra.ts "v1/openai/embeddings"; only hf-inference.ts:115-118 builds `models/${model}/pipeline/${task}`. A live router call was not possible (egress to router.huggingface.co blocked), so the router behaviour is inferred from the official client.

That route, body and response shape are hf-inference's. In the official huggingface.js client, scaleway and together use `{router}/{provider}/v1/embeddings` (deepinfra uses `v1/openai/embeddings`), with `{input, model}` in and `data[].embedding` out. kept.title: Provider-prefixed chat URL is wrong for groq, novita, fireworks-ai and hf-inference
kept.summary: chatCompletionsURL appends /v1/chat/completions after the provider segment for every provider. Several router providers use other routes (groq /openai/v1/chat/completions, novita /v3/openai/chat/completions, fireworks-ai /inference/v1/chat/completions, hf-inference models/{model}/v1/chat/completions), so WithInferenceProvider with those providers cannot reach chat. The HF router's own route, /v1/chat/completions with a "model:provider" suffix, would work for all of them. The PR rewrote this function and the WithInferenceProvider doc; the formula itself came over unchanged from base.

So `New(WithInferenceProvider("groq"), WithModel("meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct")).Call(ctx, "hi")` posts to `/groq/v1/chat/completions`, which I confirmed with an httptest probe. That path should not reach Groq's chat endpoint. The providers named in the doc (nebius, hyperbolic) use the default route and are fine. Not a regression: the base built the same URL. Suggested fix: use the router's own `{router}/v1/chat/completions` with `model: "<model>:<provider>"`, which works for every provider, or keep a per-provider route table. This depends on HF router routing, which I read from the official client and did not check with a live call.

kept.title: Embeddings put an extra /hf-inference segment on a caller URL that already names the provider
kept.summary: createEmbedding now always adds /{provider}/models/{model}/pipeline/{task} to the WithURL base, and the provider defaults to hf-inference. A caller whose URL already ends in the provider segment ends up with /hf-inference/hf-inference/... and a 404. That base, https://router.huggingface.co/hf-inference, is the one Hugging Face documents as the replacement for the retired api-inference host, and it is the only no-provider setting under which BASE embeddings worked.
kept.failure_scenario: huggingface.New(WithURL("https://router.huggingface.co/hf-inference")) used through embeddings/huggingface with the default model BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5. BASE sent POST .../hf-inference/models/BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 and got vectors. HEAD sends POST .../hf-inference/hf-inference/models/BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5/pipeline/feature-extraction and gets 404 'unable to create embeddings'. The same happens with any proxy base that already maps to one provider. Commit f40c2a9 set out to keep the caller's URL, so this breakage looks unintended.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/mho2-hf/probe_url_test.go ran against a mirror that serves /hf-inference/models/{model} and /hf-inference/models/{model}/pipeline/feature-extraction. HEAD printed: path=/hf-inference/hf-inference/models/BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5/pipeline/feature-extraction err=API returned unexpected status code: 404. BASE printed: path=/hf-inference/models/BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 err=<nil> n=1. HEAD embeddings.go:18-31 always inserts embeddingProvider(), which is hf-inference when no provider is set. The migration base router.huggingface.co/hf-inference/models/<model> is confirmed by web search (hdgarzon/tbt.cafe PR #119 and HF docs results); huggingface.co itself is blocked from the sandbox.

repro.evidence: HEAD llms/huggingface/internal/huggingfaceclient/embeddings.go:31 builds fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/models/%s/pipeline/%s", c.url, c.embeddingProvider(), model, task), and embeddingProvider() returns "hf-inference" when no provider is set (lines 16-23). BASE built "%s/models/%s". Probe probes/vrfx-mho2/emb_test.go goes through embeddings/huggingface.EmbedQuery against a mirror that serves /hf-inference/models/{m} and /hf-inference/models/{m}/pipeline/feature-extraction. HEAD with WithURL(<srv>/hf-inference): paths=[/hf-inference/hf-inference/models/BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5/pipeline/feature-extraction] err=404 'unable to create embeddings'. BASE with the same URL: paths=[/hf-inference/models/BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5] err=nil len=2. BASE with the bare base: 404. HEAD with the bare base works. So the one no-provider base that worked for BASE callers breaks at HEAD. On the vendor side, the retired host returns 410 with the text 'https://api-inference.huggingface.co is no longer supported. Please use https://router.huggingface.co/hf-inference instead.' (HF forum thread 169870, Flowise #5535, langchain4j #4146), so callers who followed HF's own migration instruction set exactly this base. f40c2a9's stated goal is to 'keep the caller's URL'. huggingface.co docs are blocked from the sandbox.

kept.title: Mistral and HuggingFace accept WithStructuredOutput, only warn, and return unvalidated output with a nil error
kept.summary: The mistral and huggingface doors meet a structured-output request with a drop warning. They never run ValidateStructuredOutput and never validate the answer, so text that breaks the schema comes back as a success. The WithStructuredOutput doc says the final response is validated against the original schema regardless. The other doors, including the ollama cloud path added in this PR, return ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported when they cannot honor a schema.
kept.failure_scenario: mistral.New(...).GenerateContent with WithStructuredOutput({capital: string, required, additionalProperties:false}) sends only response_format json_object. When the model answers {"city":"Paris"}, err is nil and content is {"city":"Paris"}. On huggingface the same call returns the prose 'Sure! Paris is the capital.' with err nil. A caller that unmarshals into its struct silently gets zero values. An invalid schema is also accepted without an error.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/mho2-mistral/probe_test.go TestProbeMistralStructuredOutput printed: err=<nil> content="{\"city\":\"Paris\"}" response_format=map[type:json_object] plus a warning 'drop: WithStructuredOutput ... sent nothing'. Probe probes/mho2-hf/probe_test.go TestProbeHFStructuredOutput printed: err=<nil> content="Sure! Paris is the capital.". llms/options.go:874-881 (doc of WithStructuredOutput). HF uses the same drop at llms/huggingface/warnings.go:51. Other doors refuse: ollamallm.go:430, anthropicllm.go:991, bedrockclient_util.go:109. Commit c3d0da7 chose a warning. BASE ignored the option silently, so this is not a regression.

repro.evidence: HEAD llms/mistral/warnings.go:34-40 and llms/huggingface/warnings.go:51-52 only add a WarningDrop for StructuredOutput. Neither door calls opts.ValidateStructuredOutput() or structuredoutput.Validate. The ollama, googleai, bedrock, anthropic and openai doors do both. Probe probes/vrfx-mho2/mistral_test.go gave these results. With a {capital} schema and a server reply of {"city":"Paris"}: err=<nil>, content="{\"city\":\"Paris\"}", response_format=map[type:json_object], plus the drop warning. With the invalid schema `[1,2]` the result is the same, err=<nil>. Probe hf_test.go: err=<nil> content="Sure! Paris is the capital." with the drop warning. llms/options.go WithStructuredOutput doc: 'the final response is validated against the original schema regardless'. This is not a regression: BASE ignored the option silently, and HEAD at least warns. It is still a contract inconsistency with every other door.
repro.comment: The mistral and huggingface doors answer `WithStructuredOutput` with a drop warning only. They never run `ValidateStructuredOutput` and never validate the answer, yet the option's doc promises that 'the final response is validated against the original schema regardless'. A probe with a `{capital}` schema (required, additionalProperties false) and a server reply of `{"city":"Paris"}` returned `err=nil` with that content; the wire carried only `response_format: {type: json_object}`. Even a non-object schema such as `[1,2]` was accepted. On huggingface the prose reply 'Sure! Paris is the capital.' came back with `err=nil`. A caller that unmarshals into its struct silently gets zero values. BASE ignored the option silently, so this is not a regression, but the other doors (openai, anthropic, bedrock, googleai, ollama) either refuse with `ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported` or validate the answer locally. Consider doing the same here: return `ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported`, or keep json_object and run `structuredoutput.Validate` on the final choice.

refute.reason: This is deliberate and pinned. Commit c3d0da7 explicitly chose to report the lost schema as a WarningDrop in ContentResponse.Warnings, and llms/mistral/warnings_test.go (WithStructuredOutput -> WarningDrop, Asked 'answer') pins it; the HF door does the same through reportHuggingFaceShapedOptions. Warnings are the library's documented way to report options a door does not honor. ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported is documented (structured_output.go:42-45) for vendor/model paths KNOWN not to accept schemas, not for doors that lack the field. BASE ignored the option completely without any signal, so this PR only improves on a preexisting gap. It could be a feature request (fail or validate locally), but it is not a release defect.

kept.judge_reason: Confirmed by reading HEAD. mistral/warnings.go:34-40 and huggingface/warnings.go:51-52 only add a WarningDrop for WithStructuredOutput. Neither door calls opts.ValidateStructuredOutput() or structuredoutput validation. Mistral sends only response_format json_object (mistralmodel.go:136-137), and HF sends nothing. Both verifiers' probes agree that a schema-violating answer (Mistral {"city":"Paris"}, HF prose) and even an invalid schema come back with err == nil. The WithStructuredOutput doc (options.go, unchanged from BASE) says "the final response is validated against the original schema regardless". The same PR's Ollama Cloud path handles this case differently: it drops JSON mode with a warning but returns ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported for a schema (ollamallm.go:429-434). So the PR's own policy treats a schema that cannot be honored as an error, not a warning. This is not a regression: BASE ignored the option silently, and HEAD at least warns. The choice was also deliberate (c3d0da7, pinned by warnings_test.go). For those reasons it stays low severity as a contract inconsistency on newly added lines, not a release blocker. The skeptic's reading of ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported as "only for documented vendor gaps" does not hold here: a door that has no schema field is a known, documented gap.
kept.comment: This isn't a regression, since the base release ignored the option silently. But the `WithStructuredOutput` doc promises that "the final response is validated against the original schema regardless", and this door only records a `WarningDrop`. It never calls `ValidateStructuredOutput` and never validates the answer. With a `{capital: string, required}` schema, Mistral receives only `response_format: json_object`. If it answers `{"city":"Paris"}`, `GenerateContent` returns that content with `err == nil`. An invalid schema is accepted the same way. The HuggingFace door (`huggingface/warnings.go:51`) does the same and returns plain prose with a nil error. A caller that unmarshals into its struct silently gets zero values unless it inspects `Warnings`. The Ollama Cloud path added in this PR returns `ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported` for exactly this case (no schema on the wire), so the doors now disagree. Consider either returning `ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported`, or, on Mistral, which does send JSON mode, validating the final content locally the way `WithCloudStructuredOutputFallback` does.

kept.title: Token-budget warning says nothing was sent while a level derived from the budget is on the wire
kept.summary: When the caller gives a thinking budget and no effort, the ollama door sends think:"low"/"medium"/"high" derived from that budget, and the huggingface door sends the derived reasoning_effort. Both doors still report a WarningDrop with an empty Sent. The Warning contract says an empty Sent means nothing reached the wire.
kept.failure_scenario: WithMaxTokens(4096) + WithReasoning("", 800) on ollama model glm-5 puts think:"low" on the wire. The warning reads 'drop: WithReasoning asked 800, WithReasoning sent nothing'. The huggingface door does the same with reasoning_effort:"low" and 'asked 800 tokens ... sent nothing'. A caller or log that trusts the warning thinks thinking was not requested at all.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/mho2-ollama/probe_test.go TestProbeTokenBudgetWarning printed: wire think: "low" and warning: drop: WithReasoning asked 800, WithReasoning sent nothing on glm-5. Probe probes/mho2-hf/probe_test.go TestProbeHFBudgetWarning printed: wire reasoning_effort: "low" and warning: drop: WithReasoning asked 800 tokens, WithReasoning sent nothing. llms/warning.go:19-20 documents the empty-Sent meaning. Same pattern in llms/huggingface/warnings.go:24-26. The fitting kind would be WarningSubstitute with Sent set to the derived level.

repro.evidence: HEAD llms/ollama/warnings.go:74-80 adds a WarningDrop with empty Sent whenever cfg.HasExplicitTokens(). resolveThink (ollamallm.go:338-355) still sends a level derived from GetEffort(maxTokens). llms/warning.go:20: 'an empty Sent means nothing reached the wire'. Probe probes/vrfx-mho2/ollama_test.go with WithMaxTokens(4096)+WithReasoning("",800): glm-5, qwen3 and gpt-oss:20b all put think="low" on the wire, and each reported 'drop: WithReasoning asked 800, WithReasoning sent nothing ... | kind=drop sent=""'. Probe hf_test.go: wire reasoning_effort="low" with warning 'drop: WithReasoning asked 800 tokens, WithReasoning sent nothing on Qwen/Qwen3-32B (the door builds no field for it)'. The HF drop comes from llms/huggingface/warnings.go:24-26.
repro.comment: When the caller gives a thinking budget without an effort, this warning says the reasoning request went nowhere, yet a level derived from the budget is on the wire. With `WithMaxTokens(4096)` + `WithReasoning("", 800)` a probe shows `"think":"low"` in the request for glm-5, qwen3 and gpt-oss:20b. The only warning is `drop: WithReasoning asked 800, WithReasoning sent nothing`, with `Sent==""`, which per `llms.Warning` means nothing reached the wire. The huggingface door does the same (`llms/huggingface/warnings.go:24-26`): `reasoning_effort:"low"` is sent, and the warning says 'asked 800 tokens … sent nothing (the door builds no field for it)'. Suggested fix: report a `WarningSubstitute` with `Sent` set to the derived level (for example `Asked: "800 tokens", Sent: "low"`), so logs and callers that read the warning see what actually went out.

refute.reason: Confirmed in code. With Effort empty and Tokens>0, ollama resolveThink (ollamallm.go:346-352) sends the level GetEffort(maxTokens) derives from the budget, and huggingface reasoningEffort (huggingfacellm.go) sends the same derived effort. Yet ollama warnings.go:74-80 and huggingface warnings.go:24-26 add a WarningDrop with empty Sent, which warning.go:19-20 defines as 'nothing reached the wire', and String() renders 'WithReasoning sent nothing'. The existing tests (TestAThinkingTokenBudgetHasNowhereToGoOnOllama, TestAThinkingTokenBudgetHasNoFieldOnThisDoor) cover only an explicit effort plus a budget, where the budget really is dropped. The budget-only case is not pinned on purpose and breaks the documented Sent contract. The impact is low (diagnostics only), but it is a real inaccuracy. BASE had no warnings and no think/effort on these doors.

kept.comment: When the caller gives a thinking budget without an effort, this warning says the reasoning request went nowhere, yet a level derived from the budget is on the wire. With `WithMaxTokens(4096)` + `WithReasoning("", 800)` a probe shows `"think":"low"` in the request for glm-5, qwen3 and gpt-oss:20b. The only warning is `drop: WithReasoning asked 800, WithReasoning sent nothing`, with `Sent==""`, which per `llms.Warning` means nothing reached the wire. The huggingface door does the same (`llms/huggingface/warnings.go:24-26`): `reasoning_effort:"low"` is sent, and the warning says 'asked 800 tokens … sent nothing (the door builds no field for it)'. Suggested fix: report a `WarningSubstitute` with `Sent` set to the derived level (for example `Asked: "800 tokens", Sent: "low"`), so logs and callers that read the warning see what actually went out.

kept.title: Cloud cassette tests skip whenever there is no ~/.ollama/id_ed25519, although any throwaway key replays them
kept.summary: newCloudTestClient now skips unless the developer's real Ollama signing key exists, and CI has none. So every cloud cassette test never runs there, including the only recorded tests of the new WithCloudStructuredOutputFallback and the updated TestCloudJSONMode. The skip message says the recordings cannot be replayed without the key, but a freshly generated key replays all of them.
kept.failure_scenario: In CI or on any machine without the ollama CLI key, go test ./llms/ollama skips TestCloudGenerateContent, TestCloudStreaming, TestCloudToolCall, TestCloudJSONMode, TestCloudStructuredOutputFallback/{non-streaming,streaming} and TestCloudWithOptions. A regression in the cloud fallback or the JSON-mode drop warning would pass unnoticed. A test-generated key under a t.TempDir HOME would let them always replay.
kept.evidence: Default HOME: go test -run TestCloud -v ./llms/ollama showed all cassette subtests as SKIP. I generated an ed25519 key with ssh.MarshalPrivateKey (probe probes/mho2-ollama/keygen_test.go) and ran with HOME=<probe>/home: all of TestCloudGenerateContent, TestCloudStreaming, TestCloudToolCall, TestCloudJSONMode, TestCloudStructuredOutputFallback/non-streaming and /streaming, and TestCloudWithOptions PASS. Only the key file's presence matters, because ollama api/client.go:184-196 signs with it and removeTimestampTransport strips ts.

repro.evidence: HEAD newCloudTestClient (llms/ollama/ollama_cloud_test.go:46-53, added by 22e878f) skips when ~/.ollama/id_ed25519 is missing. The ollama api client (ollama@v0.32.5 api/client.go stream()) signs ollama.com requests with auth.Sign, which only reads that key file. The Authorization header is scrubbed by rr.ScrubReq and removeTimestampTransport drops ts, so the signature never reaches cassette matching. Probe probes/ultra-vrf-mho3/keygen_test.go generated a fresh ed25519 key with ssh.MarshalPrivateKey into probes/ultra-vrf-mho3/home/.ollama/id_ed25519. With the default HOME (no key), `go test -run TestCloud -v ./llms/ollama` shows TestCloudGenerateContent, TestCloudStreaming, TestCloudToolCall, TestCloudJSONMode, TestCloudStructuredOutputFallback/{non-streaming,streaming} and TestCloudWithOptions/* as SKIP. With HOME=<probe>/home (GOCACHE/GOMODCACHE pinned), all of them PASS against the committed cassettes. .github/workflows has no Ollama key setup, so CI always skips them. At BASE these tests failed hard without the key, as the 22e878f message says; the PR turned that failure into a skip instead of making the tests replay.
repro.comment: This skip hides all cloud cassette tests on any machine without the developer's real `~/.ollama/id_ed25519`, and CI has none. That includes the only recorded coverage of the new `WithCloudStructuredOutputFallback` and the new JSON-mode drop-warning assertions in `TestCloudJSONMode`. The skip message says the recordings cannot be replayed without the key, but any throwaway key works: the signature only goes into the `Authorization` header, which `ScrubReq` removes, and `removeTimestampTransport` strips `ts`. I generated a fresh ed25519 key with `ssh.MarshalPrivateKey` into a temp HOME. With that, TestCloudGenerateContent, Streaming, ToolCall, JSONMode, StructuredOutputFallback/{non-streaming,streaming} and WithOptions all PASS in replay mode; with the default HOME they all SKIP. Suggested fix: in replay mode, generate a throwaway key under `t.TempDir()` and `t.Setenv("HOME", ...)` (also `USERPROFILE` on Windows) instead of skipping. Keep the requirement for the real key only when recording.

refute.reason: The skip is deliberate. Commit 22e878f added it because without any ~/.ollama/id_ed25519 the TestCloud* tests failed hard instead of skipping. But the commit's premise is wrong: the tests need some key file, not the developer's key. ollama api/client.go signs the ollama.com requests, the test scrubs Authorization, and removeTimestampTransport strips ts, so the signature never reaches cassette matching. I checked this myself. With the default HOME (no key), go test -count=1 -run TestCloud ./llms/ollama skipped TestCloudGenerateContent, Streaming, ToolCall, JSONMode, StructuredOutputFallback/{non-streaming,streaming} and WithOptions/*. With HOME pointing at a directory holding a throwaway ed25519 key, all of them PASS. CI (ci.yaml runs go test ./...) has no key, so the only recorded tests of the new cloud structured-output fallback never run. The BASE behaved differently: it did not skip, it failed loudly.

With that, TestCloudGenerateContent, Streaming, ToolCall, JSONMode, StructuredOutputFallback/{non-streaming,streaming} and WithOptions all PASS in replay mode; with the default HOME they all SKIP.
