kept.title: HuggingFace extra-body warning blames a vendor SDK the door does not use
kept.summary: The huggingface door copied extraBodyUnread from the SDK-bound doors, so its WithExtraBody warning says the request is built through a vendor SDK with nowhere to merge the fields. In fact this door marshals its own chatCompletionsPayload and could merge them.
kept.failure_scenario: WithExtraBody({"enable_thinking":false}) on the huggingface door gives a warning whose Reason says 'the door builds its request through a vendor SDK and has nowhere to merge them'. That is false: huggingfaceclient/inference.go builds the JSON body itself.
kept.evidence: llms/huggingface/warnings.go:74 against llms/huggingface/internal/huggingfaceclient/inference.go:18-27 and 51-57 (a plain struct marshalled with encoding/json, no SDK). The same constant is accurate for mistral (mistral-go SDK) and ollama (ollama api client).

repro.evidence: llms/huggingface/warnings.go:74 copies the constant used by the SDK-bound doors: "the door builds its request through a vendor SDK and has nowhere to merge them". The huggingface door imports no vendor SDK. llms/huggingface/internal/huggingfaceclient/inference.go:18-27 defines its own chatCompletionsPayload, and runChatCompletions marshals it with encoding/json (lines 51-57). Probe probes/ultra-vrf-mho3/hf/probe_test.go called GenerateContent with WithExtraBody({"enable_thinking":false}) on Qwen/Qwen3-8B. It printed body `{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-8B","messages":[...],"stream":false}` and the warning `drop: WithExtraBody asked enable_thinking, WithExtraBody sent nothing on Qwen/Qwen3-8B (the door builds its request through a vendor SDK and has nowhere to merge them)`. BASE had no warning and did not forward ExtraBody either. The drop itself is not a regression; only the stated reason is wrong.
repro.comment: This `extraBodyUnread` reason was copied from the SDK-bound doors (mistral, ollama, bedrock, anthropic, googleai), but it is wrong for this door. HuggingFace builds its own `chatCompletionsPayload` in `internal/huggingfaceclient/inference.go` and marshals it with `encoding/json`; no vendor SDK is involved. A probe calling `GenerateContent(..., llms.WithExtraBody(map[string]any{"enable_thinking": false}))` returns a WarningDrop whose Reason says the door "builds its request through a vendor SDK and has nowhere to merge them", which misleads callers about why the field was dropped. Either merge `ExtraBody` into the marshalled payload, the way the openai door does (the door owns the JSON, so this is easy), or change the reason to something accurate such as "the door does not forward extra body fields".

refute.reason: The huggingface door builds its request itself. huggingfaceclient/inference.go marshals a plain chatCompletionsPayload with encoding/json and sends it with http.NewRequestWithContext; no vendor SDK is involved. Commit e1be9fd copied the SDK-door constant into this door without changing it. The drop and the warning are correct, and the test pins only Kind and Asked. But the user-visible Reason, 'the door builds its request through a vendor SDK and has nowhere to merge them', is false here, and the door could merge the fields. This is a low-severity wording and accuracy defect, and it is new: BASE gave no warning at all.

kept.comment: This `extraBodyUnread` reason was copied from the SDK-bound doors (mistral, ollama, bedrock, anthropic, googleai), but it is wrong for this door. HuggingFace builds its own `chatCompletionsPayload` in `internal/huggingfaceclient/inference.go` and marshals it with `encoding/json`; no vendor SDK is involved. A probe calling `GenerateContent(..., llms.WithExtraBody(map[string]any{"enable_thinking": false}))` returns a WarningDrop whose Reason says the door "builds its request through a vendor SDK and has nowhere to merge them", which misleads callers about why the field was dropped. Either merge `ExtraBody` into the marshalled payload, the way the openai door does (the door owns the JSON, so this is easy), or change the reason to something accurate such as "the door does not forward extra body fields".

kept.title: Structured output refused on Converse for application inference profile and provisioned-model ARNs
kept.summary: applyConverseStructuredOutput treats every model id that lacks the substring "anthropic.claude" as a non-Claude model and refuses it unless the id is on the exact-match model-card allowlist. An opaque ARN (application-inference-profile/<id>, provisioned-model/<id>, imported/custom model) can never match, so structured output is refused before the request even when the ARN points at a supported Claude model.
kept.failure_scenario: bedrock.New(WithConverseAPI(), WithModel("arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:123456789012:application-inference-profile/a1b2c3d4e5f6")). This is an application inference profile over Claude Sonnet 4.5, which enterprises use for cost allocation. Calling GenerateContent(..., WithStructuredOutput(schema)) on HEAD returns ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported ("the model's Amazon Bedrock model card does not list structured outputs") and nothing is sent. BASE sent outputConfig.textFormat, and the call worked. Provisioned-throughput ARNs fail the same way.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/bedrock-arn-so/probe_test.go (package bedrockclient, fake BedrockRuntimeClientInterface, CreateCompletionConverse with StructuredOutput). HEAD: application-inference-profile ARN -> err="structured output: unsupported on bedrock ... model card does not list structured outputs" outputConfigSent=false; provisioned-model ARN -> same. The inference-profile ARN that embeds us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5 -> err=nil outputConfigSent=true. BASE: all ids -> err=nil outputConfigSent=true. Cause: isAnthropicModelID is a substring check, and reasoning.BedrockSupportsStructuredOutput is slices.Contains over bedrockStructuredOutputModels after bedrockModelWithoutRegion (bedrock_capability.go:52-128). Commits 82ad622 and 200f1a6 introduced the allowlist deliberately but never mention ARNs whose model cannot be read from the id.

repro.evidence: Probe probes/vbr-f123/probe_test.go TestProbeVbrF1 (public bedrock API, httptest endpoint, WithConverseAPI + WithModelProvider("anthropic") + WithStructuredOutput with a closed schema). HEAD: application-inference-profile ARN and provisioned-model ARN -> err "failed to build converse input: structured output: unsupported on bedrock for model arn:...: the model's Amazon Bedrock model card does not list structured outputs", requests=0. us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5 -> err=nil, outputConfig.textFormat sent. BASE: all three ids -> err=nil, one request, outputConfig.textFormat sent. Cause: applyConverseStructuredOutput (bedrockclient_util.go:108-121) uses isAnthropicModelID (strings.Contains "anthropic.claude") and, for everything else, reasoning.BedrockSupportsStructuredOutput = slices.Contains over an exact-name allowlist after bedrockModelWithoutRegion. An opaque ARN matches neither; WithModelProvider("anthropic") does not help, and there is no ARN handling anywhere in llms/bedrock or llms/reasoning (grep for "arn:"/"application-inference-profile" finds nothing outside tests).
repro.comment: Regression: the new structured-output gate on Converse can't handle model ids that are opaque ARNs. `isAnthropicModelID` is a substring check, and `BedrockSupportsStructuredOutput` is an exact-name allowlist, so an application-inference-profile ARN (`arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:123456789012:application-inference-profile/a1b2c3d4e5f6`) or a provisioned-model ARN is always treated as a non-listed model. `GenerateContent(..., WithStructuredOutput(schema))` then returns `ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported` ("model card does not list structured outputs") without sending anything, even when the ARN points at Claude Sonnet 4.5 and even with `WithModelProvider("anthropic")`. I checked this with a probe that uses the public `bedrock.New` + `WithConverseAPI` against an httptest endpoint. HEAD refuses both ARNs with 0 requests, while BASE sent `outputConfig.textFormat` for them and the call went through. Suggested fix: when the model id is an ARN whose underlying model can't be read from it, skip the local refusal and let Bedrock decide, or honour the configured provider or an explicit override.

refute.reason: applyConverseStructuredOutput (bedrockclient_util.go:108-121) sorts models with the substring check isAnthropicModelID and the exact-match list reasoning.BedrockSupportsStructuredOutput (slices.Contains after the region prefix is stripped). HEAD has no code that handles ARNs: grep finds no 'arn:', 'inference-profile' or 'provisioned' anywhere in llms/bedrock or llms/reasoning. So an opaque application-inference-profile or provisioned-model ARN always fails the check and gets ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported before any request is sent. ARNs are a supported input: the library has WithModelProvider for model ids that do not name their provider. Even so, ConverseInput carries only ModelID, and no option lets the caller get past the refusal. Commit 200f1a6 aimed to refuse Nova, Llama and similar models whose cards lack structured output. It never considers ARNs, so this is a side effect, not an intended choice. BASE's Converse door sent outputConfig for any model, so this is a regression.

kept.title: Converse now forwards a forced tool choice (any/named) to model families Bedrock rejects it for
kept.summary: converseToolChoice maps WithToolChoice("required"/"any"/named) to ToolChoiceMemberAny or ToolChoiceMemberTool for every model. The base door always sent auto. Bedrock documents the specific-tool choice only for Claude and Nova, and it rejects toolChoice.any on Meta Llama and tool/any on Claude Opus 5.5 (which the tables classify as Opus 5). Callers that set a forced choice on these families used to get a working call and now get a vendor 400.
kept.failure_scenario: WithConverseAPI + WithModel("us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0") + WithTools(...) + WithToolChoice("required"): HEAD sends toolConfig.toolChoice={"any":{}}, and Bedrock answers ValidationException "This model doesn't support the toolConfig.toolChoice.any field". BASE sent {"auto":{}} and the call succeeded. The same happens with a named choice ({"tool":{"name":...}}) on Llama, gpt-oss, DeepSeek or Qwen, and with any/tool on us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 ("tool_choice: type \"tool\" and \"any\" are not supported for this model"). No local guard or fallback to auto exists; only the Claude budget-thinking guard does.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/bedrock-pub/probe_test.go TestProbeToolChoiceConverse (httptest server, public bedrock API). HEAD: llama4-maverick/gpt-oss-120b/deepseek.v3.2 with "required" -> toolChoiceOnWire={"any":{}}; with a named ToolChoice -> {"tool":{"name":"get_weather"}}. BASE: {"auto":{}} in every case (base convertToolsToToolConfig hardcoded ToolChoiceMemberAuto). The AWS SDK doc comment (bedrockruntime@v1.50.4 types.go:2767) says ToolChoiceMemberTool is "Only supported by Anthropic Claude 3 and Amazon Nova models". pydantic/pydantic-ai#2802 reports Llama 4 Maverick rejecting toolChoice.any. vercel/ai#21364 reports Opus 5.5 on Bedrock rejecting tool/any. Commit 1eee249 made the choice travel on purpose but did not gate it by family.

repro.evidence: Probe TestProbeVbrF2 (public API, WithConverseAPI + WithTools + WithToolChoice). HEAD: us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0 and openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0 with "required" -> toolConfig.toolChoice={"any":{}}; with ToolChoice{Function:{Name:"get_weather"}} -> {"tool":{"name":"get_weather"}}. BASE: {"auto":{}} for every model and choice. converseToolChoice (bedrockclient_converse.go:774-783, added by 1eee249) maps ToolChoiceNamed/Any for every model with no family gate. Vendor side: the AWS SDK doc comment on types.ToolChoiceMemberTool (bedrockruntime types.go:2767) says "Only supported by Anthropic Claude 3 and Amazon Nova models". Third-party reports of Bedrock returning "This model doesn't support the toolConfig.toolChoice.any field" for Llama 4 and other non-Claude models: pydantic/pydantic-ai#2091 and #2802. For Opus 5.5 on Bedrock rejecting forced toolChoice: 567-labs/instructor#2681. No live call was possible (no keys), so the rejection of 'any' on Llama rests on these reports; the SDK doc covers 'tool'.
repro.comment: Regression: `converseToolChoice` now sends the caller's forced choice (`any` for "required", `tool` for a named function) to every model family. The previous release always sent `auto`. Bedrock accepts these fields only on some families. The SDK doc for `ToolChoiceMemberTool` says "Only supported by Anthropic Claude 3 and Amazon Nova models", and users report `ValidationException: This model doesn't support the toolConfig.toolChoice.any field` on Llama 4 and similar models (pydantic/pydantic-ai#2091, #2802), plus forced toolChoice rejected on Opus 5.5 (567-labs/instructor#2681). I ran a probe through the public `bedrock.New` + `WithConverseAPI` with `WithToolChoice("required")` and a named choice. HEAD puts `{"any":{}}` and `{"tool":{"name":"get_weather"}}` on the wire for us.meta.llama4-maverick and openai.gpt-oss-120b, while BASE sent `{"auto":{}}`. So callers that set a choice on these families get a vendor 400 where the call used to work (the 400 itself depends on vendor behaviour; I couldn't make a live call). Suggested fix: gate `any`/`tool` by family (Claude except the models that reject it, and Nova), and fall back to `auto` with a warning elsewhere.

refute.reason: Commit 1eee249 deliberately made converseToolChoice send any or tool whenever the caller forces a choice, and tool_choice_wire_test.go checks this only on amazon.nova-lite. The code applies no family gate: it maps ToolChoiceNamed to ToolChoiceMemberTool and ToolChoiceAny to ToolChoiceMemberAny for every model. The AWS SDK doc comment in bedrockruntime types.go:2767 says ToolChoiceMemberTool is 'Only supported by Anthropic Claude 3 and Amazon Nova models'. So a named choice on Llama, gpt-oss, DeepSeek or Qwen now draws a vendor ValidationException, where BASE (which always sent auto) got a working call. The best argument against the finding is that BASE silently ignored the caller's choice and a vendor 400 is more honest. But the library usually drops an unsupported parameter locally with a warning (for example RejectsPenalties), and here there is neither a guard nor a fallback. I did not verify the Opus 5.5 part; the Llama and named-choice case stands without it.

kept.title: Legacy Nova door turns an adaptive request with no effort into top effort and drops the caller's maxTokens/temperature/topP
kept.summary: novaInputToJSON derives the effort from GetEffort, which returns high for adaptive with no effort. The legacy door therefore sends maxReasoningEffort=high and clears maxTokens, temperature and topP. The Converse door treats the same request as a delegation (DelegatesDepth) and sends reasoningConfig {type:enabled} with the caller's limits intact. Commit bd34934 calls exactly this Converse behaviour a defect, and the legacy door was not updated.
kept.failure_scenario: bedrock.New(WithModel("us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0")) on the default legacy door, then GenerateContent(..., WithAdaptiveReasoning(ReasoningNone), WithMaxTokens(500), WithTemperature(0.3)). The InvokeModel body is {"inferenceConfig":{"reasoningConfig":{"type":"enabled","maxReasoningEffort":"high"}}}, so the answer limit and temperature are gone and the most expensive effort is used. The same call through WithConverseAPI keeps maxTokens=500 and temperature=0.3 and sends no effort.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/bedrock-pub/probe_test.go TestProbeNovaDelegation on HEAD. Legacy body: {"messages":[...],"inferenceConfig":{"reasoningConfig":{"type":"enabled","maxReasoningEffort":"high"}}}. Converse body: {"additionalModelRequestFields":{"reasoningConfig":{"type":"enabled"}},"inferenceConfig":{"maxTokens":500,"temperature":0.3},...}. Converse checks input.ReasoningConfig.DelegatesDepth() in setNova (bedrockclient_converse.go:228). provider_nova.go:179-186 has no such check. The commit message of bd34934 says the delegation fix should stop Nova from getting top effort, which also cleared maxTokens, temperature and topP.

repro.evidence: Probe TestProbeVbrF3: WithModel("us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0") + WithAdaptiveReasoning(ReasoningNone) + WithMaxTokens(500) + WithTemperature(0.3) + WithTopP(0.9). HEAD legacy body: {"messages":[...],"inferenceConfig":{"reasoningConfig":{"type":"enabled","maxReasoningEffort":"high"}}}, so maxTokens, temperature and topP are gone. HEAD Converse body: additionalModelRequestFields.reasoningConfig={"type":"enabled"}, inferenceConfig {maxTokens:500, temperature:0.3, topP:0.9}. BASE legacy: no reasoningConfig, maxTokens 500 and topP 0.9 kept. Code: provider_nova.go:179-186 calls options.Reasoning.GetEffort, which returns ReasoningHigh for adaptive with no effort (llms/options.go GetEffort), and then NovaClearsInferenceConfigAt(high) zeroes the three fields. setNova on Converse (bedrockclient_converse.go:227-233) checks DelegatesDepth first. Commit bd34934 fixed exactly this on Converse ("Bedrock Converse gave Nova ... the top effort, which on Nova also cleared maxTokens, temperature and topP") but did not touch provider_nova.go. The Nova 2 docs (docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/nova2-userguide/extended-thinking.html) say temperature/topP/maxTokens must be unset with maxReasoningEffort=high, so the clearing is forced once 'high' is chosen, and choosing 'high' is the defect.
repro.comment: The legacy Nova door still turns a delegated adaptive request (`WithAdaptiveReasoning(ReasoningNone)`) into the top effort. `GetEffort` returns `high` for adaptive with no effort, so `novaInputToJSON` sends `maxReasoningEffort:"high"`, and `NovaClearsInferenceConfigAt(high)` then drops the caller's `maxTokens`, `temperature` and `topP`. I ran a probe with us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0, adaptive/no effort, `WithMaxTokens(500)`, `WithTemperature(0.3)` and `WithTopP(0.9)`. The InvokeModel body is `{"inferenceConfig":{"reasoningConfig":{"type":"enabled","maxReasoningEffort":"high"}}}`, while the same call via `WithConverseAPI` sends `reasoningConfig:{type:enabled}` and keeps 500/0.3/0.9. BASE kept the caller's limits on this door. Commit bd34934 fixed exactly this on Converse (`setNova` checks `DelegatesDepth()`), but the legacy door was not updated. Suggested fix: add the same `DelegatesDepth()` branch here, sending `{type:"enabled"}` with no effort and leaving inferenceConfig untouched.

refute.reason: In novaInputToJSON (provider_nova.go:179-186), the only condition is ResolveMode()==ReasoningOn. It calls GetEffort, which returns ReasoningHigh for an adaptive request with no effort (options.go:150-151). There is no DelegatesDepth check, so the legacy door sends maxReasoningEffort=high, and NovaClearsInferenceConfigAt then zeroes maxTokens, temperature and topP. In the same situation, setNova on the Converse door (bedrockclient_converse.go:228) returns {type:enabled} and keeps the caller's limits. Commit bd34934 explicitly calls the Converse version of this behaviour a defect ('gave Nova ... the top effort, which on Nova also cleared maxTokens, temperature and topP') but did not touch provider_nova.go. No test pins the legacy behaviour for adaptive with no effort. reportNovaReasoning does emit drop warnings, but that does not make the behaviour intended. BASE's legacy Nova door sent no reasoning at all, so this is new behaviour in the PR, not a preexisting one.

I ran a probe with us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0, adaptive/no effort, `WithMaxTokens(500)`, `WithTemperature(0.3)` and `WithTopP(0.9)`. The InvokeModel body is `{"inferenceConfig":{"reasoningConfig":{"type":"enabled","maxReasoningEffort":"high"}}}`, while the same call via `WithConverseAPI` sends `reasoningConfig:{type:enabled}` and keeps 500/0.3/0.9. BASE kept the caller's limits on this door. Commit bd34934 fixed exactly this on Converse (`setNova` checks `DelegatesDepth()`), but the legacy door was not updated. Suggested fix: add the same `DelegatesDepth()` branch here, sending `{type:"enabled"}` with no effort and leaving inferenceConfig untouched.

kept.title: Converse drops top_p=0.95 under budget thinking because the floor is compared after a float32 round trip
kept.summary: keepTopP passes float64(*inferenceConfig.TopP) to ClaudeKeepsTopPWhileThinking. That value is the float32 already written to the config, so 0.95 becomes 0.949999988 and falls below ClaudeThinkingTopPFloor (0.95). Top_p is then removed and temperature 1 is sent. The legacy door compares the float64 and keeps top_p.
kept.failure_scenario: WithConverseAPI + Claude Sonnet 4.5 + WithReasoning("", 1024) + WithTopP(0.95) (no temperature): the Converse request carries temperature=1 and no top_p, and a WithTopP drop warning is emitted. The legacy door sends top_p=0.95. Anthropic accepts top_p in [0.95, 1] while thinking, so the caller's valid value is lost on one door only.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/bedrock-topp/probe_test.go (buildConverseInput and applyAnthropicReasoning on HEAD). converse asked=0.95 -> sent top_p=<nil> temperature=1. legacy asked=0.95 -> sent top_p=0.95. asked=0.96/0.97 -> both doors keep top_p. The existing TestLegacyThinkingKeepsTopPAboveTheFloor has an "exactly at the floor" case; the Converse twin TestConverseThinkingKeepsTopPAboveTheFloor omits it.

repro.evidence: HEAD bedrockclient_converse.go:145 stores inferenceConfig.TopP = aws.Float32(float32(*input.TopP)); line 216-217 then calls reasoning.ClaudeKeepsTopPWhileThinking(input.ModelID, float64(*inferenceConfig.TopP)). float32(0.95) widened back to float64 is 0.949999988079071, which is < ClaudeThinkingTopPFloor (0.95, claude_capability.go:393), so keepTopP is false, temperature=1 is set and TopP is nil'ed. The legacy door (provider_anthropic.go:869) passes the float64 input.TopP and keeps it. Ran the probe probes/bedrock-topp/probe_test.go via overlay at HEAD (env -u AWS_CA_BUNDLE go test -run '^TestProbe' ./llms/bedrock/internal/bedrockclient/): 'converse topP asked=0.95 -> sent top_p=<nil> temperature=1' vs 'legacy asked=0.95 -> sent top_p=0.95 temperature=0'; 0.96/0.97 are kept by both doors. BASE Converse always dropped top_p under budget thinking (base lines 171-172), so this is not a regression against the previous release but an off-by-rounding bug in the new keep-top_p feature that makes the two Bedrock doors disagree exactly at the documented floor.
repro.comment: The top_p floor check here runs on the float32 already written into `inferenceConfig`, so `WithTopP(0.95)` becomes 0.949999988 after `float64(float32(0.95))` and falls below `ClaudeThinkingTopPFloor` (0.95). The result: with WithConverseAPI, a Claude Sonnet 4.5 model, `WithReasoning("", 1024)` and `WithTopP(0.95)` and no temperature, the Converse request drops top_p, sends temperature=1 and warns that WithTopP was dropped. The legacy InvokeModel door compares the float64 and sends top_p=0.95. I ran a probe on `buildConverseInput` and `applyAnthropicReasoning`: at 0.95, Converse sends top_p=nil and temperature=1, while legacy sends top_p=0.95; at 0.96 and 0.97 both doors keep it. Fix: compare `*input.TopP` (the caller's float64) instead of the round-tripped float32, and add the "exactly at the floor" case to `TestConverseThinkingKeepsTopPAboveTheFloor` as its legacy twin already has.

refute.reason: Confirmed by reading the code. At bedrockclient_converse.go:145, top_p is stored as aws.Float32(float32(0.95)), which is 0.949999988. Line 217 then widens it back to float64 and compares it with ClaudeThinkingTopPFloor = 0.95 using >=, so the check fails: top_p is dropped and temperature=1 is sent. The legacy door (provider_anthropic.go:869) compares the float64 input.TopP and keeps 0.95. I found no reason to dismiss this. Commit 8918070 says a top_p 'at or above the floor' should survive, and Anthropic's documented limit is '>= 0.95'. The legacy test pins the exactly-at-floor case; the Converse twin TestConverseThinkingKeepsTopPAboveTheFloor tests only 0.97 and 0.5, so the gap is untested rather than intended. Fix: compare *input.TopP (float64) instead, or use a small epsilon. Preexisting in effect: the BASE Converse door (lines 171-172) always set temperature=1 and dropped top_p under budget thinking, so a 0.95 request gave the same wire output there. This is not a regression for callers; it is a boundary bug in the new keep-top_p feature, which leaves the two doors inconsistent.

kept.comment: The top_p floor check here runs on the float32 already written into `inferenceConfig`, so `WithTopP(0.95)` becomes 0.949999988 after `float64(float32(0.95))` and falls below `ClaudeThinkingTopPFloor` (0.95). The result: with WithConverseAPI, a Claude Sonnet 4.5 model, `WithReasoning("", 1024)` and `WithTopP(0.95)` and no temperature, the Converse request drops top_p, sends temperature=1 and warns that WithTopP was dropped. The legacy InvokeModel door compares the float64 and sends top_p=0.95. I ran a probe on `buildConverseInput` and `applyAnthropicReasoning`: at 0.95, Converse sends top_p=nil and temperature=1, while legacy sends top_p=0.95; at 0.96 and 0.97 both doors keep it. Fix: compare `*input.TopP` (the caller's float64) instead of the round-tripped float32, and add the "exactly at the floor" case to `TestConverseThinkingKeepsTopPAboveTheFloor` as its legacy twin already has.

kept.title: Legacy Claude door sends tool_choice even when the request has no tools
kept.summary: createAnthropicCompletion always sets ToolChoice from anthropicToolChoiceOnWire(options.ToolChoice). The empty tools slice is dropped by omitempty, so a call with WithToolChoice(...) and no WithTools sends a bare tool_choice, which the Anthropic Messages API rejects. The base door never sent tool_choice, and the Converse door guards the same case with len(input.Tools) > 0.
kept.failure_scenario: bedrock.New(WithModel("anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0")) on the default InvokeModel door, then GenerateContent(hi, llms.WithToolChoice("none")) with no tools. A caller might do this to keep a summarising turn tool-free, or might set tool choice globally. The body now carries "tool_choice":{"type":"none"} with no "tools" key. Anthropic answers 400 ("tool_choice may only be specified while providing tools"), so a call that worked on the previous release now fails. "auto" and "required" produce the same bare field.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeLegacyToolChoiceWithoutTools (bedrock_test overlay, httptest server capturing the InvokeModel body; model anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0; WithToolChoice only, no tools). HEAD sent {"anthropic_version":...,"messages":[...],"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}}, and likewise {"type":"auto"} and {"type":"any"}, with no tools key. BASE sent the same body without tool_choice. Code: provider_anthropic.go:234-241 builds tools as an empty slice (Tools has omitempty); line 260 sets ToolChoice unconditionally. Converse: bedrockclient_converse.go:177 builds a ToolConfig only when len(input.Tools) > 0. Vendor behaviour: anthropics/claude-cookbooks#142 says the API raises an error for tool_choice {"type":"none"} with empty tools, and anthropic-sdk-python#849 describes the same constraint. The platform.claude.com API reference does not state it, and docs.aws.amazon.com is blocked here, so this could not be checked against a live call.

repro.evidence: Code: createAnthropicCompletion builds `tools` from options.Tools (empty slice, dropped by `json:"tools,omitempty"`) and sets `ToolChoice: anthropicToolChoiceOnWire(options.ToolChoice)` without any guard; the ToolChoice field (`json:"tool_choice,omitempty"`) is new in this PR, and the base struct has no tool_choice. The Converse door guards it (bedrockclient_converse.go:176-177: `if len(input.Tools) > 0 && (...)`). Probe TestProbeV3LegacyToolChoice (self-contained bedrock_test overlay, httptest InvokeModel endpoint, model anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0, llms.WithToolChoice only, no tools). HEAD bodies: {..."messages":[...],"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}}, {..."tool_choice":{"type":"auto"}}, {..."tool_choice":{"type":"any"}} (for "required"), none with a tools key. BASE, same probe: {"anthropic_version":"bedrock-2023-05-31","max_tokens":16384,"messages":[...]} with no tool_choice for all three. Vendor side only partly confirmed: anthropics/claude-cookbooks#142 reports that the API errors for tool_choice {"type":"none"} with empty tools. Neither the Anthropic nor the AWS docs I could reach state the rule, and there was no live call.
repro.comment: The legacy InvokeModel Claude door now always sends `tool_choice` (line 260), but `tools` is dropped by `omitempty` when the call has no tools. So `GenerateContent(..., llms.WithToolChoice("none"))` with no `WithTools`, for example from a global option or a summarising turn, sends `"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}` and no `tools` key. I ran an httptest probe against `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0`. HEAD sends the bare field for none, auto and required (`{"type":"any"}`), and the previous release sent no `tool_choice` at all. Whether this fails depends on the vendor: anthropics/claude-cookbooks#142 reports that the Messages API rejects `tool_choice` when no tools are given, but I could not check it with a live call. Suggest setting `ToolChoice` only when `len(tools) > 0`, the way the Converse door already guards it in bedrockclient_converse.go:177.

refute.reason: Commit 6dcf0e0 added ToolChoice to the legacy InvokeModel payload (provider_anthropic.go:260). It sets the field without checking len(options.Tools), and nothing upstream clears it: bedrockllm.go:163 passes opts.ToolChoice straight through. Tools is []anthropicTool with omitempty, so the empty slice disappears from the JSON and tool_choice goes out alone. The Converse door in the same PR guards this case with len(input.Tools) > 0 (bedrockclient_converse.go:177), so the legacy door is the one out of line. kept.title: Converse streamed-usage fixture sends a totalTokens the vendor never sends, and the test pins it
kept.summary: The fixture sends inputTokens 13, outputTokens 304, cacheRead 3602, cacheWrite 300 but totalTokens 3919 instead of 4219. The test then asserts TotalTokens=3919 next to PromptTokens=3915 and CompletionTokens=304. That pins a total below prompt+completion, which contradicts Bedrock's usage semantics and the repo's own checks.
kept.failure_scenario: The test locks in an impossible usage object. Changing the Converse door to report a self-consistent TotalTokens (as the legacy door does, and as requireUsageAddsUp demands) would fail this test. A door that drops cache writes from TotalTokens would pass it. For the same four counters, legacy_stream_usage_test expects TotalTokens=4219 while this test expects 3919.
kept.evidence: 3915+304 = 4219, not 3919. The repo's real recording testdata/TestAmazonAutomaticCachingConverseAPI.httprr has `cacheWriteInputTokens:1365, inputTokens:3, outputTokens:55, totalTokens:1423` (3+55+1365 = 1423) and `1365 read + 77 write + 6 + 27 = 1475 total`, so the vendor's totalTokens counts all cache tokens. Also, bedrockllm_test.go requireUsageAddsUp fails when PromptTokens+CompletionTokens != TotalTokens, and legacy_stream_usage_test.go:51 asserts 4219 for identical counters. AWS prompt-caching docs (via search): totalTokens is the sum of inputTokens, cacheRead, cacheWrite and outputTokens.

repro.evidence: The fixture sends inputTokens 13, outputTokens 304, cacheRead 3602, cacheWrite 300 and totalTokens 3919 (= 13+304+3602, leaving out the cache write). The test asserts TotalTokens=3919 next to PromptTokens=3915 and CompletionTokens=304, and 3915+304 = 4219. applyConverseUsage (bedrockclient_converse.go:992) passes the vendor totalTokens through unchanged, so the test only asserts what the fixture fed in. Real vendor data disagrees with the fixture. The repo's recording llms/bedrock/testdata/TestAmazonAutomaticCachingConverseAPI.httprr has totalTokens 1423 = 3+55+1365(write), 1475 = 6+27+1365(read)+77(write) and 1539 = 3+56+1442+38, so Bedrock's totalTokens counts both cache reads and writes. The AWS docs (TokenUsage, prompt caching) say total input = inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens. requireUsageAddsUp in bedrockllm_test.go:3260 fails when PromptTokens+CompletionTokens != TotalTokens. legacy_stream_usage_test.go:51 expects 4219 for the same four counters, although commit d9ff7dc says both doors should report 'one set of token counters'. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_TokenUsage.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html
repro.comment: This fixture sends `totalTokens: 3919` for inputTokens 13, outputTokens 304, cacheRead 3602 and cacheWrite 300, so it leaves out the cache write. Line 49 then pins `TotalTokens == 3919` next to `PromptTokens == 3915` and `CompletionTokens == 304`, a total that is 300 short of prompt+completion. Bedrock does not send this: the repo's own recording `testdata/TestAmazonAutomaticCachingConverseAPI.httprr` has totalTokens 1423 = 3+55+1365 (write) and 1475 = 6+27+1365 (read)+77 (write), and AWS documents total input as inputTokens + cacheRead + cacheWrite. The same counters give 4219 in `legacy_stream_usage_test.go:51`, and `requireUsageAddsUp` would reject this object. As written, the test locks in an impossible usage object and would fail a change that makes the Converse door self-consistent. Suggest setting the fixture's `totalTokens` to 4219 and asserting 4219, so both doors are held to the same numbers.

refute.reason: The Converse door copies the vendor's usage.TotalTokens as-is (bedrockclient_converse.go, commits 4ebf6ba/d9ff7dc). The test therefore checks pass-through, which is intended. However, the fixture value 3919 equals 13+304+3602, i.e. cache writes left out, and Bedrock never sends such a value. The repo's own recording TestAmazonAutomaticCachingConverseAPI.httprr has totalTokens 1423 = 3+55+1365 (cache write included) and 1475 = 6+27+1365 read+77 write. So the fixture cannot tell correct pass-through (which would report 4219 on real data) from a door that computes input+output+cacheRead. It also pins PromptTokens(3915)+CompletionTokens(304) != TotalTokens(3919). That contradicts requireUsageAddsUp in bedrockllm_test.go:3260 and the 4219 that legacy_stream_usage_test.go:51 expects for the same counters. Runtime behaviour is fine; the defect is an unrealistic fixture that weakens the test and would fail a legitimate change. The test is new in this PR.

Line 49 then pins `TotalTokens == 3919` next to `PromptTokens == 3915` and `CompletionTokens == 304`, a total that is 300 short of prompt+completion. Bedrock does not send this: the repo's own recording `testdata/TestAmazonAutomaticCachingConverseAPI.httprr` has totalTokens 1423 = 3+55+1365 (write) and 1475 = 6+27+1365 (read)+77 (write), and AWS documents total input as inputTokens + cacheRead + cacheWrite. The same counters give 4219 in `legacy_stream_usage_test.go:51`, and `requireUsageAddsUp` would reject this object. As written, the test locks in an impossible usage object and would fail a change that makes the Converse door self-consistent. Suggest setting the fixture's `totalTokens` to 4219 and asserting 4219, so both doors are held to the same numbers.

kept.title: Credentials plus an API key on the Gemini API backend now make New fail
kept.summary: New now reads WithCredentialsFile/WithCredentialsJSON and sets them on genai.ClientConfig for every backend. On the Gemini API backend the door also sets APIKey, from WithAPIKey or from GOOGLE_API_KEY, and genai.NewClient refuses Credentials and APIKey together as mutually exclusive. A client that worked on BASE now fails at construction.
kept.failure_scenario: Two cases fail. (1) googleai.New(ctx, WithAPIKey("k"), WithCredentialsJSON(sa)), with no cloud project. (2) GOOGLE_API_KEY is set in the environment and the call is googleai.New(ctx, WithCredentialsFile(path)), for example an app whose one options builder always passes the service-account file used for Vertex. BASE ignored the credentials and authenticated with the key. HEAD returns "credentials and API key are mutually exclusive in the client initializer" and no client is built. Credentials only make sense on the Vertex branch, so detectCredentials should run only when Backend is VertexAI.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/gai-rev1/probe_test.go, run through the overlay in both checkouts. HEAD: TestProbeCredsPlusExplicitKey printed `err=credentials and API key are mutually exclusive in the client initializer...`. TestProbeCredsPlusEnvKey (GOOGLE_API_KEY=envkey plus WithCredentialsJSON) printed the same error from New. BASE: both returned err=<nil>, and the env-key request went out with x-goog-api-key=envkey. Source: genai@v1.42.0 client.go NewClient, `if cc.Credentials != nil && cc.APIKey != "" { return nil, fmt.Errorf("credentials and API key are mutually exclusive...") }`. Commit 5471dd9 meant the credentials for the Vertex backend. credentials_test.go covers only the Vertex case.

repro.evidence: HEAD new.go:67-70 calls detectCredentials() and sets config.Credentials for every backend, after the Gemini-API branch has already put APIKey into the config (from WithAPIKey, or from os.Getenv("GOOGLE_API_KEY") at new.go:57-59; EnsureAuthPresent skips the env key when credentials options are present, but the else-branch reads it anyway). genai@v1.42.0 client.go NewClient then returns `credentials and API key are mutually exclusive in the client initializer` before anything else. Probe probes/v3gai/probe_test.go, run through the overlay in both checkouts. HEAD: TestProbeCredsExplicitKey (WithAPIKey("k") + WithCredentialsJSON) and TestProbeCredsEnvKey (GOOGLE_API_KEY=envkey + WithCredentialsFile) both printed err=credentials and API key are mutually exclusive... (Backend:1 = GeminiAPI). BASE: both err=<nil>, and the requests went to https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent with key=k and key=envkey. The Vertex path works at HEAD, and credentials_test.go covers only that path.
repro.comment: `New` now calls `detectCredentials()` and sets `config.Credentials` on every backend. The previous release ignored the credentials and authenticated with the key. I reproduced both cases with an overlay probe: HEAD returns that error from `New`, and BASE sends the request with `x-goog-api-key` set to the explicit or env key. Suggested fix: run `detectCredentials` and set `config.Credentials` only when `config.Backend == genai.BackendVertexAI`. Also add a Gemini-API test next to the Vertex one in `credentials_test.go`.

Commit 34fd5d0 (PAGI-237) says WithCredentialsFile/WithCredentialsJSON were 'accepted and dropped' by the Gemini API client and must be 'refused before the request instead of being ignored'. It added TestNewRefusesTheOptionsThisDoorCannotCarry, which pins New(WithAPIKey("test-key"), WithCredentialsFile(...)) returning an error. That is the finding's case (1). kept.title: WithEndpoint in gRPC host:port form now breaks every request
kept.summary: WithEndpoint now becomes genai HTTPOptions.BaseURL, which must be a full URL. A host:port endpoint, the form the old gRPC SDKs took, parses as a URL scheme, so every request goes to a URL with no path and fails. BASE worked with that form: googleai ignored the option, and vertex handed it to the vertexai gRPC client.
kept.failure_scenario: googleai.New(ctx, WithAPIKey(k), WithEndpoint("generativelanguage.googleapis.com:443")) then GenerateContent returns `Post "generativelanguage.googleapis.com:443": unsupported protocol scheme "generativelanguage.googleapis.com"`. vertex.New(..., WithEndpoint("us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443")), such as a regional or Private Service Connect endpoint, which BASE sent over gRPC, now posts to "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443" with the model path lost. BASE googleai sent the same call to https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent.
kept.evidence: HEAD probe TestProbeEndpointDefaultTransport (probes/gai-rev1/ep) printed `err=doRequest: error sending request: Post "generativelanguage.googleapis.com:443": unsupported protocol scheme "generativelanguage.googleapis.com"`. HEAD probe TestProbeEndpointHostPort captured the URL `generativelanguage.googleapis.com:443`, while BASE captured `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent`. HEAD vertex probe: `Post "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443"`. In BASE, vertexai@v0.12.0/genai/client.go NewClient uses the gRPC endpoint format `%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443`, and caller options override it. genai api_client.go createAPIURL does url.Parse(BaseURL) followed by JoinPath. Commit 34fd5d0 honors the endpoint on purpose but does not mention the host:port form.

repro.evidence: HEAD new.go:72-74 copies WithEndpoint (option.go:122-126, opts.BaseURL = endpoint) into genai HTTPOptions.BaseURL with no normalisation. genai builds request URLs by url.Parse(BaseURL) followed by JoinPath, so a host:port value parses with the host as the URL scheme and the request path is lost. Probe probes/v3gai TestProbeEndpointHostPort with a capturing RoundTripper. HEAD: WithEndpoint("generativelanguage.googleapis.com:443") posted to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com:443` (no scheme, no /v1beta/models/...:generateContent); a full https URL worked. BASE: both forms posted to https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent, because BASE googleai ignored the option. Vertex probe probes/v3gai-vx at HEAD: vertex.New(..., WithEndpoint("us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443")) then GenerateContent gave `Post "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443"` (model path lost). BASE vertex handed the option to cloud.google.com/go/vertexai v0.12.0 genai.NewClient (gRPC), where host:port is the expected form. So this is a real regression for vertex regional or PSC endpoints. On googleai it turns a formerly ignored option into a broken client.
repro.comment: `WithEndpoint` now becomes genai `HTTPOptions.BaseURL` unchanged, but that field must be a full URL. A `host:port` endpoint, the form the old gRPC SDKs took (`cloud.google.com/go/vertexai` in the previous release), parses as a URL scheme, and every request goes to a URL with no path. An overlay probe shows it: at HEAD, `googleai.New(ctx, WithAPIKey(k), WithEndpoint("generativelanguage.googleapis.com:443"))` posts to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com:443`. `vertex.New(..., WithEndpoint("us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443"))` fails with `Post "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443"`. In BASE, googleai sent the call to `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent`, and vertex used this regional or PSC endpoint over gRPC, so existing Vertex callers break. Suggested fix: when the endpoint has no scheme, turn `host[:443]` into `https://host/`, or return a typed error from `New`. Also document that `WithEndpoint` now expects a base URL.

refute.reason: Confirmed in the code. Its message promised the option 'keep[s] working for vertex.New', and 4f6589c later broke that by moving vertex onto genai. Nothing normalizes or rejects the host:port form, so a caller that worked on BASE now fails at request time.

An overlay probe shows it: at HEAD, `googleai.New(ctx, WithAPIKey(k), WithEndpoint("generativelanguage.googleapis.com:443"))` posts to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com:443`. `vertex.New(..., WithEndpoint("us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443"))` fails with `Post "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443"`. In BASE, googleai sent the call to `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent`, and vertex used this regional or PSC endpoint over gRPC, so existing Vertex callers break. kept.title: Thinking config dropped for gemini-pro-latest and other thinking names the table misses
kept.summary: The new GeminiSupportsThinking gate recognizes only gemini-2.5, gemini-3, gemma-4 and three unversioned aliases. For gemini-pro-latest, a live Gemini API alias of the current Pro thinking model, the door sends no thinking config (no budget or level, no includeThoughts), whereas BASE did. It also records a warning saying the model does not think.
kept.failure_scenario: WithModel("gemini-pro-latest") + WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh, 0) sent BASE thinkingConfig {includeThoughts:true, thinkingBudget:1365}. HEAD sends no thinkingConfig, so the caller gets no reasoning text and loses control of the depth, and resp.Warnings says "this model does not think". Vertex tuned-model endpoints (projects/.../endpoints/N) are cut off the same way. gemini-flash-latest still works because geminiUnversionedThinking lists it, but the list has no pro-latest entry.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeProLatestThinking in both checkouts. HEAD: `gemini-pro-latest WithReasoning(high): thinkingConfig=<none>`, while gemini-2.5-pro and gemini-flash-latest both got `"thinkingConfig":{"includeThoughts":true,"thinkingBudget":8192}`. BASE: gemini-pro-latest got `"thinkingConfig":{"includeThoughts":true,"thinkingBudget":1365}`. The root is llms/reasoning/gemini_capability.go geminiUnversionedThinking, which lists only gemini-flash-latest, gemini-flash-lite-latest and gemini-robotics-er. The alias exists: gemini-cli issue #20588 asks for "gemini-pro-latest" alias support. The gate came in with commit fe7ff17, whose target was the non-thinking 2.0 and Gemma 3 families.

repro.evidence: HEAD googleai.go:1143 returns no thinking config when !reasoning.GeminiSupportsThinking(model). gemini_capability.go:35-60 accepts only the gemini-2.5, gemini-3 and gemma-4 families plus the prefixes gemini-flash-latest, gemini-flash-lite-latest and gemini-robotics-er, so gemini-pro-latest is classified non-thinking. Probe probes/v3gai TestProbeProLatest with WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0). HEAD: gemini-pro-latest thinkingConfig=<none>, and the response carries the warning 'this model does not think'. gemini-flash-latest and gemini-2.5-pro got {"includeThoughts":true,"thinkingBudget":8192}. BASE: gemini-pro-latest got {"includeThoughts":true,"thinkingBudget":1365}. Vendor side: gemini-pro-latest is a live Gemini API alias for the newest Pro model; per Google's changelog and third-party summaries it was switched to Gemini 3.1 Pro on 2026-03-06, a thinking model (see also gemini-cli issue #20588). Because that model thinks by default, HEAD still pays for thinking but loses includeThoughts (no reasoning text) and control of the depth.
repro.comment: The new `GeminiSupportsThinking` gate treats `gemini-pro-latest` as non-thinking. `geminiUnversionedThinking` in `llms/reasoning/gemini_capability.go` lists only `gemini-flash-latest`, `gemini-flash-lite-latest` and `gemini-robotics-er`. So `WithModel("gemini-pro-latest") + WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh, 0)` now sends no `thinkingConfig` and adds the warning "this model does not think". The previous release sent `{"includeThoughts":true,"thinkingBudget":1365}`, and at HEAD `gemini-2.5-pro` and `gemini-flash-latest` get `{"includeThoughts":true,"thinkingBudget":8192}` (overlay probe in both checkouts). According to Google's Gemini API docs and changelog, the alias currently points to Gemini 3.1 Pro, a thinking model. That model still thinks by default, so the caller pays for the thinking but gets no thought text and cannot set the depth. Suggested fix: add `gemini-pro-latest` to `geminiUnversionedThinking`, and route the `-latest` aliases to the Gemini 3 level control. Also consider falling back to the previous behaviour for unknown `gemini-*` names instead of treating them as non-thinking.

kept.title: vertex.New now refuses a missing location that BASE inferred
kept.summary: When no location is given, vertex.New only checks GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION and otherwise returns ErrMissingCloudTarget. BASE fell back to GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION, then CLOUD_ML_REGION, then us-central1, and the genai SDK itself also reads GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION and defaults to global.
kept.failure_scenario: vertex.New(ctx, googleai.WithCloudProject("my-proj"), googleai.WithCredentialsJSON(sa)) with GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION=europe-west4 and no GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION. BASE returned a working client. HEAD returns "vertex: a cloud project and a cloud location are both required". The same happens for callers who relied on the us-central1 default.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeVertexNoLocation (probes/gai-rev1/vx). HEAD: `client=false err=vertex: a cloud project and a cloud location are both required`. BASE: `client=true err=<nil>`. BASE source: vertexai@v0.12.0/genai/client.go inferLocation tries GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION, then CLOUD_ML_REGION, then defaultLocation. Commit 4f6589c mentions only options and GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT/GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION.

repro.evidence: HEAD vertex.go:42-50 fills a missing location only from GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION and otherwise returns ErrMissingCloudTarget. BASE vertex/new.go passed the empty location to cloud.google.com/go/vertexai@v0.12.0 genai.NewClient, whose inferLocation (client.go:106-118) falls back to GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION, then CLOUD_ML_REGION, then "us-central1". My probe (probes/vfy-vtx3/f1, internal test that reads the genai client's location through reflect) called New(ctx, WithCloudProject("my-proj"), WithCredentialsJSON(authorized_user)) with GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION unset. HEAD printed `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION="europe-west4" client=false err=vertex: a cloud project and a cloud location are both required` and gave the same error with no region set. BASE printed `client=true location="europe-west4" err=<nil>`, and with no region set `client=true location="us-central1" err=<nil>`. The new SDK would also have handled this: google.golang.org/genai@v1.42.0 client.go:225-266 reads GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION and then GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION, and sets Location="global" when both are empty, but vertex.New returns before the SDK is reached. The message of commit 4f6589c mentions only GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT/GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION and does not flag this as a deliberate break.
repro.comment: Regression: when no location is given, `vertex.New` now fills it only from `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` and otherwise returns `ErrMissingCloudTarget`. The previous release inferred the location through the vertexai SDK: `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION`, then `CLOUD_ML_REGION`, then `us-central1`. I ran a probe calling `vertex.New(ctx, googleai.WithCloudProject("my-proj"), googleai.WithCredentialsJSON(sa))` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION=europe-west4` set. The base returned a client bound to europe-west4, and with no region env set it returned one bound to us-central1. HEAD returns `vertex: a cloud project and a cloud location are both required` in both cases. The genai SDK itself would read `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION` and fall back to `global`, so a fix could keep the old fallback chain (`GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION`, `CLOUD_ML_REGION`, a default location) or require only the project and let genai resolve the location; if the break is intended, it should at least be in the release notes.

refute.reason: The refusal is deliberate, documented and fails loudly at construction. It does not break anything silently. Commit 4f6589c says vertex.New takes project and location from options or GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT/GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION and otherwise returns a typed error. llms/googleai/README.md says the package 'refuses to start without them'. TestVertexRefusesToGuessWhereItIs (vertex_test.go:54) pins ErrMissingCloudTarget on purpose, so that the client does not fall back to the us-central1 default or silently to the Gemini API backend. BASE did infer the location: vertexai@v0.12.0 inferLocation reads GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION, then CLOUD_ML_REGION, then us-central1. So the change breaks those callers on purpose; it is not a defect. The only gap worth considering: genai itself accepts GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION, and the wrapper's check runs before genai sees it. Honouring that variable too would be a cheap improvement, not a fix.

kept.judge_reason: Partly real, partly deliberate. Dropping the us-central1 default is intended: the README says the package "refuses to start without them", and TestVertexRefusesToGuessWhereItIs pins that behaviour. It is also needed, because googleai.New (new.go:46) only picks the Vertex backend when both project and location are set, and would otherwise fall back to the Gemini API. Dropping GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION does not look intended. BASE accepted it: vertexai@v0.12.0 inferLocation reads GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION, then CLOUD_ML_REGION, then us-central1. The SDK this PR moves to, google.golang.org/genai v1.42.0, documents it as equal to GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION (client.go:100 and :183, "GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION or GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION: Required") and reads it at :227. The wrapper only checks GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION, so it rejects a setup the SDK accepts, before the SDK is ever called. Two verifier probes confirm that HEAD returns ErrMissingCloudTarget when GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION=europe-west4, while BASE built a client for europe-west4. Severity is low because the error comes at construction with a clear message; nothing fails silently.
kept.comment: `vertex.New` fills a missing location only from `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`, so a deployment that sets `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION` now fails at startup with `ErrMissingCloudTarget`. The previous release accepted that variable: `cloud.google.com/go/vertexai` `inferLocation` read `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION`, then `CLOUD_ML_REGION`. The GenAI SDK this PR moves to treats it the same as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` (genai v1.42.0 client.go:100/:227: "GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION or GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION"), but this check returns before the SDK sees it. Repro: `vertex.New(ctx, googleai.WithCloudProject("p"), googleai.WithCredentialsJSON(sa))` with `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION=europe-west4` and no `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`. The base returns a client for europe-west4; HEAD returns "a cloud project and a cloud location are both required". Suggest falling back to `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION` (and possibly `CLOUD_ML_REGION`) after `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`, and adding the dropped `us-central1` default to the release notes as an intentional breaking change.

kept.title: vertex package drops exported error vars and constants, so callers no longer compile
kept.summary: The rewrite removed exported identifiers from the vertex package: ErrNoContentInResponse, ErrUnknownPartInResponse and ErrInvalidMimeType, and the constants CITATIONS, SAFETY, RoleSystem, RoleModel, RoleUser, RoleTool and ResponseMIMETypeJson. Callers that reference them stop compiling. This goes against the commit's stated aim of keeping callers compiling, which is why WithRest was kept as a no-op.
kept.failure_scenario: Code such as `errors.Is(err, vertex.ErrNoContentInResponse)` or `resp.Choices[0].GenerationInfo[vertex.SAFETY]` fails to build against the release. The googleai package has equivalents that could have been aliased, for example `var ErrNoContentInResponse = googleai.ErrNoContentInResponse` and `const SAFETY = googleai.SAFETY`.
kept.evidence: `go doc -all ./llms/googleai/vertex` diffed between BASE and HEAD. The const block and the var block with the three errors are gone. Call, GenerateContent, CreateEmbedding and CallbacksHandler survive only through promotion from the embedded *googleai.GoogleAI. Commit 4f6589c says WithRest "stays as an accepted no-op so callers keep compiling".

repro.evidence: `go doc -short` on BASE lists `const CITATIONS = "citations" ...` and `var ErrNoContentInResponse = ...`. On HEAD the only package-level identifier left is `var ErrMissingCloudTarget`. My compile probe (probes/vfy-vtx3/f2, external test package) uses vertex.ErrNoContentInResponse, ErrUnknownPartInResponse, ErrInvalidMimeType, CITATIONS, SAFETY, RoleSystem, RoleModel, RoleUser, RoleTool and ResponseMIMETypeJson. On BASE it builds and prints `PROBE true unknown part type ... citations safety system model user tool application/json`. On HEAD the build fails with `undefined: vertex.ErrNoContentInResponse`, `undefined: vertex.CITATIONS`, `undefined: vertex.SAFETY`, and so on. HEAD googleai still exports CITATIONS... and ErrNoContentInResponse, so aliases are possible. The message of commit 4f6589c says WithRest was kept "so callers keep compiling", so the removal does not fit its stated aim.
repro.comment: API break: the rewrite drops the exported identifiers of package `vertex`: `ErrNoContentInResponse`, `ErrUnknownPartInResponse`, `ErrInvalidMimeType` and the constants `CITATIONS`, `SAFETY`, `RoleSystem`, `RoleModel`, `RoleUser`, `RoleTool`, `ResponseMIMETypeJson`. Callers that use them, for example `errors.Is(err, vertex.ErrNoContentInResponse)` or `GenerationInfo[vertex.SAFETY]`, no longer compile. I checked this with a probe test that references all ten identifiers. kept.title: toolConfig sent even when the call has no tools
kept.summary: googleToolConfig now carries WithToolChoice to the wire whether or not any tools were passed. The request then has a functionCallingConfig and no functionDeclarations. BASE ignored ToolChoice entirely, and the Bedrock Converse door only builds a tool config when len(Tools) > 0.
kept.failure_scenario: An agent loop that always sets WithToolChoice("auto") or ("none") and sometimes passes no tools. HEAD sends `"toolConfig":{"functionCallingConfig":{"mode":"AUTO"}}` with no tools field. If Gemini rejects a function calling config without function declarations, that call becomes a 400 where BASE succeeded.
kept.evidence: Probe TestProbeToolChoiceNoTools. HEAD: `hasToolConfig=true hasTools=false`, body `"toolConfig":{"functionCallingConfig":{"mode":"AUTO"}}`. BASE: `hasToolConfig=false`. In llms/bedrock/internal/bedrockclient/bedrockclient_converse.go:177 the tool config is built only when `len(input.Tools) > 0`. The vendor behaviour is not confirmed: ai.google.dev is blocked from this sandbox. A web search for the error text "Function calling config is set without function_declarations" returned matches but could not be verified.

repro.evidence: HEAD llms/googleai/googleai.go:146-156: tools are converted only under `if len(opts.Tools) > 0`, but `googleToolConfig(opts.ToolChoice)` (lines 767-789) runs regardless and returns a config for any value that is not unset (auto/none/any/named). Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-langchaingo/190be914-a4ca-51a0-89e2-3fbdbb6fc0c9/scratchpad/probes/f1-toolcfg-notools/probe_test.go captures the request through a custom http.Client RoundTripper and calls GenerateContent with WithToolChoice and no WithTools. HEAD: `choice=auto hasToolConfig=true hasTools=false`, fragment `"toolConfig":{"functionCallingConfig":{"mode":"AUTO"}}`; the same for none (`"mode":"NONE"`). BASE (da7016e): `hasToolConfig=false` for both, because the base never mapped ToolChoice. The genai SDK v1.42.0 does no client-side validation; it passes toolConfig through as it is. Vendor side: ai.google.dev and docs.cloud.google.com are blocked by the sandbox egress proxy, so the official docs could not be read. A third-party fix, free-claude-code PR (github.com/Spencerx/free-claude-code/pull/204, mirroring Alishahryar1/free-claude-code), reports that "Gemini rejects the whole request: `Function calling config is set without function_declarations.`" when tool_choice (auto/any/none) is sent without tools. Its fix omits tool_choice when there are no tools. That is independent evidence of the 400, but not official documentation. The existing tests (tool_choice_wire_test.go) cover tool choice only with tools present.
repro.comment: `googleToolConfig(opts.ToolChoice)` runs even when `opts.Tools` is empty, so a call that sets `WithToolChoice("auto")` or `("none")` without tools now sends `"toolConfig":{"functionCallingConfig":{"mode":"AUTO"}}` and no `tools` field. The base never sent a toolConfig. A probe that captures the request body shows `hasToolConfig=true hasTools=false` at HEAD and `hasToolConfig=false` at da7016e. This depends on vendor behaviour: other projects report Gemini rejecting such requests with 400 `Function calling config is set without function_declarations.` (e.g. the free-claude-code fix that drops tool_choice when no tools are declared). If that holds, agent loops that always pass a tool choice break on turns without tools. Suggest building the tool config only inside the `len(opts.Tools) > 0` branch, as the Bedrock Converse door already does.

At llms/googleai/googleai.go:154, googleToolConfig(opts.ToolChoice) is set on the config outside the `len(opts.Tools) > 0` block, so any explicit choice (auto/none/any/named) sends a functionCallingConfig even when there are no functionDeclarations. I could not confirm the vendor side. An unauthenticated call to generativelanguage.googleapis.com returns 403 before validation, and docs.cloud.google.com is blocked. Web searches mention the error 'Function calling config is set without function_declarations' but none showed it verbatim. Nothing in the code or docs contradicts the claim, and the fix is a one-line guard (only set ToolConfig when config.Tools is non-empty), so it stands, pending vendor confirmation of the 400.

kept.title: Vertex silently ignores caller ClientOptions (token source, API key) and authenticates with ADC instead

A host with ADC (a GCE VM or a developer workstation) builds the client without complaint and signs every request with the ADC principal and its quota project, not the caller's token. WithAPIKey on the Vertex backend is dropped the same way: config.APIKey is set only on the Gemini branch.

Every other entry in the exported Options.ClientOptions is dropped without an error. genai v1.42.0 client.go:278 then calls credentials.DetectDefault (ADC) when Credentials==nil && APIKey=="" && HTTPClient==nil. repro.comment: `vertex.New` now goes through `googleai.New`, and that path drops every entry in the exported `Options.ClientOptions` without an error, except the two gRPC options it refuses. That includes `option.WithTokenSource`, `option.WithCredentials` and the `option.WithAPIKey` that `WithAPIKey` still appends. The previous release passed these options to the Vertex client. genai then falls back to application default credentials, so the caller's own credentials are never used. I ran a probe with a custom option appending `option.WithTokenSource(ts)` plus `WithCloudProject`/`WithCloudLocation`, with no ADC available. kept.title: Any empty stream is reported as "max_tokens is too small", even when the caller set no max_tokens
kept.summary: checkEmptyStream gates the token-limit verdict on opts.MaxTokens being non-nil. GenerateContent always fills MaxTokens from DefaultMaxTokens (16384), so the gate never tells a caller-chosen limit from the default. Every stream that ends without candidates and without a block reason becomes ErrCodeTokenLimit with a message blaming max_tokens.
kept.failure_scenario: A streaming call with no WithMaxTokens receives an HTTP 200 with an empty SSE body, for example from a proxy or gateway that cut the stream. HEAD returns llms.Error{Code: token_limit, Message: "max_tokens is too small to start an answer"}, although 16384 was sent and the caller never chose a limit. A caller that reacts to ErrCodeTokenLimit by raising max_tokens and retrying loops on an unrelated failure. BASE returned an empty success here.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/g2rev-a/probe_test.go TestProbeEmptyStreamDefaultMaxTokens on HEAD (no WithMaxTokens) printed: "code=token_limit msg=\"the model returned no candidates: max_tokens is too small to start an answer\"" and "maxOutputTokens sent: 16384". Code: googleai.go:106-108 sets opts.MaxTokens = &g.opts.DefaultMaxTokens before the call options run, so the check at googleai.go:1230 (opts.MaxTokens == nil) can never be true. Commit c61cb2d measured the heuristic only with an explicit max_tokens of 24.

repro.evidence: Own probe probes/vfy-g2-emptystream/probe_test.go: a googleai.New client (gemini-2.5-flash, no WithMaxTokens) streams against a transport that returns HTTP 200 text/event-stream with an empty body. HEAD printed: RESULT code=token_limit msg="the model returned no candidates: max_tokens is too small to start an answer"; the request body carried generationConfig.maxOutputTokens=16384. BASE, same probe: RESULT err=<nil> (empty success; it sent maxOutputTokens=2048). Code: googleai.go:105-109 always seeds opts.MaxTokens from g.opts.DefaultMaxTokens (16384) before the call options run, so the guard at googleai.go:1230 (opts.MaxTokens == nil || <= 0) only stops the verdict when someone sets WithDefaultMaxTokens(0). It never separates a limit the caller chose from the default. Commit c61cb2d justified the heuristic only with an explicit max_tokens of 24 on gemini-2.5-flash. So every stream that ends with no candidate and no block reason gets ErrCodeTokenLimit, whatever max_tokens was: the default, or an explicit large value.
repro.comment: `checkEmptyStream` means to report ErrCodeTokenLimit only when a max_tokens was set, but `GenerateContent` always fills `opts.MaxTokens` from `DefaultMaxTokens` (16384) first (googleai.go:105-109). So this guard never tells a caller-chosen limit apart from the default, and every stream that ends with no candidate and no block reason becomes `token_limit` with "max_tokens is too small to start an answer". To show it I ran a probe: a streaming call without `WithMaxTokens`, against a transport returning HTTP 200 with an empty SSE body (for example a proxy that cut the stream). HEAD returns `llms.Error{Code: token_limit}` even though `maxOutputTokens: 16384` was sent. BASE returned an empty success for the same input. A caller that reacts to ErrCodeTokenLimit by raising max_tokens and retrying will loop on an unrelated failure. Suggested fix: record whether max_tokens came from the call (or compare it with a small threshold such as the reasoning floor) and report a generic empty-response error otherwise.

refute.reason: Confirmed in code. GenerateContent (googleai.go:105-108) always sets opts.MaxTokens = getIntPointer(g.opts.DefaultMaxTokens), and getIntPointer never returns nil. The nil/<=0 gate in checkEmptyStream (googleai.go:1230) can only skip when someone explicitly passes WithDefaultMaxTokens(0) or a non-positive max_tokens. So any 200 stream with no candidates, no block reason and no content becomes ErrCodeTokenLimit 'max_tokens is too small', even at the default of 16384. The nil check shows the author meant to blame only a limit the caller chose, and that distinction is lost. Commit c61cb2d and empty_stream_test.go only tested an explicit WithMaxTokens(24); no test pins the default case. Turning an empty stream into an error rather than an empty success is defensible, but labelling it as a token-limit error at 16384 is misleading. BASE had no checkEmptyStream and returned an empty success.

kept.comment: `checkEmptyStream` means to report ErrCodeTokenLimit only when a max_tokens was set, but `GenerateContent` always fills `opts.MaxTokens` from `DefaultMaxTokens` (16384) first (googleai.go:105-109). To show it I ran a probe: a streaming call without `WithMaxTokens`, against a transport returning HTTP 200 with an empty SSE body (for example a proxy that cut the stream). HEAD returns `llms.Error{Code: token_limit}` even though `maxOutputTokens: 16384` was sent. BASE returned an empty success for the same input. A caller that reacts to ErrCodeTokenLimit by raising max_tokens and retrying will loop on an unrelated failure. Suggested fix: record whether max_tokens came from the call (or compare it with a small threshold such as the reasoning floor) and report a generic empty-response error otherwise.

kept.title: WithGRPCClient and WithGRPCConn docs still advertise options that now make New fail
kept.summary: The doc comments still say WithGRPCClient "is useful for gemini clients" and WithGRPCConn "is useful for testing embeddings in vertex clients". In this diff both options were changed to add to unhonoredOnREST, so googleai.New and vertex.New now always return ErrOptionNotHonored when either is passed.
kept.failure_scenario: A caller follows the godoc, passes googleai.WithGRPCConn(conn) to vertex.New to test embeddings as documented, and gets ErrOptionNotHonored at construction. The option's documentation says nothing about the refusal.
kept.evidence: option.go:109-117 and 139-147 on HEAD: the doc lines are unchanged context and the bodies add opts.unhonoredOnREST. new.go:64-65 returns &ErrOptionNotHonored whenever unhonoredOnREST is non-empty. Test vertex/credentials_test.go TestVertexStillRefusesAGRPCConnectionAndSaysWhatToUse confirms the refusal.

repro.evidence: option.go:109-117 and 139-147 at HEAD: the doc lines "This is useful for gemini clients." (WithGRPCClient) and "This is useful for testing embeddings in vertex clients." (WithGRPCConn) are unchanged context in the PR diff. Both bodies now append to opts.unhonoredOnREST, added in 34fd5d0. new.go:64-65 then returns &ErrOptionNotHonored for googleai.New, and since 4f6589c vertex also goes through the GenAI REST backend. The existing test vertex/credentials_test.go TestVertexStillRefusesAGRPCConnectionAndSaysWhatToUse passes on HEAD (ran: go test -run TestVertexStillRefusesAGRPCConnection ./llms/googleai/vertex/ -> PASS), which confirms vertex.New(..., WithGRPCConn(conn)) fails at construction. repro.comment: The godoc for `WithGRPCClient` ("useful for gemini clients") and `WithGRPCConn` ("useful for testing embeddings in vertex clients") was left unchanged. refute.reason: Low-severity documentation defect. The refusal is intentional: commit 34fd5d0 'refuse what this door drops' added unhonoredOnREST, and the vertex tests pin it. kept.title: ValidateReasoning refuses effort "none", which the base forwarded and OpenAI documents
kept.summary: ValidateReasoning's allow-list leaves out "none", so the openai, anthropic and bedrock doors now refuse WithReasoning(llms.ReasoningEffort("none"), 0) before the network, although the base openai door sent reasoning_effort:"none" and OpenAI documents it as a GPT-5.1+ value.
kept.failure_scenario: openai.New(WithModel("gpt-5.1")) + GenerateContent(..., llms.WithReasoning(llms.ReasoningEffort("none"), 0)) sent {"reasoning_effort":"none"} and succeeded on BASE. On HEAD it returns `invalid_request: unknown reasoning effort "none"` and nothing is sent. The Bedrock door refuses the same call too (BASE sent the request). This leaves reasoning.GrokEffort's "none" branch unreachable: the check at bedrockllm.go:115 blocks the only path to it, and WithReasoningDisabled resolves to OffOmit for Grok. The huggingface, ollama and googleai doors never call ValidateReasoning, so the same effort is accepted on some doors and refused on others.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/core-llms/openai (httptest server captures the body), run in both checkouts. HEAD: `gpt-5.1 err=invalid_request: unknown reasoning effort "none" body=` (empty; same for gpt-5.2). BASE: `err=<nil> body={"model":"gpt-5.1",...,"reasoning_effort":"none"}`. Probe probes/core-llms/bedrock (Converse, xai.grok-4-1-fast, env -u AWS_CA_BUNDLE): HEAD `err=invalid_request: unknown reasoning effort "none"`; BASE sent the request with err=nil. Commit 891554d says it refuses only "an effort no door accepts" and keeps "minimal" because it is "a real OpenAI effort". "none" was not considered, although the openai door writes reasoning.OpenAIDisableEffort="none" itself. OpenAI docs (developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.1) list reasoning_effort none (default), low, medium, high for GPT-5.1.

repro.evidence: llms/options.go:37 defines ReasoningNone = "" (the empty effort), so the allow-list in ValidateReasoning (options.go:183-186) does not include the string "none". The check runs before any request is built in openaillm.go:108, anthropicllm.go:127/177 and bedrockllm.go:115. My probe probes/vv-u1/openai/probe_test.go (httptest server that captures the body, gpt-5.1, WithReasoning(ReasoningEffort(x),0)) printed on HEAD: `effort=none err=invalid_request: unknown reasoning effort "none" body=` (nothing sent); `effort=low` was sent. On BASE: `effort=none err=<nil> body={..."reasoning_effort":"none"}`. The openai door writes "none" to the wire itself (reasoning.OpenAIDisableEffort = "none", writeDisableEffort). A second probe (probe2_test.go) shows the migration path works on HEAD: WithReasoningDisabled() sends {"reasoning_effort":"none"} for gpt-5.1. Explicit "none" still breaks callers that upgrade, and no README/CHANGELOG in the diff mentions it. GrokEffort (bedrock_capability.go:124) has a "none" branch, and its only caller, bedrockclient_converse.go:249, sits behind ValidateReasoning, so the branch cannot be reached. Commit 891554d says it refuses only "an effort no door accepts" and keeps "minimal" as a real OpenAI effort; "none" is not mentioned. developers.openai.com was blocked by the egress proxy, so I could not re-fetch OpenAI's page, but the door's own constant shows the library treats "none" as a valid OpenAI wire value.
repro.comment: `ValidateReasoning` leaves the string effort "none" out of its allow-list (`ReasoningNone` is `""`), so on the openai, anthropic and bedrock doors `WithReasoning(llms.ReasoningEffort("none"), 0)` now fails before the network with `invalid_request: unknown reasoning effort "none"`. The previous release sent `{"reasoning_effort":"none"}` for gpt-5.1, and this door already writes that value itself (`reasoning.OpenAIDisableEffort`). I checked this with an httptest probe (gpt-5.1): on HEAD the call errors and sends no body; on BASE the request goes out with `reasoning_effort:"none"`. `WithReasoningDisabled()` does produce the same wire value on HEAD, but callers passing the literal effort break on upgrade, and `GrokEffort`'s "none" branch can no longer be reached behind bedrockllm.go:115. Suggested fix: accept "none" in `ValidateReasoning` and treat it as `ReasoningOff`, or at least list the break in the release notes.

refute.reason: llms.ReasoningNone is "" (options.go:37), so the ValidateReasoning allow-list (options.go:184) does not include the wire value "none". The only test (reasoning_validation_test.go) covers the named constants plus "banana", so nothing pins "none" as refused on purpose. That branch can now be reached only through Effort="none", which bedrockllm.go:115 refuses. ReasoningOff for Grok goes through ResolveOff instead, so the branch is dead code. BASE forwarded the value. WithReasoningDisabled is a different path, and on the Bedrock Grok route it cannot produce "none" at all. This breaks a call that used to work, and the code contradicts the stated intent.

kept.title: Anthropic door rebuilds tool_choice and drops disable_parallel_tool_use
kept.summary: anthropicToolChoice rebuilds every choice ClassifyToolChoice recognises as a bare {type[,name]} struct, so extra fields of a native Anthropic tool_choice map (disable_parallel_tool_use) are dropped silently; the base door sent the caller's map verbatim.
kept.failure_scenario: llms.WithToolChoice(map[string]any{"type":"auto","disable_parallel_tool_use":true}) on the anthropic door: BASE sent tool_choice {"disable_parallel_tool_use":true,"type":"auto"}. HEAD sends {"type":"auto"}, so the model may emit parallel tool calls the caller disabled. The same happens for {"type":"tool","name":"x","disable_parallel_tool_use":true} and {"type":"any",...}. resp.Warnings is empty, and the door cannot merge WithExtraBody, so the caller has no workaround. The Bedrock InvokeModel door (anthropicToolChoiceOnWire, provider_anthropic.go:392) rebuilds the choice the same way.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/core-llms/anthropic (httptest server captures the body; model claude-sonnet-4-5, one tool), run in both checkouts. HEAD: `"tool_choice":{"type":"auto"}` and `"tool_choice":{"type":"tool","name":"get_weather"}` with `warnings=[]`. BASE: `"tool_choice":{"disable_parallel_tool_use":true,"type":"auto"}` and `"tool_choice":{"disable_parallel_tool_use":true,"name":"get_weather","type":"tool"}`. anthropicclient.ToolChoice has only Type and Name (messages.go:116). Commit bce683d meant to "leave every other choice untouched", and 20acb40 widened the rebuild to auto/none; neither mentions dropping fields.

repro.evidence: anthropicToolChoice (anthropicllm.go:1059-1072) maps every choice that ClassifyToolChoice recognises (auto/none/any/tool, including map[string]any) to anthropicclient.ToolChoice{Type,Name}. That struct has only those two fields (anthropicclient/messages.go:116-119), so any other keys are dropped. BASE passed opts.ToolChoice through unchanged (base anthropicllm.go:295). My probe probes/vv-u1/anthropic/probe_test.go (httptest server capturing the body, claude-sonnet-4-5, one tool) printed on HEAD: `"tool_choice":{"type":"auto"}`, `{"type":"any"}` and `{"type":"tool","name":"get_weather"}`, all with err=nil. On BASE: `{"disable_parallel_tool_use":true,"type":"auto"}`, `{"disable_parallel_tool_use":true,"type":"any"}` and `{"disable_parallel_tool_use":true,"name":"get_weather","type":"tool"}`. The Bedrock InvokeModel helper anthropicToolChoiceOnWire (provider_anthropic.go:391) rebuilds the choice the same way, but BASE Bedrock never sent tool_choice at all, so only the anthropic door regresses.
repro.comment: `anthropicToolChoice` rebuilds every choice that `ClassifyToolChoice` recognises into `anthropicclient.ToolChoice{Type, Name}`, which silently drops the other fields of a native Anthropic `tool_choice` map, including `disable_parallel_tool_use`. I sent `WithToolChoice(map[string]any{"type":"auto","disable_parallel_tool_use":true})` (and the `any` and `tool` variants) to an httptest server. HEAD sends `"tool_choice":{"type":"auto"}` with no warning, while the previous release sent the map unchanged, `{"disable_parallel_tool_use":true,"type":"auto"}`. As a result the model may make parallel tool calls the caller had turned off, and this door has no extra-body escape hatch to put the field back. Suggested fix: for map inputs, copy the remaining keys onto the rebuilt choice (or add `DisableParallelToolUse *bool` to `ToolChoice`); the Bedrock `anthropicToolChoiceOnWire` has the same problem.

refute.reason: anthropicToolChoice (anthropicllm.go:1059) rebuilds every choice it recognises as anthropicclient.ToolChoice{Type,Name}. The repo has no other option for parallel tool use (grep for parallel_tool/ParallelTool finds nothing), so the caller has no workaround. Commit bce683d only meant to fix the shape of the choice, not to strip fields.
