kept.title: IsTruncated misses model_context_window_exceeded, so truncated Claude answers pass as complete
kept.summary: The truncation table has no entry for Anthropic's and Bedrock Converse's model_context_window_exceeded, which Anthropic says to treat as truncated. Truncated stays false, WithFailOnTruncation does not fire, and a structured-output answer cut off by the context window is returned as success without validation.
kept.failure_scenario: Claude Sonnet 4.5+ (Anthropic API, or Bedrock Converse/InvokeModel) with a large prompt, WithMaxTokens(64000), WithFailOnTruncation() and WithStructuredOutput(...). The model fills the context window and stops with model_context_window_exceeded. GenerateContent returns err=nil and Truncated=false, with content `{"answer": "partial`. validateAnthropicStructuredOutput validates only end_turn/stop_sequence, and CheckTruncation does not recognise the reason, so the caller receives invalid JSON as a successful structured answer.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/core-llms/llms: IsTruncated("model_context_window_exceeded") = false, and CheckTruncation(FailOnTruncation=true) = <nil>. Probe probes/core-llms/anthropic2 (httptest returns stop_reason model_context_window_exceeded, with WithFailOnTruncation and WithStructuredOutput): `err=<nil> content="{\"answer\": \"partial" stop="model_context_window_exceeded" truncated=false`. Anthropic docs (platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/handling-stop-reasons): model_context_window_exceeded means "Claude stopped because it reached the model's context window limit", is returned without a beta header on Sonnet 4.5 and newer, and should be treated as truncated. The vendored aws-sdk-go-v2 bedrockruntime lists StopReasonModelContextWindowExceeded = "model_context_window_exceeded" (types/enums.go:835). No non-test code in the repo handles this value.

repro.evidence: llms/stopreason.go is a new file. truncationStopReasons contains only length, max_tokens and model_length. The anthropic door and all Bedrock paths (bedrockclient_converse.go:1092, provider_anthropic.go:600) set Truncated with IsTruncated, and validateAnthropicStructuredOutput (anthropicllm.go:1033-1037) validates only end_turn/stop_sequence. My probe probes/vv-u1/anthropic/probe3_test.go (httptest returns the partial text `{"answer": "partial`, with WithFailOnTruncation and WithStructuredOutput) printed `IsTruncated(model_context_window_exceeded)=false`. For stop=max_tokens: `err=truncated: choice 0 stopped at the output token limit ... truncated=true`. For stop=model_context_window_exceeded: `err=<nil> content="{\"answer\": \"partial" truncated=false`. Anthropic's docs (platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/handling-stop-reasons, fetched) say the value means the response filled the model's context window, that the API returns it without a beta header on Sonnet 4.5 and newer, and that the response should be treated as truncated. The vendored bedrockruntime v1.50.4 defines StopReasonModelContextWindowExceeded = "model_context_window_exceeded" (types/enums.go:835). No non-test code handles this value. Truncated and FailOnTruncation are both new in this PR, so this is a gap in the new feature, not a regression; the live stop reason depends on the vendor, but Anthropic documents it.
repro.comment: `truncationStopReasons` has no entry for `model_context_window_exceeded`. Anthropic returns that stop reason without a beta header on Sonnet 4.5 and newer (Bedrock Converse too, since the SDK enum `StopReasonModelContextWindowExceeded` exists), and its stop-reason docs say to treat it as truncated. So when an answer is cut off by the context window, `Truncated` is false, `WithFailOnTruncation` does not fire, and `validateAnthropicStructuredOutput` skips validation. I ran an httptest probe that returns `{"answer": "partial` with `WithFailOnTruncation()` and `WithStructuredOutput(...)`. For `max_tokens` it returns a `truncated` error; for `model_context_window_exceeded` it returns `err=nil`, `truncated=false` and the invalid JSON as a successful structured answer. Suggested fix: add `model_context_window_exceeded` to the truncation table, with a test covering both the anthropic and Bedrock paths.

refute.reason: truncationStopReasons (stopreason.go:8) contains only length, max_tokens and model_length. A maintainer could argue that the contract says 'output token limit'. A {"type":"function"} choice whose function is a map[string]string, an llms.FunctionReference or a *FunctionReference falls through to kindOf("function", ""), which returns ToolChoiceAny. BASE sends tool_choice {"type":"function","function":{"name":"calc"}}, so the model must call calc. HEAD sends tool_choice "required", so the model may call search instead. There is no error and no warning. The same classification makes googleai send mode ANY with no allowed names, Bedrock Converse send any, and Anthropic send {"type":"any"}.
kept.evidence: End-to-end probe (probes/core2-tc2) with an httptest server behind openai.New(WithBaseURL). kept.title: DecodeFields silently accepts and discards data after the arguments object
kept.summary: DecodeFields reads '{', the fields and the closing '}' with a json.Decoder, but never checks that the input ends there. Arguments like `{"a":1}{"b":2}` or `{"a":1} garbage` decode to the first object with no error. The json.Unmarshal calls it replaced in the googleai, ollama and bedrock doors rejected such input.
kept.failure_scenario: An OpenAI-compatible stream sends two argument objects under one tool-call index, so the accumulated Arguments is `{"city":"Paris"}{"city":"London"}`. Some providers do this with parallel calls at index 0 or duplicated final chunks. Replaying that assistant turn through the googleai, Bedrock or Ollama door now sends only {"city":"Paris"}: the second call's arguments are dropped and the history no longer matches what the model did. BASE returned an unmarshal error instead.
kept.evidence: Probe (probes/core2-toolcall) on HEAD. toolcall.Decode(`{"a":1}{"b":2}`) returned map[a:1] with err=<nil>, and json.Unmarshal returned "invalid character '{' after top-level value". The same happens for `{"a":1} trailing` and `{"a":1}]`. BASE callers: base/llms/googleai/googleai.go:676, base/llms/ollama/ollamallm.go:282 and base/llms/bedrock/bedrockllm.go:235 all use json.Unmarshal. HEAD callers: googleai.go:703, ollamallm.go:326 and bedrockllm.go:22. Suggested fix: after the closing token, require dec.Token() to return io.EOF (or check dec.More()==false and no more input).

repro.evidence: Probe probes/uvx-f2dec in internal/toolcall at HEAD: Decode(`{"a":1}{"b":2}`) returned map[a:1] with err=nil, and so did `{"city":"Paris"}{"city":"London"}` (map[city:Paris]), `{"a":1} garbage` and `{"a":1}]`. json.Unmarshal rejects all of them ("invalid character ... after top-level value"). DecodeFields (arguments.go:50) reads the closing '}' and returns without checking for EOF. BASE callers used json.Unmarshal: base googleai.go:676, ollamallm.go:282, bedrockllm.go:235. HEAD callers use toolcall: googleai.go:703, ollamallm.go:326, bedrockllm.go:22. Whether a provider actually produces concatenated argument objects is not shown, but the silent truncation on replay is.
repro.comment: `DecodeFields` stops after the closing `}` and never checks that the input ends there, so trailing data is silently dropped. A probe shows `toolcall.Decode(`{"city":"Paris"}{"city":"London"}`)` returns `map[city:Paris]` with no error. The same happens for `{"a":1} garbage` and `{"a":1}]`. The `json.Unmarshal` calls this replaces in the googleai, Ollama and Bedrock doors rejected these inputs with "invalid character after top-level value". So a malformed or concatenated arguments string, for example from a stream that merged two calls under one index, is now replayed as only its first object, and the history no longer matches what the model did. Fix: after the closing token, require the next `dec.Token()` to return `io.EOF` and return an error otherwise.

refute.reason: DecodeFields (internal/toolcall/arguments.go:50-54) reads the closing '}' and returns without checking for EOF, so `{"a":1}{"b":2}` or `{"a":1} junk` decode to the first object with no error. Doors that build arguments with json.Marshal never produce such input. Garbled or concatenated arguments can still come from OpenAI-compatible streaming accumulation and then be replayed through another door, and the change swaps a loud error for silent data loss. Severity is low but the code clearly leads there. The fix is a trivial EOF check.

kept.title: Compile's doc says the schema is used verbatim, but admitNullable now rewrites type
kept.summary: The Compile doc comment still says 'The schema is used verbatim; no keywords are injected or stripped'. In fact {"a":null} passes validation. On a door that does not honour nullable on the wire (openai, anthropic), a null answer is accepted with no error.

repro.evidence: At HEAD, llms/structuredoutput/validator.go:20-21 still says 'The schema is used verbatim; no keywords are injected or stripped', but line 27 (added in this PR, commits 80840e1/bb80316) calls doc = admitNullable(doc). For every node with nullable:true, admitNullable (lines 41-66) rewrites the node's type to include "null". I ran a probe that compiles {"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"type":"string","nullable":true}},"required":["a"]} and validates {"a":null}. At HEAD it returns err=<nil>. At BASE da7016e it returns 'response does not match schema: jsonschema validation failed'. The doc lines are outside the diff hunk, so the anchor is line 27.

kept.title: Exclude partial indexes are never used by the store's own queries
kept.summary: The partial-index predicate is rendered as `(cmetadata ->> 'k') IS DISTINCT FROM 'v'`. PostgreSQL's predicate prover only reasons about plain operator clauses, not DistinctExpr, so an equality filter `(cmetadata ->> 'k') = $n` never implies it. Every index declared with Exclude is therefore unreachable from SimilaritySearch and Search: it is built and maintained on every write but never read.
kept.failure_scenario: The store is created with WithMetadataIndexes(MetadataIndex{Keys: []string{"doc_type"}, Exclude: map[string]string{"doc_type": "memory"}}) and then runs SimilaritySearch(..., WithFilters({"doc_type": "answer"})), where answers are 1% of rows. The plan never uses the partial index; it scans via the collection_id index or does a seq scan. With `<>` the same index is chosen. So the documented purpose ("the index then spans that minority") is not delivered, while writes still pay for maintaining the index.
kept.evidence: I started a local PostgreSQL 16.13 with pgvector 0.6.0 inside the probe dir. Plain SQL with enable_seqscan=off: an IS DISTINCT FROM partial index still gave `Seq Scan on t`, while the `<>` variant gave `Bitmap Index Scan on t_partial_ne`. The Go probe probes/vs-partialidx (internal test on HEAD, real store: New + WithMetadataIndexes + AddDocuments of 5000 docs + EXPLAIN of the recorded SimilaritySearch SQL/args with enable_seqscan=off) printed `Index Scan using probe_partial_emb_collection_id ... Filter: (... (cmetadata ->> 'doc_type') = 'answer')` for the declared index. After adding the same index with `<>` it printed `Index Scan using probe_partial_ne ... Index Cond: ((cmetadata ->> 'doc_type'::text) = 'answer'::text)`. PostgreSQL's predtest.c operator_predicate_proof (REL_16_STABLE, REL_18_STABLE and master) says: "Both expressions must be binary opclauses ... in future we might extend this logic to other operator-based constructs such as DistinctExpr". The fix is to use `<>`: rows without the key cannot match an equality filter anyway. TestStoreCreatesTheDeclaredMetadataIndexes only checks that the index exists, not that it is used.

repro.evidence: Reproduced this on my own PG 16.13 + pgvector 0.6.0 cluster (probes/ver-pgv). Plain SQL on 100k rows, 1% 'answer': with only the `IS DISTINCT FROM 'memory'` partial index, `WHERE (cmetadata->>'doc_type') = 'answer'` gives `Seq Scan on t`, both with default settings and with enable_seqscan=off. The index is picked only when the query repeats the IS DISTINCT FROM predicate verbatim. After adding the same index with `<> 'memory'`, the default plan is `Index Scan using t_partial_ne`. Store-level probe (HEAD, New+WithMetadataIndexes{Keys:[doc_type],Exclude:{doc_type:memory}}, AddDocuments 20k docs, EXPLAIN of the recorded SimilaritySearch SQL/args): with the declared index the plan is `Seq Scan on ver_part_emb`, or `Index Scan using ver_part_emb_collection_id` with seqscan off, and the doc_type equality is only a Filter. After adding the `<>` twin the plan is `Index Scan using ver_part_ne ... Index Cond: ((cmetadata ->> 'doc_type') = 'answer')`. filterPredicates (pgvector.go:500) only emits `(cmetadata ->> 'k') = $n`, so no store query can reach the declared Exclude index. The feature is new in this PR (metadata_index.go is a new file, commit 504595c), so this is a feature that does not work, not a regression.
repro.comment: The partial-index predicate is rendered as `(cmetadata ->> 'k') IS DISTINCT FROM 'v'`. PostgreSQL's predicate prover (predtest.c) only reasons about plain operator clauses, not DistinctExpr, so the store's own filter `(cmetadata ->> 'k') = $n` never implies it. Every index declared with `Exclude` gets built and maintained on each write, but SimilaritySearch/Search never use it. I checked this on PG 16.13 + pgvector 0.6.0: a store with `WithMetadataIndexes(MetadataIndex{Keys: []string{"doc_type"}, Exclude: map[string]string{"doc_type": "memory"}})` and 20k docs gets a Seq Scan for `WithFilters({"doc_type": "answer"})` (a collection_id index scan with enable_seqscan=off). The same index written with `<> 'memory'` is chosen (`Index Scan ... Index Cond: ((cmetadata ->> 'doc_type') = 'answer')`). Use `<>`: a row without the key can never match an equality filter, so leaving it out of the index loses nothing. A test should assert the plan uses the index, not only that the index exists.

The reviewer's EXPLAIN probe matches this. The code comment gives the reason for IS DISTINCT FROM as keeping rows without the key in the index, but such rows can never match the store's equality filters, so that reason does not help. kept.title: ANALYZE in init fails New on mixed-dimension tables with pgvector < 0.7
kept.summary: This is a different failure from earlier finding #12, which is about performance. createMetadataIndexesIfNotExist runs `ANALYZE <embedding table>` on every start. Before pgvector 0.7.0, the btree comparison of vectors raises "different vector dimensions". So on a table that holds more than one embedding width, which the PR explicitly supports in SimilaritySearch, ANALYZE errors, init rolls back, and pgvector.New fails.

The same New without WithMetadataIndexes succeeds, and the base never ran ANALYZE.

The PR's own suite fails the same way on this pgvector: with PGVECTOR_CONNECTION_STRING set, TestStoreCreatesTheDeclaredMetadataIndexes fails at New with this error after TestSimilaritySearchToleratesAMixedWidthTableUnderFiltersAndThreshold wrote 64- and 32-dim rows into the shared default table. The reviewer reproduced the error both in psql and through New. #12 is about lock contention and cost at the same line; this finding is a hard failure to open the store, so it is a different defect, not a duplicate. The base never ran ANALYZE.

kept.title: Pinecone results re-sorted by descending score, which reverses euclidean indexes
kept.summary: getDocumentsFromMatches now re-sorts matches by Score, highest first. For a Pinecone index with the euclidean metric, the score is a distance: lower means more similar, and Pinecone already returns matches most-similar first. The new sort therefore reverses the order and puts the least similar document first. The base kept Pinecone's order.
kept.failure_scenario: A euclidean Pinecone index returns matches with scores 0.05, 0.40 and 1.20, nearest first. HEAD returns docs in the order farthest (1.20), middle, nearest. BASE returned nearest, middle, farthest. Retrievers and chains that take docs[0], or feed documents in rank order, now get the worst match first.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/vs-pinecone (internal test calling getDocumentsFromMatches with matches in euclidean order) printed on HEAD: `0 farthest 1.20 / 1 middle 0.40 / 2 nearest 0.05`, and on BASE: `0 nearest 0.05 / 1 middle 0.40 / 2 farthest 1.20`. The sort came from commit 2ba6eae ("Improved sorting ... to maintain relevance order"); its intent was tie-breaking, not changing the metric direction. Pinecone's metric semantics (euclidean scores are distances, lower is more similar) are documented by Pinecone and summarised at theneuralbase.com/pinecone/learn/beginner/score-interpretation-per-metric. docs.pinecone.io and pinecone.io are blocked by the sandbox proxy, so I could not quote them directly.

repro.evidence: Own probe (probes/ver-pine, internal test calling getDocumentsFromMatches with matches in Pinecone's euclidean order 0.05, 0.40, 1.20). HEAD printed `0 farthest 1.20 / 1 middle 0.40 / 2 nearest 0.05`; BASE printed `0 nearest 0.05 / 1 middle 0.40 / 2 farthest 1.20`. The sort at pinecone.go:215-220 orders by Score descending no matter which metric the index uses. The store never reads the index metric (no 'Metric' or 'euclidean' anywhere in vectorstores/pinecone), and go-pinecone v4.0.1 supports euclidean indexes (models.go:19). Pinecone's euclidean scores are distances, lower means more similar, and results come back nearest first (secondary sources: theneuralbase.com score-interpretation-per-metric and pinecone.io/learn/vector-similarity via search; docs.pinecone.io is blocked by the sandbox proxy, so I could not quote it). The sort came from 2ba6eae, whose test only covers cosine-like descending scores and tie-breaking. For cosine and dotproduct indexes the sort is a no-op apart from ties. Note: BASE's scoreThreshold (`>=`) already assumed higher-is-better, so euclidean + threshold was already wrong, but the plain order is a new regression.
repro.comment: `getDocumentsFromMatches` now re-sorts matches by `Score` descending. For a Pinecone index with the `euclidean` metric the score is a distance (lower = more similar), and Pinecone already returns matches nearest first, so this sort reverses them and puts the worst match at `docs[0]`. A probe calling `getDocumentsFromMatches` with scores 0.05/0.40/1.20 in Pinecone's order returns farthest, middle, nearest on this branch; the previous release returned nearest, middle, farthest. Retrievers and chains that take the top document, or feed documents in rank order, silently get the least relevant context first. The tie-breaking goal of 2ba6eae can be kept without changing the direction: preserve Pinecone's order and only order runs of equal scores by text (or read the index metric once and sort in the matching direction). This relies on Pinecone's documented euclidean semantics; I could not open docs.pinecone.io from the sandbox.

refute.reason: HEAD's getDocumentsFromMatches does sort.SliceStable by Score, highest first. BASE kept the order Pinecone returned. Pinecone documents euclidean-index scores as squared distance, with the most similar result having the lowest score and returned first. The new sort therefore reverses the ranking for euclidean indexes. Nothing in the package or docs limits the store to cosine or dotproduct: there is no metric option or documentation, and no test pins the order. Commit 2ba6eae says the sort is meant to 'maintain relevance order' and add a stable tie-break, so reversing it was not intended. Mitigating point: the score threshold (>= in [0,1]) already assumed similarity semantics in BASE, so euclidean plus a threshold was already wrong. The reversed order with no threshold, which is the default, is a new regression.

kept.title: jina WithBatchSize(0) or a negative value now panics
kept.summary: applyOptions no longer replaces the batch size for a known model once the caller used WithBatchSize, even when that value is 0 or negative. EmbedDocuments then passes it to embeddings.BatchTexts, which computes len(texts)/batchSize and panics. The base overwrote any value with the model's default for known models, so this call worked before.
kept.failure_scenario: An application builds jina.NewJina(jina.WithBatchSize(cfg.BatchSize)) with an unset (zero) config field, which the commit notes pentagi passes together with the model. EmbedDocuments(ctx, []string{"a","b"}) panics with `runtime error: integer divide by zero`. A negative value panics in makeslice. On BASE the same code embedded both texts with BatchSize=512.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/vs-jina (httptest Jina server, NewJina(WithAPIBaseURL, WithAPIKey, WithBatchSize(0)), EmbedDocuments of 2 texts). HEAD printed `BatchSize=0` and `PANIC: runtime error: integer divide by zero`. BASE printed `BatchSize=512` and `embs=2 err=<nil>`. The change came from commit fe380f3 ("keep the batch size the caller asked for"), which intended to honour positive values, not to crash on zero. A guard such as `batchSizeFromCaller && BatchSize > 0` would keep that intent. This is separate from earlier finding #15, which is about the comment.

repro.evidence: Code: embeddings/jina/options.go:87 at HEAD now skips the model default whenever batchSizeFromCaller is set, with no check for a positive value. EmbedDocuments passes j.BatchSize to embeddings.BatchTexts, which computes len(texts)/batchSize and make(..., len/bs+1). My probe probes/vfy3-jina (httptest Jina server, NewJina(WithAPIBaseURL, WithAPIKey, WithBatchSize(bs)), EmbedDocuments([a b])) printed at HEAD: `bs=0 BatchSize=0` / `bs=0 PANIC: runtime error: integer divide by zero` and `bs=-1 BatchSize=-1` / `bs=-1 PANIC: runtime error: makeslice: cap out of range`. At BASE: `bs=0 BatchSize=512 embs=2 err=<nil>` and `bs=-1 BatchSize=512 embs=2 err=<nil>`. This is a regression for the default and known models. A custom unknown model with WithBatchSize(0) already panicked on BASE. The change came from commit fe380f3. This differs from #15, which is about the comment only.
repro.comment: Regression: once `WithBatchSize` is called, `applyOptions` keeps the caller's value even when it is 0 or negative, and `EmbedDocuments` then passes it to `embeddings.BatchTexts`, which divides by it. With `NewJina(WithBatchSize(0))`, typical for an unset config field, `EmbedDocuments(ctx, []string{"a","b"})` panics with `integer divide by zero`, and `WithBatchSize(-1)` panics with `makeslice: cap out of range`. On the previous release both calls embedded the two texts with BatchSize=512. I showed this with an httptest-backed probe run against both HEAD and BASE. Suggested fix: honour the caller only for positive values (`o.batchSizeFromCaller && o.BatchSize > 0`), or fall back to a sane default before batching.

refute.reason: Confirmed by reading the code. In HEAD, embeddings/jina/options.go:87 skips the model default whenever WithBatchSize was called (batchSizeFromCaller), so a value of 0 or a negative value reaches embeddings.BatchTexts (embedding.go:110). There `len(texts)/batchSize` divides by zero, and a negative value panics in make. BASE (options.go:86) always replaced the value for the three known models, so the same call worked there. The strongest counter-argument is that a zero batch size is invalid input: openai, voyageai, huggingface and bedrock pass WithBatchSize(0) through and panic the same way, and BASE jina panicked too for an unknown model. Even so, a call that worked in the previous release (known model plus a zero from config) now panics instead of returning an error. Commit fe380f3 was meant to honour positive values, and nothing (no test or doc) pins 0 as intended. A guard like `batchSizeFromCaller && BatchSize > 0` fixes it cheaply.

kept.comment: Regression: once `WithBatchSize` is called, `applyOptions` keeps the caller's value even when it is 0 or negative, and `EmbedDocuments` then passes it to `embeddings.BatchTexts`, which divides by it. With `NewJina(WithBatchSize(0))`, typical for an unset config field, `EmbedDocuments(ctx, []string{"a","b"})` panics with `integer divide by zero`, and `WithBatchSize(-1)` panics with `makeslice: cap out of range`. On the previous release both calls embedded the two texts with BatchSize=512. I showed this with an httptest-backed probe run against both HEAD and BASE. Suggested fix: honour the caller only for positive values (`o.batchSizeFromCaller && o.BatchSize > 0`), or fall back to a sane default before batching.

kept.title: Float filter values in exponent form never match stored JSON numbers
kept.summary: filterPredicates binds non-string values as fmt.Sprintf("%v"). For float64, %v switches to exponent notation from 1e6 up and below 1e-4. JSON stores the same numbers in plain decimal, so `cmetadata ->> 'k'` never equals the bound text. The commit claims non-string values can now match, but this breaks for any filter decoded from JSON, where every number is a float64.
kept.failure_scenario: A document is stored with Metadata {"user_id": 1234567}. An HTTP API decodes the request body `{"user_id": 1234567}` into map[string]any (giving float64) and passes it to WithFilters. The bound value is "1.234567e+06" while `->>` yields "1234567", so SimilaritySearch returns 0 documents with no error. The same filter with int 1234567 returns the document. The base never matched non-strings either, so this is an incomplete fix rather than a regression.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/vs-floatfilter (HEAD, local PG 16.13 + pgvector 0.6.0) printed: `json-decoded filter 1.234567e+06 -> 0 docs err=<nil>`, `int filter -> 1 docs err=<nil>`, and `bound value for float64: "1.234567e+06"`. Commit ec0ee19 says: "Non-string filter values now render as their text form rather than fmt's %!s(int=5), so a filter that could never match before can match." Formatting float64 with strconv.FormatFloat(v,'f',-1,64), or json.Marshal, would match what encoding/json stored.

repro.evidence: filterPredicates (vectorstores/pgvector/pgvector.go:502) binds fmt.Sprintf("%v", v). cmetadata is a `json` column (pgvector.go:181/212) written by pgx via encoding/json, and `->>` returns the stored text. Probe probes/vfy3-pgfloat (HEAD, no DB) compares the bound value with json.Marshal of the same value decoded from a JSON body: `{"user_id":1234567}` bound="1.234567e+06", stored 1234567, match=false; `{"ts":1727500000}` bound="1.7275e+09", stored 1727500000, match=false; `{"price":0.00001}` bound="1e-05", stored 0.00001, match=false; `{"user_id":42}` matches; an int 1234567 filter binds "1234567". The original reviewer's probe on real PG 16 + pgvector showed 0 docs for the float filter and 1 doc for the int filter. BASE rendered non-strings as `%!s(float64=...)`, which never matched, so this is not a regression. It is an incomplete fix of what commit ec0ee19 claims ("a filter that could never match before can match"), and the miss is silent.
repro.comment: Non-string filter values are bound as `fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)`. For `float64`, `%v` switches to exponent form (from 1e21 up and below 1e-4), while the `json` column holds what `encoding/json` wrote, and `->>` returns that text. Every number in a filter decoded from a JSON request body is a `float64`. So `{"user_id": 1234567}` binds `"1.234567e+06"` against a stored `1234567`, and `{"ts": 1727500000}` binds `"1.7275e+09"`. `SimilaritySearch` then returns 0 documents with no error, while the same filter with an `int` matches. I confirmed the mismatch with a probe that compares `filterPredicates`' bound value with `json.Marshal` of the same value. The previous release never matched non-string values either, so this is an incomplete fix rather than a regression, but commit ec0ee19 advertises that such filters now match. Suggested fix: render numbers the way encoding/json does, e.g. `strconv.FormatFloat(v, 'f', -1, 64)` for floats, or `json.Marshal` for any non-string scalar.

refute.reason: pgvector.go:502 binds `fmt.Sprintf("%v", filter[k])`. For a float64, %v uses exponent form when the exponent is below -4 or at least 21. Hmm, more exactly: %v is %g with the shortest representation, which gives exponent form from 1e21 up only for strconv 'g' with -1 precision... In practice Go's %v prints 1234567.0 as 1.234567e+06 (exponent form once the exponent is 6 or more at shortest precision) and 0.00001 as 1e-05. PostgreSQL's `->>` on a JSON number stored via json.Marshal renders plain decimal (1234567, 0.00001). The two texts differ, so the predicate never matches and the search silently returns no rows. Filters decoded from JSON always hold float64, so this input is realistic, for example numeric IDs of a million or more. Commit ec0ee19 explicitly claims that non-string values can now match, so this is a gap in the intended fix, not designed behaviour. It is preexisting: BASE used '%s', which produced %!s(float64=...) and never matched any non-string value. strconv.FormatFloat(v,'f',-1,64) or json.Marshal would close the gap.

kept.comment: Non-string filter values are bound as `fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)`. For `float64`, `%v` switches to exponent form (from 1e21 up and below 1e-4), while the `json` column holds what `encoding/json` wrote, and `->>` returns that text. Every number in a filter decoded from a JSON request body is a `float64`. So `{"user_id": 1234567}` binds `"1.234567e+06"` against a stored `1234567`, and `{"ts": 1727500000}` binds `"1.7275e+09"`. `SimilaritySearch` then returns 0 documents with no error, while the same filter with an `int` matches. I confirmed the mismatch with a probe that compares `filterPredicates`' bound value with `json.Marshal` of the same value. The previous release never matched non-string values either, so this is an incomplete fix rather than a regression, but commit ec0ee19 advertises that such filters now match. Suggested fix: render numbers the way encoding/json does, e.g. `strconv.FormatFloat(v, 'f', -1, 64)` for floats, or `json.Marshal` for any non-string scalar.

kept.title: Perplexity tool: two constants removed (compile break); the four kept were retired 2026-09-27
kept.summary: This hunk deletes the exported ModelSonarReasoning and ModelR11776, so any caller that references them no longer compiles. The stated reason is that the vendor no longer serves them. Yet the four IDs kept (sonar, the default ModelSonar, sonar-pro, sonar-reasoning-pro, sonar-deep-research) and the /chat/completions endpoint this tool calls through openai.New were retired on 2026-09-27. The PR also moves examples/perplexity-completion-example to "sonar-pro".
kept.failure_scenario: A caller referencing perplexity.ModelSonarReasoning fails to build after upgrading. A caller using perplexity.New() with the default ModelSonar, or the updated example, gets a vendor error from https://api.perplexity.ai/chat/completions after the 2026-09-27 sunset, one day before this review. The tool as shipped cannot answer.
kept.evidence: Commit 884772f says "The Perplexity tool exported sonar-reasoning and r1-1776; the vendor's model list carries neither" (deliberate removal, no deprecation step). tools/perplexity New() uses openai.WithBaseURL("https://api.perplexity.ai") with model ModelSonar. github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/pull/5137 quotes the vendor: "the /chat/completions Sonar endpoint (and the sonar* model IDs served through it) will be sunset on 2026-09-27" for sonar, sonar-pro, sonar-reasoning-pro and sonar-deep-research. github.com/maximhq/bifrost/issues/7236 says the same and names the Agent API (/v1/responses, model perplexity/sonar) as the replacement. docs.perplexity.ai is blocked by the sandbox proxy, so I could not read the vendor changelog directly.

repro.evidence: Compile break, demonstrated: probe probes/vfy3-pplx (package perplexity_test referencing perplexity.ModelSonarReasoning and ModelR11776). At HEAD it fails with `undefined: perplexity.ModelSonarReasoning` / `undefined: perplexity.ModelR11776`. At BASE it passes and prints `sonar-reasoning r1-1776 sonar`. Commit 884772f removed them deliberately, with no deprecation step. Nothing else in the repo references them. Sunset, vendor-dependent: docs.perplexity.ai, llmgateway.io and usagepricing.com are blocked by the sandbox egress proxy. github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/pull/5137, written by a Perplexity-affiliated author (andrewmadson-pplx), quotes: "Perplexity has announced that the /chat/completions Sonar endpoint ... will be sunset on 2026-09-27" for sonar, sonar-pro, sonar-reasoning-pro and sonar-deep-research, with the Agent API (/v1/responses) named as the replacement. Several independent trackers say the same (itsatony/retrievr-mcp#2, Canonry/canonry#1202, JuergenB/artwork-archive#111, the llmgateway.io retirement blog). tools/perplexity.New uses openai.WithBaseURL("https://api.perplexity.ai") with the default ModelSonar, i.e. /chat/completions. I did not make a live call (no key), so the post-sunset error itself is not observed.
repro.comment: This hunk deletes the exported `ModelSonarReasoning` and `ModelR11776` with no deprecation step, so callers referencing them no longer compile. A probe referencing both builds on the previous release and fails at HEAD with `undefined: perplexity.ModelSonarReasoning`. The remaining constants have a bigger problem, though this part depends on the vendor. Perplexity announced that the `/chat/completions` Sonar endpoint and the `sonar`, `sonar-pro`, `sonar-reasoning-pro` and `sonar-deep-research` IDs are sunset on 2026-09-27, with the Agent API (`/v1/responses`) as the replacement. Sources: models.dev PR #5137 by a Perplexity author, plus several downstream migration issues. I could not read docs.perplexity.ai from the sandbox or make a live call. If that holds, `perplexity.New()` (default `ModelSonar` through `openai.New` against `https://api.perplexity.ai`) and the updated `perplexity-completion-example` (`sonar-pro`) can no longer get an answer, so pruning two IDs does not fix the tool. Still, the PR touched this exact list and the example to 'refresh' the model IDs and left the tool pointing at a retired API, so it is a real defect of what ships in this release.

kept.title: SimilaritySearch now depends on an embedding-table `uuid` column, so it fails on tables created by Python langchain_postgres
kept.summary: The rewritten SimilaritySearch selects the embedding table's `uuid` (line 343) and sorts on it as a tie-break (`ORDER BY data.distance, data.uuid`, line 361). On BASE, SimilaritySearch never read that column. A store opened over tables laid out by langchain_postgres, whose embedding key column is `id`, now fails every similarity search.
kept.failure_scenario: A Go service opens pgvector.New over the default-named langchain_pg_embedding/langchain_pg_collection tables that a Python langchain_postgres ingester created (embedding table: id varchar PK, collection_id, embedding, document, cmetadata jsonb). init succeeds, and so does Search. SimilaritySearch returns `ERROR: column langchain_pg_embedding.uuid does not exist (SQLSTATE 42703)`. On BASE it returned the matching documents. The package deliberately shares defaults, including the advisory-lock id, with Python langchain.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/vce2-pyschema/probe_test.go against a private PostgreSQL 16.13 with pgvector 0.6.0. It creates vce2_py_coll(uuid,name UNIQUE,cmetadata) and vce2_py_emb(id varchar PK, collection_id, embedding vector, document, cmetadata jsonb) plus one row, then calls New and SimilaritySearch without and with a flow_id filter. HEAD: `SimilaritySearch: docs=0 err=ERROR: column vce2_py_emb.uuid does not exist (SQLSTATE 42703)` (the filtered call gives the same). BASE: `docs=1 err=<nil>` for both. kept.title: The dimension guard is written before the metadata filters, so every candidate vector is detoasted before a cheap filter can reject its row; the WithMetadataIndexes doc describes the wrong mechanism
kept.summary: Inside the fenced CTE, `vector_dims(embedding) = $1` comes before the metadata predicates (`AND %[3]s`). PostgreSQL keeps quals of equal estimated cost in the order they are written, so vector_dims fully detoasts every row's vector before `(cmetadata ->> 'k') = $n` rejects the row. This defeats the saving the rewrite set out to make whenever no metadata index covers the whole filter. In addition, the new WithMetadataIndexes doc (options.go:92-95) says the metadata predicates narrow rows only after a distance has been computed for each row. For this query that is false, because `<=>` is only in the target list.
kept.failure_scenario: The collection has 40k rows of 1536-dim vectors. A filtered SimilaritySearch whose key has no metadata index (or only a leading-key index, with the other filter keys unindexed) detoasts all 40k vectors. The measured scan time was 296 ms. With the metadata predicate written before vector_dims, the same scan took 15 ms. The distance itself is never computed for rejected rows, contrary to what the option's doc claims.
kept.evidence: Private PG16.13 with pgvector 0.6.0, table vce2l_emb with 40,000 rows of 1536 dims. `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, VERBOSE)` of the exact HEAD statement shape shows `Seq Scan ... Filter: ((collection_id = $0) AND (vector_dims(embedding) = 1536) AND ((cmetadata ->> 'doc_kind') = 'x'))` with `(embedding <=> ...)` only in Output, and Execution Time 296.394 ms. The same query with the metadata predicate written first shows the Filter in that order and Execution Time 15.379 ms. Both have Rows Removed by Filter 40004. Code: pgvector.go:350-351, options.go:92-95.

repro.evidence: On PG 16.13 / pgvector 0.6.0 I built uvf2_emb in the HEAD schema: 40,000 rows of random 1536-dim vectors, 323 MB total with the vectors in TOAST, attstorage 'e'. I ran EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, VERBOSE, BUFFERS) on the exact HEAD statement shape as a prepared statement with params. HEAD order gives Filter `((collection_id = $0) AND (vector_dims(embedding) = 1536) AND ((cmetadata ->> 'doc_kind') = 'x'))`, `<=>` only in Output, Buffers ~160k (hit 129k + read 31k), Execution 271-295 ms. With the metadata predicate written before vector_dims: same plan, Filter order swapped, Buffers 642, Execution 18-21 ms. For a 10%-selective value ('y', 4000 rows kept): 286 ms vs 66 ms. pg_proc shows procost=1 for vector_dims, int4eq, texteq and json_object_field_text, so both quals cost the same and the planner keeps the written order (order_qual_clauses is a stable sort by cost). The WithMetadataIndexes doc (options.go:92-95) says the predicates narrow the rows 'only after a distance has already been computed for each row'. That is false at HEAD: the distance is computed only for surviving rows. The real cost is the vector_dims detoast. Not a regression: BASE hoisted the metadata filters outside the CTE and so detoasted every row of the whole table and computed a distance for it. HEAD is faster than BASE but leaves ~15x on the table.
repro.comment: Inside the fenced CTE, `vector_dims(embedding) = $1` is written before the metadata predicates. All of these quals have the same estimated cost (procost 1), so PostgreSQL keeps the written order. As a result, every row in the collection has its vector fully detoasted before a cheap `(cmetadata ->> 'k') = $n` can reject the row. On PG 16.13 / pgvector 0.6.0 with 40k rows of 1536-dim vectors, EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) of this exact statement shape with an unindexed filter key gives ~160k buffers and 270-295 ms. Moving the metadata predicate ahead of `vector_dims` cuts that to 642 buffers and 18-21 ms, and 286 ms becomes 66 ms for a 10%-selective value. Suggested fix: emit `innerQuery` before the `vector_dims` guard. The ordering vector_dims-before-`<=>` still holds, because `<=>` is only in the target list. Also correct the `WithMetadataIndexes` doc: without an index the cost comes from detoasting in the dims guard; no distance is computed for rows the filter rejects.

refute.reason: The code confirms it. Inside the MATERIALIZED CTE, `vector_dims(embedding) = $1` is written before the metadata predicates (pgvector.go:350-351). Both predicates cost the same to the planner (one function plus one equality operator, default procost 1), so order_qual_clauses keeps them in written order. A 1536-dim vector (~6 KB) is stored out of line, and vector_dims has to detoast it. Every row in the collection is therefore detoasted before a cheap `(cmetadata->>'k') = $n` can reject it. Only a metadata predicate that can raise no error needs to come later, so moving it ahead of vector_dims is safe, and no test pins the current order. The new WithMetadataIndexes doc (options.go:92-95) is also wrong for this query: `<=>` is only in the target list, so no distance is computed for rows that are filtered out. On preexisting: BASE was worse, not better. It ran vector_dims over the whole table in every collection and applied metadata filters outside the CTE. So the full detoast is not a regression; what is new is the missed saving and the incorrect doc.

kept.title: Every store start holds a ShareLock on the embeddings table across ANALYZE, blocking all writers; the doc calls later starts 'a catalog lookup'
kept.summary: The doc comment says that after the first build 'every start afterwards is a catalog lookup'. That is not what happens. CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS takes a ShareLock on the table even when the index exists, because PostgreSQL resolves the relation with its lock before checking IF NOT EXISTS, and init holds that lock until commit. init then runs ANALYZE over the whole table before committing, so every pgvector.New with WithMetadataIndexes blocks every INSERT into the table, from any process, for the whole ANALYZE. This is separate from finding #12 (other store constructions waiting on the advisory lock): here ordinary AddDocuments writers stall. On BASE the same ShareLock from the collection_id index was held only for milliseconds.
kept.failure_scenario: A service restarts, or opens a store per request, with WithMetadataIndexes on a large embeddings table. On each New, concurrent AddDocuments calls from other replicas stall until the ANALYZE sample (up to 30k rows, detoasting each sampled vector) finishes and init commits.
kept.evidence: Probe probes/vce2-analyze-lock/probe_test.go on private PG16.13 with pgvector 0.6.0, table of 40,000 rows of 1536 dims (hot cache). An INSERT was started 30 ms after pgvector.New began. With WithMetadataIndexes=false, New took 7.8 ms and 6.0 ms and the INSERT took 9.9 ms and 3.2 ms. With WithMetadataIndexes=true (index already existing), New took 74 ms and 70 ms and the INSERT took 31 ms and 38 ms, blocked until init committed. ANALYZE's own ShareUpdateExclusiveLock does not conflict with RowExclusiveLock, so the wait is the ShareLock from CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS (utility.c T_IndexStmt: RangeVarGetRelidExtended(..., ShareLock, ..., RangeVarCallbackOwnsRelation) before the existence check), held until commit.

repro.evidence: On PG 16.13 in psql, `BEGIN; CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uvf2_emb_collection_id ...` on an index that already exists prints `NOTICE: ... already exists, skipping`. It still leaves a granted ShareLock on uvf2_emb in pg_locks until commit, and a concurrent INSERT with lock_timeout=300ms fails with 'canceling statement due to lock timeout'. Go probe probes/uvrf-f3 on the 40k x 1536 table, metadata index already present: it waits until another backend holds a granted ShareLock on the table, then issues an INSERT. HEAD with WithMetadataIndexes: New 70-119 ms, INSERT 69-112 ms (blocked for the whole of init). HEAD without it: New 5-8 ms, INSERT 2-4 ms. BASE: New 4-9 ms, INSERT 2-4 ms. The 40k-row table's standalone ANALYZE takes ~47 ms, and the sample grows to 30k rows/pages on large tables. The ShareLock itself is taken already at BASE by the collection_id index, and also by each metadata CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS. What is new is that init keeps the tx open across `ANALYZE` (metadata_index.go:191) before commit, so the writer-blocking window grows from milliseconds to the ANALYZE duration on every New. The doc at metadata_index.go:160 ('every start afterwards is a catalog lookup') is therefore wrong. This is the same statement as already-reported #12, but with a different and more severe consequence (ordinary writers from any process stall, not only store constructions), so it is not a pure duplicate. It could be posted as a reply in #12's thread.
repro.comment: This adds to the ANALYZE comment on line 191. Besides serialising store constructions, it blocks ordinary writers. `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` takes a ShareLock on the table even when the index already exists, because the relation is locked before the existence check, and init holds that lock until commit. Init then runs `ANALYZE` over the whole embeddings table inside the same transaction. As a result, every `pgvector.New` with `WithMetadataIndexes` blocks all INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the table, from any process, for the whole ANALYZE, contrary to 'every start afterwards is a catalog lookup'. Measured on PG 16.13 with 40k x 1536-dim rows and the index already present, using a probe that inserts as soon as it sees the ShareLock: a concurrent INSERT took 69-112 ms (New 70-119 ms). The same probe gave 2-4 ms without metadata indexes and on da7016e. In psql, `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` on an existing index inside an open transaction makes a concurrent INSERT hit lock_timeout. Suggested fix: run ANALYZE only when an index was actually created in this call, for example by checking `pg_indexes`/`to_regclass` first and skipping the CREATE entirely when the index exists. If ANALYZE is kept, run it after commit, outside the locked transaction.

refute.reason: The ShareLock mechanics are right: T_IndexStmt resolves the relation with ShareLock before checking IF NOT EXISTS, and the lock is held until commit. But init already holds that ShareLock in the same transaction in both BASE and HEAD, from `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS <table>_collection_id` (pgvector.go:219-222, and likewise in BASE). The only thing that lengthens the time writers are blocked is the unconditional `ANALYZE` on every start inside the init transaction (metadata_index.go:191). That is the defect already reported as #12, at the same code. Blocked writers are another consequence of it, and the same fix removes both: ANALYZE only after an index is actually built, or outside the init transaction. The misleading 'every start afterwards is a catalog lookup' comment is a symptom of the same unconditional ANALYZE.

kept.judge_reason: The mechanics are confirmed by two independent PG16 probes, and the skeptic accepts them. `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` takes a ShareLock on the table before it checks whether the index exists, and init holds that lock until commit. init then runs an unconditional `ANALYZE` (metadata_index.go:191) before `tx.Commit`, so on every `pgvector.New` with metadata indexes, INSERTs from any process wait for the whole ANALYZE. Measured on 40k×1536: New takes 70–119 ms and a concurrent INSERT is blocked for 69–112 ms. Without metadata indexes, or on BASE, the INSERT takes 2–4 ms. The root cause and the fix are the same as #12. But #12 only says that other store constructions wait on the advisory lock. That undersells the impact, because ordinary AddDocuments writers from every replica stall too. The doc comment at line 160, "every start afterwards is a catalog lookup", is also plainly false. So I keep it at the doc-comment line as an extension of #12, not a pure duplicate. If one thread is preferred, it can go in as a reply to #12 instead.
kept.comment: This comment says "every start afterwards is a catalog lookup", but that isn't true, and the impact is wider than #12 describes. `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` takes a ShareLock on the table before it checks whether the index exists (utility.c resolves the relation with that lock first). init keeps holding the lock through the unconditional `ANALYZE` at line 191 until `tx.Commit`. So every `pgvector.New` with `WithMetadataIndexes` blocks all INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the embeddings table, from every replica, for as long as the ANALYZE runs. The same happens with a store opened per request, or on a restart. On PG16 with a 40k×1536 table where the index already existed, New took 70–119 ms and a concurrent INSERT was blocked for 69–112 ms. Without metadata indexes, and on the previous release, the INSERT took 2–4 ms. The block will be much longer on large or cold tables, where ANALYZE samples up to 30k pages. Suggested fix, which also covers #12: run `ANALYZE` only when an index was actually built, e.g. check `pg_indexes` / `to_regclass` before `CREATE INDEX`, or run it after the init transaction commits. Then update this comment to match.

kept.title: Cohere batches on Bedrock use the default batch size 512, above the vendor's 96-texts-per-call limit (pre-existing)
kept.summary: EmbedDocuments splits texts with b.BatchSize (default 512) and sends each batch as one Cohere InvokeModel `texts` array. Bedrock's Cohere Embed accepts at most 96 texts per call, so any document set larger than 96 fails with the default options. This is not a regression: the PR edited this loop (the variable rename and the new CheckEmbeddings) and kept the limit.

kept.title: Ollama Cloud replay tests always skip in CI; the new cloud assertions and 3 changed cassettes never run
kept.summary: newCloudTestClient skips every TestCloud* test when ~/.ollama/id_ed25519 is missing. Replay does not need the real key: the signature and ts are scrubbed. So CI never runs the cloud tests this PR added or changed.
kept.failure_scenario: CI or any machine without ~/.ollama/id_ed25519 runs `go test ./llms/ollama/`. TestCloudJSONMode (new WarningDrop/WithJSONMode assertions), TestCloudStructuredOutputFallback/{non-streaming,streaming} (new in this PR) and TestCloudGenerateContent/Streaming/ToolCall/WithOptions all report SKIP. Their cassettes TestCloudJSONMode.httprr and TestCloudStructuredOutputFallback-*.httprr, changed or added here, are never replayed. A regression in the Ollama door's cloud structured-output fallback or its drop warning would ship green.
kept.evidence: Full offline run of the 41 httprr packages with a logging overlay of internal/httprr/rr.go: all 8 ollama cloud (sub)tests SKIP with "no ~/.ollama/id_ed25519 ...". These are the only changed non-vectorstore cassettes that no test opened. I then generated a throwaway key (openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 > $TMPHOME/.ollama/id_ed25519) and ran HOME=$TMPHOME go test -run TestCloud -v ./llms/ollama/. Every subtest PASSes (TestCloudGenerateContent, Streaming, ToolCall, JSONMode, StructuredOutputFallback/non-streaming+streaming, WithOptions/*), and a hit-logging overlay shows every record of the 3 changed cassettes replayed. The skip was added deliberately in 22e878f ("skip cloud tests without the local signing key"). A test-generated key under t.TempDir()/t.Setenv("HOME") would make them run everywhere.

repro.evidence: HEAD llms/ollama/ollama_cloud_test.go:46-52 (added in PR commit 22e878f) calls t.Skip when ~/.ollama/id_ed25519 is absent. Running `go test -p 2 -run TestCloud -v ./llms/ollama/` at HEAD in this sandbox (no ~/.ollama) gives SKIP for TestCloudGenerateContent, TestCloudStreaming, TestCloudToolCall, TestCloudJSONMode, TestCloudStructuredOutputFallback/{non-streaming,streaming} and TestCloudWithOptions/{temperature_variation,seed_for_reproducibility}; the package still reports ok. Only TestCloudRefusesAStructuredOutputSchema runs. The PR changed TestCloudJSONMode.httprr and added TestCloudStructuredOutputFallback-{non-streaming,streaming}.httprr (git diff --stat da7016e 355dc71 -- llms/ollama/testdata). I generated a throwaway key with `openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519` in my probe dir and ran the same command with HOME=<probe>/home. Every one of those tests and subtests PASSes against the committed cassettes, so replay does not depend on the real key. .github/workflows/ci.yaml does not provision any Ollama key.
repro.comment: This skip means every `TestCloud*` replay test is skipped on any machine without `~/.ollama/id_ed25519`, and CI is one of those machines. So the new `TestCloudStructuredOutputFallback/{non-streaming,streaming}` tests and the changed `TestCloudJSONMode` assertions never run, and their cassettes are never replayed. The key only has to exist, not be the recording key. I generated a throwaway one (`openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519`), pointed `HOME` at it, and `go test -run TestCloud -v ./llms/ollama/` passes every cloud test and subtest against the committed recordings. Without it, all 8 of them SKIP and the package still reports `ok`. Suggested fix: in `newCloudTestClient`, when replaying, generate an ed25519 key under `t.TempDir()`, write it to `.ollama/id_ed25519` and `t.Setenv("HOME", dir)` instead of skipping. kept.title: Bedrock replay is not hermetic against AWS_CA_BUNDLE or AWS_PROFILE; tests fail spuriously
kept.summary: The PR set out to make the Bedrock replay hermetic (5667829, c2c5872). replayCredentials pins region and static credentials, but config.LoadDefaultConfig still reads the ambient AWS_CA_BUNDLE and AWS_PROFILE. Either one makes every Bedrock replay test fail before any cassette lookup.
kept.failure_scenario: A developer or CI runner with AWS_CA_BUNDLE exported (common behind corporate TLS proxies, and set in this sandbox) runs `go test ./llms/bedrock/`. TestLLM, TestLLMConverse, TestAmazonNova and every other cassette test fail with "unable to add custom RootCAs HTTPClient, has no WithTransportOptions, *http.Client". With AWS_PROFILE naming a profile absent from ~/.aws/config, they fail with "failed to get shared config profile, does-not-exist". The cassettes themselves are fine.
kept.evidence: In HEAD, `go test -run '^TestLLM$|^TestAmazonNova$' ./llms/bedrock/` with AWS_CA_BUNDLE=/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt: FAIL, error quoted above. `env -u AWS_CA_BUNDLE`: all Bedrock tests pass (full run: TestLLM, TestLLMConverse and 30+ TestAmazon* PASS). `env -u AWS_CA_BUNDLE AWS_PROFILE=does-not-exist`: FAIL "failed to get shared config profile, does-not-exist". AWS_CONFIG_FILE/AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE pointing at missing files: still ok. This settles CLAUDE.md item 4: the earlier Bedrock failures came from the environment, not the cassettes. The same LoadDefaultConfig path is used by conformanceClient in llmtest_converse_test.go.

repro.evidence: HEAD setUpTestWithTransport (bedrockllm_test.go:37-39) still calls config.LoadDefaultConfig with WithHTTPClient(&http.Client{Transport: rr}) plus replayCredentials (region and static creds only). LoadDefaultConfig still resolves ambient AWS_CA_BUNDLE and AWS_PROFILE. Ran in HEAD: `go test -count=1 -run '^TestLLM$|^TestAmazonNova$' ./llms/bedrock/` with AWS_CA_BUNDLE=/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt gives FAIL, 'unable to add custom RootCAs HTTPClient, has no WithTransportOptions, *http.Client'. `env -u AWS_CA_BUNDLE` gives ok. `env -u AWS_CA_BUNDLE AWS_PROFILE=does-not-exist` gives FAIL, 'failed to get shared config profile, does-not-exist'. The same LoadDefaultConfig pattern is in llmtest_converse_test.go:51 (conformanceClient), replay_signing_test.go:32 and bedrockllm_test.go:3150/3229. BASE is no better: in BASE TestAmazonNova fails with or without AWS_CA_BUNDLE (it has no replay credentials) and TestLLM skips. So this is not a regression, but the hermetic-replay fix in 5667829/c2c5872 is incomplete. This also answers CLAUDE.md item 4: the earlier Bedrock failures came from the sandbox env, not from the cassettes.
repro.comment: The replay is still not hermetic. `replayCredentials` pins only the region and static credentials, but `config.LoadDefaultConfig` still reads the ambient `AWS_CA_BUNDLE` and `AWS_PROFILE`. With `AWS_CA_BUNDLE` set (common behind corporate TLS proxies), `go test -run '^TestLLM$|^TestAmazonNova$' ./llms/bedrock/` fails before any cassette lookup with `unable to add custom RootCAs HTTPClient, has no WithTransportOptions, *http.Client`. With `AWS_PROFILE=does-not-exist` it fails with `failed to get shared config profile, does-not-exist`. With both unset, all tests pass. The same pattern is in `conformanceClient` (llmtest_converse_test.go) and replay_signing_test.go. Suggested fix: in replay mode, skip `LoadDefaultConfig` and build an `aws.Config{Region: replayRegion, Credentials: ..., HTTPClient: httpClient}` literal, so no shared config or env is consulted. A regression test that sets these variables would keep it that way.

kept.title: WithEndpoint now becomes a REST base URL; the host:port endpoints vertex callers passed produce an unusable URL
kept.summary: WithEndpoint now sets Options.BaseURL, and vertex.New goes through googleai.New. A gRPC-style endpoint such as "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443", the form the old Vertex SDK used and the only form its gRPC transport accepted, now becomes a scheme-less base URL, and every request fails.
kept.failure_scenario: vertex.New(ctx, WithCloudProject(p), WithCloudLocation("us-central1"), WithEndpoint("us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443")) worked in the base because the old SDK takes option.WithEndpoint in host:port form. In HEAD New succeeds, but GenerateContent fails with `Post "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443": unsupported protocol scheme "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com"`, and the model path is lost from the URL. A googleai (Gemini API) caller that passed a host:port endpoint, which the base ignored, now breaks the same way. Vertex callers that passed WithGRPCConn/WithGRPCClient (honored by the base vertex door) now get ErrOptionNotHonored from New. Commit 34fd5d0 had promised these options "keep working for vertex.New", and 4f6589c then routed vertex through googleai.New.
kept.evidence: Probe llms/googleai/vertex (HEAD): with a capturing transport the request URL is `[us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443]`. With a plain http.Client: `gen err: doRequest: error sending request: Post "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443": unsupported protocol scheme ...`. WithGRPCConn(nil) gives `googleai: this client cannot honor WithGRPCConn; ...`. Old SDK cloud.google.com/go/vertexai@v0.12.0 genai/client.go:60-66 builds `endpoint := fmt.Sprintf("%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443", location)` and prepends option.WithEndpoint(endpoint), which the caller's WithEndpoint overrides. The WithEndpoint doc comment still says it appends a ClientOption and does not say a scheme is required.

repro.evidence: HEAD option.go:124 sets opts.BaseURL = endpoint, and new.go:72-74 passes it to genai HTTPOptions.BaseURL. vertex.New (vertex/vertex.go:52) now goes through googleai.New. BASE vertex.New passed ClientOptions to cloud.google.com/go/vertexai@v0.12.0 genai.NewClient. That client builds `%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443` and prepends option.WithEndpoint(endpoint) (genai/client.go:60-66), which the caller's WithEndpoint overrides, so host:port was the expected form (gRPC by default). Probe (overlay, llms/googleai/vertex, HEAD) with project p, location us-central1 and WithEndpoint("us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443"): New returns nil error. With a capturing transport the request URL is `[us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443]`, and the model path is gone. With a plain http.Client: `doRequest: error sending request: Post "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443": unsupported protocol scheme "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com"`. With `https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com` the URL is correct (.../v1beta1/projects/p/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent). WithGRPCConn(nil) makes vertex.New fail with `googleai: this client cannot honor WithGRPCConn; ...`. Commit 34fd5d0 said these options 'keep working for vertex.New'; 4f6589c then routed vertex through googleai.New.
repro.comment: `WithEndpoint` now becomes the genai REST `BaseURL`, and `vertex.New` now goes through `googleai.New`. Vertex callers who passed the endpoint in the host:port form the old Vertex SDK used (`us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443`, its default form, see vertexai@v0.12.0 genai/client.go:60-66) now get a client that cannot send a request. I checked with an overlay probe on vertex.New: New succeeds, then GenerateContent posts to the bare `us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443` without the model path and fails with `unsupported protocol scheme "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com"`. `https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com` works. kept.title: Pinecone results re-sorted by descending score: euclidean indexes now return the farthest match first
kept.summary: getDocumentsFromMatches now sorts every result by Score descending, although for a euclidean-metric index Pinecone's score is a distance (lower is more similar) and Pinecone already returns matches nearest-first.
kept.failure_scenario: A store on a euclidean index: Pinecone returns matches with scores 0.05, 0.4, 1.7 (nearest first). The base kept that order. HEAD returns farthest (1.7), middle, nearest. A retriever with numDocuments/topK then puts the least relevant document first, so chains that use the head of the list use the worst match. Cosine and dotproduct indexes are unaffected.
kept.evidence: Probe vectorstores/pinecone (internal test, overlay) calling store.getDocumentsFromMatches with matches [nearest 0.05, middle 0.4, farthest 1.7]. HEAD prints `farthest 1.7 / middle 0.4 / nearest 0.05`. BASE prints `nearest 0.05 / middle 0.4 / farthest 1.7`. The sort was added in 2ba6eae for test stability. Pinecone documentation (via search; docs.pinecone.io is blocked here) says that for euclidean a lower score means a closer match.

repro.evidence: HEAD vectorstores/pinecone/pinecone.go:213-220 (added in 2ba6eae 'for test stability') sorts every result by Score descending. Probe (overlay, internal test) calling Store{textKey:"text"}.getDocumentsFromMatches with matches [nearest 0.05, middle 0.4, farthest 1.7] and threshold 0. HEAD prints farthest 1.7 / middle 0.4 / nearest 0.05. BASE prints nearest 0.05 / middle 0.4 / farthest 1.7. Pinecone sources found by search (docs.pinecone.io and www.pinecone.io are blocked by the egress proxy here) say that for the euclidean metric lower scores are more similar and results come back most-similar first, i.e. ascending score. Cosine and dotproduct indexes are unaffected. Pre-existing and separate: the score threshold (`>=`, limited to [0,1]) already assumed higher-is-better in BASE.
repro.comment: The new `sort.SliceStable` orders every result by descending `Score`, but on a euclidean-metric Pinecone index the score is a distance (lower = closer), and Pinecone already returns matches nearest-first. So a euclidean-index store now returns the farthest match first, and a retriever or chain that uses the head of the list gets the least relevant document. I checked with an overlay probe on `getDocumentsFromMatches` with scores [0.05, 0.4, 1.7]: HEAD returns 1.7, 0.4, 0.05, while the previous release kept Pinecone's order 0.05, 0.4, 1.7. This relies on Pinecone's documented euclidean semantics (lower score = more similar). Suggested fix: keep the order Pinecone returns and break ties only between equal scores (a stable sort that compares only equal-score neighbours by text), or make the sort direction depend on the index metric.

refute.reason: Commit 2ba6eae adds sort.SliceStable by Score descending in getDocumentsFromMatches, only for test stability. BASE kept Pinecone's order, which is always nearest-first. Pinecone documents that for the euclidean metric the score is a squared distance, where lower means more similar, so HEAD puts the farthest match first on euclidean indexes. The strongest counter-argument is that the existing scoreThreshold filter (score >= threshold) already assumes higher means better, so euclidean was only partly supported in BASE. That flaw is preexisting and applies only when a threshold is set. With no threshold (the default), BASE returned the right order and HEAD reverses it. The store does not restrict or check the metric, so euclidean indexes are a valid input. Sorting only to break ties, or relying on Pinecone's order, would avoid the regression.

Suggested fix: keep the order Pinecone returns and break ties only between equal scores (a stable sort that compares only equal-score neighbours by text), or make the sort direction depend on the index metric.

kept.title: vertex.New with WithHTTPClient silently drops the caller's credentials and ADC
kept.summary: The New doc promises authentication from WithCredentialsFile/JSON or ADC, but when WithHTTPClient is also given the GenAI SDK sends through that client as-is. The credentials are dropped and requests go out without an Authorization header. The PR's own ErrOptionNotHonored message tells gRPC callers to switch to exactly WithHTTPClient.
kept.failure_scenario: vertex.New(ctx, WithCloudProject(p), WithCloudLocation(l), WithCredentialsFile(sa.json), WithHTTPClient(clientWithTimeouts)) succeeds, but every request goes out without Authorization, and Vertex answers 401. With WithHTTPClient and no credential option, ADC is never looked up. A caller who follows the `shape the transport with WithHTTPClient instead` advice after WithGRPCConn is refused ends up in this state.
kept.evidence: Probe llms/googleai/vertex (HEAD) with WithCredentialsJSON(authorized_user JSON) + WithHTTPClient(capturing transport): `new err: <nil>`, `requests: [us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com auth=]` (empty Authorization). The same probe on the BASE gives `new err: WithHTTPClient is incompatible with gRPC dial options`: the combination failed loudly there. genai@v1.42.0 NewClient builds the auth transport (httptransport.NewClient with cc.Credentials) only `if cc.HTTPClient == nil`, and it runs DetectDefault only when HTTPClient is nil.

repro.evidence: HEAD googleai.New (llms/googleai/new.go:41-42, 67-71) sets both config.HTTPClient and config.Credentials. genai@v1.42.0 client.go:278 runs DetectDefault only when `cc.HTTPClient == nil`, and client.go:308-324 builds the authenticated transport (httptransport.NewClient with cc.Credentials) only when `cc.HTTPClient == nil`. When the caller supplies a client, the Credentials are never attached. The SDK documents this: the HTTPClient field says 'For Vertex AI, this client must handle authentication appropriately. Otherwise, call UseDefaultCredentials'. Probe (probes/vx-verify3, vertex.New with WithCloudProject/WithCloudLocation/WithCredentialsJSON(authorized_user)/WithHTTPClient(capturing RT), then GenerateContent) on HEAD: `new err: <nil>`, `requests: [us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com auth=]`, with or without WithRest. BASE, default gRPC path: `new err: WithHTTPClient is incompatible with gRPC dial options`, a loud failure. BASE with WithRest: `requests: [us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443 auth=]`, so the old REST path had the same credential drop, following the google-api-go convention that option.WithHTTPClient overrides the other options. The regression is therefore partial: the default path used to fail at New and now builds a client that sends requests without Authorization. The new vertex.New doc comment (vertex.go:25-29) promises credential/ADC auth, and ErrOptionNotHonored (new.go:93) points gRPC callers to WithHTTPClient, which puts them in this state. Vertex would reject the unauthenticated request (401). That part is the vendor's behaviour and was not run live, but the request provably has no Authorization header.
repro.comment: `vertex.New` promises authentication from `WithCredentialsFile`/`WithCredentialsJSON` or ADC, but once `WithHTTPClient` is also given, the GenAI SDK uses that client as-is. genai v1.42 builds the auth transport and runs `DetectDefault` only when `ClientConfig.HTTPClient == nil`, so the credentials are silently dropped. A probe with `WithCredentialsJSON(...)` + `WithHTTPClient(capturingClient)` shows `vertex.New` succeeding and `GenerateContent` sending to `us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com` with an empty `Authorization` header; Vertex will answer 401 (vendor side, not run live). On the base, the default gRPC path refused this combination at construction (`WithHTTPClient is incompatible with gRPC dial options`), and the new `ErrOptionNotHonored` message now tells gRPC callers to use exactly `WithHTTPClient`. Suggested fix: when a custom HTTP client is combined with named credentials (or Vertex with no API key), wrap it with the credentials, e.g. `httptransport.AddAuthorizationMiddleware` / `ClientConfig.UseDefaultCredentials` on a copy of the client. Otherwise, refuse the combination with a typed error and document that the supplied client must authenticate itself.

refute.reason: Confirmed in code. HEAD googleai.New (llms/googleai/new.go:40-71) puts both config.HTTPClient and config.Credentials, built by detectCredentials, into genai.ClientConfig. genai@v1.42.0 client.go:278 runs DetectDefault only when HTTPClient==nil, and client.go:308-324 wraps Credentials in an auth transport (httptransport.NewClient) also only when HTTPClient==nil. The fix is cheap: when both are set, call httptransport.AddAuthorizationMiddleware or UseDefaultCredentials. On preexisting: BASE rejected the combination loudly on its default gRPC path ("WithHTTPClient is incompatible with gRPC dial options"). With WithRest it went through google-api-go, where WithHTTPClient also overrode the credentials, so that one path already dropped them silently.

kept.title: vertex.New refuses a missing location that the base and both SDKs resolve (default region, GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION)
kept.summary: New returns ErrMissingCloudTarget whenever no location comes from the options or GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION. The base door defaulted to us-central1 (or GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION / CLOUD_ML_REGION), and the new GenAI SDK itself also reads GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION.

kept.evidence: Probe llms/googleai/vertex, run with GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION/REGION/CLOUD_ML_REGION unset except where set by t.Setenv. BASE prints `no location err: <nil>` and `region env err: <nil>`. HEAD prints the ErrMissingCloudTarget message for both. vertexai@v0.12.0 genai/client.go inferLocation falls back to GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION, then CLOUD_ML_REGION, then defaultLocation "us-central1". genai@v1.42.0 NewClient falls back from GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION to GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION. BASE used cloud.google.com/go/vertexai@v0.12.0 genai/client.go:106-118 inferLocation: explicit, then GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION, then CLOUD_ML_REGION, then default us-central1. HEAD line 274 has `func ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string, p Provider) bool`, changed by d07f16d so that Bedrock can exclude Opus 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5. The commit message does not mention compatibility. Probe (probes/verify-sig-f2, an external reasoning_test file calling `reasoning.ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget("claude-opus-4-5")`): BASE compiles and prints true. HEAD fails to build with `not enough arguments in call to reasoning.ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget; have (string) want (string, reasoning.Provider)`. The in-repo callers (anthropic, bedrockclient) were updated. Of the exported funcs in llms/reasoning, this is the only one whose signature changed (DefaultIsReasoningModel only gained a nolint comment). The break is only at compile time, not a silent behaviour change, and it only matters to applications that call this helper directly, so the severity is low.
repro.comment: This changes the signature of the exported helper `reasoning.ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget` from `func(string) bool` to `func(string, Provider) bool`. Any application that calls `reasoning.ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model)` stops compiling after this release. A probe calling it with only a model compiles and returns true on da7016e, and fails on 355dc71 with `not enough arguments ... want (string, reasoning.Provider)`. The Bedrock distinction from d07f16d is correct, but it can be added without breaking callers. Keep `ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string) bool` as the first-party answer (equal to the new function with `ProviderAnthropic`), and add a provider-aware variant such as `ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudgetOn(model, p)` for the doors. If the break is intentional, note it in the release notes.

refute.reason: BASE exports func ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string) bool in the public llms/reasoning package. HEAD changes it to (model string, p Provider), which breaks compilation for any external caller. d07f16d had a real reason: Opus 4.5 accepts effort with a budget on the first-party API but not on Bedrock. It still could have kept the old name as a first-party wrapper. The rest of this PR does keep compatibility shims: WithRest stays as a no-op 'so callers keep compiling' (4f6589c), and there are Deprecated markers in count_tokens.go and options.go. That makes this silent signature break inconsistent with the release's own policy. Severity is low, because it is a narrow capability helper that is mostly used internally, but I found no evidence that the break was intended for external callers.
