dropped.title: Hint reports default-on Claude as disablable on ProviderOpenAI while the openai door refuses the off on OpenRouter
dropped.summary: For a default-on Claude on ProviderOpenAI, CannotDisable comes from ResolveOff, which answers OffDisableThinkingObject for an anthropic/ route. The openai door refuses that off on public hosts (sendsClaudeThinkingObject needs !publicProviderHost), so the hint and the door disagree on OpenRouter.
dropped.failure_scenario: ReasoningSupportFor("anthropic/claude-sonnet-5", ProviderOpenAI).CannotDisable == false, so a UI shows the off switch. The same model on openai.New(WithBaseURL("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1")) with WithReasoningDisabled() returns ErrReasoningOffUnsupported. anthropic/claude-opus-5 behaves the same way.
dropped.evidence: Probe TestProbeHintOR (llms/openai): anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 cannotDisable=false doorErr=`reasoning cannot be disabled`; anthropic/claude-opus-5 same. Door: openaillm.go setReasoningOff, case OffDisableThinkingObject with ClaudeThinkingDefaultsOn && !sendsClaudeThinkingObject.

repro.evidence: Probe TestProbeV3Hint (llms/openai, internal test that reuses sendOffToHost from claude_thinking_off_route_test.go) at HEAD 355dc71: for anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, anthropic/claude-opus-5 and bare claude-sonnet-5, llms.ReasoningSupportFor(m, ProviderOpenAI).CannotDisable=false. With WithReasoningDisabled(), http://openrouter.ai/api/v1 returns `reasoning cannot be disabled for model ...` and sends no request, while api.anthropic.com/v1 and a private LiteLLM host send {thinking:{type:disabled}}. Cause: the hint calls reasoning.ResolveOff(model, p), which returns OffDisableThinkingObject for a default-on Claude on a bare or anthropic/ route (off.go:69-75). setReasoningOff (openaillm.go:605-607) refuses that off when !sendsClaudeThinkingObject, and sendsClaudeThinkingObject needs !publicProviderHost(o.host); openrouter.ai is in APIKeyRequiredBaseURLs. The hint only receives (model, provider), so it cannot tell the hosts apart. The field doc (reasoning_support.go:22-25) promises that CannotDisable is set for models known to reject disabling, and here the library itself rejects the off locally. BASE: the refusal came in with commits d861f6e/0bd22a3 in this PR. Low impact: only a UI hint is wrong, and the call fails with a typed error, not silently.
repro.comment: For a default-on Claude on `ProviderOpenAI`, `CannotDisable` comes from `ResolveOff`, which answers `OffDisableThinkingObject` for a bare or `anthropic/` name. The openai door refuses that off on any public provider host, because `setReasoningOff` → `sendsClaudeThinkingObject` requires `!publicProviderHost`. So `ReasoningSupportFor("anthropic/claude-sonnet-5", ProviderOpenAI).CannotDisable == false` and a UI shows the off switch. The same model on `openai.New(WithBaseURL("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"))` with `WithReasoningDisabled()` returns `ErrReasoningOffUnsupported` before any request is sent. I checked this with a probe: sonnet-5 and opus-5 are refused on openrouter.ai and sent on a private LiteLLM host, and the hint says disablable in both cases. The hint takes no host, so either document that `CannotDisable` is host-independent on ProviderOpenAI, or report the conservative answer (true) when the off depends on a gateway that forwards the thinking object.

refute.reason: The mismatch comes from the API's design, not from a bug. ReasoningSupportFor(model, provider) takes no host, and ProviderOpenAI covers many hosts: the LiteLLM-style gateway, where anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 does accept thinking:{disabled}, and resellers like OpenRouter, where it does not. The field doc also treats CannotDisable=false as best-effort: it is set only for models known to reject disabling. Commit d861f6e made this split on purpose. It moved the route allow-list into ResolveOff (so the hint reports CannotDisable for the deepinfra/, perplexity/ and openrouter/ routes it can see from the name). It left the host check in the door, which fails before any request is sent with a typed ErrReasoningOffUnsupported. That commit's own test pins this refusal on OpenRouter. The caller gets an explicit error, not silent misbehaviour. BASE was worse: its hint also said the model could be disabled, while its door fell through (OffDisableClaude was not handled) and sent nothing, so the model kept thinking with no error. Fixing this would need a host-aware hint API, which is a feature request, not a regression.

dropped.judge_reason: The behaviour is real, but it is neither a defect nor a regression, so it does not need an inline comment. At HEAD, `ReasoningSupportFor("anthropic/claude-sonnet-5", ProviderOpenAI)` calls `ResolveOff`, which returns `OffDisableThinkingObject` (off.go:69-75), so `CannotDisable` is false. On an OpenRouter base URL, the door's `setReasoningOff` (openaillm.go:605-607) refuses the off because `sendsClaudeThinkingObject` requires `!publicProviderHost`. The disagreement comes from the API's design. `ReasoningSupportFor(model, provider)` has no host parameter. The same `anthropic/…` name on `ProviderOpenAI` is served both by LiteLLM-style private gateways, where the door does send `thinking:{type:disabled}`, and by OpenRouter, where it refuses. So the hint is correct for one host class and cannot tell the two apart. The type is documented as a best-effort hint that is "never authoritative". The PR made the part it can see from the name route-aware on purpose: `ClaudeThinkingObjectRoute` in `ResolveOff` gives `CannotDisable` for deepinfra/, openrouter/ and similar prefixes. When the hint is wrong, the caller gets a typed `ErrReasoningOffUnsupported` before any request is sent, not silent misbehaviour. BASE was worse on the same path. I checked BASE: its hint also said `CannotDisable=false` (`ResolveOff` returned `OffDisableClaude` for default-on Claude on `ProviderOpenAI`), but its `setReasoningOff` handled only `OffUnsupported` and `OffEffortNone`. The off was therefore a silent no-op on every host, and the model kept thinking. The PR makes this path strictly better. Fixing the remaining gap would need a host-aware hint API, which is a feature request, not a release blocker.

dropped.title: Exported ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget changed signature (added Provider)
dropped.summary: The public function reasoning.ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string) became ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string, p Provider). It is the only exported signature change in the package, and no README or doc in the diff mentions it.
dropped.failure_scenario: A downstream application that calls reasoning.ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget("claude-opus-4-5") no longer compiles against this release.
dropped.evidence: Compared exported declarations of llms/reasoning between BASE and HEAD (grep of ^func/^type, comm -23). The only changed exported signature is ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget. Commit d07f16d introduced the provider argument on purpose (Opus 4.5 rejects effort with budget on Bedrock).

repro.evidence: BASE llms/reasoning/claude_capability.go:107 has `func ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string) bool`. HEAD claude_capability.go:274 has `func ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string, p Provider) bool`, introduced deliberately in d07f16d because Opus 4.5 rejects effort with budget on Bedrock. The function is exported, so any external call with one argument stops compiling. `git diff da7016e 355dc71 -- '*.md'` has no mention of the function, and there is no CHANGELOG entry. ClaudeEffortsFor and ClaudeClampEffort are new in HEAD, so they break nothing. In-repo callers were all updated.
repro.comment: This changes the signature of an exported function: `reasoning.ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string)` becomes `ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string, p Provider)`. Downstream code that calls `reasoning.ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget("claude-opus-4-5")` no longer compiles against this release, and neither the README nor the release notes mention it. The provider argument is justified (d07f16d: Opus 4.5 rejects effort+budget on Bedrock). To keep the API compatible, keep the one-argument function (e.g. as a deprecated wrapper that assumes the Anthropic API) and add a new provider-aware function such as `ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudgetOn(model, p)`. Otherwise, call out the break in the release notes.

refute.reason: The change is intentional and needed for correctness. Commit d07f16d measured that Opus 4.5 accepts effort with a budget on the first-party API but returns 400 on Bedrock, so a single-argument, model-only predicate cannot give the right answer. It is a loud compile-time break, not a silent behaviour change. The release rule is about not breaking callers silently. The function is a low-level capability helper whose package doc describes it as shared by the provider adapters, and all in-repo callers were updated. The module is github.com/vxcontrol/langchaingo with no major-version suffix (v0 semver), so no API stability is promised. A downstream caller gets a clear compiler error with an obvious fix (pass the provider). At most, the release notes could mention it; that is not a defect in the code.

dropped.judge_reason: Not a defect worth an inline comment. The signature change is real: BASE claude_capability.go:107 has ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string), and HEAD :274 has ClaudeSupportsEffortWithBudget(model string, p Provider). Commit d07f16d made the change on purpose. Its measurements show that Opus 4.5 accepts output_config.effort with a thinking budget on the first-party API but gets a 400 on Bedrock, so a predicate that looks only at the model name cannot be right for both providers. All three in-repo callers (anthropicllm.go:215, bedrockclient_converse.go:211, provider_anthropic.go:865) pass the provider explicitly. The break shows up at compile time, and the fix for a caller is obvious. The release rule is about not breaking callers silently, and this break is not silent. The module is github.com/vxcontrol/langchaingo with no /vN suffix, so it is v0 semver with no stability promise. The function first appeared in the previous release (1fc1299, 2026-07-17). The package doc describes it as a low-level capability helper shared by the provider adapters, and the high-level public entry point for applications is llms.ReasoningSupportFor. A repo-wide comparison of exported signatures shows it is the only change here that breaks existing call sites; the other changes are moves, type aliases or added variadic parameters. At most it deserves a line in the release notes. It does not need a code change.

dropped.title: Efforts doc says empty means unknown or no effort, but Gemini 3 is Known, takes levels and has empty Efforts
dropped.summary: The new doc on ReasoningSupport.Efforts says it is empty only when the model is unknown or takes no effort. The Google branch returns Known=true, Mechanism=Adaptive and Efforts=nil for Gemini 3.x, whose door maps minimal, low, medium and high to thinking_level.
dropped.failure_scenario: A UI that follows the documented contract (read Mechanism and Efforts; empty Efforts on a Known model means no effort control) hides the effort selector for gemini-3-pro-preview and gemini-3-flash-preview, although googleai's thinkingLevelForEffort sends LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH for them.
dropped.evidence: Code: reasoning_support.go:139-153 has the comment 'Efforts stays unset: this package does not classify the Google level names' and sets Mechanism Adaptive for GeminiUsesThinkingLevel. reasoning_support_test.go TestGoogleHintNamesItsMechanism expects Known and Adaptive for gemini-3-pro-preview, and TestNonOpenAIModelsKeepTheirOwnBranch expects empty Efforts. googleai.go:1155-1157 and 1243-1258 map efforts to thinking levels.

repro.evidence: At HEAD, llms/reasoning_support.go:28-29 documents Efforts as 'empty both when the model is unknown and when it takes none'. The Google branch (lines 139-153) returns Known=true and Supported=true, sets Mechanism=Adaptive for GeminiUsesThinkingLevel/GeminiTogglesThinkingByLevel, and leaves Efforts nil. Its own comment says 'Efforts stays unset: this package does not classify the Google level names'. The googleai door does take efforts for these models: in resolveThinkingConfig (googleai.go:1155-1157), thinkingLevelForEffort (googleai.go:1243-1258) maps minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max to MINIMAL/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH thinking_level. I ran a probe (overlay test in ./llms) at HEAD. It printed gemini-3-pro-preview and gemini-3-flash-preview as Known=true Supported=true Mechanism=1 (Adaptive) Efforts=[], and gemini-2.5-flash as Mechanism=2 (Budget). BASE (da7016e) also returned Known=true Efforts=[] for Gemini 3, but its doc said only 'nil when unknown', which was already inconsistent. The PR rewrote the doc and made it more specific, and the new text is still false for Gemini 3.x. The harm is limited to the UI hint and the documented contract; the wire path is unaffected.
repro.comment: The new doc on `ReasoningSupport.Efforts` says it is empty only when the model is unknown or takes no effort. The Google branch below contradicts this. For Gemini 3.x (`gemini-3-pro-preview`, `gemini-3-flash-preview`), `ReasoningSupportFor(..., ProviderGoogleAI)` returns `Known=true`, `Mechanism=Adaptive` and `Efforts=[]`, yet the googleai door's `thinkingLevelForEffort` sends MINIMAL/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH `thinking_level` for those efforts. I checked this with a probe test in `./llms`: HEAD prints `Known=true Mechanism=1 Efforts=[]` for both models. A UI that follows the documented contract would treat the model as taking no effort and hide the effort selector. Suggested fix: fill `Efforts` for the thinking-level Gemini models (low/medium/high, plus minimal where `GeminiAcceptsMinimalLevel`), or reword the doc so that empty `Efforts` on a Known model with an Adaptive mechanism means the tiers are unclassified.

refute.reason: The failure depends on a paraphrase of the doc, not on the doc itself. reasoning_support.go:28-29 says Efforts is empty both for unknown models and for models that take no effort, "so read Mechanism before offering a control". It does not say that empty Efforts on a Known model means no effort control. For Gemini 3.x the Google branch returns Mechanism=ReasoningMechanismAdaptive. The field doc and the const doc from commit 69ff140 define that value as "takes an effort level", so a UI that follows the documented contract offers an effort selector and does not hide it. Empty Efforts is deliberate: the branch comment says "Efforts stays unset: this package does not classify the Google level names", in line with the type's rule not to invent tiers it cannot back (commit 69ff140). The list of empty-Efforts cases is at most incomplete, since it omits a known level model whose tiers are not listed. That is a wording nit, not a behaviour defect. The cited test TestNonOpenAIModelsKeepTheirOwnBranch covers gemini-2.5-flash, a budget model, not Gemini 3. The mismatch is also preexisting: BASE already returned Known=true with nil Efforts for Gemini while its doc said "nil when unknown".

dropped.judge_reason:
This is at most a wording gap in the docs, and the failure scenario does not follow from them. The facts check out: at HEAD the Google branch returns Known=true, Mechanism=Adaptive and Efforts=nil for Gemini 3.x (reasoning_support.go:139-153), and the googleai door maps minimal, low, medium and high to thinking_level (googleai.go:1155-1157, 1243-1258).

The documented contract does not tell a UI to hide the effort selector:
- The field doc (lines 28-29) says to read Mechanism before offering a control. The Mechanism doc (lines 31-32) defines Adaptive as taking an effort level, so a UI that follows the docs offers an effort control for Gemini 3.
- The type-level doc (lines 14-15) already covers this case: 'unknown effort tiers and default state are left nil rather than guessed'. The Google tiers are left unclassified on purpose, as the branch comment says ('Efforts stays unset: this package does not classify the Google level names').

Commit 53c3215 wrote the field doc to warn that budget-only models also report empty Efforts. The field doc's list of empty cases leaves out 'Known level model whose tiers are not listed', but read together with the type doc and the Mechanism doc the contract holds. The behaviour is also preexisting: BASE returned Known=true with nil Efforts for Gemini, and the PR changes neither the wire path nor what Gemini 3 reports in Efforts. A comment here would only suggest a wording tweak and is not worth a release-review inline comment.

dropped.title: Anthropic door refuses forced tool choice plus reasoning for non-Claude models, unlike the shared guard
dropped.summary: The door's inline check refuses any model whose thinking resolved to "enabled". Every model the door does not classify, including non-Claude models behind Anthropic-compatible endpoints, resolves to budget thinking, so all of them are refused locally. The shared llms.CheckClaudeTurnLimits, and the Bedrock door after commit cfd6ad0, only apply the rule to Claude thinking generations. The two copies of the rule already disagree.
dropped.failure_scenario: anthropic.New(WithBaseURL(<Anthropic-compatible endpoint>), WithModel("deepseek-chat" | "kimi-k2-thinking" | "glm-4.6" | "MiniMax-M2")) + WithReasoning(High,0) + WithTools + WithToolChoice("any") fails before any request with ErrForcedToolUseWithThinking ('model "deepseek-chat" runs manual thinking...'). BASE sent the request. llms.CheckClaudeTurnLimits returns nil for the same inputs.
dropped.evidence: Probe probes/anth2-nonclaude, for 4 non-Claude names: "anthropic door err=model \"deepseek-chat\" runs manual thinking, which rejects a forced tool choice ... sent=false | shared CheckClaudeTurnLimits=<nil>" (same for the others). Commit cfd6ad0 made this fix for Bedrock ("Every non-Claude family therefore counted as manual thinking ... Gate it on the model being a Claude thinking generation"), but the Anthropic door's check from 272ae0b was never gated. Whether each third-party endpoint accepts forced tool choice together with thinking is vendor behaviour I could not check; their docs host was blocked by the egress proxy.

repro.evidence: Own probe probes/v3-anthnonclaude: anthropic.New(WithBaseURL(test server), WithModel(m)) + WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0) + WithTools + WithToolChoice("any"). HEAD, for deepseek-chat, kimi-k2-thinking, glm-4.6 and MiniMax-M2: err='model "..." runs manual thinking, which rejects a forced tool choice; use tool_choice auto or none', no request sent. BASE sent the request for all of them: {..."tool_choice":"any","thinking":{"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":8192}}. The inline check at anthropicllm.go:235 (commit 272ae0b) keys off thinking.Type=="enabled", which every unclassified name resolves to. The shared llms.CheckClaudeTurnLimitsOnWire (turn.go:128-133) additionally requires reasoning.ClaudeSupportsThinking(model), and cfd6ad0 applied that gate to Bedrock for this exact reason, so the two copies of the rule disagree. Mitigation: the door does send a manual-thinking payload to these endpoints, so an endpoint that copies Anthropic's rule would reject the request anyway. Vendor docs could not be read (api-docs.deepseek.com and dev.to blocked by egress). Search snippets suggest Kimi's Anthropic-style API shows tool_choice any, and MiniMax supports only auto/none. Whether a refusal is wrong therefore depends on the endpoint.
repro.comment: This inline forced-tool guard refuses any model whose thinking resolved to `enabled`, and every model name the door does not classify resolves to budget thinking. So non-Claude models behind Anthropic-compatible endpoints (`deepseek-chat`, `kimi-k2-thinking`, `glm-4.6`, `MiniMax-M2`) with WithReasoning + WithToolChoice("any") now fail locally with ErrForcedToolUseWithThinking, where the base sent the request (probe: HEAD err before any request, BASE sent `tool_choice:"any"` + `thinking:{type:enabled}`). The shared `llms.CheckClaudeTurnLimitsOnWire` returns nil for the same inputs because it also requires `reasoning.ClaudeSupportsThinking(model)`, and cfd6ad0 added that gate to Bedrock for this reason, so the two copies of the rule now disagree. Whether each third-party endpoint accepts forced tool choice together with thinking is vendor behaviour I could not confirm (their docs were unreachable from here). Suggest gating on `reasoning.ClaudeSupportsThinking(model)` or calling the shared guard, so the rule lives in one place.

refute.reason: For every model the Anthropic door does not classify, it actually sends thinking {type:"enabled", budget_tokens} on the wire (anthropicllm.go ~207). That is the difference from Bedrock: commit cfd6ad0 gated the Bedrock guard because Bedrock sends no thinking payload for non-Claude families. Keying the Anthropic door's check to the payload it sends (thinking.Type == "enabled") is consistent with the rule, not a divergence from it. Vendor behaviour also contradicts the claim for the main example. DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible API enables thinking by default. Public reports (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3 issue #1376, langchain issue #40769, any-llm #1384) show DeepSeek rejects forced or named tool_choice in thinking mode with 400 "Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice". So BASE's request would have failed at the vendor anyway, and the local typed refusal only saves a round trip. Kimi's thinking models likewise limit tool_choice to auto/none. The claim that these endpoints accept forced tool use together with thinking is an unverified assumption, and the evidence available points the other way.

dropped.judge_reason:
The mechanism is real, but it does not break anything. For any model name it does not classify, the Anthropic door sends thinking {type:"enabled", budget_tokens} on the wire (anthropicllm.go ~207-211). The check at line 235 keys off that exact payload, so it follows the rule for what is actually sent.

Commit cfd6ad0 gated only the Bedrock door, and its message gives the reason: "no thinking payload is ever sent for them" on Bedrock. The shared CheckClaudeTurnLimitsOnWire is used by doors (Bedrock, OpenAI) that send no Anthropic thinking payload for non-Claude families. So the two copies of the rule differ because the doors send different requests, not because one of them is wrong.

Vendor evidence goes against the failure scenario for every example model:
- DeepSeek returns HTTP 400 "Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice" for forced or named tool_choice in thinking mode (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3#1376, langchain#40769, any-llm#1384).
- Kimi docs: with thinking enabled, tool_choice can only be "auto" or "none".
- MiniMax's Anthropic-compatible API supports only auto and none for tool_choice.

The BASE request would have come back 400 from the vendor anyway. HEAD only turns that round trip into a typed local error. Any endpoint where the refusal is actually wrong would be a speculative proxy case with no evidence behind it.

dropped.title: Forced-tool guard misses Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, which reject forced tool use on every request
dropped.summary: The new guard refuses a forced tool choice only under manual (budget) thinking. Anthropic documents that Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 reject tool_choice any/tool on every request, so these calls still go out and come back as a vendor 400 instead of the typed error.
dropped.failure_scenario: WithModel("claude-opus-5-5" | "claude-fable-5-1" | "claude-mythos-5-1") + WithTools + WithToolChoice("any"), with or without WithReasoning. The request is sent, and per the vendor docs it returns 400. claude-sonnet-4-5 with reasoning gets the local typed error.
dropped.evidence: Probe probes/anth2-forced: claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5-1 and claude-mythos-5-1 print "err=<nil> sentRequest=true" for both the default and the reasoning variants. claude-sonnet-4-5 with reasoning prints the ErrForcedToolUseWithThinking message. Vendor doc https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking ('Response prefill and forced tool use'): "The exceptions are Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Mythos 5.1, which reject forced tool use on every request with a 400 error."

repro.evidence: HEAD llms/anthropic/anthropicllm.go:235 refuses a forced tool choice only when `thinking.Type == "enabled"` (manual/budget thinking). The Bedrock-side twin, llms/turn.go:133 CheckClaudeTurnLimitsOnWire, likewise checks only `budgetThinking`. Neither looks at the model. My probe probes/vfy-anth-ultra (TestProbeVfyForced, httptest server that captures the body) gave these results at HEAD: claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5-1 and claude-mythos-5-1, with and without WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0), return err=<nil> and send tool_choice={type:any} (the reasoning variant also sends thinking={type:adaptive}). claude-sonnet-4-5 with reasoning returns the local ErrForcedToolUseWithThinking and sends nothing. Vendor doc https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking, section 'Response prefill and forced tool use', says: "The exceptions are Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Mythos 5.1, which reject forced tool use on every request with a 400 error. On those models, use tool_choice: {\"type\": \"auto\"} with strict tool use or structured outputs instead." The same page's 'Tool choice limitation' item repeats the exception. At BASE the same models also send the request (BASE even sends tool_choice as the bare string "any") and BASE has no guard for any model. So this is not a regression. It is a gap in the new guard: the newest models get a vendor 400 instead of the typed error. The failure is loud, not silent, so severity is low.
repro.comment: The new forced-tool guard fires only under manual (budget) thinking. Anthropic's thinking docs ('Response prefill and forced tool use') say Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 reject `tool_choice` `any`/`tool` on *every* request with a 400. I pointed `anthropic.New(WithModel("claude-opus-5-5" | "claude-fable-5-1" | "claude-mythos-5-1"))` at a capturing httptest server and called it with `WithTools` + `WithToolChoice("any")`, with and without `WithReasoning`: each call returns err=nil and sends `tool_choice:{type:any}`. The real API would answer with a 400, while claude-sonnet-4-5 with reasoning gets the local `ErrForcedToolUseWithThinking`. This is not a regression (the base had no guard), but the typed error misses exactly the models the vendor calls out. Suggested fix: add a model-level predicate in `reasoning` (e.g. `ClaudeRejectsForcedToolUse(model)` covering opus-5-5/fable-5-1/mythos-5-1 and their -latest aliases) and apply it in both this guard and `llms.CheckClaudeTurnLimitsOnWire` (Bedrock), with an error message that points to `auto` plus strict tools or structured output. The 400 itself comes from the vendor docs; I did not observe it on a live call.

refute.reason: The vendor doc does say Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 refuse forced tool use on every request, but leaving them unguarded was a deliberate choice. Commit 4d72434 ('test(anthropic): pin that Fable takes a forced tool choice') quotes that vendor statement and declines to add the restriction: Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 'have no route here, so the restriction cannot be checked and must not be guessed onto the family'. The same commit adds TestFableTakesAForcedToolChoiceWithoutThinking to keep the request going out. The guard added in 272ae0b is scoped on purpose to what the maintainers could verify: manual (type=enabled) thinking, at anthropicllm.go:235 and llms/turn.go CheckClaudeTurnLimitsOnWire. Missing it does not break callers silently. The call still fails loudly, only with the vendor's 400 instead of the local typed error. BASE had no guard at all and sent the same request, so nothing regresses. At most this is a nice-to-have extension, not a release defect.

dropped.judge_reason:
The vendor claim is accurate. Anthropic's docs, and the bundled claude-api reference, say Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 return 400 for tool_choice any/tool on every request. The guard at anthropicllm.go:235 does not cover them, so those calls reach the vendor. It is still not a release defect worth an inline comment, for four reasons.
(1) It is not a regression. BASE had no guard, and it sent tool_choice as the bare string "any", a shape bce683d fixed as invalid ("send the tool choice in the shape Messages accepts"). So forced tool choice did not work at BASE for any model.
(2) The failure is loud, not silent. The caller gets the vendor's 400 ("tool_choice: type \"tool\" and \"any\" are not supported for this model"), only not the local typed error.
(3) The guard does what it says. 272ae0b scopes ErrForcedToolUseWithThinking to the manual-thinking rule, a different, mode-dependent restriction; a model-wide ban would need its own error. The Bedrock twin in llms/turn.go is scoped the same way.
(4) The maintainers weighed this exact vendor statement and declined it on purpose. Commit 4d72434 quotes it and says Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 "have no route here, so the restriction cannot be checked and must not be guessed onto the family". It also pins TestFableTakesAForcedToolChoiceWithoutThinking, because claude-fable-5 accepts forced tool choice and a family-wide gate would break it.
Opus 5.5 appears only as a name in a reasoning-detection test and is otherwise unclassified. Adding it would be a follow-up enhancement, not a blocker for this release.

dropped.title: In-memory result-ordering fix has no test; the existing test tolerates unsorted results
dropped.summary: inmemory.SimilaritySearch now sorts results by score instead of reversing the hnsw heap. The change is in a commit titled refactor(tests) and has no test pinning it. TestMockSimilarityScoreCalculation still searches for the highest score itself, so it passes with the old unsorted output and would not notice the bug coming back.
dropped.failure_scenario: On BASE, 20 documents and a top-8 search return scores in the order 0.96, 0.57, 0.79, 0.93, 0.98, 0.83, 0.995, 1.0, so retrievers and chains take a low-scoring document first. HEAD returns them sorted. Removing the SortStableFunc at inmemory.go:181 would pass every test in the package.
dropped.evidence: Probe vectorstores/inmemory/zz_probe_trc_inmem_test.go run on both checkouts. HEAD: `sorted=true [d0:1.0000 d1:0.9954 d2:0.9821 ...]`. BASE: `sorted=false [d3:0.9611 d15:0.5713 d8:0.7938 d4:0.9338 ...]`. The production change is in commit a412982 'refactor(tests): streamline test setup…'. The only other change to inmemory_test.go is the httprr migration.

repro.evidence: The production change is real. At HEAD, inmemory.go:181 replaces slices.Reverse with SortStableFunc by descending score. Probe /tmp/.../scratchpad/probes/v3inmem/probe_test.go adds 20 docs and runs a top-8 search. HEAD: sorted=true d0:1.0000 d1:0.9910 ... d7:0.8040. BASE: sorted=false d7:0.8040 d6:0.8577 ... d0:1.0000, i.e. ascending, lowest score first. But the key claim, that removing the sort would pass every test in the package, is wrong. I ran the package tests at HEAD with an overlay of inmemory.go that puts back `slices.Reverse(docs)`, and again with no ordering at all. Both runs fail TestInMemoryAsRetrieverWithScoreThreshold (inmemory_test.go:365) and TestInMemoryAsRetrieverWithMetadataFilterNotSelected (inmemory_test.go:440) with `cached HTTP response not found`. The recorded chat request embeds the retrieved documents in score order, so the cassettes pin the ordering. The unmodified package passes. The ordering is therefore covered, if only indirectly through the cassettes, and a regression would be noticed. TestMockSimilarityScoreCalculation does tolerate unsorted output, but that alone doesn't leave the fix unpinned.

refute.reason: The central claim is false: removing the sort would not pass every test in the package. I ran a mutation through an overlay, replacing slices.SortStableFunc at inmemory.go:181 with the old slices.Reverse. Two tests fail with an httprr cassette mismatch: TestInMemoryAsRetrieverWithScoreThreshold and TestInMemoryAsRetrieverWithMetadataFilterNotSelected. Their recorded chat/completions request bodies pin the order in which retrieved documents are put into the RetrievalQA prompt. An unsorted result changes the request body, and replay fails. The unmodified package passes. The ordering is therefore pinned, if indirectly. That TestMockSimilarityScoreCalculation itself tolerates unsorted output is at most a nice-to-have for an explicit unit test, not an unguarded regression.

dropped.title: WithMaxRetries(0) means one attempt for embeddings but five for chat on the same Model
dropped.summary: The new embeddings retry loop treats maxRetries as a total attempt count and turns 0 into 1. The chat SDK turns 0 into its default of 5, and the option's doc says 'maximum number of retries'. So one setting gives different retry behaviour on the two surfaces of one Model, and WithMaxRetries(1) allows no retry at all on embeddings.
dropped.failure_scenario: mistral.New(WithMaxRetries(0)) against a server answering 503: CreateEmbedding sends 1 request and Call sends 5. With WithMaxRetries(1), embeddings are never retried, although the doc promises up to one retry.
dropped.evidence: Probe probes/mho2-mistral/probe_test.go TestProbeMistralZeroRetries printed: 'WithMaxRetries(0) embeddings attempts: 1' and 'WithMaxRetries(0) chat attempts: 5'. mistral-go client.go NewMistralClient maps maxRetries==0 to DefaultMaxRetries=5 and loops i<maxRetries. client_options.go WithMaxRetries doc: 'maximum number of retries'.

repro.evidence: HEAD mistralembed.go:72-75 does `attempts := maxRetries; if attempts < 1 { attempts = 1 }`. The chat path goes through mistral-go v1.1.0 NewMistralClient, which maps maxRetries==0 to DefaultMaxRetries=5 and loops `i < maxRetries`. New() defaults maxRetries to sdk.DefaultMaxRetries (5), so only an explicit WithMaxRetries(0) diverges. Probe probes/ultra-vrf-mho3/mis/probe2_test.go counted transport attempts with a 503 server: chat with WithMaxRetries(0) made 5 transport attempts, while CreateEmbedding made 1. On the wire it depends on the 503 body. With an empty body the server got 5 chat hits; with a JSON body it got 1 hit plus 4 local "ContentLength=165 with Body length 0" failures, because the SDK reuses a drained request body. At BASE, embeddings also went through the SDK, so WithMaxRetries(0) behaved like chat does now. Part of the finding is refuted: WithMaxRetries(1) gives 1 attempt on both surfaces and at BASE. The SDK treats the value as a total attempt count, so this is not a divergence. The 'maximum number of retries' doc is pre-existing and inaccurate for both surfaces alike.
repro.comment: The new embeddings retry loop treats `maxRetries <= 0` as one attempt, but the chat path still goes through mistral-go's `NewMistralClient`, which maps `0` to `DefaultMaxRetries` (5). So an explicit `WithMaxRetries(0)` means one attempt for `CreateEmbedding` and five for `Call`/`GenerateContent` on the same Model. At the base release, embeddings went through the SDK too, so both surfaces agreed. A probe against a 503 server counted 1 transport attempt for embeddings and 5 for chat. (How many of those 5 reach the server depends on the SDK reusing a drained body; with a JSON error body only the first goes out.) For N >= 1 both surfaces agree, because the SDK also counts total attempts; only `WithMaxRetries`'s "maximum number of retries" doc is wrong there. Suggested fix: pick one meaning for 0. Either map it to `sdk.DefaultMaxRetries` in the embeddings path too, or pass the SDK 1 when the caller asks for 0. Then correct the option doc to say it is a total attempt count.

refute.reason: For values of 1 or more, the new embeddings loop means the same thing as the chat SDK. mistral-go client.go loops i < maxRetries, so WithMaxRetries(1) is one attempt on chat as well. Commit 55c4161 and its test TestTheEmbeddingCallRetriesAsManyTimesAsTheCallerAsked (3 -> 3 requests) deliberately treat the value as an attempt count, matching the SDK. 'WithMaxRetries(1) allows no retry on embeddings' is therefore the same on both surfaces and not a divergence. The default is sdk.DefaultMaxRetries=5 (mistralmodel.go:35), so both surfaces make 5 attempts unless the caller overrides it. The only divergence is an explicit 0. There embeddings makes 1 attempt, which is the literal meaning of 'zero retries' and exactly what BASE embeddings did (one request, always). The chat path's 0->5 is a quirk of the vendor SDK that predates this PR. Copying that quirk would send 5 requests to a caller who asked for none, so this is not a defect to fix in the embeddings code.

dropped.judge_reason:
Only half the finding holds up, and that half is not a defect worth a comment.

The WithMaxRetries(1) claim is wrong. mistral-go v1.1.0 client.go loops `for i := 0; i < c.maxRetries; i++`, so the SDK also treats the value as a total attempt count. WithMaxRetries(1) gives one attempt on chat, on embeddings, and at BASE. There is no divergence. The "maximum number of retries" doc wording was already wrong before this PR, for both surfaces.

The only real difference is an explicit WithMaxRetries(0). Embeddings now make 1 attempt (mistralembed.go:72-75). Chat makes 5, because NewMistralClient maps 0 to DefaultMaxRetries. The default is unaffected: New() sets maxRetries to sdk.DefaultMaxRetries (mistralmodel.go:35), so callers who never set the option get 5 on both surfaces.

The 0 -> 1 mapping is deliberate. Commit 55c4161 added TestZeroRetriesStillSendsTheRequestOnce for it, and it matches the literal meaning of "zero retries". The chat side's 0 -> 5 comes from the vendor SDK and predates this PR. Copying it would send 5 requests to a caller who asked for none.

The wire impact vs BASE is also small. The SDK sends the same *http.Request again after its body has been read, so a 503 that carries a JSON body (the normal Mistral case) got 1 real request plus local "ContentLength=N with Body length 0" failures. That is what the reproduce verifier observed. At BASE, SDK-routed embeddings in practice did not retry either.

At most this is a cosmetic inconsistency caused by a pre-existing SDK quirk, not a release regression.

dropped.title: Converse door now fails any BinaryPart that is not one of four image types, including text/plain
dropped.summary: convertUserOrAssistantMessage treats every BinaryContent (message Type "image") as an image and returns ErrUnsupportedImageFormat when the MIME type is not jpeg/png/webp/gif. A text/plain part that the base Converse door sent as a text block now fails before the request. The sentinel lives in an internal package, so callers cannot match it with errors.Is.
dropped.failure_scenario: WithConverseAPI + Claude Sonnet 4.5. Messages: a system prompt, then a user message whose only part is llms.BinaryPart("text/plain", []byte("hello world")). The base release sent {"messages":[{"content":[{"text":"hello world"}],"role":"user"}]} and got an answer. HEAD returns "failed to build converse input: failed to convert messages: bedrock: unsupported image mime type: text/plain" and sends nothing. The error calls a text document an image, and bedrock.WithConverseAPI's doc still advertises document input.
dropped.evidence: Probe TestProbeConverseBinaryTextAlone (overlay, httptest Converse endpoint). HEAD: err=failed to build converse input: failed to convert messages: bedrock: unsupported image mime type: text/plain, and no request was sent. BASE: err=<nil>, body={"inferenceConfig":{},"messages":[{"content":[{"text":"hello world"}],"role":"user"}],"system":[...]}. Code: bedrockllm.go:249-255 maps every llms.BinaryContent to Type "image"; bedrockclient_converse.go:666-671 rejects any MIME type mimeTypeToFormat does not know; ErrUnsupportedImageFormat is declared in llms/bedrock/internal/bedrockclient, so code outside the module cannot import it. The new tests pin only image/heic (converse_image_test.go:87).

repro.evidence: Code: bedrockllm.go:249-255 maps every llms.BinaryContent to bedrockclient.Message{Type:"image"}. At HEAD, convertUserOrAssistantMessage (bedrockclient_converse.go:666-671) calls mimeTypeToFormat (provider_nova.go:400, which knows only jpeg/png/webp/gif) and returns `fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrUnsupportedImageFormat, msg.MimeType)` for anything else. The base version (base bedrockclient_converse.go:548-553) sent any non-empty Content as a text block. Probe TestProbeV3ConverseTextPlain (WithConverseAPI, claude-sonnet-4-5; system prompt plus a user message with a single BinaryPart): HEAD text/plain gives requests=0, err="failed to build converse input: failed to convert messages: bedrock: unsupported image mime type: text/plain"; application/json fails the same way; image/png is now sent correctly as an image block. BASE: text/plain and application/json give requests=1, err=<nil>, body {"messages":[{"content":[{"text":"hello world"}],"role":"user"}],...}. Base also sent image/png bytes as a text block, so base image input was itself broken; the regression is limited to text-like MIME types. ErrUnsupportedImageFormat is declared in the internal package llms/bedrock/internal/bedrockclient. The WithConverseAPI doc (bedrockllm_option.go:72) still advertises "Multimodal input support (text, images, documents)".
repro.comment: The Converse door now treats every `BinaryContent` as an image and fails on any MIME type other than jpeg/png/webp/gif, text included. `llms.BinaryPart("text/plain", []byte("hello world"))` with `WithConverseAPI()` now returns `bedrock: unsupported image mime type: text/plain` and sends nothing. The previous release sent it as a `{"text":"hello world"}` block (httptest probe: application/json fails the same way at HEAD and worked on the base). The fix to images is right, since the base sent image bytes as text. But text-like parts regressed, the error calls a document an image, and `ErrUnsupportedImageFormat` lives in an internal package, so callers cannot match it with `errors.Is`. Suggest keeping `text/*` (and JSON) as text blocks or mapping them to a Converse `DocumentBlock`, re-exporting the sentinel from `llms/bedrock`, and making the `WithConverseAPI` doc about "documents" match what is supported.

refute.reason: This is intended. Commit 132377f says 'A mime type Converse has no format for now fails before the network instead of travelling as text'. In BASE the Converse converter ignored the message type and sent every BinaryContent's raw bytes as a text block: PNG bytes arrived as garbage text and PDFs as mojibake. text/plain only 'worked' by accident of that bug. The default door (legacy InvokeModel) never supported a text/plain BinaryPart either: BASE sent it to the vendor as an image block, and ab2eae3 now makes it fail locally with the same allow-list and sentinel. Converse, legacy Anthropic and Nova therefore now agree. Text belongs in llms.TextPart; BinaryPart maps to an image on every door (bedrockllm.go:249-255). What remains is cosmetic: the error wording says 'image', and the sentinel is not re-exported from package bedrock. Neither is the claimed regression.

dropped.judge_reason:
The probes are right that the behaviour changed. At BASE, WithConverseAPI sent a text/plain BinaryPart as a text block; HEAD refuses it before the network with ErrUnsupportedImageFormat. It is still not a defect worth an inline comment:
(1) BASE only handled text/plain because of a bug. The BASE Converse converter never read msg.Type, so it sent every BinaryContent's raw bytes as a text block. PNG and JPEG arrived as replacement-rune garbage and PDFs as mojibake. Commit 132377f (PAGI-256) fixes that and says why: "A mime type Converse has no format for now fails before the network instead of travelling as text."
(2) Across the library, a BinaryPart means an image. The bedrock README says so (BinaryPart -> Message{Type:"image"}), and bedrockllm.go:249-255 maps every BinaryContent to Type "image". The legacy Bedrock Anthropic and Nova paths and the direct anthropic door (anthropicllm.go:793) send it as an image block, the openai door sends it as image_url, and ollama puts it in images. On the default Bedrock door, a text/plain BinaryPart got a vendor 400 at BASE. HEAD's ab2eae3 refuses it locally with the same allow-list and sentinel, so Converse and legacy now agree. Text belongs in llms.TextPart.
(3) The new failure is loud and happens before the request, not a silent break. It replaces silently sending corrupted bytes for every non-text binary input.
(4) The rest is cosmetic or was already there. The error text says "image" for a text MIME. The sentinel sits in an internal package, but package bedrock re-exports no sentinels at all, so this is not a break from an existing pattern. The WithConverseAPI "documents" claim was not changed by this PR, and it was not true at BASE either.

dropped.title: Saturation table breaks the bedrockclient test build on 32-bit targets
dropped.summary: TestConverseMaxTokensSaturatesInsteadOfWrapping puts the untyped constants math.MaxInt32+1 and 3_000_000_000 into an `int` struct field. That field overflows where int is 32 bits, so the whole bedrockclient test package stops compiling on 386 and arm.
dropped.failure_scenario: `GOARCH=386 go test ./llms/bedrock/internal/bedrockclient/` (or any 32-bit ARM runner) fails with a build error. Every test in the package is lost there, not just this one. On BASE the same command passes.
dropped.evidence: On HEAD, `GOARCH=386 go test -p 2 ./llms/bedrock/internal/bedrockclient/` prints `bedrockclient_converse_test.go:1150:25: cannot use math.MaxInt32 + 1 (untyped int constant 2147483648) as int value in struct literal (overflows)` and `:1151:29: cannot use 3_000_000_000 ... (overflows)`, then `FAIL [build failed]`. The same command on the BASE checkout prints `ok`. Fix options: a `//go:build` guard (for example on unsafe.Sizeof(int(0))==8 via a 64-bit-only file), or build the out-of-range values at run time.

repro.evidence: At HEAD, `GOARCH=386 go vet ./llms/bedrock/internal/bedrockclient/` fails with `bedrockclient_converse_test.go:1150:25: cannot use math.MaxInt32 + 1 (untyped int constant 2147483648) as int value in struct literal (overflows)`. The same command on BASE (da7016e) is clean. The table field is `in int`, and the rows {math.MaxInt32+1} and {3_000_000_000} were added in 058e344 ('saturate max tokens instead of wrapping'), so the whole test package fails to compile wherever int is 32 bits. The repo has no .github/workflows that target 386 or arm, so no CI run shows the break today. It affects anyone who runs tests on a 32-bit target.
repro.comment: The saturation table puts untyped constants `math.MaxInt32 + 1` and `3_000_000_000` into an `int` field. Where `int` is 32 bits these overflow at compile time, so every test in the bedrockclient package is lost on 386/arm, not just this one. `GOARCH=386 go vet ./llms/bedrock/internal/bedrockclient/` at 355dc71 reports `bedrockclient_converse_test.go:1150:25: cannot use math.MaxInt32 + 1 (untyped int constant 2147483648) as int value in struct literal (overflows)`. On da7016e the same command is clean. Suggested fix: build the out-of-range values at run time and skip those rows when `strconv.IntSize == 32` (where they can't occur anyway), or move the two rows into a 64-bit-only file with a `//go:build amd64 || arm64 || ...` constraint.

refute.reason: The overflow is real: `GOARCH=386 go vet` on HEAD fails at bedrockclient_converse_test.go:1150 and passes on BASE for this one package. But 32-bit has never been a target of this repo. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yaml) runs only ubuntu-latest amd64. BASE itself does not build on 386: `GOARCH=386 go vet ./...` on BASE fails in production code at vectorstores/pgvector/pgvector.go:144/161/184 (int64 advisory-lock constants passed as int), and also on the chroma, milvus and weaviate dependencies. HEAD adds the same overflow pattern in three other new tests (internal/numutil/num_test.go:18, llms/googleai/googleai_unit_test.go:1148, llms/openai/extra_body_merge_test.go:59), so this is a repo-wide 64-bit assumption, not a regression in this spot. Importers never compile _test.go files, so no application calling the library is affected. Adding a build tag or runtime-built values here would be cosmetic while the repo stays unbuildable on 386.

dropped.judge_reason: The overflow is real. On HEAD, `GOARCH=386 go vet ./llms/bedrock/internal/bedrockclient/` fails at bedrockclient_converse_test.go:1150:25 (`math.MaxInt32 + 1` into an `int` field), and the same package is clean on BASE. It does not harm anyone who uses the library, though. It sits only in a _test.go file, which importers never compile, and `GOARCH=386 go build ./llms/bedrock/...` on HEAD succeeds, so the production code still builds on 32-bit. 32-bit has never been a target of this repo either. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yaml) runs only ubuntu-latest amd64. BASE already fails to compile on 386 in production code: `GOARCH=386 go vet ./vectorstores/pgvector/` on BASE reports overflows at pgvector.go:144/161/184, where the int64 advisory-lock constants are passed as int. HEAD also adds the same 64-bit-only test pattern in three other new tests: internal/numutil/num_test.go:18, llms/googleai/googleai_unit_test.go:1148 and llms/openai/extra_body_merge_test.go:59. This spot is one case of a repo-wide 64-bit assumption, not a release regression. An inline comment here would be cosmetic, so I am dropping it.

repro.evidence: Probe internal/httprr zz_probe_v3llmprov_test.go (overlay, HEAD): a fake transport returns X-Litellm-Key-Spend, Llm_provider-Openai-Organization: org-REALORG, Llm_provider-Openai-Project: proj_REALPROJECT, Anthropic-Organization-Id: 1904456a-real and Openai-Project: proj_direct. repro.comment: The response scrubber now drops `X-Litellm-*` and masks `Openai-Organization`/`Openai-Project`, but the same identifiers still get into recordings under other names. I checked with a recorder probe: a response with `Llm_provider-Openai-Organization`, `Llm_provider-Openai-Project` and `Anthropic-Organization-Id` is written to the cassette verbatim, and only `X-Litellm-*` is removed. LiteLLM documents that it returns upstream response headers prefixed with `llm_provider-` (docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/response_headers). So re-recording through the gateway, as internal/httprr/README.md now describes, would likely record the org and project ids. This part depends on LiteLLM's forwarding, and no cassette has these headers yet. Direct recordings already leak today: 32 anthropic cassettes carry one real `Anthropic-Organization-Id`, and `TestMoonshot_MultiTurnToolCallWithReasoning.httprr` carries a `Msh-Project-Id`. Suggested fix: strip the `llm_provider-` prefix before running the org/project rules, add `Anthropic-Organization-Id` and `Msh-Project-Id` to the masked set, and extend the repo sweep to check them.

existing.summary: noPrefillClaude is missing the -latest aliases that the PR classifies as adaptive-only elsewhere.
existing.failure_scenario: ClaudeRejectsAssistantPrefill("claude-opus-latest") is false while "claude-opus-4-7" is true, so a request to claude-opus-latest ending on an assistant turn gets a vendor 400 instead of ErrAssistantPrefillUnsupported.

existing.title: OpenAI effort caps not limited to ProviderOpenAI
existing.summary: The OpenAI effort-caps branch is not limited to ProviderOpenAI, so the reasoning hint advertises controls that other doors never send.
existing.failure_scenario: ReasoningSupportFor("openai.gpt-5.6-luna", ProviderBedrock) reports Known with efforts low..xhigh, while the Bedrock door resolves MechanismNone and sends nothing.

In HEAD, reasoning_support.go:115 `if caps := reasoning.OpenAIReasoningCapsFor(model); caps.Known` has no provider guard. OpenAIReasoningCapsFor strips the vendor prefix through modelSpellings, so Bedrock-style IDs match. Probe (reasoning package, via llms.ReasoningSupportFor): openai.gpt-5.6-luna and openai.gpt-5.2 return Known=true with Efforts [low medium high xhigh] and Mechanism=Adaptive for ProviderBedrock, ProviderOllama, ProviderGoogleAI and ProviderOpenAI alike. moonshotai.kimi-k3 returns Known=true with [low high max] on every provider. For the same names, reasoning.ResolveMechanism, which picks the Bedrock converse door's wire mechanism in bedrockclient_converse.go:260, returns MechanismNone (0), so that door sends no reasoning field. The harm is limited to a misleading UI hint, not a wire error.
repro.comment: This branch applies the OpenAI effort-caps table to every provider because the `p == reasoning.ProviderOpenAI` guard the previous release had was dropped. I ran a probe: `ReasoningSupportFor("openai.gpt-5.6-luna", ProviderBedrock)` (also `openai.gpt-5.2` and `moonshotai.kimi-k3`, on Bedrock, Ollama or GoogleAI) reports `Known=true` with effort levels (`low..xhigh` or `low/high/max`) and `Mechanism=Adaptive`. refute.reason: The strongest counter-argument: commit 8ed1f1c deliberately made the OpenAI caps branch provider-independent ('keep known reasoning efforts behind any transport label'), and TestOpenAIHintSurvivesTheTransportLabel pins gpt-5 and o3 as Known on ProviderBedrock. For that id the Converse door resolves MechanismNone: IsGptOssModel is false, so no reasoning_effort is sent. A probe confirmed the hint reports Known=true with Efforts [low medium high xhigh] and Mechanism=Adaptive while ResolveMechanism returns MechanismNone. This contradicts the type's own contract ('never fabricates a capability it cannot back') and the other Bedrock hint tests, which keep the hint aligned with what the Converse door sends (for example TestTheBedrockHintPresentsNoReasoningWhereTheConverseDoorHasNone). BASE gated this branch on p == ProviderOpenAI, so Bedrock got Known=false. The misleading hint is new.

existing.title: tool message with extra parts fails
existing.summary: handleToolMessage now fails on any part of a tool message that is not a ToolCallResponse.
existing.failure_scenario: A tool message with parts [ToolCallResponse, TextContent] returns "invalid content type for tool message"; the base used Parts[0] and ignored the rest, and the OpenAI door tolerates text parts.

repro.evidence: At HEAD, handleToolMessage (llms/anthropic/anthropicllm.go:918-935) loops over all msg.Parts and returns ErrInvalidContentType on the first part that is not llms.ToolCallResponse. BASE (da7016e, line 870) only type-asserted msg.Parts[0] and ignored the remaining parts. The change came from commit 32c5a67 "fix(anthropic): send every tool result of a tool message", whose message says it "still refuses a part of any other kind". I ran a probe calling handleToolMessage directly in both checkouts (probes/anthropic-toolmsg-textpart, via overlay). With parts [ToolCallResponse{a}, TextContent{"note"}], HEAD returns err="anthropic: invalid content type for tool message", while BASE returns err=nil with a user message holding one tool_result for a. With parts [TextContent, ToolCallResponse], both versions fail, so the regression is limited to a trailing non-response part. The OpenAI door handles the same message differently: its handleToolMessage (llms/openai/openaillm.go:263-278) explicitly skips llms.TextContent parts ("ignore text content, it should be handled on ExtractToolParts call"), so a mixed tool message that OpenAI accepts is now refused by the Anthropic door.
repro.comment: `handleToolMessage` now refuses a tool message that contains any part other than `llms.ToolCallResponse`. A tool message with parts `[ToolCallResponse{ID:"a"}, TextContent{"note"}]` used to be sent as a single `tool_result`, because the previous release read only `Parts[0]`. Now it fails with `anthropic: invalid content type for tool message`. The OpenAI door explicitly skips `TextContent` in tool messages, so conversation history built for OpenAI breaks when it is replayed through Anthropic. I confirmed this with a probe that calls `handleToolMessage` on the same message: HEAD returns the error, BASE returns `{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"a",...}]}`. Suggested fix: keep collecting every `ToolCallResponse` (the multi-result fix from 32c5a67 is right). Skip `TextContent` parts, or send them as trailing `text` blocks, which the Messages API allows after `tool_result` blocks. Return the error only when no `ToolCallResponse` is present or a part has a truly unsupported type.

refute.reason: The code confirms the regression. In BASE, handleToolMessage (anthropicllm.go:870) read only Parts[0]: [ToolCallResponse, TextContent] succeeded and the text was silently dropped. In HEAD (anthropicllm.go:918-935, commit 32c5a67), the loop returns ErrInvalidContentType on any part that is not a ToolCallResponse, so that call now fails. The strongest case for dismissing it is the commit message, which says the door 'still refuses a part of any other kind'. But BASE refused only a non-tool first part and never refused trailing parts, so rejecting trailing text is new behaviour and not a kept one. Also, the commit set out to fix multiple tool results; it did not set out to reject text. The input occurs in practice: the other doors accept text in tool messages on purpose. openai handleToolMessage has an explicit 'case llms.TextContent: // ignore text content' and ExtractToolParts forwards it. googleai maps ChatMessageTypeTool to RoleUser with all parts. Bedrock anthropic maps the tool role to user content. The Anthropic Messages API also accepts text blocks next to tool_result in a user turn, so these parts could be sent as text blocks instead of making the call fail. No test pins the rejection: tool_results_test.go covers only multiple ToolCallResponse parts. A caller that worked on the previous release now gets an error, and none of the reasons to dismiss it hold up.

existing.title: think sent to models that cannot think
existing.summary: resolveThink sends think (a level or true) on every ReasoningOn request regardless of whether the model can think; the base door never sent think.
existing.failure_scenario: WithModel("llama3.2") + WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh,0) puts "think":"high" in the request (checked). Ollama v0.32.5 returns HTTP 400 "llama3.2 does not support thinking", so a call that used to succeed now fails.

BASE had no Think field at all (grep finds no 'Think' in base llms/ollama). Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-langchaingo/190be914-a4ca-51a0-89e2-3fbdbb6fc0c9/scratchpad/probes/v1-ollama-think/probe_test.go uses ollama.New(WithServerURL(httptest), WithModel("llama3.2")) and GenerateContent(..., llms.WithReasoning(llms.ReasoningHigh,0)). The fake server copies the Ollama server's check. HEAD request body is {..."options":{"num_predict":16384},"think":"high"} and the result is `400 Bad Request: "llama3.2" does not support thinking`. BASE request body has no think field and the call returns ok. The server-side rule is taken from the vendored module github.com/ollama/ollama@v0.32.5 server/routes.go:469-473: when the model lacks CapabilityThinking and `req.Think != nil && req.Think.Bool()` it returns 400 "%q does not support thinking". api/types.go ThinkValue.Bool() returns true for "high"/"medium"/"low"/"max" and for true. Think=false (ReasoningOff) is harmless because Bool() is false. The intent commit is 74419cd 'send the thinking switch instead of leaving it to the server'.
repro.comment: `resolveThink` now sends `think` (a level, or `true`) on every `ReasoningOn` request whatever the model is. The previous release never set `think`. Ollama's chat handler (v0.32.5 `server/routes.go:469-473`) returns HTTP 400 `"<model>" does not support thinking` when a model without the thinking capability gets a truthy `think`, and `ThinkValue.Bool()` is true for "high"/"medium"/"low"/"max". So a caller that applies `WithReasoning` to all models (e.g. `WithModel("llama3.2")` + `WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh, 0)`) used to get an answer and now gets a hard error. I reproduced it with a probe against an httptest server that copies that check: HEAD sends `"think":"high"` and fails with the 400, BASE sends no `think` and succeeds. Suggested fix: only send a truthy `think` to models known to think (e.g. drive it from `reasoning.OllamaEffortsFor`/capabilities, or `/api/show` capabilities), and otherwise leave it nil with a warning. `think:false` for `ReasoningOff` is safe and can stay.

refute.reason: BASE never set ChatRequest.Think; HEAD's resolveThink (commit 74419cd) sends a level or true on every ReasoningOn request with no check that the model can think. The vendored Ollama v0.32.5 server/routes.go:470 returns HTTP 400 '%q does not support thinking' when Think.Bool() is true for a model without the thinking capability. So WithReasoning on llama3.2, which BASE silently ignored, now fails. The commit's purpose was to make WithReasoningDisabled reach the wire (think:false, which non-thinking models accept); nothing shows the enable-side break was intended. reportOllamaThinking gives no warning for this case, and think_request_test only covers glm-5. The best counter-argument is that an explicit reasoning request on a non-thinking model deserves a loud error. Even so, this is a silent compat break for applications that apply one reasoning setting across all models, and the error comes from the vendor, not a typed local refusal.

So a caller that applies `WithReasoning` to all models (e.g. `WithModel("llama3.2")` + `WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh, 0)`) used to get an answer and now gets a hard error. I reproduced it with a probe against an httptest server that copies that check: HEAD sends `"think":"high"` and fails with the 400, BASE sends no `think` and succeeds. Suggested fix: only send a truthy `think` to models known to think (e.g. drive it from `reasoning.OllamaEffortsFor`/capabilities, or `/api/show` capabilities), and otherwise leave it nil with a warning. `think:false` for `ReasoningOff` is safe and can stay.

existing.failure_scenario: OpenRouter with deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1 or z-ai/glm-4.6, and vLLM with zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air or deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3, all return ErrStructuredOutputUnsupported (checked). The base passed these through.

existing.title: Qwen DashScope rules on any host
existing.summary: The Qwen stream-only and enable_thinking rules treat bare qwen3-<N>b names as DashScope names on any host (o.host is ignored).
existing.failure_scenario: LM Studio or vLLM serving "qwen3-8b" with WithReasoning on a non-streaming call fails locally with ErrThinkingRequiresStream, and plain calls get "enable_thinking":false added (checked).

repro.evidence: openaillm.go:311 calls reasoning.QwenThinkingRequiresStream(model) and :321 calls QwenThinkingEnabledByFlag(model) without o.host. dashScopeSpelling (qwen_capability.go:30) only strips an optional 'dashscope/' prefix, so any bare name matching ^qwen3-\d+(\.\d+)?b(-a\d+b)?$ is treated as the DashScope model on any host. Only the guest rule uses DashScopeRoute(model, o.host). BASE sends no enable_thinking at all (grep finds only a doc comment). Probe TestProbeV1QwenHost in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-langchaingo/190be914-a4ca-51a0-89e2-3fbdbb6fc0c9/scratchpad/probes/v1-openai-host/probe_test.go runs against an httptest host (non-DashScope). At HEAD, model qwen3-8b with WithReasoning(High) non-streaming returns `reasoning on model "qwen3-8b" is available only on a streaming call` and sends nothing, and a plain call sends {"model":"qwen3-8b",...,"enable_thinking":false}. At BASE the first sends reasoning_effort:"high" with nil error, and the second sends no extra field. Reach: a bare qwen3-8b id occurs with vLLM --served-model-name, llama.cpp --alias, or LM Studio community GGUF keys. LM Studio's default key is qwen/qwen3-8b, which contains a slash and does not match. The extra top-level enable_thinking is ignored or harmless on vLLM, so the main harm is the local ErrThinkingRequiresStream.
repro.comment: The DashScope-only Qwen rules here (`QwenThinkingRequiresStream` at L311, `QwenThinkingEnabledByFlag` at L321) are called with the bare model name and ignore `o.host`. `dashScopeSpelling` treats any `qwen3-<N>b` name as a DashScope model whatever the endpoint is. A probe against a non-DashScope base URL (standing in for vLLM `--served-model-name qwen3-8b`, llama.cpp `--alias`, or LM Studio) shows two effects on HEAD. A non-streaming `WithReasoning(ReasoningHigh, 0)` on `qwen3-8b` fails locally with `ErrThinkingRequiresStream` and nothing is sent, and a plain call gets `"enable_thinking":false` added. BASE sent `reasoning_effort:"high"` and returned normally. Suggested fix: route the name through `reasoning.DashScopeRoute(model, o.host)` (as the guest-model rule on the next lines already does) and apply the stream-only and enable_thinking rules only to the `dashscope/` spelling.

refute.reason: The scope is narrower than the finding suggests. dashScopeSpelling rejects any name containing '/', and the regex needs the dash form, so vLLM's default 'Qwen/Qwen3-8B', LM Studio's 'qwen/qwen3-8b' and Ollama's 'qwen3:8b' are not matched (probe). Commit e360eb0 knowingly relied on re-hosts using slashed names. Still, any OpenAI-compatible server that exposes the bare name (vLLM --served-model-name qwen3-8b, a LiteLLM or llama.cpp alias, LM Studio community GGUF identifiers) matches QwenThinkingRequiresStream regardless of o.host. There, a non-streaming WithReasoning call now fails locally with ErrThinkingRequiresStream, and plain calls get enable_thinking:false. BASE had neither rule, so those calls went through. The enable_thinking:false field is mostly harmless on such servers, since unknown top-level fields are ignored, but the local refusal is a real regression. DashScopeRoute(model, o.host) already exists and would fix it.

existing.title: duplicated gpt-oss mapping
existing.summary: The Ollama door keeps its own gpt-oss detection and level mapping, duplicating reasoning.OllamaEffortsFor and GptOssEffort.
existing.failure_scenario: The two copies already disagree: gptOSSLevel("") returns "high" while GptOssEffort("") returns "".

refute.reason: The divergence given as the failure cannot happen. resolveThink (llms/ollama/ollamallm.go:338) and reportOllamaThinking (warnings.go) call gptOSSLevel only when ResolveMode()==ReasoningOn. On that path GetEffort (llms/options.go:141-172) always returns a non-empty value: the explicit Effort, "high" for Adaptive, low/medium/high from Tokens, or "high" for Mode==ReasoningOn. So gptOSSLevel("") is never evaluated. ValidateReasoning limits Effort to minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max. For every one of these, gptOSSLevel and reasoning.GptOssEffort (gptOssCaps.ClampEffort) give the same result: minimal->low, low->low, medium->medium, high->high, xhigh->high, max->high. The two name checks also agree for real Ollama names. takesOnlyGPTOSSLevels strips everything up to the last '/' and matches the gpt-oss prefix, as modelSpellings does. modelSpellings only adds handling for Bedrock regions, platform dots such as openai.gpt-oss and fine-tune wrappers, which do not show up as Ollama model tags. The two helpers also target different wires (the Ollama think level vs the Bedrock reasoning_effort field), so keeping them separate is a style/duplication nit with no behaviour difference, not a defect callers can hit. BASE had no think handling in the ollama door at all, so this is new code, not preexisting.

existing.judge_reason: The stated failure cannot happen. resolveThink (llms/ollama/ollamallm.go:338) and reportOllamaThinking (llms/ollama/warnings.go:47) reach gptOSSLevel only when ResolveMode()==ReasoningOn. On that path GetEffort (llms/options.go:141-172) never returns "": ResolveMode gives ReasoningOn either for Mode==ReasoningOn, and GetEffort then falls back to "high", or because Adaptive, Effort or Tokens is set, and each of those yields a non-empty effort. So gptOSSLevel("") is never evaluated. For every effort that can arrive (minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max), gptOSSLevel and reasoning.GptOssEffort (gptOssCaps.ClampEffort) return the same value: minimal->low, low->low, medium->medium, and high/xhigh/max->high. The two name checks also agree on Ollama tags. takesOnlyGPTOSSLevels lowercases the name, strips everything up to the last '/' and matches the gpt-oss prefix, which is what modelSpellings does. modelSpellings adds only Bedrock region, platform-dot and fine-tune-wrapper handling, and those forms do not occur in Ollama tags. The helpers also feed different wires: GptOssEffort is used only by Bedrock's reasoning_effort field, while gptOSSLevel builds the Ollama think level. What is left is code duplication with no behaviour difference a caller can hit, so it does not warrant an inline defect comment in a release review.

existing.title: default max output tokens raised to 16384
existing.summary: The googleai/vertex default max output tokens rose from 2048 to 16384 and is always sent, even when the caller sets no limit.
existing.failure_scenario: vertex.New + gemini-2.0-flash (an 8k-output model) without WithMaxTokens sends maxOutputTokens=16384, outside the model's supported range, so Vertex rejects the request with a 400.
existing.evidence: earlier review, vendor behaviour not re-measured

repro.evidence: The wire change is demonstrated. A probe (probes/gai-maxtok-pen) used googleai.New with a capturing http.Client and no WithMaxTokens. At HEAD, gemini-2.0-flash sends generationConfig {"candidateCount":1,"maxOutputTokens":16384}. At BASE the same call sent {"maxOutputTokens":2048,"temperature":0.5,"topK":3,"topP":0.95}. vertex.New now wraps googleai.New (llms/googleai/vertex/vertex.go), so Vertex goes through the same newGenerationConfig; the old base vertex door also always sent GetMaxTokens()=2048. HEAD has no per-model clamp: no Gemini output-limit table in llms/reasoning or llms/googleai. Vendor side: Gemini rejects an out-of-range value with 400 'Unable to submit request because it has a maxOutputTokens value of N but the supported range is from 1 (inclusive) to 8193 (exclusive)' for 8k-output models (bolt.diy #955; gemini-cli #7578/#8048 show the same check with the 65537 bound), and gemini-2.0-flash's documented output limit is 8192. Caveat: the example model, Vertex gemini-2.0-flash and flash-lite, reached retirement on 2026-06-01 (litellm PR #42850 citing Google's model-versions page), and current 2.5 and 3.x models accept up to 65536. So today the harm is limited to 8k-output models that are still served, such as Gemma on the Gemini API and legacy or pinned models. I could not measure this live: no keys, and ai.google.dev and docs.cloud.google.com are blocked from the sandbox. The recorded cassettes cover only gemini-2.5-flash, 2.5-pro and 3-flash-preview. The 2048→16384 change also raises output length and cost by default for every caller.
repro.comment: The googleai/vertex default output limit went from 2048 to `llms.DefaultMaxTokens` (16384), and `newGenerationConfig` always sends it, even when the caller never set a limit. A probe with a capturing HTTP client and no `WithMaxTokens` shows `"maxOutputTokens":16384` at this head versus `2048` on main-vxcontrol. Gemini rejects values above a model's output limit with 400 `...maxOutputTokens value of 16384 but the supported range is from 1 (inclusive) to 8193 (exclusive)`, so a call to any 8k-output model that still works today would fail by default. This includes Gemma on the Gemini API and legacy or pinned 2.0-era models; gemini-2.0-flash itself was retired on Vertex on 2026-06-01. This depends on vendor behaviour I could not call live. Suggest sending `maxOutputTokens` only when the caller or a `WithDefaultMaxTokens` set it, or clamping it to a per-model output limit. At minimum, note the 8x larger default output and cost in the changelog.

refute.reason: The change is deliberate. Commit 476f3a6 ('stop truncating answers at 2048 tokens') moved googleai to the library-wide llms.DefaultMaxTokens (16384) because the 2048 default cut Gemini answers off with MAX_TOKENS, and it re-recorded 16 cassettes and updated TestDefaultOptions to pin the new value. The base also always sent a default (2048), on both the googleai and the vertex doors, so only the number is new. The failure scenario depends on gemini-2.0-flash, an 8k-output model. Gemini 2.0 Flash and Flash-Lite (and their -001 versions) were shut down on both Vertex and the Gemini API on 2026-06-01, so that request fails today no matter what maxOutputTokens says. Every Gemini model still served (2.5-flash/pro/flash-lite, 3.x) allows up to 65536 output tokens, and all 32 cassettes that send 16384 (gemini-2.5-flash, 2.5-pro, 3.8-flash) got 200 responses. The vendor error does exist ('supported range is from 1 (inclusive) to 8193 (exclusive)'), but no live Gemini model is shown to trigger it at 16384. Gemma-on-Gemini-API is the only unproven residual case and is not what the finding claims. Callers who need a lower cap can use WithMaxTokens or WithDefaultMaxTokens.

existing.judge_reason: This is a false positive, so there is nothing to post. The change is deliberate and fixes a real bug. Commit 476f3a6 ("stop truncating answers at 2048 tokens") moved googleai onto the library-wide llms.DefaultMaxTokens (16384), which already existed at BASE and is the default for the other doors. The old 2048 default cut Gemini answers off with finishReason MAX_TOKENS. For thinking models the cap also has to cover thought tokens, so 2048 was actively harmful there. Sixteen cassettes were re-recorded against gemini-2.5-* and 3.x models and all returned 200. BASE also always sent a default maxOutputTokens (2048) on both the googleai and the vertex doors, so the only new thing is the value. The finding's failure scenario needs gemini-2.0-flash or flash-lite, the 8k-output models. Google shut those down on 2026-06-01, per litellm PR #42850 and the Vertex and Gemini API retirement notices. Before today (2026-09-28), that request already fails no matter what maxOutputTokens says. Every Gemini model still served (2.5-flash, 2.5-pro, 2.5-flash-lite, 3.x) accepts up to 65536 output tokens, well above 16384. The vendor error "supported range is from 1 (inclusive) to 8193 (exclusive)" is real, but no live model has been shown to trigger it at 16384. The only leftover case is Gemma served through the Gemini API. Nothing shows that it rejects 16384; third-party listings even give gemma-3-27b-it a 16384 output limit. That case is also not what the finding claims. A raised cap does not raise cost unless an answer would otherwise have been truncated, and truncation is exactly the bug the change fixes. Callers who want a lower cap still have WithMaxTokens and WithDefaultMaxTokens.

existing.title: penalties forwarded to every Gemini model
existing.summary: newGenerationConfig now forwards frequency/presence penalties to every Gemini model; the base never sent them.
existing.failure_scenario: A caller that sets penalties for all providers now gets 400 "Penalty is not enabled for models/..." from Gemini models that do not support penalties.
existing.evidence: earlier review, vendor behaviour not re-measured

repro.evidence: Commit 0f1bd3c ('carry seed and both penalties to the generation config') added FrequencyPenalty and PresencePenalty to newGenerationConfig at googleai.go:1096-1097 with no model gate. A probe (probes/gai-maxtok-pen) called gemini-2.5-flash, the door's DefaultModel, with WithFrequencyPenalty(0.5) and WithPresencePenalty(0.3). HEAD sends generationConfig {"candidateCount":1,"frequencyPenalty":0.5,"maxOutputTokens":16384,"presencePenalty":0.3}. BASE sent no penalty fields: the googleai config literal omitted them, and the base vertex door never set them. No warning is emitted either, because warnings.go lists the penalties as carried. Vendor side: several independent reports show the Gemini API answering 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT 'Penalty is not enabled for models/gemini-2.5-flash' (vercel/ai #8943, which also covers gemini-2.5-pro, fixed in the AI SDK by not sending them; litellm #26108 dated 2026-04-20). vercel/ai #4022 shows the same for gemini-exp-1206. Penalties reportedly work only on the 2.0/1.5 families, which are now retired on Vertex. No cassette or test in the PR records a penalty request, and I could not make a live call.
repro.comment: `newGenerationConfig` now sends `frequencyPenalty` and `presencePenalty` to every Gemini model, while main-vxcontrol never sent them (and the old Vertex door didn't either). A probe with a capturing HTTP client and `llms.WithFrequencyPenalty(0.5)` on the default model `gemini-2.5-flash` shows `"frequencyPenalty":0.5,"presencePenalty":0.3` in the request at this head and no penalty fields at the base. Several public reports show the Gemini API rejecting exactly this with 400 `Penalty is not enabled for models/gemini-2.5-flash` (also gemini-2.5-pro and gemini-exp-1206; see vercel/ai#8943 and BerriAI/litellm#26108). So a caller that passes shared penalty options to all providers goes from a silently ignored option to a hard failure on the default model. The failure depends on vendor behaviour; I could not call it live. Suggest gating the penalties by model, the way `reasoning.RejectsPenalties` does for DeepSeek and Grok: drop them with an `llms.WarningDrop` on models that don't accept them, instead of forwarding them unconditionally.

refute.reason: In the base, the Gemini generation config had no penalty fields, so WithFrequencyPenalty and WithPresencePenalty were silently ignored and the call succeeded. Commit 0f1bd3c (PAGI-177) deliberately adds FrequencyPenalty and PresencePenalty to newGenerationConfig with no model gate, and the vertex door now shares that path (bf0f012). Vendor behaviour is well documented: Gemini 2.5 models return 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT 'Penalty is not enabled for models/gemini-2.5-flash' (vercel/ai#8943; litellm#26108, filed April 2026, still current), and penalties were only supported on the gemini-2.0 line, which is now retired. The door's own default model is gemini-2.5-flash, so a caller who sets penalties for every provider goes from a working call in the base to a hard 400 in this release. No cassette records a successful Gemini call with penalties. The library's own convention for models that reject penalties (reasoning.RejectsPenalties for deepseek/grok: drop the field with a WarningDrop) was not applied to Gemini. Intent does not excuse the regression, because the commit's premise that 'the vendor validates them' is exactly what makes these requests fail.
